pages.name: Inquisition Contacts
pages.text:
No Inquisitor or Interrogator is without a web of contacts to feed them information or provide easier access to their faction’s resources and knowledge. In the field, most acolytes quickly learn to follow their superior’s example and cultivate a local network of spies and informants. An acolyte’s contacts can feed them valuable information and useful resources to further their mission or uncover the heresies hidden around them. Despite outward appearances, the Imperium is a turbulent sea of competing agendas and ruinous intrigue, where who you know and how credible a threat you pose are often far more important considerations than what is right or expedient.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.qxkAEAcB9xAl56Xa#personal-influence]{Contacts} are valuable tools for players. They are often a more expedient, not to mention interesting, way to get what they want from a Faction without going through the front door. For GMs, Contacts can begin as simple NPCs, a means of conveying information about a specific mission, who can later evolve into significant characters who their players care about. Contacts like these can generate twists and turns in the plot, come to player characters with problems that honour demands they solve, and be a reliable source of drama. A Contact going underground or disappearing entirely is a clear plot point for characters to investigate around their missions. Some might have perished in a player’s service, but others might backstab them and become a new enemy.

Using Contacts

Factions within the Adeptus Terra should provide Inquisitors and their acolytes with the services they need upfront. But often, bureaucracy and politicking behind the scenes can slow requests or stall them outright, particularly in situations such as:

  • The Patron’s or characters' Influence with a Faction is too low or negative.

  • Something the characters need from the Faction has highly restricted access.

  • Publicly interacting with the Faction could negatively affect the mission’s security or the party’s @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.KbejcPMug5gfoWWz]{Subtlety}.

  • Someone with significant regional authority inside the Faction is actively working against the characters or the Inquisition.

However, gathering individual Contacts within the Adeptus Terra and Factions beyond can help parties avoid these blockades or overbearing official procedures. They can get what they need faster, without undue oversight, potentially revealing more information than they would have received otherwise.

The following list represents what Contacts can provide to the characters and, the reasons for seeking them out:

  • Access: Entrance to restricted facilities or off-limits areas, often without supervision

  • Equipment: Faster requisition of restricted equipment or supplies (greater than Common Availability)

  • Information: Specialist or forbidden knowledge, intelligence regarding movements and rumours within the Contact’s Faction

  • Protection: Asylum within a Faction’s facilities or security granted by their agents

  • Services: Faster or discrete access to services the Contact’s Faction provides (such as medicae care, guidance, hirelings, or transportation)

Additionally, Faction Contacts listed in the rest of this chapter show examples of unique Rewards they can provide when players go above and beyond in dealing with them. Do not forget that some Contacts may be actively seeking the aid of the Inquisition; they may bring something to the table with their request or begin cooperating with a higher initial Loyalty.

Finding Contacts

During a mission, characters can search for Contacts using an appropriate social or investigative Skill, such as Intuition (Group or Human), Logic (Investigation), Lore (Adeptus Terra), or Rapport (Inquiry).

The GM will determine the Difficulty of the Test, considering any associated problems present in the world. For example, the Test could have a lower Difficulty if their Influence with the Contact’s related Faction is in good standing or a higher Difficulty if the party’s Subtlety rating is low and the Contact may wish to avoid interacting with Inquisition acolytes.

Outside of a mission, characters can encounter Contacts using the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX.JournalEntryPage.AuM2Lzd784VPe32b#consult-savant]{Consult Savant}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.r6clx5uYnIpkdaRq.JournalEntryPage.z9PTik4AMrYlbVhR#cultivate-network]{Cultivate Network}, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.r6clx5uYnIpkdaRq.JournalEntryPage.z9PTik4AMrYlbVhR#secure-information-network]{Secure Information Network} Endeavours or simply by spending time making the Tests described above.

The Influence characters have over their Contacts is recorded personally between the Contact and the characters. However, any Influence from related Factions is calculated with the Contact’s Influence, both positively and negatively.

Example

The characters have been working directly with Hogarth Drevet, a Ministorum preacher, for some time and garnered +2 Influence with him personally. However, the characters have −1 Influence with the Adeptus Ministorum, meaning they have a total of +1 Influence with Drevet. Due to his ties with the Ministorum, he must consider the Faction’s standing with the characters and act appropriately.

When approaching a new Contact from an existing Faction, the Contact’s baseline Influence begins at the same level (or their Patron’s Influence, if they can reveal such information safely). Outside known Factions, the GM should choose the initial level of Influence based on the Contact’s first impressions of the characters, which could easily be negative. The GM should secretly track their level of Influence, revealing it to the characters only if they investigate the Contact’s background or behaviours directly.

Characters who pursue the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX.JournalEntryPage.AuM2Lzd784VPe32b#consolidate-influence]{Consolidate Influence} Endeavour can negatively affect their Contact’s behaviour towards them. While their overall Influence with the related Faction improves, and any loss with their Contact’s personal Influence effectively balances out, the personal Influence decrease must be considered. The Contact may feel the characters have blatantly abused their Influence over them or unduly tied their reputation to any future actions the characters take — many believe Inquisition acolytes take foolish risks. The Contact may have witnessed this type of behaviour from the characters in the past.

Managing Contacts

Characters need to provide a means of secure communication with their Contacts. This could be as simple as setting up an established meeting place (perhaps their place of work or worship, away from prying eyes), building a communication network of cyphers and vox channels, or choosing a dead-drop location to pass letters.

Players should meet regularly with their Contacts, whether they have new information or not. Most Contacts feel safer and more reciprocal if a character appears to care about their well-being. Characters can do this during their downtime (GMs are encouraged to give this time freely outside other Endeavours). Contacts left idle for too long might grow complacent or detached, causing their loyalty to degrade.

A Contact’s attitude towards the characters aligns with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.qxkAEAcB9xAl56Xa]{Influence Table}, from the viewpoint of ‘This Contact Will Typically…’ instead of ‘Faction’.

You have proven yourself

Actions that can improve Influence with a Contact:

  • The characters act to protect the Contact from enemies within their Faction.

  • The characters act to protect the Contact from enemies outside their Faction or in the broader world (including the rest of the Inquisition).

  • The characters work to fulfil the Contact’s personal requests.

  • The characters aid the Contact with their Influence over other Factions or NPCs.

  • The characters raise the Contact’s station in life, professionally or personally.

Improving Influence with a Contact is more complicated than causing it to degrade — but definitively more manageable than changing the opinion of their entire Faction.

You ask too much…

Actions that can degrade Influence with a Contact:

  • Asking the Contact to risk their own standing with their Faction

  • Asking the Contact to do something unlawful or go against the Lex Imperialis

  • Asking the Contact for something more than their level of Influence can provide

  • Taking actions that place the Contact in danger

  • The Contact suspects the characters are lying to them or hiding pertinent information

  • Consider how the Contact feels about the Inquisition and whether the characters have revealed who their true master is to the Contact

  • The characters have blackmailed the Contact to work for them (this may cause their Influence to be locked in place, rather than degrade — until the Contact finds a way to free themselves from the characters)

Contacts that are mistreated or feel betrayed will make themselves hard to find or communicate with. Some within the Adeptus Terra may throw themselves upon the mercy of their Faction’s leaders, who may snub the party and their Patron by extension (possibly affecting their Influence). More radical elements may seek retaliation against the players' betrayal, becoming new enemies with their Faction’s backing behind them.

Creating & Making Contacts

While Contacts can arise out of existing or incidental NPCs, GMs can prepare a handful of Contacts before their sessions. Consider what Factions the players are likely to interact with and choose or create suitable Contacts that have ties to these Factions. For example, if they need to gain access to an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} datavault to follow a lead, an Administratum scribe would be an ideal Contact to make. But you could also consider an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus} Tech-Priest who regularly maintains aspects of the datavault or an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionist} thief who claims to know of a secret or unsecured entranceway.

Often, characters encounter NPCs that the players come to adore or perhaps revile. These make excellent candidates for Contacts since they are already present in the world, have an established personality, and players may care deeply about what happens to them (for better or worse). Consider giving them a higher or lower initial Influence, depending on how their previous interactions with the characters went.

As with the examples in the rest of this chapter, Contacts have a few key aspects you should consider when making your own:

  • What base-level information or services can the Contact provide (often tied to their representative Faction)?

  • What special rewards can the Contact provide players if they are treated well?

  • What big favours might the Contact ask of the players, presented as small adventure hooks or things for the players to pursue during their downtime?

  • What secrets does the Contact have that, if learned, the players could hold over them?

  • Who or what is the Contact’s true master? Who are they more afraid of versus the players? Does the Contact have any privileged or dangerous information about them?

  • Find an existing stat-block in Imperium Maledictum or another supplement that closely matches the type of Contact you are creating. What other Skills, Traits, or Equipment does the character need?

pages.name: Agira Chernov, Administratum Clerk
pages.text:
Agira Chernov, Administratum Clerk

Please don’t touch that. There is a system to all of this. Now, what do you need? I’m very busy. The data is not wrong. 10,000 units. Delivery within the decade. What is it you said? I’m very busy. Collation is underway. Please don’t touch that.

Born and trained on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Macharia}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Agira Chernov} is nearly the perfect @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} clerk: armed with a photographic memory and a mind for sticking to bureaucratic procedure. Agira has the aptitude to rise higher within the Administratum, but in her years of service, she has sworn away from moving beyond the rank of clerk. She tried it once and found it infuriating and understimulating. Her brusque demeanour tends to push others away, so she shuffled from post to post as higher officials tired of her lack of decorum. Eventually, she found her way back to the datavaults.

Her natural eidetic memory has filled her head with incalculable amounts of data, facts, and jumbles of cyphers and numbers. But her photographic memory does not work on people. She recognises faces, but putting names to them is often challenging if she does not see them in a dataslate or voxcaster. She can recall precisely how many tonnes of recaf were delivered to the hive over the past six months, but recalling the name of an assistant clerk she saw earlier that day would be a significant challenge to her.

Not all information @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Agira} has stored within her photographic memory is something she rightfully should have seen. After digging through datavaults and pulling on hidden threads, she encountered many forbidden lores. Naturally, she could not help but commit it to memory before it was too late. Despite destroying all traces of what she found, she is haunted by nightmares of what is now etched into her memory for good. So far, she has managed to evade any sort of Inquisitorial investigation but fears it is only a matter of time before someone comes digging around in her head for her darkest secrets.

She is terrified of psykers, knowing that her memory contains heretical texts they might be able to read with their unnatural abilities. She fears being mind-wiped, a fate for her almost worse than death — the decades of information gathered in her head represent her identity and the only thing she truly knows and loves.

To overcome the noise of her brain and all the information rattling within it, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Agira} medicates herself to sleep each night with the hardest amasec she can afford. This behaviour leaves her vulnerable and less effective outside her work. At nearly fifty years old, her age is starting to show on her gaunt face. The years have been kind, but she makes no attempts to care for her looks — they do not matter to the books, scrolls, and dataslates, so neither do they matter to her.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Agira} can be placed in any large @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} facility or datavault across the Macharian Sector.

Requests

  • It is by no means a formal request, but @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Agira} appreciates a quality bottle of amasec from time to time, especially one better than she can typically afford.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Agira} recently requested some logs from a datavault related to something she should not have seen, but her access was denied. She needs someone to gain access and strike her request from the record, paranoid that someone has noticed her snooping around.

  • A Tech-Priest recently visited her datavault, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Agira} believes they altered some existing records. What is on paper does not match what is in her head. She asks the characters to track this Tech-Priest down and discover what they have been up to.

Rewards

  • At a basic level of trust, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Agira} gives the characters access to search the records of her assigned datavault and anything legitimate she holds in her head.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Agira} knows that data is valuable, and so is its destruction. At a high level of trust, she offers to destroy information or alter records for the characters or their Patron.

  • With her greatest trust, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Agira} shares the horrific information she holds in her head, the secrets she should not know.

pages.name: Celestina Visconti, Socialite
pages.text:
Celestina Visconti, Socialite

Fine work, wouldn’t you say? Such graceful lines and splendid angles on a sculpture meant to show the God-Emperor at His most human... no wonder the sculptor who made it turned out to be a daemon-worshipping heretic. Now, did I ever mention to you that this was just the first one in a matched set of three?

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.9kYI2Oshwn0wqWUo]{Celestina Visconti} is the assumed name of a Highborn socialite who has a taste for the arts. She is famous for her wit, charm, and beauty and is a constant presence in high society. With her luminary status among the wealthy and the elite, few suspect she is a Progena, a graduate of a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.7E0Gkel1gSaxTgVu]{Schola Progenium}. Her noble title is a fabrication — instead, she has been specially trained to serve as the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum’s} eyes and ears among the gilded halls of hive city nobility.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.9kYI2Oshwn0wqWUo]{Celestina }is a petite lady who has been the beneficiary of countless cosmetic and rejuvenat procedures intended to keep her appearance youthful. Her face is stretched and fastened by various hooks while gilded tubes and wires snake through a gap between her face and the rest of her visage. Most notable, however, is that her face moves like an animatronic puppet as her eyebrows, lips, and chin shift until they form her intended expression — a process that lags a second or two longer than it naturally would.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.9kYI2Oshwn0wqWUo]{Celestina }is never without @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.Y6oJff3F4qo2Xhlx]{Modesta}, her assistant servoskull. Modesta’s chassis was made from the skull of a former peer, one who Celestina had to kill to ensure her graduation. It is covered in brass shell casings beaten flat, punctuated with a dagger embedded in Modesta’s forehead. The glass eye of the blade’s former wielder, a heretic who discovered Celestina’s true allegiance, sits in one of Modesta’s eye sockets, a steadfast reminder to her that she is always being watched.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.9kYI2Oshwn0wqWUo]{Celestina }revels in the lifestyle afforded by her role as a covert operative among the Imperium’s upper class. Given years to cultivate her assumed identity, Celestina can grant favoured characters access to exclusive hive spire locations to assist their investigations. Yet despite the love for her lifestyle, Celestina knows she must constantly prove her worth as a spy to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum}. As such, she is not above planting evidence to throw a scapegoat or two at her handlers to remain in their good graces.

The blade sheathed in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.Y6oJff3F4qo2Xhlx]{Modesta}'s forehead is a Knife with the Inflict (Poisoned) Trait and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.rD6BtFSjpfupZss1]{Mono-edge} Modification. It can only be drawn by Celestina’s hand or with her permission.

Requests

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.9kYI2Oshwn0wqWUo]{Celestina's} charms have attracted the wrong kind of attention… again. She discreetly tells the characters to convince a rather aggressive suitor from a notable @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#rogue-traders-of-note]{Rogue Trader Dynasty} to leave her well alone.

  • A local @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.cvpsLwcsXf4myIpK]{Adeptus Administratum} official is threatening @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.9kYI2Oshwn0wqWUo]{Celestina}'s cover. Their audit of the various nobility in the hive city means they will be able to trace her funding back to a dark corner of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Ministorum} and, thereby, her patron. She requests the characters dig up something she can use as blackmail on the official so that she can counter his audit with some dirt of her own.

Rewards

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.9kYI2Oshwn0wqWUo]{Celestina's} word is enough to open a host of doors in exclusive locations and the homes of the elite in the hive city. As long as the players keep up appearances as part of her entourage, she can drag them to almost any social function.

  • As an agent of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.9kYI2Oshwn0wqWUo]{Celestina} can pass on information to her handlers at the top of the Ministorum hierarchy and vice versa. Beneficial, if the players require Ministorum support at a moment’s notice.

pages.name: Darius Dauphine, Prison Warden
pages.text:
Darius Dauphine, Prison Warden

Welcome to Void’s Hold. Keep your hands to yourself and try not to think too hard; some of the inmates might hear you.

On the penal world of Jriak V, in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.y6qA7KARTXADwzeV]{Cytheris Subsector}, lies a secluded island chain home to a holding facility for captured psykers. Officially noted in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} record as Managruut prison, after the island where it is based, the facility was dubbed ‘Void’s Hold’ by those who toil there. Among the facility's many overworked staff is Warden @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.wyyOOGQNpAYh5Txm]{Darius Dauphine}.

Quiet and contemplative, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.wyyOOGQNpAYh5Txm]{Warden Dauphine} almost seems slow to the casual observer, but the traumas he has faced in his years of service to the Emperor have made a steel cage around his mind. Fear, joy, and pleasure are as foreign to Dauphine as sunlight is to inmates in the lowest levels of Managruut. Once an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} soldier, he served his time on the front lines but was taken captive by @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari} pirates. Darius was eventually rescued during a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#the-deathwatch]{Deathwatch} operation against the pirates, his near-lifeless body pulled from beneath a pile of corpses less fortunate than he. In the years after, he was interrogated by an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} Inquisitor and received a host of augmetic implants to stitch his mind back together and fortify it.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.wyyOOGQNpAYh5Txm]{Darius} owes his continued career to the same @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} Inquisitor, who saw fit to install him as Warden of Void’s Hold, but not without further debt or duty. Occasionally, the lowest reaches of the facility are used to hold xenos captives, typically @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari}, which Dauphine is sworn to keep secret. The psykers held in the upper levels are said to obscure any detection of the xenos held below by their sovereign affiliates, acting as a shroud. Dauphine is uncomfortable with this aspect of their arrangement, especially when the Inquisitor requests that he extract information from these prisoners and keep them alive. He would have difficulty holding back if it were not for his mental augments; his desire for vengeance is deep-seated.

The Ordo Xenos Inquisitor he is sworn to could be @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius}, one of his many aliases, or another of your own invention.

Requests

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.wyyOOGQNpAYh5Txm]{Darius} passes a handwritten message to the characters; letters scrawled like he was not looking at what he was writing. Decoding the scribbles, Darius fears his Inquisitor patron put a monitoring device inside his mental augments. He wants them removed without the Inquisitor’s knowing but lacks the agency to inspect them without getting caught.

  • Managruut Prison is running out of cell space. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.wyyOOGQNpAYh5Txm]{Warden Dauphine} would be grateful if the characters could petition the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.upGG1JZPDbC7dpJJ]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica} or use their influence with the organisation to divert or hasten the arrival of a Black Ship to Jriak V.

Rewards

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.wyyOOGQNpAYh5Txm]{Warden Dauphine} has many contacts across the penal world of Jriak V and other facilities beyond the system. Characters seeking to locate a particular inmate (including those obscured by redacted records) may be able to do so with Dauphine’s help.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.wyyOOGQNpAYh5Txm]{Warden Dauphine} could make space in Vold’s Hold for the characters to hold captured psykers or xenos entities they apprehend. Though without significant Influence over him, Darius’ patron would be informed about what the characters aim to secure.

pages.name: Hogarth Drevet, Imperial Cultist
pages.text:
Hogarth Drevet, Imperial Cultist

In my long years, I see that the Imperial Creed has been riddled with bullet holes. Countless ages and crusades have punctured its edifice, chapters torn like limbs severed; we brothers are its dutiful chirurgeons.

Brother @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5fAQrj0KDjAXkHRY]{Hogarth Drevet} is a devoted member of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum} living in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy#hive-skarthius]{Hive Skarthius}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy]{Persepolis}. He is an amiable attendant of a well-tended, modest, and largely forgotten shrine located in the mid-levels of the hive and has worked there for as long as anyone can remember. His current rank and station are often misleading; Drevet has a protracted and war-torn past and, despite appearances, carries considerable influence. He has the ear of many high-ranking officials in Persepolis and is a front-line survivor of many battlefields.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5fAQrj0KDjAXkHRY]{Drevet} has been gifted extensive augments and rejuvenat treatments to extend his life; he is currently around one hundred and fifty years old. He crusaded with the Frateris Militia in his early years alongside the Black Templars in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.y6qA7KARTXADwzeV]{Cytheris Subsector}. He charged headfirst into the fray side-by-side with the angels of the Emperor against heretics who strayed far from the Imperial Creed. One fateful day, he was struck down in single combat against a traitor guardsman, suffering wounds that he spent the next decade recovering from. He was told by the chirurgeon who revived him that an unnamed Space Marine personally carried him from the frontlines to the reserves to ensure he survived.

His shrine, the Cenotaph of Anamnesis, is more of a library than a traditional place of worship, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5fAQrj0KDjAXkHRY]{Drevet} is as much a fixture as the shrine’s collection of historical tomes — he became a scholar during his recovery period, filling his mind with all aspects of the Imperial Creed and tasked with complex research tasks. High-ranking nobles and servants of the Adeptus Terra visit the shrine regularly to converse with Drevet and hear his long-lived words of wisdom or hear a story from his time on the battlefield.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5fAQrj0KDjAXkHRY]{Drevet} has refused promotion many times; superiors within the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Ministorum} see him as the perfect example of a war hero, but Drevet is not a man who turns away from an incomplete duty. His current commitment keeps him bound to the library. He is reconciling the Imperial Creed against the tenets and potential revisions uttered by the now-returned Lord Commander and Imperial Regent @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.VVyxPjdULmCks7NP]{Roboute Guilliman} and how it pertains to the turbulent histories of the Macharian Sector.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5fAQrj0KDjAXkHRY]{Hogarth} is conflicted by this work and challenged by it — what his contacts in Terra provide him often fails to align with delicate aspects of the Creed. He knows that failing to complete his work here could result in civil war across the sector, so he works in secret despite the prying eyes of his superiors and to maintain outward appearances.

He is also armed with a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.tjUKnuDKTCCon28r]{Chainsword}, which he often fiddles the trigger of when nervous, and even carries about his library with him at all times. Regardless of his former injuries, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5fAQrj0KDjAXkHRY]{Drevet} can still hold himself in a fight, and sometimes, he yearns to return to the battlefield.

Requests

  • The local @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} lacks sympathy for @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5fAQrj0KDjAXkHRY]{Hogarth's} cause and refuses him entry to certain records and datavaults in the hive to further his research. Hogarth would have greater trust in the characters if they could use their influence to get him access, above or below board.

  • Brother @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5fAQrj0KDjAXkHRY]{Drevet} recently attended a service in the depths of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy#hive-skarthius]{Hive Skarthius} in a ruined cathedrum. The preacher alluded to the existence of divine beings other than the God-Emperor. Drevet believes the preacher is a heretic and requests the characters find out who else is associated with them before their vile doctrine spreads further through the hive.

Rewards

  • Brother @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5fAQrj0KDjAXkHRY]{Drevet} may be persuaded to grant the characters access to some of his library if they need it to investigate local cults further. His wizened advice, he gives freely.

  • He maintains secure, hidden places in the lower levels of the hive where he stores volatile texts and conducts sacred rites. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5fAQrj0KDjAXkHRY]{Drevet} can provide access to trusted characters if they need to rest, recover, or hide from heretics.

pages.name: Vesta Lorraine, Art Dealer
pages.text:
Vesta Lorraine, Art Dealer

You have a fine eye to recognise a remarkable piece of art, but we both know that is not why you’re here.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.DiCcUGLaqWptKqE9]{Vesta Lorraine} runs a sculpture gallery on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.nLrpWOo3BjHLB0FG]{Proteus Secundus}, located in the upper levels of Hive Raghul. It features pieces from across the Imperium, some of which predate the founding of the Macharian Sector. Most of the pieces are abstract, and their meanings have been lost to antiquity. All are in remarkably well-preserved condition. Everything is for sale, though only those who dwell in the spire’s highest levels have the resources or influence to acquire such works.

When meeting with clients, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.DiCcUGLaqWptKqE9]{Vesta} delivers an anecdote about each piece. Some deal with the speculated meaning of the sculpture, while others discuss the materials used or the world of origin. In some cases, they explain how the sculpture entered their gallery. In most cases, the stories mention how she first encountered the work while serving as seneschal to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#rogue-traders-of-note]{Klaskoloff Dynasty}. Vesta loves to namedrop, and any time the story can include a prominent member of spire society, she makes it a point to include the name or at least allude to it.

The art gallery is not @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.DiCcUGLaqWptKqE9]{Vesta}’s only source of income. It works well to grow her client base and allay the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.gQxTENJSdTQTVfDM]{Vigilites'} interest in her business, however Vesta also participates in the Silent Trade, acting as a broker for illicit xenos goods between interested parties. She has a variety of xenotech artefacts hidden in stashes across the hive and her gallery. She suggests that these were acquired during their service to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#rogue-traders-of-note]{Klakoloff Dynasty} but never explicitly stated as much. Notably, new items continue to enter this collection, suggesting that Vesta maintains active connections with Silent Trade suppliers. This collection seldom includes weaponry. Instead, it features a range of more esoteric devices, many of which she claims are merely convenience items from different xenos cultures.

If asked, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.DiCcUGLaqWptKqE9]{Vesta} refuses to explain how or when she left the service of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#rogue-traders-of-note]{Klaskoloff Dynasty}. If the characters follow up or investigate the Rogue Trader’s affiliates, they deny any knowledge of Vesta. However, they do so with a wink and a smile.

Requests

  • A noble attempted to sell a sculpture to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.DiCcUGLaqWptKqE9]{Vesta}. While the piece was exceptional, she believes it is a dangerous xenos artefact. Vesta refused to buy the cursed thing but wants the seller tracked down and the piece destroyed before it does any damage and outs her operations.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.DiCcUGLaqWptKqE9]{Vesta} acquired a spiralling sculpture that resembles chitinous armour plates. After displaying it for only a few days, she believes she can hear faint whispers emanating from the object and has not slept properly since. She hopes the characters take it off her hands and adequately dispose of it.

Rewards

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.DiCcUGLaqWptKqE9]{Vesta} is familiar with many xenotech artefacts. She can often identify their origins and sometimes a general understanding of their functions in exchange for service.

  • Becoming significantly indebted to the characters, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.DiCcUGLaqWptKqE9]{Vesta} may invite them to a Silent Trade secret auction. These auctions include many sculptures and works of art, among them xenos artefacts in disguise that fall under the Inquisition’s purview.

  • If the characters do seek xenos weaponry, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.DiCcUGLaqWptKqE9]{Vesta} has several contacts in the Silent Trade with whom she can arrange meetings. However, the characters need a high level of influence before she entertains this idea.

pages.name: Jerithin Hammer, Bounty Hunter
pages.text:
Jerithin Hammer, Bounty Hunter

Don’t worry sire, my boys and I will get you to across the hive, straight to the voidport, no interference from the gangs. But of course, there is the matter of payment. Tell me, what have the cog folk been cooking up over in Sector Seven-Theta?

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5CCbRXAMBtwviuFE]{Jerithin Hammer} is a retired gunslinger who runs a small network of informants and enforcers who scuttle through the reaches of the lower levels of Hive Oberyl on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.JbRBjmzRfWtxIo40]{Leonova}. He spent his youth protecting nobles and hunting down outlaws, making a name for his efficiency with a pistol and deadly accuracy. Now he leans on his substantial roster of former contacts to drive his enterprise.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5CCbRXAMBtwviuFE]{Jerithin} appears to be in his mid-forties, with rugged, well-worn features and short dark hair. He shows some signs of having rejuvenat treatments — his life experiences certainly cover more than one ordinary lifespan. He wears a long coat and always has a las pistol holstered on his thigh. Outwardly, he appears to spend his days drinking and gambling. From his corner seat in local watering holes, where he deals in games of chance all day long, he meets with contacts, peddles information between them, and wiles away his boredom with risky bets and watered-down drinks. It is where he has become comfortable doing business, down in the muck with his agents, and never too far from a full glass of amasec.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5CCbRXAMBtwviuFE]{Hammer} began his career as a decorated @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.actors.Actor.O49jTi2TzoFQH5GT]{Macharian Vigilite}. When he became embroiled in an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-hereticus]{Ordo Hereticus} Inquisitor’s investigation and informed on several of his former comrades, Hammer quickly left their ranks and fell to the underbelly of the hive. There, Hammer turned a hand at bounty hunting and protector for hire, which went hand in hand with a new lifestyle of drinking, gambling, and gossip-mongering. From time to time, the Inquisitor’s agents still call upon him for information or to act as a local guide — Jerithin knows he cannot refuse their call. Otherwise, he wishes to survive as long as possible and keep doing what he deems honourable.

His informants include people in hive society’s upper and lower echelons. The nobles he has worked for are happy to inform the man who saved their lives. Conversely, on the lower levels, his contacts garnered through bounty hunting include enemies and allies, former competitors, and retired gangers who know he honours his agreed prices.

Use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.bB0rMr6Gez3M9bME]{Ganger} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ZUWBWGM4eH7xFZ8P]{Dreg} stat-blocks to represent his network of informants and runners. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5CCbRXAMBtwviuFE]{Jerithin} can be placed in any hive city or relatively large Imperial settlement with a history of Infractionist activity.

Requests

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5CCbRXAMBtwviuFE]{Hammer} needs a local gang ousted from one of his favourite watering holes. There are just too many of them for him to deal with alone, and he is not as fast as he once was. They should think he is not involved.

  • A former employer of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5CCbRXAMBtwviuFE]{Hammer}, a noblewoman from the hive spires, has been accused of heresy by someone in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Ministorum}. Hammer knows this is false and wants the characters to look into it, thinking someone is framing her for political gain.

  • An outlaw @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5CCbRXAMBtwviuFE]{Hammer} brought to justice long ago, thought dead, has resurfaced in the hive. Hammer is paranoid that this man will seek revenge upon him. He fears using his agents might draw undue attention to himself. He requests that the characters investigate on his behalf.

Rewards

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5CCbRXAMBtwviuFE]{Hammer} prefers to reward people with information, or if something needs investigating, he can deploy members of his network to dig it up. His contacts include local dealers and low-hive artisans, who can source equipment for the characters under the table.

  • Though it has been a long time since he put a hole in someone, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5CCbRXAMBtwviuFE]{Hammer} would serve those he truly trusts by personally following them into battle, convincing those within his enterprise to join him.

pages.name: Lethic Arandir, Rogue Psyker
pages.text:
Lethic Arandir, Rogue Psyker

It is not lost, it just has not been found yet. Nothing is ever lost unless it is destroyed. That I can do nothing about, unfortunately

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vvgA1lyNkcTDw1xP]{Lethic Arandir} is a finder. People pay her good money to find lost things or lost people. Some call her a bounty hunter, but she never really gets her hands dirty; she identifies accurately where said bounty is holed up, but never goes as far as actually trying to claim it herself. In truth, Arandir is a rogue psyker who does everything she can to hide her powers. She uses them to make money through finding but intends never to use her powers in front of witnesses.

Gaunt and hollow-faced, with sunken eyes and stringy brown hair, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vvgA1lyNkcTDw1xP]{Lethic} is constantly bundled up in robes and clothes and always seems cold, no matter the temperature. Her thin fingers fidget with the edge of her long coat, and her eyes constantly move about as she sees wisps of the Warp gathering around her. Born into a merchant family, Lethic never took to the family business. She continually wandered away from her duties and often returned with some lost oddity or another. Soon she realised that her ability to find lost items and people could get her paid by those desperately looking for them.

So far, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vvgA1lyNkcTDw1xP]{Arandir} has been lucky enough to avoid the Inquisition’s notice. She is preternaturally conscious of those looking for her and aims to keep her head down. However, she is savvy (or foolhardy) enough to recognise that befriending a few low-level acolytes and Inquisitorial minions might warn her if the eyes of the Inquisition were about to fall upon her. If she learns who they are, Arandir will be eager to initiate contact with the characters, perhaps approaching them before they even know about her services.

She primarily uses the Minor and Divination @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.3mzwixuzgerGUpu1]{Psychic Powers} listed in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vvgA1lyNkcTDw1xP]{Rogue Psyker} stat-block. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vvgA1lyNkcTDw1xP]{Lethic} can be encountered on any sufficiently populated Imperium world or voidstation.

Requests

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vvgA1lyNkcTDw1xP]{Lethic} is careful when using her psychic powers, but recently, there was a witness. Lethic asks the characters to silence this witness. She knows exactly where they are, naturally, but they are on the staff of a local noble and stay within their estate. Lethic cannot get close without rousing suspicions.

  • A customer has hired @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vvgA1lyNkcTDw1xP]{Lethic }to find an exceedingly rare artefact. Unfortunately, she has tracked the artefact to a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.actors.Actor.O49jTi2TzoFQH5GT]{Macharian Vigilite} lockup. She needs someone with sufficient authority to access the lockup and retrieve the artefact.

  • Naturally, if the characters figure out that @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vvgA1lyNkcTDw1xP]{Lethic} is a rogue psyker, they would gain significant trust if they did not hand her over to the authorities or the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Astra Telepathica}. However, if she sees the characters exploiting her with this information, she will aim to disappear and has plentiful plans to do so without them catching her.

Rewards

  • The primary reward for gaining @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vvgA1lyNkcTDw1xP]{Lethic}’s trust is her ‘finding’ abilities, which are handy for finding items relevant to their investigations or Rare or Exotic equipment or items. Until she gains significant confidence in the characters, she will prefer to work alone (to better preserve her secrets). She can accompany the characters in person when greater trust is established, speeding up their findings.

  • If she trusts the characters well enough to keep her secret, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vvgA1lyNkcTDw1xP]{Lethic} is happy to use her powers in front of them or aid them in psychic rituals or related endeavours. (She gains access to the remaining @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.3mzwixuzgerGUpu1.JournalEntryPage.V5zDWussZivkFavj#divination]{Divination} Psychic Power).

pages.name: Mizo Leskar, Astropath
pages.text:
Mizo Leskar, Astropath

What you ask of me, challenges my oaths to the choir and this damnable house. But I cannot ignore the things I’ve seen here. Nethecaré thinks I’m disposable. They’ll consider it a betrayal if they find out I’ve been talking to you. If that happens, I know what fate awaits me at the Emperor’s table. So, I will assuredly take you down with me

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.4neMMGpoX4oC0yOt]{Mizo Leskar} is an exceptional psyker and former choir member of Hive @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf]{Rokarth}’s @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.lydNVBL1CeXU15kz#the-crystalline-reflectory]{Crystalline Reflectory}. At the behest of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#castyx]{House Castyx}, they were seconded to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#nethecare]{House Nethecaré} as the personal astropath of the house’s inner circle. Whilst Mizo enjoys the sense of individuality and newfound relative peace operating outside the psychic choir, they detest the house they are now bound to. Never have they been privy to so many terrible secrets all at once.

Yet @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.4neMMGpoX4oC0yOt]{Mizo} is duty-bound to comply with the house’s requests. The psyker is caught between representing the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.upGG1JZPDbC7dpJJ]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}, the direct orders of Planetary Governor @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#castyx]{Castyx}, and the most influential members of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#nethecare]{House Nethecaré}. Mizo spends their time between Hive Dalal and the Brass Hive on @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf]{Rokarth}, carted about unceremoniously at the house’s behest. The chorister knows this position is impossible to escape but wishes dearly to serve a more pious master.

Mizo is a flexible contact; should the characters require an astropath Contact on a planet other than @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.59y8WFXTbwKRwiRI]{Voll}, Mizo can be placed in another planetary governor’s court. With their Divination powers, it is plausible for Mizo to seek the characters out on Voll and make contact on their own.

Requests

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.4neMMGpoX4oC0yOt]{Mizo} has learned that a member of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#nethecare]{House Nethecaré’s} inner circle, Brynna Molsk, is secretly a rogue psyker. Not as powerful as Leskar by any means, Brynna has avoided detection by authorities for her entire life, yet she suspects that Mizo now knows of her hidden curse. Her presence disrupts Mizo’s abilities, like a constant buzzing in their ears. Mizo wants to get rid of her but is unable to do so.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.4neMMGpoX4oC0yOt]{Mizo} believes that someone is plotting to assassinate @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#castyx]{Planetary Governor Castyx}. They catch fleeting images in their visions of a strange spined snake coiling around the Governor’s neck and dark figures taking over the Governor’s court. Mizo is unsure what to do with this information. If they were to report this to superiors in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#nethecare]{House Nethecaré}, they are sure these warnings would land on deaf ears; Mizo thinks they could be involved.

Rewards

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.4neMMGpoX4oC0yOt]{Mizo} has snippets of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#nethecare]{House Nethecaré’s} most profound secrets in their mind and has slowly been piecing them together. The house goes against @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#castyx]{Lord Castyx’s} decree to share all the research they find in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.59y8WFXTbwKRwiRI]{Voll’s} acid wastes and their experimentations into psychic abilities go far beyond their remit. They are secretly working with an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} Inquisitor. They have detected a hidden psychic presence on Voll and kept it a secret (this could point to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W.JournalEntryPage.jt0zc7az5xNehcIZ#the-heralds-howl]{Herald's Howl} being present on Voll or psychic-capable strains of the acynadi they harvest).

  • It is rare for anyone in the Imperium to have a personal astropath in their pocket. If the characters gain the heights of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.4neMMGpoX4oC0yOt]{Mizo}’s trust, they will find the time to send psychic messages on behalf of the party — significantly reducing the time it takes them to contact entities outside the system.

pages.name: Orhys-Phi-07ET, Stranded Explorator
pages.text:
Orhys-Phi-07ET, Stranded Explorator

We do not have time for… Wait! I need to examine your sidearm immediately.

The Essential Revolutions was due to depart from the Macharian Sector shortly after the onset of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#silence-and-darkness]{Noctis Aeterna} and examine worlds along the sector’s barely explored borders. But, due to resource reallocation issues, extensive breakdowns, and tangled @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} bureaucracy, the voidship is moored at a void port above @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.jB9sg2SDLZJGZrac]{Eskutchax} for the next few decades. Until then, Explorator @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.rilaQaBPslIRzGco]{Orhys-Phi-07et} is effectively stranded with idle mechadendrites and minimal resources to continue his research.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.rilaQaBPslIRzGco]{Orhys-Phi-07et} believes he was built to be an Explorator, as any blessed machine is built for a specific purpose. Unlike his brothers, who appear content to wait for their ship’s departure, Orhys-Phi-07et believes he can get a head start on his Quest for Knowledge and has a hunger for travel. He is particularly interested in the Imperium’s lost technology and believes that during the Macharian Crusade, experimental weapons were fielded and never properly recovered. His ultimate goal, though farfetched, would be to discover a lost STC, thereby cementing his name in the annals of the Cult Mechanicus.

Though he keeps these feelings to himself, Orhys-Phi-07et does not believe in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus’} philosophy of insularity from the rest of the Adeptus Terra. He thinks the Explorator Fleet could be more agile and further their knowledge if they worked more closely with other factions, members of the Inquisition chief among them. He is eager to push the boundaries of where he can operate and investigate, but he does so with extreme caution. He knows that if his fellow Tech-Priests knew what he wanted to achieve, he would lose his station on the Essential Revolutions and be reassigned elsewhere by the Magos in charge.

He has garnered an extensive communication network across the sector for sharing information with other Explorators, Tech-Priests, and datavaults within the Mechanicus. This allows him to communicate with the characters at any significant port of call.

Requests

  • Until the Essential Revolutions is ready to depart (decades from now), @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.rilaQaBPslIRzGco]{Orhys-Phi-07et} would jump at the chance to accompany the party if they were to set out to any barely explored worlds. At the very least, he is hungry for any information they can retrieve from nearby @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Mechanicus} facilities to aid his quest.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.rilaQaBPslIRzGco]{Orhys-Phi-07et} feels that something more than bureaucratic failures is holding back the Essential Revolutions from departing, but he lacks the authority to investigate the delays and thinks that his fellow Tech-Priests would not want him poking around. He would be incredibly grateful if the characters could investigate in his stead and share what they discover.

Rewards

  • The Explorator can access many archives and datavaults that typical @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Mechanicus} agents do not — including classified analysis of xenos and heretical technology and the Explorator Fleet’s world surveys.

  • As an Explorator, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.rilaQaBPslIRzGco]{Orhys-Phi-07et} can recognise and analyse xenotech and archaeotech. If the characters recover a device of unknown purpose and origin, he may be able to help them discern both points. In many cases, he can demonstrate its function.

pages.name: Zarin Varuna, Logistics Officer
pages.text:
Zarin Varuna, Logistics Officer

Did you hear what happened on Somrot? No? Well, what if I told you the local Mechanicus found an Aeldari artefact buried underground? Hand over those solars and I’ll tell you the rest…

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ncXwqNsh38L8CyRo]{Zarin Varuna} is a dutiful servant of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#rogue-traders-of-note]{Hawkscar Dynasty} and a logistics officer aboard the Innocent, the voidship of the infamous Captain Ion Hawkscar. He is a cheerful yet wary man who has made careful, but largely successful, contact with individuals from a number of xenos species and works as an information broker for his captain. Zarin has a long roster of contacts throughout the sector due to the nature of his vocation and the vast distances plied by his captain.

Some think @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ncXwqNsh38L8CyRo]{Zarin} is simply a scapegoat for Captain Hawkscar, allowing his captain a measure of plausible deniability if he were ever discovered to be making contact with xenos entities. Zarin knows this is true, but does the hard work regardless, rewarded with sufficient autonomy to make his own deals and decisions. That said, he only trades in information and strictly stays away from the Silent Trade, striving never to be caught red-handed with any heretical xenos technology.

The true worth of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ncXwqNsh38L8CyRo]{Zarin}’s work is his contact with certain Craftworld @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari} and elements of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#the-leagues-of-votann]{Leagues of Votann} within the Macharian Sector and along its borders. He primarily made contact at Hawkscar’s behest to ensure the Dynasty was steering clear of any problematic xenos claims or traps at the reaches of the sector. He found that the xenos were eager to trade for similar information on Imperial movements and holdings in the sector, which he provided, but Zarin has never relinquished information that could interfere with Hawkscar’s interests. Furthermore, Zarin often arranges for xenos guides and mercenaries to complete missions without his captain’s knowledge, occasionally trading the service of his personnel (including himself) to xenos forces.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ncXwqNsh38L8CyRo]{Zarin} is a versatile Contact; he travels wherever the Innocent goes in the sector and can travel freely from orbit to planet with his own Arvus Lighter. He is often accompanied by three @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.pXsZLEawZr8Tf8Ym]{Armsmen} named Nila Lensk, Laskor Rausch, and Ekhter Viers, who protect him and the Lighter.

Requests

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ncXwqNsh38L8CyRo]{Zarin} declares that he will never work with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari} again. In one particularly disastrous deal with them, Zarin believes he became marked for assassination (or ‘consumption’, he is not exactly sure) by a Kabalite Warrior named Vivithrax Vhrex. He knows of the abandoned Imperial void station in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.d0lv2v4FkeIb43jj]{Drimor Subsector} the Kabal often uses and would feel greater peace of mind if the Kabal, or at least Vhrex, were no more.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ncXwqNsh38L8CyRo]{Zarin} believes that one of the armsmen assigned to him is informing captain Hawkscar of his various deals and actions. Effectively, someone to replace Zarin if the captain tires of him. He would appreciate it if someone could figure out who it is without the armsmen knowing they are being investigated. If Zarin knew, he could better control the information flow and ensure his essential position within the Innocent’s crew.

Rewards

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ncXwqNsh38L8CyRo]{Zarin} has a significant portion of xenos presence in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.d0lv2v4FkeIb43jj]{Drimor Subsector} mapped out — many parts he is sure the Inquisition know nothing about. He would only pass on such volatile information to those he truly trusted.

  • With sufficient influence, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ncXwqNsh38L8CyRo]{Zarin} can arrange face-to-face meetings with local xenos entities and broker the employ of xenos mercenaries among the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#the-leagues-of-votann]{Votann} factions he maintains contact with.

pages.name: The Inquisition Armoury
pages.text:
The Imperium is plagued with war and strife, conspiracy and heresy. The Inquisition, and those who serve it, delve deeper into the darkness than anyone else, bringing with them the Emperor’s light — and often, his fury. For this duty, the Inquisition must be well-equipped. This chapter contains a selection of wargear used by the Inquisition on the front lines of the hidden war for the soul of the Imperium, along with new essential tools for espionage and investigation.

Availability

The iconic arsenal of the Inquisition is beyond rare among open markets or traders. Some weaponry takes years to craft, wrought from materials almost impossible to acquire, and anointed by the most faithful of the Ministorum. Others are appropriated from the enemy itself, reverse-engineered tools of the xenos, or handcrafted along the Radical path, from secrets torn from the enemy and used to shape weapons, fighting Chaos with Chaos.

Rare equipment might be possible to locate across a breadth of worlds using an Availability Test; see @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.k5sND1C17nY9xB1G]{Trading Equipment}. Many of the items found in this chapter, however, are Exotic. These items might be unknown to many acolytes without specialised knowledge or research and beyond discovery in simple bartering. Exotic items are only available if the GM determines they are.

PATRON REQUISITION

Many Patrons firmly believe in using the right tool for the job, Inquisitors do not differ. As research or investigations begin to turn up more information, hints of the dangers ahead, or the peculiar nature of some of those threats, an Inquisitor might provide their acolytes with wargear that would otherwise be impossible to acquire.

Icons of Ordo and Philosophy

The Holy Orders of the Inquisition are known to differ not only in their approach but in their preferred tools. Such pieces of wargear become commonplace among their warriors, even symbolic. Many within the Orders can recognise a Malleus acolyte by the Daemonhammer they carry or a Hereticus acolyte by the Inferno Pistol strapped to their thigh.

Beyond these philosophical and methodological differences, Inquisitors across the spectrum of doctrine and darkness attain vastly different wargear. Various equipment throughout this chapter may note that certain items are limited to specific Ordos or specific to the Puritan or Radical Inquisitors and are, therefore, only possible to acquire with the agreement of the GM and a compelling narrative explanation.

pages.name: Melee Weapons
pages.text:
The Inquisition has a unique arsenal of Melee Weapons; each forged to fight the specific enemies of each Major Ordo or draw upon their enemy’s powers in unique ways to turn the tide. General rules for wielding @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.novkkBnSD2XC7Lgh]{Melee Weapons} are outlined in Imperium Maledictum, along with related @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.wsM53RDPPrqwS3Te#weapons-and-armour-traits]{Weapon and Armour Traits} and related @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.novkkBnSD2XC7Lgh#melee-weapon-types]{Melee Weapon Types}.

Exotic Melee Weapons

Exotic in both rarity and design, melee weapons of this classification draw on elements from multiple existing types or have wholly unique effects that confuse Imperial categorisation. Wielding most of these strange weapons would brand you a heretic by the Inquisition, often xenos in origin and effect.

Mundane Weapons

These weapons often predate the Imperium. They were simple tools once made of metal and wood, derived from primal Human designs. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.novkkBnSD2XC7Lgh#mundane-weapons]{Mundane Weapons} typically have only a few simple Traits.

Daemonbane Weapons

Many of the Inquisition’s weapons and armour are forged in the fires of faith. Anointed materials are wrought into staves and hammerheads, sanctified with holy oils and censers, and engraved with sigils to banish daemons and disrupt a psyker’s powers. Daemonbane weapons are astonishingly rare. Most are wielded by the Grey Knights, but some have been granted to the most dedicated servants of the Ordo Malleus.

Naming The Damned

The secret of forging a Nemesis Weapon, if it is still known at all, is held by no more than a handful of Inquisitors within the Ordo Malleus. It is known that the price of doing so is high, and this must be so, for otherwise such efficacious arms would surely be more prevalent.

The Inquisitor Vespar Draal of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.tFbQS9Pwk46yjwFq.JournalEntryPage.AyQTdRJpdVm3zqdF#ordo-hereticus]{Ordo Hereticus} is known to have set out to learn the means of forging such a weapon centuries ago, for he suspected his compatriots in the Ordo Malleus of corruption most foul. Though it is said he was successful, the endeavour would ultimately claim his life. His belongings are held within Vault of Follies on Suluk. These amount to a handful of his surviving written records, alongisde a great hammer of a dark metal. His grimoire is said to contain, among other things, the most accurate account of the death of Lord Solar Macharius, and the true name of a Greater Daemon.

Null

Null weapons are crafted to syphon away psychic energies, weakening daemonic entities and robbing rogue psykers of their power. Tests made to Manifest a psychic power that targets the Zone of the wielder, any individual within that zone, or made within Short Range of a wielder of a Null weapon, suffers from Disadvantage. Additionally, daemons treat the Zone of a wielder with a Null weapon as a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.zQYkbNcsJmGintdL#hazard]{Minor Hazard}.

Power Weapons

Typically reserved for the exceptionally wealthy, well-connected, or higher-ranking members of the Imperium’s military. They are deadly close combat weapons that, by using little-understood technology, generate a disruption energy field that amplifies their lethality. Power weapons often deal high Damage and have the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.wsM53RDPPrqwS3Te#penetrating-(rating)]{Penetrating} Trait while active. The following weapons have additional abilities, noted at the end of their entries.

Tainted Weapons

Used by the minions of the Dark Gods and by Radical Inquisitors who seek to use the enemy’s tools against the enemy, there are many weapons wrought by corruption. Each time the wielder of a Tainted Weapon spends or burns a Fate Point in relation to using the weapon, they gain 2 Corruption Points. Additionally, Tainted Weapons gain bonus damage equal to the wielder’s Corruption up to their Willpower Bonus (WilB).
