pages.name: Ranged Weapons
pages.text:
Inquisitors and their acolytes have a diverse selection of ranged weaponry available to them, depending on whatever covert conditions their mission requires. Often they must go outside the Imperium’s knowledge to acquire these armaments through xenos trade or syphoning energies from the very Warp. General rules for wielding @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.luQOhxIEeYF6tMgt]{Ranged Weapons} are outlined in Imperium Maledictum, along with related @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.wsM53RDPPrqwS3Te#weapons-and-armour-traits]{Weapon and Armour Traits} and related @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.luQOhxIEeYF6tMgt#ranged-weapon-types]{Ranged Weapon Types}.

Bolt Weapons

Standing alongside the Lasgun, Bolt weapons are the Imperium’s most iconic firearms, especially within the arsenal of its higher-echelon warriors. A Bolter’s rapid rounds of explosive death can tear most enemies apart in seconds, a much-needed trait against the enemies of Ordo Malleus Inquisitors. When loaded with standard Bolt ammunition, Bolt weapons have the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.wsM53RDPPrqwS3Te#penetrating-(rating)]{Penetrating} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.wsM53RDPPrqwS3Te#spread]{Spread} Traits.

Crossbow Weapons

The low-tech Crossbow is rarely seen on the battlefields of the 41st Millennium, only on some feral or feudal worlds. However, more specialised crossbows are still in use and have become iconic implements among some Ordo Hereticus retinues. Though often cumbersome, their boon comes from the specialist ammunition they can fire. Crossbow Weapons typically have the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.wsM53RDPPrqwS3Te#penetrating-(rating)]{Penetration} Trait.

Flame Weapons

Despite their differences, the Imperium and their most foul enemies stand together in recognising the potency of wielding liquid flame upon the battlefield, a terrifying combination of destruction and purity. Flame weapons always have the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.wsM53RDPPrqwS3Te#flamer]{Flamer} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.wsM53RDPPrqwS3Te#inflict-(condition)]{Inflict} (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#ablaze]{Ablaze}) Trait, and often have limited magazines.

Graviton Weapons

Graviton weapons date back to the Dark Age of Technology. They are extremely rare and jealously guarded by members of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.XFPir4cg9PIHWNkc]{Adeptus Mechanicus}. The weapons are believed to fire exotic particles that affect the gravitational field within a small area. While the lowest power setting might knock a creature prone, the higher settings can crumple armour, rupture organs, and breach bulkheads.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.OKRR6Tvq5nG6C7i7]{Graviton Pistols} are a pistol version of the larger Graviton Gun. Though the pistol version has a smaller magazine and slightly lower damage potential, they remain just as potent and exotic a weapon.

Graviton weapons deal additional Damage to a creature equal to their Armour. Any creature that takes damage from a Graviton weapon must make a Challenging (+0) Endurance Test or be rendered Prone. Targets wearing armour have −1 SL to this test, and armour with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.wsM53RDPPrqwS3Te#heavy-(rating)]{Heavy} Trait grants −2 SL instead.

Kroot Weapons

The deceptively crude appearance of the Kroot belies the potency and efficacy of their armoury, especially after their union with the T'au Empire. Such weapons might find their way into the hands of the Ordo Xenos.

The most common and iconic weapon of the xenos species is the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.sKSZINM2ReZUzaHi]{Kroot Rifle}. Modelled after their ancestor’s fighting staffs, the rifle was once a slug-thrower that used a chemical propellant. T'au ingenuity has adapted the weapon to fire charged pulse rounds of significant stopping power. Despite this, the Kroot continue to affix blades to the muzzle and the stock of the Kroot Rifle, making it a surprisingly effective melee weapon. When used as a Melee Weapon, it counts as a Mundane @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.bS4Uy21y8pkp7I7P]{Sword} (2 + StrB Damage) using the Two-handed specialisation, with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.wsM53RDPPrqwS3Te#two-handed]{Two-Handed} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.wsM53RDPPrqwS3Te#defensive]{Defensive} Traits.

Kroot also utilise a longer range, sniper variant of their iconic rifles, bereft of the blades to preserve the weapon’s balance. Other variations include the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.Uf7UNIPc8MQ5CcSC]{Kroot Gun}, a heavy weapon commonly seen mounted upon lumbering warbeats, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.aeVZFr1efspD3Ffq]{Kroot Pistols}, often paired with deadly hunting knives for furious close-quarters combat.

Malefic Weapons

Like Tainted Weapons, Malefic Weapons are touched by daemonic or warp energies. The wielder adds their Corruption, up to their Willpower Bonus (WilB), to the Damage the weapon deals.

Pulse Weapons

Technology hailing from the T’au Empire, these Pulse Weapons are the iconic backbone of their Fire Warrior caste infantry. Recovered from Pathfinder and Fire Warrior teams who have encroached upon Imperial territory, such weapons might find their way into the hands of the Ordo Xenos for study. Compared to Imperial Plasma weaponry, Pulse Weapons are much more stable, have a greater range, and are significantly less prone to overheating, yet still powerful enough to burn clean through power armour. In addition to using refined induction fields to propel lethal bursts of plasma over great distances, most pulse weapons come with gyroscopic aim-stabilisation systems that cause the rifle to remain steady when firing such long distances.

Shuriken Weapons

Shuriken Weapons are those wielded almost exclusively by the mysterious Aeldari. Crafted from wraithbone, each weapon, no matter its size, uses gravitic accelerators to fire razor-sharp discs of plasti-crystal material. A volley of such razored discs can easily shred living matter, pierce metal, and even penetrate plasteel armour.

While @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.NRYzJX3bg1t8qNbZ]{Shuriken Pistols} are a common and reliable sidearm among various Aeldari elements, the larger @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.2n5DOXPtBbCLMv1T]{Shuriken Rifle} is more commonly used among its citizen soldiers, corsairs, and pirates. Sometimes such weapons are gifted, in the rare and exceptional times when the perfidious Aeldari and the Holy Inquisition find their goals aligned. Even so, these weapons are rarely seen among the Ordo Xenos and avoided by more puritanical Inquisitors.

When attacking, Shuriken weapons gain +1 SL.

Solid Projectile Weapons

The Inquisition maintain close ties to the Adeptus Arbites when operating within Imperial population centres. Through a legacy of joint operations, their specialised STC designs of the humble shotgun have repeatedly been requisitioned into many an Inquisitor’s arsenal. Solid projectile weapons vary wildly in their statistics and Traits and tend to accept a wider variety of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.luQOhxIEeYF6tMgt#ammunition]{Custom Ammunition}.

Specialised Ranged Weapons

Extreme rarities even among an Inquisitor’s arsenal, Specialised Ranged Weapons defy standard categorisation. Most require an esteemed weaponsmith to craft or maintain, especially when such weapons hail from xenos origins. Specialised Ranged Weapons always come with a unique combination of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.wsM53RDPPrqwS3Te#weapons-and-armour-traits]{Traits}.

Splinter Weapons

Splinter Weapons are the name given to various weapons used by Drukhari warriors, xenos notorious for raiding worlds and ships. These weapons use magno-electric impulses to shatter crystallised neurotoxins and propel them at supersonic speeds along the accelerator barrel. While these weapons might not reliably penetrate heavier armour, the splinters and shards fired from these weapons can debilitate and kill from even a single scratch.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.7rzrR5VhG6YQyaAY]{Splinter Rifles} are the mainstay weapon for the Drukhari. They are lightweight and have a considerably large ammunition chamber. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.S7VPXYNKbpqjGsnh]{Splinter Pistols} are lightweight sidearms, and though they have a shorter effective range, the shots fired are no less toxic or virulent.

Some Splinter Weapons come with monomolecular blades affixed, whether to aid in close-quarters boarding actions or sadistic melee combat. These Splinter Rifles and Splinter Pistols count as having the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.bme7IUpsgm3NzL83]{Melee Attachment} weapon modification, which are further improved with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.rD6BtFSjpfupZss1]{Mono-edge} weapon modification. Increase the listed price of these weapons by 300 Solars.

pages.name: Grenades And Explosives
pages.text:
The Holy Orders have a unique array of Grenades and Explosives that act towards debilitating the enemy rather than causing them direct harm, making them effective tools for capturing opponents or placing them in a weakened state to better deal with later. General rules for using @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.Slqoyw0d5t8b9amF]{Grenades and Explosives} are outlined in Imperium Maledictum, along with related @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.wsM53RDPPrqwS3Te#weapons-and-armour-traits]{Weapon and Armour Traits}.

How can this be?!

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.nd8zBS07KVlPzaAd]{Hallucinogen} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.rT0gpcguAkqemsFr]{Psychotroke} Grenades are an excellent way for the GM to engage with characters, tailoring their induced visions to elements of their backstory. A lost friend bearing a timely warning, a latent fear made manifest, or a forgotten encounter that might suddenly prove relevant — a canny GM can evoke these elements and provide suitable disruption to the character’s current actions. GMs should feel free to ignore the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.Dy8XzuHFhHpVFytC]{Hallucinogenic Effects} Table if such a tailored vision would be more appropriate and engaging!

pages.name: Requisitions
pages.text:
In pursuit of the Inquisition’s duty, Inquisitors frequently use their authority to call upon elements from within the Imperium or specialist services found only among the Holy Ordos. Inquisitorial Requisitions represent the unique nature of such authority.

Interfactional Support

You can use Influence to requisition support from other Factions. This can typically be achieved by contacting a local senior member of a Faction, presenting your Rosette, and negotiating some form of aid. The two important elements of any requisition are the target and the resource. The target is an individual with a position of power within their Faction.

The resource is what you want to requisition, such as the use of a location or the command of operatives and agents specific to that Faction. When you use Interfactional Support in this way, you’re essentially ‘borrowing’ a Boon from an individual that could be considered a Patron. For example, if your group of acolytes were storming the headquarters of a cultist cell, you could contact a Senior Officer of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} and requisition some @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.jVqhxWe0o7nWz3Qj]{Seconded Troopers} until the end of the mission. It is also possible to requisition your own Patron, or another Inquisitor, to acquire resources or services permitted only for the Holy Ordos.

You can make these requisitions using your Personal Influence or the Patron Influence of your Inquisitor through Limitless Authority. Any requisition requires a Rapport Test modified by Influence. If you succeed, the target temporarily grants you the resource.

'Who should we ask?'

Both @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.QrGsY2UZDirxvDaB.JournalEntryPage.wL2GpbQI5o9JTpNA]{Patrons} @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.ZzHsqdssD6GJyhDE]{Patrons of the Inquisition} contain a wealth of Patrons and Boons that are useful resources when making requisitions. If you know there’s a powerful Astropath in the area, you can take a look at Imperium Maledictum and assume that they can provide you with their Duty Boon: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.niqxBVj5cdI03Woj]{Astropathic Communication}, as well as potentially any of the Boons in their Table, provided you can petition them successfully using Influence with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.BLOQk9yJsb03nyDH]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}. Similarly, if you need a voidship to travel freely and without notice, you might petition a Rogue Trader or Voidship Captain.

During your Inquisitorial investigations, you might find yourself on unfamiliar worlds needing support but uncertain who to petition for aid. Typically, you can make a Rapport (Inquiry) Test to determine who wields power in the local area and which Faction they belong to. The Gamemaster might also allow more difficult Rapport (Inquiry) Tests to determine an individual that can provide you with a specific Boon you’ve identified as crucial to your mission.

'Limitless Authority?'

These rules effectively extend the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.3M9o35qxoxiQRzP5]{Limitless Authority} Boon that almost all Inquisitors possess. Officially, the legitimate Factions of the Imperium (all but the Infractionists) cannot refuse a call for aid from the Inquisition. However, life’s impediments in the grim darkness of the 41st Millennium often mean such requisitions go unfulfilled.

Some may not believe the request comes from a genuine acolyte and may believe their request is a subversive attempt by Infractionists who’ve heretically falsified Inquisitorial connections. Others may be unable to fulfil the request because they are understaffed or undersupplied; the acolytes might be unable to gain backup if no such squad of troopers is available to join them. Unscrupulous individuals of power use the very mechanisms of the Imperium itself to obstruct the Inquisition and hoard resources for themselves; the Administratum might bury requisitions under mountains of obtuse paperwork, while the Imperial Fleet might hold a ship with requested supplies ‘under inspection’ for days or weeks.

For all these reasons and many more, a request made by the supposedly undeniable Inquisition might not be fulfilled or delayed indefinitely. Any ‘failed’ requisition can be narrated in your games of Imperium Maledictum using these principles. Without a doubt, players and GMs should consider the party’s @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.KbejcPMug5gfoWWz.JournalEntryPage.XyTxLhjDZDkpE0Lz]{Subtlety} Level when making requisitions. Any inquiry could stir up suspicion, whereas the more exposed the party are, the more likely they are to be taken seriously.

Patron Influence

You can use your Patron Influence with a Rapport Test to make a requisition of a powerful representative of an Imperial Faction. You may use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.3M9o35qxoxiQRzP5]{Limitless Authority} Boon to do so. If you succeed on the Test, you gain the requested resource. Typically, such requisitions cannot be denied, but negative SL might indicate that the requisition takes time to be fulfilled, isn’t fully completed, or is an absolute failure, as determined by the Gamemaster and the circumstances, keeping the points outlined in ‘Limitless Authority?’ in mind. Note that the party’s @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.KbejcPMug5gfoWWz.JournalEntryPage.XyTxLhjDZDkpE0Lz]{Subtlety} may be affected when spending Patron Influence outside of Overt or Exposed Levels.

Personal Influence

If you have @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.qxkAEAcB9xAl56Xa#personal-influence]{personal Influence} or a Contact within a Faction, you can make a requisition of them. If you succeed on the Test, you gain the requested resource. If you fail the Test, it will threaten to decrease your party’s @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.KbejcPMug5gfoWWz.JournalEntryPage.XyTxLhjDZDkpE0Lz]{Subtlety} Rating.

Esoteric Wargear

The primary purpose of Inquisitorial Requisition is to represent the ability of the Inquisition to call upon various Factions within the Imperium. It is also used for more specific resources that most factions would not have access to, such as requesting the services of a Blank for a mission to hunt down a rogue psyker, or a daemonologist, to aid in a ritual of binding. Inquisitorial Requisition should not simply allow acolytes to borrow or purchase wargear; instead, wargear requisitions should use Endeavours or Patron Boons. Additionally, Inquisitorial Requisitions should not be used for the severely radical or outright heretical, such as acquiring Daemonblades, using daemonhosts, or receiving xenos wargear. Such things are remarkably difficult to acquire or require forbidden knowledge and are better represented by pursuing @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX.JournalEntryPage.AuM2Lzd784VPe32b]{Endeavours}.

pages.name: The Heresies Macharia
pages.text:
Inquisitor Lord Hieronymo Drake is dead. Before the veil of the Noctis Aeterna lifted from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.lpu6iuTHw50UavbI]{Belnshudha}, cut off from the rest of the sector, Drake and his forces fought on the planet’s surface. To his horror, the Inquisitor realised he had underestimated the enemy’s strength. Where Drake expected an entrenched cult, he found a company of heretic Astartes anointing a Noctilith Crown with the blood of fools who had rallied to their heretical banner. The foul traitors called forth endless scores of daemons from the Warp, threatening to provide the Ruinous Powers with a foothold at the heart of the sector. Ultimately, the Inquisitor Lord had no choice but to order an Exterminatus of the planet while remaining trapped on the surface. Without their sacrifice, the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.y6qA7KARTXADwzeV]{Cytheris Subsector} and the rest of the Macharian Sector would be lost.

The remaining Inquisitors of the Macharian Sector have carried on without an Inquisitor Lord ever since, free from Drake’s scrutiny. Though he commanded their respect, Drake was sometimes, in the eyes of his peers, far too conservative in his methods. The Inquisitors have been left to their own devices for too long, without coordination or cooperation, and mired in their increasingly radical methods without checks or balances.

But all that is about to change. Drake’s former Interrogator, now elevated to the position of Inquisitor herself, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst} sees a great opportunity: to unite the Inquisitors of the sector in a series of Conclaves and coordinate their efforts against the sector’s most significant threats and eventually see a new Inquisitor Lord put in place. But can the other Inquisitors truly trust Horst in this endeavour? Is she simply invoking her mentor's name and towering reputation to elevate her position, or does she have an ulterior motive in mind?

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Horst}’s summons is the inciting incident behind the Heresies Macharia, a decades-spanning Inquisition campaign framework for Imperium Maledictum. A series of seven Conclaves, gathering the Inquisitors of the sector and their retinues together in one place, provides an opportunity to share leads and resources. Each Inquisitor has reasons to attend the Conclave and hear their fellows out. Some earnestly believe unity can be found; others believe that strife breeds strength or wish to keep an eye on their rivals.

Your characters and their Patron are attendees of these Conclaves, privy to the arguments and rumoured perils. Each Conclave influences the party’s subsequent missions, the trials and threats they face for the coming years, and the horrors they must conquer before the next Conclave. But heresy is everywhere, hidden across the sector, even in the dark corners of @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis}. Problems left unchecked anywhere fester into sector-threatening horrors. Each Inquisitor schemes to save the Imperium in their own distinct way, and their intense politicking within the Holy Orders often consumes those who participate in it.

pages.name: Running Conclaves
pages.text:
The Heresies Macharia campaign framework is punctuated by a series of seven Inquisitorial Conclaves, with years set aside between each one for characters and their Patrons to complete their missions, follow up on their own tasks, and return in time to @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} for the next one to begin. It is intended that GMs build their own threats, missions, and opportunities around and on top of these events, with the Heresies Macharia providing mission outlines and larger plots as a backdrop. To make the characters' involvement more personal and tailored to the players' desires, the GM must work hard to bring everything together.

Each Conclave, laid out across the chapter, presents the following information:

  • Dramatis Personae: Who among the sector’s Inquisitors have attended this Conclave. Apart from the first Conclave, not every Inquisitor will participate in each gathering. Inquisitors are not bound to the authority of their peers and may be busy elsewhere, resolving what they deem to be more critical issues.

  • Intrigues: Rumours and secrets characters can hunt down outside main Conclave sessions, including new Contacts and resources they can acquire. These intrigues may point to fallout from previous Conclaves, set up side missions for characters to pursue in the years between, or seed future Strifes.

  • Strifes: These points represent the main issues discussed at the Conclave, including which Inquisitors are bringing them forward and who might stand against them. Typically, there will be two to three Strifes to discuss per Conclave, each with its own Operation (an outline of the mission or missions related to resolving the Strife) and Outcome (what happens if the party is successful or not, and what might happen if another Inquisitor deals with the problem instead).

Your Patron

The Heresies Macharia allow parties to follow any of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40]{six sample Patrons provided} or add their own Inquisitor Patron to the mix, allowing them to bring their own concerns to each Conclave. Consider how the other Inquisitors might react to their presence and goals. Depending on their Ordo or Philosophy, they could be friendly or antagonistic towards them, and the same goes for their acolytes.

The Heresies Macharia has been designed with Inquisitorial Patrons in mind, but other Faction Patrons can participate. Such a Patron would be at an extreme disadvantage when faced with the allconsuming authority of the Inquisition and would likely quickly become subject to the will of one or more of the Inquisitors present. While this may present exciting opportunities for storytelling, deception, and intrigue, we recommend that parties select an Inquisitor Patron.

Rewarding Patrons

As the campaign progresses, player characters are rewarded or punished for their efforts. The GM should reward their Patron in the same manner. The Outcome of each Conclave summarises what happens in the world and alterations to the involved @UUID[.jt0zc7az5xNehcIZ#an-inquisitor-lord-ascends]{Patron’s Legitimacy scores}, but there are two other ways a Patron can grow.

Primarily, the Patron can be rewarded or docked @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.qxkAEAcB9xAl56Xa]{Influence}. Consider the Factions they or the party involve themselves with during the Strife. How do those Factions feel about the Patron — and, by extension, the behaviour of their acolytes — by the end? Reward or remove a point of Influence accordingly.

Secondly, there are additional Boons and Liablities. Reward these in the event of extreme success or devastating failure. The Macharian Sector’s sample @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40]{Inquisitor Patrons} each have a table of suggested boons and liabilities to choose from, but you are not limited to them. If the group created their own Patron, as GM, you should look at the options available in advance — do any tie into potential plots and outcomes? On the other hand, a Patron can lose a Boon they already have if it no longer makes sense for them to have access to that Boon. The same goes for Liabilities if the outcome of the Strife allows the Patron to ‘overcome’ that Liability for good.

Conclave Process

Enough happens at Inquisitorial Conclaves for them to be considered missions or sessions in and of themselves. The following list outlines the general process we advise when running a Conclave.

  1. Describe the characters' arrival. How did they reach Suluk? Did they arrive in plenty of time, or are the meetings about to begin? Did they travel with their Inquisitor, or are they already in attendance?

  2. Tell the players which characters are in attendance. Give the players a rundown of the Inquisitors present and any noticeable characters in their retinues or witnesses brought into the Conclave halls (see each Conclave’s Dramatis Personae and Intrigues sections).

  3. Tell them what Strifes are on the agenda. In the central chambers of the @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} facility, the Inquisitors read the Conclave’s agenda. Be sure to include who is involved in each Strife and indicate any supposed threats (see each Strife’s tagline for a quick summary). Consider what Inquisitors not directly involved in the Strife think of it, though most may consider these events to be not worth their time.

  4. Give the players time to investigate. As the Patrons gather in the central chambers to debate, the players have time to search the @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} facility and uncover more information. Some of the helpful activities they can pursue are as follows:

    1. Investigate other Inquisitors and their retinues. Find out what the other Inquisitors are up to. Dig deep enough, and they can find clues to indicate any Radical behaviour, hidden goals, or philosophies — though they should watch their backs, as other acolytes will be doing the same.

    2. Investigate Mare Cinis. The Inquisition facility on Suluk is a labyrinthine hold containing a wealth of Ordo-gathered information and secrets. They might find something to aid their characters or Patron in the missions ahead or uncover hidden aspects of the Strifes being discussed.

    3. Attend Conclave meetings. Though it may be difficult to gain entry to the central chamber at times, listening carefully to the Inquisitors and their debates can reveal hidden enmities, alliances, and philosophies that could be relevant later. Some characters may have to provide witness testimony or information pertinent to the matters at hand.

    4. Look into additional Intrigues. There may be more going on at each Conclave than what is discussed within the central chambers. Characters can gather threads, Contacts, and clues for more missions or look into anything of personal relevance.

  5. Present their findings to their Patron. Here, the Patron has asked the player characters to provide a report on any new information they have gathered about the current Strifes. Players debate and decide among themselves — much like the Inquisitors within the central chambers — which Strife they are interested in pursuing as a group. As GM, roleplay the Patron much like you would in a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.1diRtTeN2hbZUhOY]{mission briefing}. The Patron may have interest in one Strife over another if it involves their Philosophy or rivals, but the final choice should ultimately land with the players.

  6. Depart for the mission. Give characters time to make any last actions, check the Inquisitorial archives on Mare Cinis, for example, or gather any gear from the moon’s stockpiles. Decide whether or not their Patron is accompanying them or if they have other important matters to attend to.

If players are stuck, unsure of what they can do (during step #4), their Patron could urge them to investigate one thing in particular or present a few options. It could benefit their cell if all the options are covered, or they could work together to tackle a single mystery.

Acolyte Agency

Though primarily the Patron and other Inquisitors lead the debates at each Conclave, as GM, encourage your players to discuss these dire issues among themselves. What do they believe is the best course of action? You can take these discussions further and allow your players to take on the guise of the Inquisitors present and roleplay the arguments between them. Present everyone at the table with each Conclave’s Strifes, and let them discuss where they think it is best to go next as a group (though keep the particulars of the Operations and Outcomes to yourself). From this, you will better understand their desired direction for the campaign.

Bring their debates to a close in the form of a report: the Patron requests the characters' input in the form of an official report with their recommendations for action attached. The Patron is by no means bound by their deliberations, but as GM, the Patron’s opinion should reflect what the players desire to pursue.

Remind the players that the Inquisition cannot be everywhere simultaneously, despite the propaganda they perpetuate among the citizenry. Ensure the players understand they alone cannot tackle all the new Strifes presented. You will need to track what issues have been left to other Inquisitors to resolve and what problems are discarded entirely. These situations may return in worse states later if not dealt with at all, and you can seed these into future Conclaves via new Strifes or Intrigues of your own design.

Intrigues, Rumours and Threats

The time players have to investigate @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} outside the central chambers is the perfect opportunity to introduce new Contacts, rumours and ancillary missions into your Heresies Macharia campaign. Each Conclave’s Intrigues section provides some pertinent options, mostly related to the current Strifes. Still, those say nothing of what the players' Patron or characters wish to personally pursue — to further the goals of their philosophy or work towards defeating a particular threat or nemesis.

During a Conclave, @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} is a goldmine of information. Specialists from every Ordo Majoris are in attendance, including agents seconded to the Inquisition from every Faction within the Adeptus Terra. But schedules are tight, and security is high; characters must barter and politick their way into face-to-face meetings, especially with other Inquisitors. Often, it is best to start with members of their outer circles and work their way in, trading small favours and nuggets of information themselves.

Moreover, the moon’s halls echo with whispers and rumours. Outside the central chambers is a veritable information market, but few words are traded freely. Acolytes and agents from across the Macharian Sector are present, and everyone is searching for something — volatile rumours, weaponised secrets, new information to curry favour with their Inquisitor or just a solid favour. As GM, consider what your characters are looking for and who could provide it to them. At the same time, characters should consider what occurrences, clues, and assets from previous missions they could trade for favours or new information.

Characters should not forget the most significant threats to the Macharian Sector may well be present in the Conclave’s halls. The Inquisitors are among the most powerful and dangerous mortals in the sector, and so is much of the company they keep. They may have been brought together to combat the sector’s threats, but with all the sector’s Inquisitors in one place, there is a greater chance they will get in each other’s way, and acolytes are easily trodden over. Members of their retinues may serve multiple masters, those who expect their involvement with the Inquisition to bear recompense and are looking for angles of their own. So, characters should tread carefully — there are ample records of brazen backstabbings and betrayals in the central chambers of Mare Cinis alone.

Mare Cinis

Each Conclave gathers on Suluk, a moon of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy]{Persepolis}. All that remains on the moon is an ancient Imperial outpost surrounded by a great ash plain dubbed the Mare Cinis. Long ago, the Inquisition cleansed the moon when its people accepted xenos aid during a daemonic incursion. They have since blockaded the moon, preventing anyone but Inquisitorial retinues and their agents from landing there. The Inquisitors have reappropriated parts of the base as lodgings, storage or datavaults, and the deepest levels of the facility hold hidden caches of forbidden knowledge and secret chambers.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy]{Persepolis} is located at the heart of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.y6qA7KARTXADwzeV]{Cytheris Subsector}. The hive world is the capital of the Macharian Sector and is a major crossroad and point of pilgrimage for citizens. Inquisitors and their acolytes have little trouble securing transport to arrive in time to join the Conclave.

pages.name: Major Plotlines
pages.text:
As characters weave through the ongoing Strifes of the Heresies Macharia, a number of major plotlines continue to build and progress in the background. As GM, you should be aware of and keep track of these elements and their potential repercussions.

The Interrogator Elevated

Gathering the Inquisitors of the sector together is no trifling matter, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst} knows this; the other Inquisitors could consider her a troubling upstart or see through her plans from the get-go, and the consequences could conceivably end in violence. But she has been planning the Macharian Conclaves for a long time and finally believes it is worth the risk to put them into action.

Primarily, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Horst} intends to gain the favour of her fellow Inquisitors to either reach the position of Inquisitor Lord herself or elevate someone she judges worthy of the position (or someone she can manipulate). Either way, this would improve her authority in the sector and open doors for her to achieve her other goals.

Secondarily, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Horst} desires to know what led to the death of her former master, Inquisitor Lord Hieronymo Drake, on the planet @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.lpu6iuTHw50UavbI]{Belnshudha}. Horst already investigated @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#battle-group-fortis]{Battle Group Fortis} to exhaustion, and those ordered to enact Exterminatus upon the planet found little to pursue. But her investigation is a cover for her misdeeds and the actual actions that led to her ascension. Now she is cleaning up her former master’s messes, hearing utterances of the ‘Kryptman Protocol’ loosely tied to Drake’s previous activities that she wishes to thoroughly investigate in secret.

The Kryptman Protocol

The truth is this: Hieronymo Drake spent the latter years of his life seeding a network of loyal acolytes and sleeper agents throughout various institutions across the sector, including the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} and @UUID[unknown]{Navis Imperialis}. These agents are charged with a singular task: upon receipt of a code phrase known only to Drake, hidden hypno-indoctrinated orders within their minds are revealed, compelling them to action. By utilising the resources and authority they had accumulated, they are to use the Imperium’s arsenals to ravage numerous worlds along the border of the Macharian Sector and render them lifeless. Each agent knew only of their specific task, which was often hidden in the depths of their mind.

None save Drake knew of the scale of destruction this secretive cabal would unleash.

The Kryptman protocol intends to create a cordon of lifeless worlds, a firebreak to prevent Leviathan from feeding on the sector’s biomass. This stalls the inevitable invasion and buys time until the Imperium can find a better solution. But even Drake lacked the will to use this weapon before the Hive Fleet’s arrival, knowing the sacrifice of billions of lives and countless productive worlds would alter the Macharian Sector for centuries.

He considered it entirely possible that, in saving the heart of the sector, he would condemn it to a conflagration of civil strife and privation to equal that of the Macharian Heresy. He kept all this a secret from the rest of the Inquisition, partially out of fear that his work would become undone and because Drake feared that the High Lords of Terra would find out and force his hand and sacrifice the Macharian Sector to protect Segmentum Solar.

Excommunicate Traitoris

Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius} of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} treads on thin ice. He has avoided contact with the rest of the Inquisition for decades to further his @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.UAWh0hEvWDwob6CT]{Isstvanist} goals without any of his peers getting in the way, but he knows that Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus}, a Puritan member of the Ordo Xenos, is on his tail, Serranus knows that Thracius has consorted with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari} and that alone is enough for Serranus to think of him a traitor.

However, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius} is a self-aware adherent of Radical @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.UAWh0hEvWDwob6CT]{Isstvanist} philosophy; he knows that many see his actions as heretical and that their interference is expected, so Thracius has spent decades preparing for a personal shadow campaign to continue his efforts hidden from the Inquisition’s oversight. Primarily, he has established numerous false identities, some amongst the Inquisition itself, employing psychic powers and the potent shape-changing chemical polymorphine to shroud his true identity.

As the Macharian Inquisition is called to Conclave, the time has come for him to fake his death and disappear into the background, allowing his carefully constructed aliases to thrive and effectively take his place. Furthermore, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius} does not trust @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Horst's} intentions at face value. He even suspects the former Interrogator of having plotted against her master. After all, too many Inquisitors fall afoul of assassination by their own Interrogator.

Was there even a Noctilith Gate on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.lpu6iuTHw50UavbI]{Belnshudha} to begin with? Furthermore, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius} knows enough about the Kryptman Protocol to piece together some version of the truth — might @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Horst} be an Agent of the High Lords of Terra tasked with intentionally sacrificing the sector?

At the very least, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius} knows that these Conclaves might rattle the cages of the Macharian Inquisition and may compromise his identity. Thankfully, he still has a seat at the table under the guise of Inquisitor Kai Varol. An @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} Inquisitor who rose from the ashes of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.dOdB17RuClYozQ15]{Noctis Aeterna}, a hero of the Imperium that repelled xenos invasions through the years of blinding, has become well-established within the Macharian Sector. Impersonating another Inquisitor is an incredibly fraught prospect, but Thracius has the advantage of being one. His only means of survival may be to nudge the Inquisition, as a whole, carefully in the right direction or even go as far as claiming the title of Inquisitor Lord for himself.

The Herald's Howl

For generations, the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cults} of the Macharian Sector have been slowly infecting its worlds, seeding their tainted lineage among the people and patiently awaiting the inevitable arrival of their star-borne saviours. But many within the cults are not content to wait for their day of ascension; they intend to hasten the fated arrival of the Tyranid Hive Mind and have concocted a horrifying plan that spans multiple worlds, one the Inquisition must act upon or risk losing the entire sector.

The unintelligible minds of the Patriarch alliance have instructed their cults to abduct Human psykers, conjoining them into a horrifying union of chitin and soft encephalic flesh, thrumming with psychic energy. A grotesque mass of neural matter capable of projecting a monumental psychic wail. The Maguses’ have dubbed this the Herald’s Howl, intended as an unignorable signal to summon their longed-for star gods, a beacon screaming, ‘Come to us! We have found worlds ripe for your enlightenment!’

Whether this gruesome plot will achieve its intended goal is impossible to tell. If the Herald’s Howl succeeds, they might accelerate the arrival of Hive Fleet Leviathan in the Macharian Sector, hastening it by generations. Even if the profane ritual fails, Inquisitors of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-malleus]{Ordo Malleus} suspect that such a massive gathering of psychic potential may provide an open door to daemonkind — thereby trading a xenos threat for a grand-scale daemonic incursion.

Ultimately, the characters and their Patron's actions will decide how the Herald's Howl resolves. Some of the most likely outcomes are thus:

  • They might seek to destroy the Herald’s Howl before it can draw the attention of the Hive Fleet.

  • A Radical group might seek to nullify the Howl somehow but preserve it for study.

  • They might fail to deal with the Howl entirely, forcing them to enact the @UUID[.jt0zc7az5xNehcIZ#the-kryptman-protocol]{Kryptman Protocol}.

  • They might let the Herald’s Howl come to fruition, luring a tendril of Leviathan away from Holy Terra. A group which has uncovered the Kryptman Protocol might seek to use Drake’s hidden network to combat the Tyranids when they arrive.

An Inquisitor Lord Ascends

In serving the goals of the Conclave, each Inquisitor’s actions in the field further their legitimacy as a successor to Inquisitor Lord Drake. This is not an election between the sector’s Inquisitors but rather an ascension to a higher position based on their actions and presence of power. Throughout the Heresies Macharia, each Inquisitor is given a Legitimacy score to track the development of an Inquisitor’s worthiness.

  • This score starts at zero for each Inquisitor.

  • An Inquisitor’s Legitimacy score should not be shared directly with the players.

  • If they wish to find out which Inquisitors are in the running, they can investigate during a Conclave (similar to gauging their Subtlety) to see who is ahead.

Each Strife’s Outcome includes a Legitimacy increase for the characters’ Patron (or the Inquisitor their Patron serves) if they successfully resolve the Strife. If they do not work to resolve the Strife, another Inquisitor will take the opportunity to do so, with the Outcome section indicating which Inquisitor increases their Legitimacy instead.

At the @UUID[.AYJ70cmnV5Y6rDDt]{final Conclave}, the Inquisitor with the highest Legitimacy score has demonstrated that they alone exhibit the capacity to hold rank and respect as Inquisitor Lord. By taking the boldest actions, they will have shown the will to act where others would hesitate, the pragmatism to know what must be excised for the survival of the Imperium as a whole, and the wisdom contained in their own philosophy as a means to enact the God-Emperor’s will. However, note that this position will not free an Inquisitor from rivalry; their opponents may continue to work against them in the shadows.

pages.name: Conclave I
pages.text:
Conclave I

For the first time since the end of the Noctis Aeterna, an Inquisitorial Conclave has been called on Suluk. In a glass-domed assembly chamber, with a view to the distant hive spires of Persepolis far below, six Inquisitors and their allies have gathered to determine the fate of the Macharian Sector.

Dramatis Personae

The six Inquisitors operating in the Macharian Sector, including their retinues and representative allies, are in attendance at the first Conclave. The GM should ensure that the characters can meet with or learn about each of the six Inquisitors during this first Conclave.

Sylvestrine Horst

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Horst} (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-hereticus]{Ordo Hereticus}) bears herself with a calm determination. She has yet to appoint an Interrogator but is accompanied by a retinue of acolytes clad in gold masks, each one the face of an Imperial saint. They precede members of the Sisters Famulous from the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#the-adepta-sororitas]{Adepta Sororitas} @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.A9cvKlA41X8qPyEw]{Order of the Hallowed Glass}.


Konstan Serranus

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus} (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos}) is a dour and zealous man; his augmetic arm is a testament to his absolutism. A retinue of heavily augmented acolytes and a Magos representing the Tech-Priests of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.jB9sg2SDLZJGZrac]{Eskutchax} accompanies him.


Alis Raud

Tall, heavily armoured, and resolute, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-malleus]{Ordo Malleus}) has all the bearing that many would imagine of an Inquisitor. Accompanying her are representatives of her myriad contacts — noble house agents, Rogue Trader associates, and Navis Imperialis officers.


Aegidius Halikarn

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Aegidius Halikarn} (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-hereticus]{Ordo Hereticus}) is watched warily by the other Inquisitors, for his pursuit of heretics is dogged and absolute, having excised corruption from within sacred Imperial institutions. The known Radical leads a compact retinue comprised of older yet hardened agents: former @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.bkP99HZ6JJ7IWd8U]{Tempestus Scions}, and other soldiers recruited from among the specialised ranks of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum}.


Kai Varol

Kai Varol (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos}, alias of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius}) comes across as wise and furtive, accompanied by specialists from the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}. He mainly watches the proceedings, observing with cold calculation, speaking only when he feels the moment is right.


Ksenia Baek

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Ksenia Baek} (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-hereticus]{Ordo Hereticus}) is an intense woman whose dominant psychic presence breeds discomfort in her peers. She leads a cadre of psykers, members of her retinue and representatives of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.upGG1JZPDbC7dpJJ]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}.

Intrigues

The presence of so many Inquisitors, their retinues, and their allies provides characters with ample opportunity to make Contacts who may later prove helpful to them and their Patron. Among the attendees are:

  • Antonius Tavnir, a representative of House Tavol of the @UUID[.bUgRB72Mw5eaLfL6]{Merchant Fleet}

  • Sister Famulous Lysara of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.A9cvKlA41X8qPyEw]{Order of the Hallowed Glass}, operating among the nobility on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.si7mc5k5MVLqN049]{Xenophon}

  • Magos Tal-Theta 661 of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus} serving on the forge world @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.jB9sg2SDLZJGZrac]{Eskutchax}

  • Knight-Centura Augustina, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.CBLdHnFWFqdhfRKx]{Sister of Silence} of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}

  • Kharket Graan, an astropath in service to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Ksenia Baek}

@UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} holds intrigues beyond the glut of attendees. The Inquisitorial base contains a wealth of information accessible to those with vermillion-level clearance, access to much of which can also be granted by an Inquisitor to their acolytes if justified. The datavaults and libraries include records of heretic activity dating back to the Macharian Crusade and beyond, ancient accounts passed down from Inquistitor to Inquisitor. However, access may be limited due to the sheer number of other acolytes competing for the same assets or information — but this may provide an opportunity for the characters to learn about what may be of interest to the other retinues.

Strife I-A
The Void Stalker

Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius} of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} is presumed dead. A shattered @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari} battleship lies at the edge of the sector — one Inquisitor petitions for its immediate destruction, and another seeks to investigate, confirming the fate of Thracius.

The tomb of thousands of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari} souls has claimed a new occupant — Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius}. Tarran Selvir, the sole surviving acolyte of Inquisitor Thracius, delivers the news of his master’s death. During an expedition aboard the Aeldari Void Stalker, he witnessed his master gunned down by remnants of the ship’s automated defences, a total freak accident.

  • Kai Varol suggests contacting @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Valerius Nabopalassar} of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} to study whatever Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius} sought to recover.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus} loathes the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari} utterly and raises instead the vessel’s destruction. If the voidship, even in its shattered state, has brought about the death of an Inquisitor, it continues to pose a threat, making destruction imperative.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} is unconcerned with the voidship’s fate but suggests @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius}’s body is recovered to prove the Radical Inquisitor’s death.

Operation

The characters embark upon a long journey to the edge of the sector to investigate Inquisitor Thracius's death and scour the remains of an Aeldari vessel before it attracts undue attention.

Regardless of whether the Void Stalker is to be destroyed or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius}’ field research recovered, Kai Varol approaches characters undertaking this mission, offering to contact Selim @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#rogue-traders-of-note]{Iaysus}, a Rogue Trader whose voidship is already bound from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy]{Persepolis} to the region where the wrecked @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari} vessel was last sighted. Unbeknownst to the Conclave or characters undertaking this mission, Selim Iaysus and Inquisitor Kai Varol are both aliases of Inquisitor Eskender Thracius, whose past investigations into Aeldari technology had brought him dangerously close to being deemed Excommunicate Traitoris by @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud}. Under his alias of Selim Laysus, Thracius aims to ensure his field notes are recovered, either by characters undertaking this mission or by Selim’s voidsmen.

The Void Stalker

One of the largest classes of Aeldari voidship, the Inquisition has recorded sightings of these vessels dating back to the Gothic War. The Macharian Inquisition has no records of investigating such a vessel up close. Despite its wrecked state, surrounded by a debris field of its shattered stern and solar sails, parts of the voidship remain operational, including its voidshields and holofield. Characters can discover that the reason for its decimated state is pure accident — contact with a freak meteorite storm.

A boarding action to recover the body of Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius} provides an opportunity for an assured controlled shipboard demolition, saving the expenditure of macro-tons of the God-Emperor’s ordinance. Upon approach, it becomes evident that the debris field is not the only hazard surrounding the Void Stalker; some of its automated defences remain operational, commanded by the souls of dead Aeldari still interred within the voidship’s operational technology. Small vessels approaching the wreck must run a gauntlet of starcannon and bright lance fire.

Characters who board the Void Stalker find its crew long dead, unlit halls littered with desiccated Aeldari bodies. However, derelict @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.CuYIq94DC9jXSdCG]{Wraithguard}, wraithbone war constructs, still undertake guard patrols. The sound of their unmaintained forms scrapes against the vessel’s corridors, reverberating through voidsuits with an almost musical, sharp shrillness.

Characters may come across the bodies of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius’} acolytes (save Selvir, the one survivor who fled), who fell while holding the position of Thracius’ field laboratory close to the shattered remnants of the vessel’s bridge. The Inquisitor’s research is present, with stacks of cogitators watched by inert servo-skulls, but Thracius’ corpse is absent.

Upon reaching this area of the vessel, the characters begin to detect traces of other living creatures aboard the vessel, approaching their position. A team of House Iaysus @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.kYpTOdUezMczq5eC]{Voidsmen} also travelled to the Void Stalker, seeking to recover @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius}’ research. Their orders, purportedly left by the late Inquisitor Thracius, included commands to avoid any other operatives aboard and, if discovered, eliminate all witnesses.

Outcome

Whichever operation the characters undertake, their Patron gains +1 Legitimacy on their triumphant return. The failure to recover the body of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius} plants a seed of suspicion within the characters’ Patron. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud}, who had already begun to suspect Thracius of radicalism bordering on heresy, is incentivised to further investigate Thracius’ last activities.

If characters recover @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius}’ research, their Patron gains the favour of Kai Varol and Valerius Nabopalassar, an Aeldari specialist to whom the research is passed (secretly yet another of Thracius’ aliases).

If the characters’ Patron does not take action, or should they fail to destroy the voidship, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Serranus} commandeers a small naval fleet to destroy the xenos voidship. He earns +1 Legitimacy and the ire of Kai Varol (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius}). Robbed of his research, Thracius will take action against Serranus when the time is right.

Strife I-B
Goros Pok

Four prominent cults have risen to power on Goros Pok, each one is suspected of heresy. One Inquisitor seeks to cut the heads off each cult and let each body wither without leadership. Another suggests eradicating them, to quell any further uprisings on the planet.

In the wake of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#silence-and-darkness]{Noctis Aeterna}, cult uprisings and civil unrest on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok} have become commonplace. The planet’s inhabitants struggle to cope with the growing mounds of rotting unclaimed agricultural produce and subsequent belief that the God-Emperor ignored their plight. Characters deployed to tackle this Strife could spend years investigating and purging these cults.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst} argues that strike teams should be deployed to investigate each cult and subsequently eradicate its leadership. Surgically removing each cult’s leadership will cause the body to wither without their direction.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Aegidius Halikarn} believes the Inquisition should eradicate the major cults entirely but through subterfuge, infiltration, and goading them into internecine conflicts between one another.

Severina Melnyk, Interrogator to Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Baek} presents an initial report on each of the major cults:

  • The Blood-crop Combine, whose increasing blood sacrifices resemble Khornate cult practices.

  • The Twisted Sickle, followers of an alleged three-armed saint, preaching of the God-Emperor’s return.

  • The Harrower-In-Green, hold that the produce stored but uncollected was the Emperor’s will. They now gather and hold vast stockpiles of produce, jubilant in its rot as intended by Him on Terra.

  • The Changing Season, of whom little is known, save for their association with ritual killings. But are a cause for concern due to confirmed Warp phenomena associated with each killing.

Operation

The characters begin a years-long mission on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok} to determine the fate of the suspect cults, the planet, and potential implications for the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.MzIWAwZ8jPAOydDi]{Yix Subsector}.

Regardless of which plan of action they seek, characters are deployed to the surface of Goros Pok. They must first contact Confessor Verity Tiberius, who oversees the planet’s spiritual needs and has come to identify the major strains of unsettling zealotry that risk deviation from the Imperial Creed.

Further investigation demands working alongside the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.cvpsLwcsXf4myIpK]{Adeptus Administratum}, who has become inundated with reports on cult activity, many of which they have yet to realise the importance of. The situation on Goros Pok is exceptionally fragile, and any mismanaged strike against these cults will likely spur mob violence rather than a shadow war, as one group of zealots assigns blame and labels of heresy to another. The planet’s enforcers do not have the resources to quell the rising of multiple cults or a full blown civil war, but they may be able to crack down on individual cults if given the correct guidance.

In investigating each cult, characters can discover the following information, key in dealing with each one:

  • The Blood-crop Combine continue to worship the God-Emperor, but some of their rites draw close to worshipping only the act of violence itself, ‘returning blood to the soil’. This cult is not beyond saving; only a few rising death cult members have swayed towards Khornate influence, and their salvation would bear a strong ally for the Inquisition on Goros Pok.

  • Central to The Twisted Sickle's worship is a three-armed woman bearing xenos-tainted genetics and a prodigious psychic capability to bend the wills of those around her. They are the beginnings of a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cult} cell whose goal is to disrupt supply chains out of Goros Pok, bloating the planet’s biomass and ripening it for Hive Fleet invasion.

  • The Harrower-In-Green was initially perceived as an aspect of the God-Emperor, but more and more of the cult’s rites worship Him by this name alone and pay no heed whatsoever to the teachings of the Imperial Creed. A shadow leadership of Nurgle cultists steer citizens towards greed and excess.

  • The Changing Season sees the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.dOdB17RuClYozQ15]{Noctis Aeterna} as the death throes of a season some 10,000 Terran years long. A group of heretic psykers leading this group are guided by a voice from the Warp, under whose guidance they perform sacrificial rites to ‘ready the soil for the season’s turn’. Behind the scenes, a Tzeentchian daemon sees Goros Pok’s landscape as a prime target for manipulation and chaos.

Outcome

Characters who succeed in their operation on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok} earn +2 Legitimacy for their Patron.

If they carried out @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Horst}’s plan of targeted strikes, the cults are curtailed with minimal impact to Goros Pok’s tithe production, and they earn the Inquisitor’s respect.

If they play the cults against each other or eradicate them, their corruption will be purged from the world, but with it, the planet’s productivity falls dangerously low. Famine begins to spread on worlds reliant upon Goros Pok for sustenance.

If the characters take no action in this Strife, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Halikarn} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud} combine their resources to incite war between the four cults, earning both of them +1 Legitimacy, and the latter above results for the planet and sector.

Strife I-C
The Fate of the Lucanus

Reports from multiple sources claim unusual activity on Calvus Station, an isolated asteroid mining colony in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.4LYxCIJ2ansZ5wFk]{Andosk Subsector}. They claim sightings of a predatory xenos species, co-occurring with increased nonstandard worship practices among the populace.

A strange report comes from the crew of the freighter Lucanus, brought to light and delivered to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus}. The voidship’s communications were scrambled on its most recent return to Calvus Station, other than a cacophonous screeching emitted by the vessel’s astropath, one that was felt by nearby choirs in the subsector.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus} argues that the source of this corruption must be uncovered and excised, lest it pose a risk to navigation in the subsector.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Ksenia Baek} suggests capturing and studying the affected psyker (and any other psykers in the station) to curtail and understand the source of the unnerving psychic phenomenon.

Operation

The characters are sent to investigate Calvus Station and uncover the hidden xenos threat. Unbeknownst to them, this represents their first steps towards confronting the Herald’s Howl.

VoidstationS

Voidstations are space-tight structures of varying sizes, some small outposts, others as large as cities. All voidstations are built for a purpose, and most have some tie to the Imperial Fleet, acting as supply depots, orbital defences, or voiddocks. Some, like Calvus, are built into the sides of massive asteroids where their citizens work tirelessly to excavate the rare ores. Daily life is not unlike that in a hive city, but resources are often even more scarce. Life is more deadly too, with often only a thin plasteel wall between citizens and endless vacuum.

Characters deployed to Calvus Station find the Lucanus undergoing repairs, apparently after damage it suffered in transit. The crew claim this as an inconsequential delay, although the bridge is maintained off-limits by @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.kYpTOdUezMczq5eC]{voidsmen} on orders from the voidship’s officers, who are currently aboard the asteroid station.

On Calvus Station, life appears to continue in its normal cycles of industrial drudgery, although many of the workers bear oddly similar appearances: hairlessness, visible veins on the head and neck, and heavy brow ridges. Any queries about these features are met with dismissal and claim that these features are merely the effect of the conditions of working in the asteroid field, between limited radiation shielding and artificially enhanced gravity

Characters can meet with the station’s governor, Mordren Tiris. She claims that the officers are guests in her residence and that the astropath’s signals are due to them undergoing an augmetic installation and medical treatment after an incident during the vessel’s last voyage through the Warp. Shortly after meeting, Tiris tries to arrange the characters’ deaths through an industrial accident or by @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.KvLrPAQ0gmIWSvfX]{Purestrain Genestealers} attacking by night.

In searching Calvus Station, characters can uncover that the vessel’s officers have been killed and that the station is under the subtle control of a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cult}, comprising some forty percent of the workers, with Governor Tiris at its head. The cult operates from a shrine complex in the bowels of the asteroid, which they will sell their lives to defend. Here, a coven of Genestealer Cult psykers, commanded by Tiris, are holding the captured astropath, trying to reach some other entity through the tortured astropath’s distorted psychic screaming.

The chamber of the psykers is host to a piece of information with potentially vital significance — a star chart is scrawled across the ceiling in a vile parody of a painted Imperial chapel, depicting a great monstrous wyrm strewn across the Macharian Sector. Five dozen star systems seem to have been picked out with some special embellished symbolism, but its meaning, their exact coordinates, and which systems they represent are uncertain, even to the Genestealer Cultists present — the artwork conveyed a raw psychic image from the Patriarch, with no further details to aid in its interpretation.

Outcome

If the characters complete the mission, their Patron gains +1 Legitimacy. Recovering images of the Star Map suggests the potential of a broader Genestealer Cult threat lying in wait across the Macharian Sector, a significant concern for the Macharian Inquisitors at future Conclaves. They can claim the Lucanus as an asset but need to find a crew to operate it — their Patron could help.

If the characters fail to end the distorted psychic signal and the activities of the Genestealer Cult on Calvus Station, they complete their plan to hijack the Lucanus. They gain greater logistical interconnectivity in setting up the Herald’s Howl.

If no others undertake this mission, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Ksenia Baek} sends her acolytes to complete the mission, granting her +1 Legitimacy. Her operatives recover pict recordings of the Star Map, as well as the astropath and a Genestealer Cult psyker.

Conclave I Conclusion

The Inquisitors depart @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} with growing concern at the deaths of two Inquisitors in quick succession, particularly @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud}, who had already begun to suspect @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius} of heresy. Despite the large-scale chaos on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok}, the fate of the Lucanus may have greater importance than anyone has yet realised.

pages.name: Conclave II
pages.text:
Conclave II

The second Conclave turns to corruption lying deeper beneath the surface. Of central concern is the fate of Inquisitor Lord Heironymo Drake. Multiple Inquisitors have pored over his notes left in Mare Cinis and discovered a personal archive, from which both his research and the information that led him to his death may be recovered.

Dramatis Personae

In attendance at the second Conclave are: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud}, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Aegidius Halikarn}. An agent of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Kai Varol} expresses that their Inquisitor is pursuing a lead relating to the cult discovered on @UUID[.qMGtMcmwPnXnwPds#strife-i-c-the-fate-of-the-lucanus]{Calvus Station}. An astropath delivers a message on behalf of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Ksenia Baek}, who is busy elsewhere undertaking a joint operation with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.upGG1JZPDbC7dpJJ]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}.

Intrigues
