Both @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Kai Varol} have begun to suspect @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst}’s involvement in the death of Inquisitor Lord Drake. Raud is making this suspicion known by her handling of the @UUID[.ugwIBQXf8tEWYSE0#strife-ii-b-the-drake-archive]{Drake Archive}. Kai Varol is pursuing this investigation by ordering his acolytes to work from the Conclave’s shadows. Characters may recognise multiple acolytes in service to Kai Varol around the facility, despite him having no formal presence at the Conclave.

Each Inquisitor claimed an area of the @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} base during the first Conclave, but as @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Ksenia Baek} has not returned, nor have any of her retinue, characters with security and infiltration training could attempt to access the rooms that she claimed, including cogitators with communication records. Baek’s communications have expressed particular concern about the incident on Calvus Station.

Strife II-A
The Fall of House Kition

On the mercantile hive world of Asterion, a House Tavol informant serving Alis Raud reports that a competing Highborn arms manufacturer, House Kition, is preparing a martial coup to take over the planet.

House Tavol have been stockpiling arms rather than contributing them to the Imperial Tithe and amassing a corps of heavily armed troops. Rumours circulating among the noble houses of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X0XXyOc86SRCgd4h]{Asterion} claim a dozen origins for these troops, from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} deserters and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionist} mercenaries to abhumans and mutants. Merchants on Asterion are already under Inquisitorial observation for rumoured involvement in the so-called Silent Trade, but a potential coup backed by unknown forces warrants immediate scrutiny.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst} is familiar with the political order on Asterion due to her Ordo Sororitas Famulous contacts among Asterion’s Highborn families. She suggests that if the troops prove heretical, they be eliminated; House Kition would then surely collapse from its own subsequent economic weakness without threatening the stability of Asterion’s trade network.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Aegidius Halikarn} is incensed at the possibility of allowing traitors to go unpunished by the Inquisition, suggesting instead that if House Kition is found guilty of heresy, both the house and its army should be eliminated entirely, regardless of the consequences to a political system that Halikarn sees as contemptibly corrupt.

Operation

The characters travel to Asterion. Time is of the essence; they must investigate House Kition and dismantle their coup before it begins and destabilises Imperial rule in the system.

Before they leave @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst} advises characters deployed to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X0XXyOc86SRCgd4h]{Asterion} to make contact with Sister Famulous Lysara of the Order of the Hallowed Glass. She has worked closely with multiple Highborn houses of Asterion and can introduce characters to the Mavins, trade lord rulers of Asterion’s noble houses. Characters will soon learn that the Mavins do not perceive House Kition as a threat — House Kition’s apparent drop in production has led the Mavins to pay it little mind, allowing the house to gather its fighting force largely unobserved.

Through investigation, characters learn that House Kition’s leader, Mavin Aloysius Kition, perceived the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#silence-and-darkness]{Noctis Aeterna} as the death knell of Asterion’s bickering Mavins. The crisis demonstrated the need for a new form of governance with greater stability, which House Kition is equipped to provide and enforce.

In truth, House Kition's planned coup is supported by forces beyond what they realise or understand. If the characters are able to remove the armour from a captured or slain Silent Guard, they encounter physiology resembling the cultists found or reported on @UUID[.qMGtMcmwPnXnwPds#strife-i-c-the-fate-of-the-lucanus]{Calvus Station}.

The Silent Guard are a cell of the Herald’s Howl that originally formed in Asterion’s lower hives. Their leader, Primus Velten Zarn, made contact with House Kition during the chaos of the Noctis Aeterna.

Zarn suggested to Kition that a coup could save the crisis-stricken planet, sowing the seeds of ambition backed with an offer of troops allegedly from an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} regiment whose vessel was unable to leave the planet. Zarn intends to kill Kition during the coup and claim the role of Governor for himself, impersonating the deceased Kition using a stolen supply of polymorphine. This will elevate the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cult} and allow them to spread their influence through the populace in preparation for their day of ascension.

If members of House Kition become aware that they or their troops are under threat, they feel forced to begin their play for the Planetary Governor. The Silent Guard is ordered to eradicate the Board Solar, the governing council of Mavins, a blow aimed at swiftly removing the leadership of all opponents to House Kition, then besiege the spire of the Planetary Governor.

Outcome

If characters successfully complete their operation on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X0XXyOc86SRCgd4h]{Asterion}, their Patron gains +2 Legitimacy. Eliminating the Silent Guard brings House Kition into steep political decline, with rival houses buying out their manufactorums. Eliminating House Kition entirely sends shockwaves through the Mavins' already damaged trade networks. If the characters fail in their mission and House Kition’s rise was not prevented, Velten Zarn uses his new position as Planetary Governor to begin proliferating arms to other cells of the Herald's Howl throughout the Macharian Sector. If the characters’ Patron does not take action, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Aegidius Halikarn} leads a shadow war to destroy the Silent Guard and House Kition, earning +2 Legitimacy.

Strife II-B
The Drake Archive

The Conclave investigates an archive of information that Inquisitor Lord Drake left behind, locked away in a vault on Mare Cinis. The information within drives them to chase down two Rogue Traders and travel to a planet quarantined by Inquisitorial decree.

The notes in Inquisitor Lord Drake's vault include multiple references to an archive hidden in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.y6qA7KARTXADwzeV]{Cytheris Subsector}, although even the Inquisitor Lord’s former Interrogator, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud}, is unaware of its location or what it might contain. What has been decyphered so far imparts the names of two @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#rogue-traders-of-note]{Rogue Traders}, Captain Ion Hawkscar and Captain Darius Klaskoloff, and a code phrase to be repeated to each of them: ‘CUSTODIA. RECONDITUS. ADSTRUM. ASPECTUM’.

Given that members of the Conclave suspect @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst} having some hand in the death of her mentor, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} expresses that it is imperative an impartial party access the archive and return its contents to the Conclave so that the Inquisitor Lord’s records of Macharian heresies be put to continued use.

Operation

The characters begin their hunt for the two Rogue Traders; though the Captains are unaware, each holds information that can reveal the location of the archive.

Prior to the characters’ departure, they are contacted by an agent of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Kai Varol}, who requests they return to him any information recovered that may implicate @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst} in the death of Inquisitor Lord Drake — Varol recognises that often the greatest threat to an Inquisitor comes from within their own retinue.

Additionally, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst} reluctantly agrees to equip the characters with a Rosette simulacra that had belonged to the late Inquisitor Lord — it is almost certain that this will be required to access the archive.

Characters attempting to locate each Rogue Trader find that Captain Hawkscar is in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.y6qA7KARTXADwzeV]{Cytheris Subsector}, while Captain Klaskoloff is more difficult to locate, his vessel plying the edges of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.d0lv2v4FkeIb43jj]{Drimor Subsector}. Neither of them ever remembers meeting Inquisitor Lord Drake. Characters looking into either Rogue Trader’s history or flight logs discover they crossed paths in system ID3421-G3 (in the Cytheris Subsector) decades ago, but neither remembers meeting the other.

Investigating ID-3421-G3, characters can learn that the planet Vitezovich, within the system, has been stricken from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.VVyxPjdULmCks7NP#galaxy-of-peril]{Astra Cartographica} records. No records exist of this planet other than its name, location, and the fact that it was subject to Exterminatus four centuries ago and cordoned by Inquisitorial decree ever since.

If characters repeat the code phrase to either Rogue Trader, their eyes glaze over momentarily before seemingly returning to their senses. Upon activation, each is instinctively driven to gather an armed force and travel to Vitezovich, where they are to rendezvous and begin bombarding the planet, letting nothing stand in their way.

Investigating Vitezovich directly involves donning voidsuits, as little of the planet’s atmosphere remains. The location of the archive is uncertain; only faint signs of life can be detected on the surface. They will find the archive being defended by a force of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.kYpTOdUezMczq5eC]{voidsmen} acting on a subconscious imperative to prevent any save Inquisitor Lord Drake from entering the facility.

The archive is centred on a datavault, protected by automated defences, in the form of wall and floor mounted servitor turrets. They will not fire on the bearer of Inquisitor Drake’s Rosette; others are automatically targeted by heavy stubber fire. The central datavault can be accessed by the bearer of Drake’s Rosette, though everything within is heavily cyphered. Returning the data to @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} requires them to unplug massive arrays of hardware and transport it by voidship — a more complicated task if the activated Rogue Traders will soon arrive and once more bombard the planet.

Outcome

If the Inquisitor Lord’s archive is returned to @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis}, it provides information on the Inquisitor’s concerns in the Macharian Sector. However, little of it will be decyphered until the start of the next Conclave. The most populous data in the archive is designated the ‘Kryptman Protocol’, detailing a failsafe procedure of mass extermination in the event of a Tyranid invasion of the Macharian Sector.

Characters recovering the Archive will earn the respect of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Kai Varol} should their search for information regarding Inquisitor Lord Drake’s death prove fruitful. Either way, their Patron gains +1 Legitimacy and access to the archive; therefore, they are the first to learn of the Kryptman Protocol.

If the characters’ Patron does not take action or they fail to recover the archive, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Kai Varol} secretly launches the recovery operation. He retrieves Inquisitor Lord Drake’s archive and becomes the first to learn of the Kryptman Protocol.

Characters may wish to aid in deprogramming the Rogue Trader captains, revealing more information on Drake’s cyphers (to assist in their investigations later) and gain +1 Influence with their respective Dynasties.

Strife II-C
The Eskutchax Incongruity

As the long siege of Eskutchax continues, a recent victory by Black Templar forces has left behind a heretical artefact in dire need of investigation and disposal.

Arnaut Cisneros, Interrogator to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus}, received a message from his Tech-Priest contact, Magos Tal-Theta 661, raising concern over an artefact left in the wake of retreating heretic forces. The Tech-Priests and Black Templar Space Marines are equally uncertain of what should be done with the artefact after attempts to destroy it proved ineffectual.

  • Despite his ongoing relationship with the Tech-Priests of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.jB9sg2SDLZJGZrac]{Eskutchax}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus} recognises that the disposal of a Chaos artefact is outside his expertise, so he recommends that Ordo Hereticus forces investigate and dispose of the object.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} requests that the artefact be returned and taken into Inquisitorial custody, claiming to have a means of safely sealing away or disposing of it.

Operation

Characters are deployed to the beleaguered forge world Eskutchax, where the artefact lies in the shattered remains of a manufactorum under guard by the Adeptus Astartes.

Shortly after arrival, they are briefed by Magos TalTheta 661. The artefact, identified as the core of a shattered Daemon Engine, spreads a corrupting scrap code into nearby technology, poisoning the machine spirit with glitches and malfunctions.

Thus far, it has proved difficult to extract and has forced the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus} and Adeptus Astartes to hold their distance — the scrap code poses too significant a risk towards augmetics and power armour.

Magos Tal-Thera 661 hypothesises that the corruptive energies could be contained by a group of psykers creating a barrier around the artefact (such as @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.weeeCywXm9wF54Ly]{Psychic Barrier}). However, this is a challenging prospect to entertain in the presence of the zealous Black Templars.

The manufactorum surrounding the artefact’s location has been affected by ongoing malfunctions and infestations of Glitchlings, diminutive daemons being called from the Warp by the machines’ daemonic infection (use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.pGOi4dyYeKojE9vm]{Nurgling} stat-block to represent them, except their Traits and Attacks inflict Stunned in addition to Poisoned). Should characters safely navigate the corrupted forge fane, they will discover that another problem has arisen — the artefact is now missing.

Furthering their investigation, characters learn from Magos Tal-Theta 661 or other Tech-Priests that the Warpsmith Omneros’ attacks on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.jB9sg2SDLZJGZrac]{Eskutchax} included the strategic binding of daemons into the engines of this conquered forge fane. Many Tech-Priests are keeping this quiet to spare their technology from the likelihood of destruction by the Black Templars. While the faithful of the Omnissiah have undertaken blessing upon blessing, the infection cannot be excised without the removal or destruction of the Daemon Engine core. As a result, the corruption has been left unchecked, and daemonic scrap code has possessed numerous augmented workers, servitors, and skitarii, who have moved the Daemon Engine core from its resting place. Driven by the Daemon Engine core, the possessed bear it on the first steps of what, if not stopped, will become a pilgrimage in the shadows, spreading the scrap code across every one of the planet’s forge fanes.

To retrieve the core, characters will need to locate it by following a trail of malfunctions and error reports and eliminate its corrupted bearers. They travel by subterranean maintenance tunnels, in the direction of the equatorial forge fane from which the Consuls govern @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.jB9sg2SDLZJGZrac]{Eskutchax}.

This process will demand discretion, as engaging in open battle will draw the attention of the Adeptus Astartes, alerting them to the deeper infestation of daemonic corruption, and likely leading them to undertake a purge of heresy that would devastate the industry and population of Eskutchax. Should the core be captured, the daemonic virus will fight to protect itself throughout the extraction process, overriding nearby machinery and summoning Glitchling swarms to prevent its excision.

Outcome

If the Daemon Engine core is successfully extracted, the scrap code can finally be purged from the forge fanes of Eskutchax. Upon returning the artefact to the Inquisition, the characters’ Patron gains +2 Legitimacy and +1 Influence with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus}. If they side with the Black Templars, they gain +1 Influence with them instead of any Legitimacy. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} departs with the Daemon Engine core to undertake a psychic ritual to nullify it. In secret, she does so by tearing the daemon from this vessel and binding it to an imprisoned Human host.

If characters fail to extract the Daemon Engine core, Magos Tal-Theta 661 reluctantly informs the Black Templars of the daemonic scrap code emanating from the core. The Adeptus Astartes exorcise the corruption with extreme prejudice, devastating the corrupted forge fane.

If no other Inquisitor undertakes this operation, it is left to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud}, who gains +2 Legitimacy for retrieving and containing the Daemon Engine core.

Conclave II Conclusion

With the recovery of the Drake Archive, a tool of dreadful power has been brought under Inquisitorial control, either that of the Conclave or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius}. Meanwhile, the House Kition incident has heightened @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Serranus}’ existing concerns, for it suggests @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cult} activity on a far larger scale than initially considered.

pages.name: Conclave III
pages.text:
Conclave III

Mare Cinis is in lockdown, and a botched attack by a rogue Interrogator is halted at the last minute. Servitors repair sections of the base marred by traces of explosives while Inquisitorial retinues stand vigil, their Patrons not yet confident that the threat has passed.

Dramatis Personae

In attendance at the third Conclave are: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Aegidius Halikarn}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Kai Varol}, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Ksenia Baek}. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} is absent but is represented by her Interrogator, Damien Savantas, who reports that Inquisitor Raud is occupied with an investigation in the Drimor Subsector.

Intrigues

In @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud}’s absence, Kai Varol (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius}) believes he has greater freedom to act. The @UUID[.ugwIBQXf8tEWYSE0#strife-ii-b-the-drake-archive]{Drake Archive} has shed little light on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst}’s possible involvement in the Inquisitor Lord’s death. Varol may contact the characters, requesting they infiltrate the section of the base occupied by Sylvestrine Horst to access her personal logs.

However, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud} is not unrepresented at the Conclave. The characters may be approached by Damien Savantas, who seeks to recruit their support in hunting @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius}. He has been interrogating Tarran Selvir for many years (the acolyte who returned with news of Thracius’ alleged death).

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud} has learned that @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius} was one of multiple identities attributed to the same individual and that he may not be dead after all. Raud has suspicions that Thracius is working within the Conclave under another false identity but remains uncertain who this imposter may be, asking the characters whether they have any suspicions and offering to meet again if they believe they have learned anything pertinent..

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst} has appointed an Interrogator: Yorin Veldir, an inscrutable individual wearing a mask of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW]{Saint Macharius}. The characters' Patron is eager to know what information can be gathered about them, as this Interrogator is currently an uncertain factor for the Conclave. Those who dig into Interrogator Veldir’s past may learn that Horst recruited them from the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.WE1MLa1KVRHMD8wJ.JournalEntryPage.P8rukYyQeyPJ1ubs]{Imperial Navy} and that they served as an officer aboard one of the vessels that enacted Exterminatus upon @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.lpu6iuTHw50UavbI]{Belnshudha} (the planet where Inquisitor Lord Drake met his demise).

Strife III-A
The Rogue Interrogator

A rogue Interrogator has fled Mare Cinis after their botched attack on the Conclave, which, if successful, could have slain the entire Macharian Inquisition.

Arnaut Cisneros, Interrogator to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranu}s, attempted to sabotage @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} but was caught in the act, detonating the explosives they had already planted to cover their escape, and fleeing to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy]{Persepolis} below.

  • To the gathered Conclave, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Serranus} declares Cisneros Excommunicate Traitoris, with the full support of each other Inquisitor present.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Serranus} is infuriated, particularly as he was already preparing to undertake a key operation when the attack occurred; this setback may cost him valuable time in his investigations of a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cult} bearing striking resemblance to that found on @UUID[.qMGtMcmwPnXnwPds#strife-i-c-the-fate-of-the-lucanus]{Calvus Station}.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Serranus} asserts that his current investigation is of such importance that it cannot wait for him to recover the heretic Interrogator, a claim supported by @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Kai Varol}, who first uncovered the lead that Serranus is pursuing. While he is reluctant to shift the responsibility of eliminating Cisneros to another, his hand is forced, and he requests the aid of the Conclave.

Operation

The characters begin their chase across Persepolis, plumbing the depths of Hive Valios to find the escaped Interrogator and catch them before they can do anything worse.

Characters pursuing Cisneros may wish to examine @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis}'s voidship flight records. Shortly after the attack, a small transport departed the base; the tracking data suggests it crashed on the planet below, on the outskirts of Hive Valios. Given Cisneros’ status as Excommunicate Traitoris, their movements will be severely limited. However, locating Cisneros may become a near-insurmountable task if they entered the decaying industrial labyrinth of Valios’ lower hive levels.

On the surface, a trail of malfunctioning machinery on the hive edge leads characters into the lower hive. Limited enforcer presence and the endless winding tunnels require the characters to work with local guides and bounty hunters. They must track the rogue Interrogator’s movements across decaying zones and industrial complexes filled with desperate, impoverished wretches.

The trail left by Cisneros suggests a link between their treachery and the @UUID[.ugwIBQXf8tEWYSE0#strife-ii-c-the-eskutchax-incongruity]{Daemon Engine core} found on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.jB9sg2SDLZJGZrac]{Eskutchax}. Cisneros, infected with daemonic scrap code, first reported this incident at the second Conclave after returning from Eskutchax. Due to Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Serranus}’ practice of augmenting his acolytes, the daemon was able to inhabit Cisneros' augmetics and wrest control of what flesh remained. Cisneros remains conscious, trapped in their own body.

The daemon seeks to infect the hive’s cogitator network with scrap code. The few Cisneros sightings reported by lower hive citizens have been at cogitator arrays, servitor colonies, and datavaults. However, as the daemon finds these systems disused or disconnected from the hive’s wider cogitator network, its actions have become increasingly erratic. The characters learn from the hive’s Tech-Priests that Cisneros found a tech reliquary containing @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.px7pplClKR01chqM]{Servitors} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.Y6oJff3F4qo2Xhlx]{Servo-skulls}, infecting them all.

If located, the first instinct of the possessed Cisneros is to flee. If cornered, the daemon fights to the death — its hosts, rather than its own — dominating any nearby industrial machinery to defend itself.

Outcome

Characters who destroy Cisneros demonstrate the capability of their Patron to resolve other Inquisitors’ problems, earning them +1 Legitimacy. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus} is greatly appreciative and more willing to work with the characters’ Patron, particularly concerning the @UUID[.jt0zc7az5xNehcIZ#the-heralds-howl]{Herald’s Howl}. If recovered alive, Cisneros provides valuable information on Serranus’ actions. However, Cisneros has been declared Excommunicate Traitoris, putting the characters and their Patron under suspicion as possible traitors themselves if they provide shelter.

If his hand is forced, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus} sends his own acolytes to destroy Arnaut Cisneros, losing both a potentially valuable lead in investigating the Herald’s Howl and multiple operatives, whose augmetics make them ill-equipped to face the scrap code-infected Interrogator (he gains no Legitimacy).

Strife III-B
The Return of Knight Commander Justinian

The Inquisition is urged to investigate strange occurrences on Xenophon after the disappearance and subsequent reappearance of one of their most distinguished officers.

A Castellan from the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum}, Jak Greiss, comes before the Conclave to petition aid from the Inquisition. The famous Knight Commander Justinian was found clinging to driftwood by Astra Militarum troops, allegedly having escaped tortuous captivity beneath the oceans of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.si7mc5k5MVLqN049]{Xenophon}. The Commander’s mind and body have both suffered horrendously from the torture inflicted upon him by his captors; he has only been able to recount being dragged into the oceans by a group of Xenophonians. However, he struggles to remember what transpired after that and who kept him captive after being thrown, weighted, into the sublime green ocean.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.si7mc5k5MVLqN049]{Xenophon} is designated a garden world, with more water than landmass. It presents hazards in its marine flora and fauna, which have claimed the lives of many careless officers taking leave on the planet over the years. However, these recent events shed light on potential heretic or xenos activity on the planet.

  • Given that what exactly befell Knight Commander Justinian in the oceans of Xenophon remains uncertain, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Aegidius Halikarn} suggests a decoy operation — send an acolyte with a false identity to bait the heretics, tricking them into kidnapping another supposed @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} officer, thereby revealing their identification, and path to elimination.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Kai Varol’s} concerns lie with sending acolytes to investigate what occurred after the cultists left the Commander to sink beneath the waves, for indeed, whatever shadow has hold over Xenophon originates in those dark waters.

Operation

Characters depart to Xenophon to begin their investigation, soon to plunge into a worldwide conspiracy involving a cult of Drukhari-worshipping locals.

Characters can talk to Castellan Greiss before they depart to gain more insight into Justinian. He is a tank commander who survived countless battles fighting heretics at the edge of the sector. He has a phobia of deep water and was reluctant to take leave on Xenophon.

Garden Worlds

Garden worlds are among the rarest planets in the galaxy — those few naturally suited to sustaining Human life with no terraforming required. These veritable paradises are often protected to retain their natural beauty and atmosphere; even the boot of the Imperium knows to tread lightly on them. As such, populations are kept relatively low, and these planets are used as training bases or for recreational use. Experiencing life on such a world is a rare blessing for anyone who can.

He is in a near catatonic state, under heavy guard in his leave-housing on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.si7mc5k5MVLqN049]{Xenophon}. If questioned as to why the Castellan has requested the Inquisition’s aid, he claims that the locals are challenging to deal with, and due to the planet’s draw as a shore leave destination, its governing bodies hold too much sway with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} and might interfere with an internal investigation.

If characters choose to masquerade as @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} officers or observe other officers taking leave on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.si7mc5k5MVLqN049]{Xenophon}, they will find that isolated officers are sometimes kidnapped at night by a group that throws their victims into the ocean, sacrifices to beings they call the Pearl-eyed Ones. Unaware of Justinian’s status, the cultists kidnapped and subsequently released him in an attempt to avoid scrutiny. This cost the cultists dearly in the eyes of their masters.

Characters may investigate beneath the waves by diving or submersible, though the latter will arouse suspicion among the cultists. Diving below the coral reefs, characters find ancient Aeldari structures centred around an inactive Webway portal. The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari} are using it to collect victims offered to them by the Xenophonian cultists.

The cult has ritually sacrificed people to the Drukhari since before the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-macharian-conquests]{Macharian Crusade}. It is deeply ingrained into local culture, and even the Planetary Governor works with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari}. Many locals know of the practice, a tradition they carefully conceal. This relationship is built on generations of ritual and maintained by both sides, with the Drukhari eliminating any threats to this supply of victims. If the cultists become aware they are under investigation, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.b8x4YQfSyzlvU4LX]{Drukhari Kabalite Warriors} move to eliminate the investigators.

With a captured or slain Drukhari in hand, characters may be able to call military support from their Patron’s allies, as well as mobilise visiting @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} forces against the xenos-allied cultists and Drukhari. Should their Webway portal come under attack, the Drukhari withdraw from Xenophon entirely, offering the cultists safety from the Imperial forces if they follow them — a final cruel ploy for one last batch of victims.

Outcome

Ending the cultic activity on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.si7mc5k5MVLqN049]{Xenophon} by eliminating the cultists or breaking the Drukhari hold over the world earns the characters’ Patron +1 Legitimacy and +1 Influence with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum}.

Failing to identify the cultists or the Drukhari influencing them from beneath the waves will allow the killings to continue, gradually eroding the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum’s} body of officers in the Macharian Sector.

If no other Inquisitor undertakes this operation, it falls to Kai Varol (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius}), who gains +1 Legitimacy on completion of the mission. In discovering xenos involvement, Varol aquires further understanding of the Webway. It eventually benefits his experiments with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari} technology, developing into a means of covert travel and access to Aeldari sites.

Strife III-C
The Ghost of Luna

The Black Ship, Ghost of Luna, has stalled above Jotungarth. The psykers aboard exhibit the same unnerving behaviour — each is emitting a beautiful and inscrutable psychic song blocking the light of the Astronomican from the ship’s navigator.

An @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.upGG1JZPDbC7dpJJ]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica} voidship has been cordoned off by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}. Psykers aboard continue to deteriorate, their condition threatening to end all navigation to and from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.wHl3ZP7wM7OQvSLC]{Jotungarth}.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Ksenia Baek} sees investigating the vessel and planet as imperative. Given her connections to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.upGG1JZPDbC7dpJJ]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}, she is concerned that the corruption of these psykers may spread to others. However, psykers lead Baek’s acolytes and are at considerable risk of corruption if they investigate.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus} suggests the ship be immediately destroyed; what is the loss of a few psykers when the whole sector is already rife with them? Let the debris fall into the frozen waters of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.wHl3ZP7wM7OQvSLC]{Jotungarth} and be forgotten. Navigators on nearby vessels have already begun to notice the discordant song.

Operation

Characters depart for Jotungarth to investigate the stranded Black Ship. They will soon discover the consequences of Inquisitor Lord Hieronymo Drake’s actions and learn more about the dead Inquisitor’s past.

Before departure, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Ksenia Baek} suggests that the characters contact Knight-Centura Augustina aboard the Ghost of Luna. If the players or their Patron are in good standing with Baek, she also offers the services of a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.CBLdHnFWFqdhfRKx]{Sister of Silence} from her retinue to accompany them.

Aboard the Black Ship, the characters’ first experience boarding the vessel will be the singing echoing through the decks, both audible in realspace and their minds, unless in the presence of a blank. If characters meet Knight-Centura Augustina, she informs them that the psychic song began when the Black Ship arrived in orbit around @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.wHl3ZP7wM7OQvSLC]{Jotungarth}. The characters can investigate the ship and conclude that nothing is amiss mechanically. A psyker who risks exposure to the song can tell it originates on Jotungarth itself.

Deploying to the surface of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.wHl3ZP7wM7OQvSLC]{Jotungarth}, characters discover widespread psychic awakenings, unnatural phenomena, and even minor daemonic activity throughout the planet’s city-vessels. These all originate with those who have heard the same psychic song, and any psychically attuned members of the party will be aware of it too. As they aid city-vessel authorities in tackling these events, they must find a way to track and pinpoint the psychic song. Quelling enough psychic activity will ‘clear the air’ and lead them to the source. Additionally, Jotungarth has an abundance of master seers and oracles that could aid in pinpointing the phenomena; many will be distressed by this psychic signal and eager to help. The characters could work with local astropath choirs to attempt to overcome the daemonic song with a hymn of their own, or assemble enough sanctioned psykers to divine the location of the source through a dangerous psychic ritual.

Characters can track the ultimate source of the psychic song to a remote and hidden bastion, buried within a massive iceberg bearing Inquisition insignia. Automated defences guard the facility but will surrender and open itself to anyone with vermillion-level clearance. It soon becomes apparent that the facility belonged to Inquisitor Lord Hieronymo Drake. He was using the facility to study the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.M6XWkYc0lfuKl2hU]{Daemonhost} he captured within. Since Drake’s death, the solitary daemon has loosened its bonds, freeing its psychic voice to reach others nearby.

Black Ships

The Black Ships of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.upGG1JZPDbC7dpJJ]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica} travel the Imperium, charged with collecting and transporting psykers back to Terra to fulfil the God-Emperor’s Tithe. These massive dread galleons are effectively prison vessels. Their cavernous holds are filled with psyker containment units and other tools to combat Warp manifestations, an oppressive backdrop to the screams of the lost and the damned that echo their halls. Each crew member must be capable of withstanding psychic influence — whether by extensive mental augmetics, the Pariah Gene, or being a powerful psyker in their own right.

Several parts of Drake's research point to cults on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.lpu6iuTHw50UavbI]{Belnshudha}, suggesting that he allowed their heretical activites to thrive for some time. Also, it indicates that Drake extracted the daemonhost from Belnshudha some time ago. Other aspects of his research here point to the @UUID[.jt0zc7az5xNehcIZ#the-kryptman-protocol]{Kryptman Protocol}, seeking ways to turn the daemonhost’s power into a weapon of Exterminatus. Characters find more cyphers and keys; they can return them to @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} to further research on the Drake Archive.

Outcome

Characters must decide what to do with the daemonhost. Return with it to @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis}, hand it over to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud}, or destroy it. Whatever outcome here, their Patron earns +1 Legitimacy and +1 Influence with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.upGG1JZPDbC7dpJJ]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}. The Ghost of Luna is free to continue on the long way back to Holy Terra.

If no other Inquisitor takes action in this Strife, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Ksenia Baek} locates and destroys the daemonhost gaining +1 Legitimacy for her efforts.

Conclave III Conclusion

In the wake of Cisneros’ attack, the Inquisitors hesitate to attend the following Conclave, particularly @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus}, although his desire to be elsewhere is driven by growing @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cult} activity. With the deaths of acolytes in multiple operations, trust between the Inquisitors is diminishing; each suspects the others of some measure of sabotage.

pages.name: Conclave IV
pages.text:
Conclave IV

House Tavol has mistakenly dealt with traitors and risks the scrutiny of the Inquisition. A strange Imperial voidship is haunting the Gallosque Nebula. Inquisitor Raud reveals the fate of Halikarn’s undercover agent.

Dramatis Personae

In attendance at the fourth Conclave are: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Aegidius Halikarn}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Kai Varol}, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Ksenia Baek}. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus} is noticeably absent.

Intrigues

If the characters seek information on the black market and arms movements, particularly in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.d0lv2v4FkeIb43jj]{Drimor Subsector}, they could approach Antonius Tavnir, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-defiant]{House Tavol} agent. In return, Tavnir seeks protection and assurances from the Conclave that he will live to see the end of his problems (see @UUID[.bUgRB72Mw5eaLfL6#strife-iv-a-traitors-in-tavol]{Strive IV-A: Traitors in Tavol}). But Tavnir is loyal first to Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud}; the Inquisitor will learn about anything the characters gain from Tavnir.

Inquisitor Kai Varol (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius}) is keen to talk directly to the characters. Depending on his relationship with the players' Patron, he may reach out directly or through a proxy, such as one of his acolytes. He will happily entertain them personally if they seek information on any xenos entities in the sector, especially anything @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari}-related. Varol hopes to find a suitable candidate to become a double agent in his service. He will approach them privately before the Conclave adjourns, sowing seeds of dissent and offering protections whilst potentially holding some form of blackmail against them.

Inquisitor Varol also speaks openly about gathering more information about @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cult} activity across the sector, imploring the other Inquisitors to talk to their contacts after finding more strange correlations in his own gathered datasets.'

Strife IV-A
Traitors in Tavol

Noble House politics has spilled over into the Inquisition’s Conclave. House Tavol fights within itself, split between purity and profits. The nobles have stoked the fires of heresy, and now the Inquisition must serve them justice.

Antonius Tavnir, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-defiant]{House Tavol} agent, has been brought before the Conclave by Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud}. The agent has evidence that others within House Tavol have mistakenly supplied arms to Traitor Guard regiments, thought loyal, across planets in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.d0lv2v4FkeIb43jj]{Drimor Subsector}.

Tavnir is taking a significant risk in revealing this information to the Inquisition, so much so that Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud} was forced to extract him. He and many facets of his house are now woefully at the mercy of the Inquisition.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} has ordered the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} to deal with the Traitor Guard. She believes Tavnir and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-defiant]{House Tavol} should be left to continue operating as they were (fruitful branches of her existing spy network for some time) and requires a team to re-insert the agent into the house’s hierarchy.

  • But @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst} opposes her, calling for the house to be fiercely investigated to uncover any further 'mistakes' and then summarily dismantled.

Operation

Characters depart to investigate House Tavol, dragging Antonius Tavnir with them. Each day they tarry, the traitor regiments grow in power, and heresy within House Tavol digs in deeper.

Either outcome requires the party to escort Tavnir. They must track down and silence the other house traders who know Tavnir is a double agent, allowing him to retake his position. Otherwise, they can use Tavnir to dig deeper into the house’s records to find further signs of heretical trade. While investigating various @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-defiant]{Tavol} holdings and NPCs around Drimor, new heresies come to light:

One of the Traitor Guard regiments, stationed on the mining world of Krakau, contains hidden worshippers of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.iJzmX5SguvLyGws1#nurgle-clues]{Nurgle}. In response to increased @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cult} activity opposing them, they sought weaponry from Tavol. The two heretic organisations secretly vie for control of the planet under the noses of the ruling nobility. Without intervention, their conflict threatens to spill into the local populace and overthrow the local rulers.

A second regiment is stationed on the feral world of Barbarosk. The traitor regiments have been bolstering their numbers, recruiting from the local populace by preaching twisted narratives of the God-Emperor’s truths. They paint the people of Kharmin, a nearby system, as heretics. They have been moving troops to Kharmin under the guise of material supplies from the feral world, planning to assault the capital hive.

The characters can discover that Tavnir set up the original deals to incriminate his competition in the house and elevate his position, abusing his agency under Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud}. If found out, Raud is not kind in her retribution and orders the characters to execute Tavnir once their operation is complete.

Outcome

If the characters follow Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud}’s proposition and succeed, they and their Patron gain favour with Raud and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-defiant]{House Tavol}, influential contacts and allies for future operations. Additionally, their Patron gains +1 Legitimacy. If the characters favour @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst}’s opposing plan, Horst cuts through House Tavol viciously, gaining +1 Legitimacy. Many cunning nobles receive warnings from Tavnir and scatter to the void. House Tavol becomes a troublesome enemy of the Inquisition, working deeper in the shadows.

Strife IV-B
The Lost Recongregator

Inquisitor Raud announces to the Conclave that Mordo Talut, one of Inquisitor Halikarn’s long-standing acolytes, has been arrested for treason on Jenesse. A surprised Halikarn scrambles to investigate.

Local authorities in Hive Nostra have arrested a long-serving deep-cover acolyte named Mordo Talut. He is currently being held and charged with treason against the Planetary Governor. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Halikarn} is surprised by this development; Mordo has always been an exceedingly cautious Interrogator.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} strongly suggests that @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Halikarn} cleans up his mess by silencing this acolyte before any of the Inquisition’s secrets are spilt or extract him before his execution. Mordo invoked Halikarn’s name, which has stayed in his captor’s hand for now.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst} offers her aid in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Halikarn}’s stead, claiming that a number of her Faceless operatives are already working in the subsector; she hopes to gain Halikarn’s favour.

  • Furthermore, the other Inquisitors present now acutely suspect that @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud} has informants in all of their networks.

Operation

Characters depart for Jenesse, aiming to find Mordo Talut and investigate the Nostrafax nobility. Hive Nostra is rife with hidden heresies, and signs point to other ancient troubles in the system.

Characters sent to investigate Mordo Talut’s arrest meet with Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Halikarn} before they depart. Halikarn would prefer Mordo Talut be extracted safely, seeming almost sentimental towards this acolyte, but understands if they have no choice except to eliminate him. He reveals that Mordo was digging into the legitimacy of noble houses in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.y6qA7KARTXADwzeV]{Cytheris Subsector}, believing they might be harbouring descendants of General Lysander, one of Macharius’ generals who betrayed the Imperium after the Lord Solar’s death. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#machariuss-generals]{General Lysander's betrayal} was so dire that all titles and rights granted to his household were stripped away. Nevertheless, a few of his more ambitious descendants still lay claim to the traitor's name and privileges, which, by Imperial Lex, burdens them with his guilt as well.

Investigating Hive Nostra, the capital hive of Jenesse, characters can discover that Mordo Talut was taken into custody by the Planetary Governor's personal guard. Strangely, these guards are present at positions of power all across the hive and stave off the characters’ investigation as best they can. Infiltrating House Nostrafax, they can learn that Governor Nostrafax disappeared some time ago with Mordo in tow. The officers in his personal guard (also appointed members of the Nostrafax family) have taken control of the local government, enacting an underhanded martial law meant to hold Nostrafax’s place until his eventual return.

Characters can learn from the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.gQxTENJSdTQTVfDM]{Vigilites} or Nostrafax’s staff that the Governor and Mordo left Jenesse aboard the Sorrow of Juun, an Imperial frigate. They can track the Sorrow by securing local contacts in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}, as both factions monitor the movements of voidships through the system. Mechanicus agents see the opportunity to wrest plentiful favours and influence from the characters. Meanwhile, by securing and analysing data from the Imperial Fleet, characters can discover evidence of scrubbed star charts and records, indicating potential traitors within the local fleet.

The Sorrow’s trail leads to Aegos, a world hidden within the nearby Argent Zone, one forbidden approach by Inquisitorial decree. This apparent feudal world is home to settled remnants of the traitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#machariuss-generals]{Lysander’s} family and forces. Living and plotting from their secluded fiefdom, they have been slowly seeding their lineage back into Imperial nobility and the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet} via Jenesse’s houses for some time, seeking to re-emerge once they have gathered enough influence. Nostrafax is a high-ranking member of this lineage.

Mordo Talut is trapped on Aegos. Nostrafax and his family ponder what to do with him whilst seeking to extract information — what does @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{ Halikarn} know of their plans? The characters could infiltrate the feudal planet and quietly extract Mordo, as Halikarn desires. Alternatively, they could seek a greater Inquisitorial force to bear upon Aegos to cleanse it of traitors. Houses on Jenesse that oppose Nostrafax’s rule may be able to back them in this endeavour.

Outcome

If the characters are successful, they gain @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Halikarn}’s favour and +1 Legitimacy for their Patron. Halikarn now knows that an Inquisitor was once involved with the sector’s re-written histories, someone who initially saved Lysander’s remnants but is unsure who it may have been. Otherwise, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Horst}’s Faceless agents make a mess of the situation on Jenesse and Aegos. They manage to dispose of Mordo and scrub the records of the operative’s presence, earning Horst +1 Legitimacy. Many of the traitor Lysander’s descendants escape and their heresies linger to resurface in the future.

Strife IV-C
The Vice of Eternan

The Vice of Eternan, after having wrecked a voidport in the Paleon system, is now blinking in and out of realspace. This rogue voidship moves across the sector in fits and spurts, astray in the Warp for reasons unknown.

In the preceding year, The Vice of Eternan, an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet} transport ship, suffered a catastrophe whilst taking on cargo at a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.A9cvKlA41X8qPyEw]{Paleon}-orbiting port. Still moored to the station, the voidship suddenly dove into the Warp, wrecking much of the port and killing thousands of crew, travellers, and dock workers.

Such an event would not usually interest the Inquisition, but since the Vice’s disappearance, the voidship has been blinking in and out of realspace, detected at different coordinates throughout the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.UbH7oOtTYfjFlKRt]{Gallosque Nebula}. Whenever it resurfaces, local vox networks have recorded unholy screaming across their channels, and its presence seems to disturb astropath choirs in the Gallosque Subsector.

  • Kharket Graan, an astropath in the service of Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Ksenia Baek}, claims they have visions of the ship's future appearances.

  • Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Baek} seeks to hunt the voidship and simply wipe it out before it causes any more issues, but she is reticent to deal with it, claiming to be heavily occupied with other matters.

  • Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud} wishes to investigate the events surrounding the disaster carefully and unravel the mystery rather than destroy the ship outright.

Operation

The characters begin their hunt for the Vice of Eternan, hoping to investigate its mysteries or ensure its destruction before it causes another wide-scale disaster in the sector.

The first task for any group of characters to tackle this issue is to gather a battlegroup of Imperial voidships to travel to the Vice’s next emergence point. The astropath, Kharket Graan, projects they have some time to get into position within a strait of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.UbH7oOtTYfjFlKRt]{Gallosque Nebula}. That’s where the voidship will appear next, but all must depart immediately. Their Patron has acquired a Gellar Field stabilisation array from Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Baek}, a rare and precious device reluctantly provided by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus}. Such a powerful device could keep the Vice anchored long enough to investigate.

As soon as the Vice appears, the party are sent aboard, along with the stabilisation array’s attendant Tech-Priests, and backed up by a security team of Navy Breachers to protect them. Installing the stabilisation array is no simple task; emitters must be placed at different points across the ship and then protected against interference.

Aboard, it becomes apparent that @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cultists} attacked the ship as the Vice was taking on cargo. The cultists have been locked in skirmishes with the remaining crew since the incident occurred. Currently, the cultists have control over the ship’s engine room, desperately trying to hold their ground and wrestle control of the ship’s damaged engines to prevent the next Warp transition.

Matter of Time

The Warp has not been kind to the Vice and its crew — characters learn that events on the ship have only occurred within a week of the initial attack, and each transition seems to break even more of the voidship’s functions and integrity. Consider the possibility that the Vice threatens to make a Warp transition before the stabilisation array is put in place and what that could mean for the characters to be trapped aboard.

The Cult’s Magus learned that the ship was secretly transporting a complement of incarcerated psykers to a holding facility elsewhere in the sector — to be later picked up by a Black Ship en route to Terra. The Magus needs the psykers to fuel their experiments towards forming the @UUID[.jt0zc7az5xNehcIZ#the-heralds-howl]{Herald’s Howl}. Their keeper, Ulena Cadavore (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.VWoY9PpvbDqQYv8X]{Black Ship Crewmember}), has been doing her best to keep her volatile cargo out of their hands, though most of her fellow guards are now dead. The psychic screams felt in the sector result from the incarcerated psykers' containment failing, tortured by the rapid Warp transitions and presence of the malignant Broodmind.

The remaining crew are protecting themselves in pockets all over the ship. Very few of them are left, having been picked off gradually by a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.KvLrPAQ0gmIWSvfX]{Purestrain Genestealer}. The Magus believes that the Genestealer will singlehandedly win their war of attrition, allowing them total control of the ship.

Outcome

If the characters can secure the Vice of Eternan and purge it of xenos taint, their Patron gains the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.oXyZ2hmINFVN3EPT]{Voidship} Boon and +1 Legitimacy. If the Vice escapes back to the Warp, rumours of it grow every year as it continues to haunt space within the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.UbH7oOtTYfjFlKRt]{Gallosque Nebula} — where it appears next could cause further disaster.

If Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Baek} deals with this Operation alone, she gains +1 Legitimacy but secretly extracts the psykers on board to further her experiments (initially unaware that some have received the ‘Genestealer’s Kiss’). She destroys The Vice of Eternan to cover her tracks, ultimately dooming anyone else aboard.

Conclave IV Conclusion

The fourth Conclave ends with the Inquisitors finding little satisfaction in their dealings. Of all those present, only Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud} seems pleased with how things have gone, rattling the cages of the other Inquisitors. Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Varol} departs early, his warnings of growing @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cult} activity in the sector ringing in the ears of all those present. Despite these misgivings, most agree to meet again

pages.name: Conclave V
pages.text:
Conclave V

Inquisitor Raud’s investigation into Eskender Thracius has led her to a terrible truth: there is a definitive traitor in the Conclave. Eskender Thracius, however, has one card yet to play that may cover his escape…

Dramatis Personae

In attendance at the fifth Conclave are: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Ksenia Baek}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Aegidius Halikarn}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud}, and Kai Varol (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius}). @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus}’ continued absence without communication has become a concern among the Inquisitors.

Intrigues

If characters or other operatives returned the daemonhost from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.wHl3ZP7wM7OQvSLC]{Jotungarth} to @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} (@UUID[.1EujWPAAI3xsXmIk#strife-iii-c-the-ghost-of-luna]{Strife III-C: The Ghost of Luna}, they learn it was subsequently claimed by @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} and moved to her chambers in Mare Cinis.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst} may confide in the characters that she finds @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud}’s handling of daemons deplorable; keeping them contained as daemonhosts only serves to anchor their corruption in realspace — a criticism she also held of her mentor, the late Inquisitor Lord Drake. She claims that members of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-malleus]{Ordo Malleus} often believe they have much firmer control over daemonkind than in reality. She encourages characters to inform her of any of Raud’s activities they learn of if daemonhosts are involved.

Characters may notice that @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Kai Varol} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} have gathered larger retinues than usual. Aside from the usual @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5rrnycKS5mMDjQJc]{Acolytes} in both retinues, Kai Varol’s forces include a trio of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5a6Q3NRdPonZjiGr]{Death Cult Assassins}, who appear armed with weapons that do not match any Imperial STC. Characters who have interacted with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari} technology (such as in @UUID[.qMGtMcmwPnXnwPds#strife-i-a-the-void-stalker]{Strife I-A: The Void Stalker}) may recognise similarities to the xenos design.

Strife V-A
Excommunicate Traitoris

The revelation of a traitor in the Conclave’s midst has everyone place their hands on their weapons. Tensions rise in the Conclave hall, putting a hold on further proceedings until the traitor can be dealt with.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} reveals to the Conclave the results of her investigation into @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius} — through interrogation, observation, and missions undergone by her spy network — she has learned that Thracius yet lives under one of numerous false identities, each maintained through extensive use of polymorphine.

She declares that his capture is vital. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud} lists the false identities @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius} operates under, ending with an accusation that Kai Varol is the most recent.

  • Kai Varol, or rather, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius}, reveals the truth of these allegations but argues that his loyalty to the Inquisition is absolute. In turn, he reveals that the @UUID[.jt0zc7az5xNehcIZ#the-heralds-howl]{Herald’s Howl} has captured @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus}, a situation he seeks to leverage (see @UUID[.HAzjoFV6pghpy0ou#strife-iv-b-the-lost-recongregator]{Strife V-B: An Inquisitor Compromised}.

  • The assembled Inquisitors call a vote on whether @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Thracius} is declared Excommunicate Traitoris or whether such decisions should be delayed until @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Konstan Serranus} is secured. The characters may discuss this vote with their Patron, and the players' choice should be reflected in the final decision).

Operation

With Alis Raud’s revelations out in the open and the Inquisitors present having picked a side, the fate of Eskender Thracius must be dealt with.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius} will not be taken without a struggle. If he is declared Excommunicate Traitoris, a battle erupts in the Conclave hall. Thracius makes a fighting retreat to his section of @UUID[.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} under covering fire from his @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5rrnycKS5mMDjQJc]{Acolytes}, armed with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari} weaponry. His quarters have been rigged with automated and servitor-controlled defences in anticipation of the day his cover is blown, including an emergency launch bay. From there, he escapes on a Valkyrie and commandeers an Imperial Fleet voidship in orbit around the moon. His acolytes are swiftly defeated following his departure, but the characters, the Inquisitors, and their retinues may have been badly wounded by the traps Thracius set.

If @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius} is left to continue as part of the Macharian Inquisition, the characters' Patron suggests uncovering the depths of Thracius’s heresy is a worthwhile goal. Their Patron seeks irrefutable leverage over the Radical Inquisitor, believing it is only a matter of time before Thracius must be taken down. In this, the characters pursue the clues below but know that Thracius is still lurking within the Macharian Inquisition, so they must tread carefully.
