Your Role defines the way you serve your Patron. It determines how you play the game and approach scenarios. You can choose a role from among the following or allow your Patron to choose one for you and gain 50 XP in return:

  • The Core Book Roles: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.5ewutQ9qVF8zhEGI]{Interlocutor}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.XAXnQluFkxD2gsmG]{Mystic}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.sHSbkzrtFfIdmrJl]{Penumbra}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.OS9fWy8dYBTURFLE]{Savant}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.KznGxzLZLr1QaCoN]{Warrior} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.TrSAGoKhRuNOwYhK]{Zealot}.

  • The new Inquisition focused Roles: @UUID[.2s0Vnxq4jh7ud6el]{Assassin}, @UUID[.j7wtNMhT96bMRSng]{Cruciator}, @UUID[.qrCcJTlOyVPGREXf]{Explicator} or @UUID[.0SrKKzUVDAcr3xL3]{Seeker}.

5) EQUIPMENT

Your character begins with equipment determined by your Origin, Faction, and Role. Note their effects and statistics appropriately on your character sheet, and add any other relevant bonuses. Basic @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y]{Equipement} can be sourced from Imperium Maledictum, and any Inquisition Specialist Equipment is highlighted in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.BbyZqcWs3HbrAO3Y]{The Inquisition Armoury}.

6) ADDING DETAIL

Name, physical appearance, distinguishing features, and age are all important parts of your character. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.PwG5oioCaLgyqLWX]{Imperium Maledictum} gives suggestions and tables to help select and inspire these details. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.dPY9cqcTEXjgtaA7]{Character Goals} are outlined in Imperium Maledictum, but there are more @UUID[.QrZJuogjiR8wb1eN#general-goals-intro]{Inquisition-focused options}. As an option, your Group may choose to give each character a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-tables.RollTable.9SLhM8FOgluaUwvO]{Random Talent} via the table in Imperium Maledictum.

7) BRINGING YOUR CHARACTER TO LIFE

Consider answering the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.jO0rmqIrT2EL3tyo#ten-questions]{Ten Questions} presented in Imperium Maledictum. Roll for your character’s @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.jO0rmqIrT2EL3tyo#divination]{Divination}. And consider their connections to other party members and their Patron, using the @UUID[.QrZJuogjiR8wb1eN#inquisition-connections]{Inquisition Connections} Table or the Core Book @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-tables.RollTable.r1enfoBH64ajVnBa]{Connections} Table.

8) FINISHING TOUCHES

Complete your character by calculating the following derived stats and final details:

  • Maximum Wounds: This is equal to your Strength Bonus (StrB) + (2 x Toughness Bonus (TghB)) + Willpower Bonus (WilB).

  • Critical Wounds: This equals your Toughness Bonus (TghB).

  • Initiative: This equals your Perception Bonus (PerB) + Agility Bonus (AgB).

  • Fate: Your character begins with 3 Fate.

  • Handedness: Choose your character’s dominant hand (left or right).

  • Further details on these stats can be found in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.jO0rmqIrT2EL3tyo#finishing-touches]{Imperium Maledictum}.

ADVANCEMENT

Each Advance in a Characteristic raises the Characteristic by 1. Unless stated otherwise, the Characteristics of a normal Human cannot rise above 60. Each Advance in a Skill increases the Skill by 5. You can have a maximum of four Advances in a Skill and four Advances in a Specialisation. Purchasing new Talents costs 100 XP each. Additionally, during character creation, your character may gain Talents or Advancements that they do not meet the requirements for. This is the only exception to the rule; whenever you purchase any other Advance or a Talent with XP, you must meet the listed requirements. For further detail on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.Dqrpb0F6t5gayyXE]{Advancement} see, Imperium Maledictum.

pages.name: Macharian Origins
pages.text:
The myriad worlds of the Macharian Sector give rise to an almost infinite number of circumstances and environments your character could be born to or experience in their early life. Your character’s Origin describes their formative years and impacts not just the Factions they are most likely to affiliate with and the type of world where they spent their youth, but other Characteristics relevant to their backstory and abilities. The Origins offered here provide possible starting points that denote your character having crossed paths with the Inquisition or its many enemies or highlight unique skills that make your character a worthwhile asset likely to be directly recruited by the Inquisition.

To determine your character’s Origin, choose either of the following options:

  • Roll 1d100 to determine your Origin randomly using the following @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.KGkYtn1T21Gdrl5e]{Inquisition Origins} Table or the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-tables.RollTable.nyaEnNOrR8Sq8Wf4]{Origin} Table in Imperium Maledictum, then gain 25 XP.

  • Choose an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.IOuNLIGWoHRDvHab]{Origin} from Imperium Maledictum and apply the bonuses.

  • Choose an Inquisition Origin and apply the bonuses. All Inquisition Origins have multiple choices within.

For customising your Origin further, note that any bonuses received typically add up to 100 XP. As always, the details and background of these Origins can be altered to better suit your character — though it is always best to discuss any changes with the GM.

@TableHTML[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.KGkYtn1T21Gdrl5e]{Origin}

pages.name: Faction
pages.text:
The Imperium Factions within the Macharian System represents a complex web of interconnected duties, functions, politics, and beliefs. While all Factions are ostensibly united in the ultimate goal of furthering the God-Emperor’s conquests and glory, there are many ways in which relationships between them do not always flow smoothly. You served one of these Factions, raised and trained for a specific Duty that you performed until your Patron plucked you from monotonous obscurity. Your Faction has deeply influenced who you are, what you know, and your beliefs about the world. As such, choosing a Faction for your character is pivotal in determining the kind of person they might be.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.ZJ4j0hrbxg7bL2K4]{Imperium Maledictum} contains detailed information about all of the Factions and a selection of Duties your character might have been trained to undertake as their endless service to the Imperium. In this book, information on these Factions focuses on how they perceive the Inquisition and how a member of the Faction might find themselves crossing paths with the Inquisition and ultimately being recruited as an acolyte. Some Factions have more harmonious ties to the Inquisition than others, such as the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum} or the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}. Others have more opportunities for friction with the Inquisition, such as @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.uhAdgxtMePoyNdnm]{Infractionists} or the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}. If your character was born to one of these non-Inquisition Factions, the following offer suggestions to build your initial feelings about the Inquisition and determine a backstory for how they came to be in an Inquisitor’s employ.

Additionally, the Inquisition Faction has been expanded to detail characters with a background in the Ordo Hereticus, Ordo Malleus, and Ordo Xenos for those who wish to begin their journey as experienced Inquisition acolytes. To determine your Faction, choose either of the following options:

  • Choose a Faction and gain its benefits.

  • Roll 1d100 to determine your Faction randomly and gain 75 XP.

Ignore any requirements for Talents and Skill Specialisations gained from your Faction.

@TableHTML[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.Pkm3KwRj2lxWDoK7]{Result}

Adeptus Administratum

The Administratum is the ever-grinding gears that move all things within the Imperium of Man. The unstoppable inertia of bureaucracy stills for no one, not even the hallowed duty of the Inquisition. Everything has its right place in the ledgers of the Administratum, and even the most powerful Inquisitor or acolyte is just another variable within a logic engine, just one of the many cogs the Administratum keeps churning into unknowable infinity. Of course, the Inquisition must frequently avail itself of the Administratum’s wealth of information, connections, and power but, despite the immense weight behind the Inquisitorial rosette, members of the Administratum do not generally assign any particular importance to their workings or needs. Procedure must be upheld lest the entire unwieldy system shudder to an inconvenient or disastrous halt. In the Noctis Aeterna’s tumultuous wake, the adepts of the Macharian Sector have all the more reason to focus inwards on the increasingly complex administrative tangles that continue to be uncovered or perhaps to look outwards in search of more direct methods to fill the gaping holes in their records and chains of communication.

Because Inquisitors often lack the time or inclination to deal with administrative tasks, hidden swathes of their retinue may be taken from the Administratum. An Administratum member who is more forthcoming than their peers is a valuable Inquisitorial asset for cutting through troublesome red tape. Such connections are courted frequently to varying degrees of success. The ciphers of the Administratum provide another point of interaction: the ability to deliver secured messages without the need to entrust them to the interpretation of an astropath or an interceptable transmission is a service some Inquisitors desire to avail themselves of. Conversely, a particularly zealous ordinate might find it expedient to make themselves useful to an Inquisitor’s retinue for greater access to the worlds of the Macharian Sector and the records held there within.

Adeptus Astra Telepathica

The sanctioned psykers and astropaths of the Adeptus Astra Telepathica have more reason than many to become intimate parts of the Inquisition’s workings. Raised in the use of their powers for service to the Imperium, some members of this Faction may even have personal connections to psychically-potent Inquisitors who once shared the training grounds and halls at the Scholastica. Sending messages across the gaping maw of space requires the focus and grit of one trained to send and receive. So, some Inquisitors will retain the services of only trusted astropaths to ensure their communications remain secure, with no interference from rivals or enemies. Similarly, psykers might frequently find themselves in the employ of the Inquisition, whether for their abilities to combat the entities of the Warp or their more intimate skills to touch the minds of accused heretics and unravel their sins.

By their very nature, members of the Adeptus Astra Telepathica stare deep into the maelstrom of Chaos every time they reach for their psychic powers, and this proximity can bring their purity into disrepute. For all that they may work more frequently with the Inquisition than many other Factions, they are without a strong reason to mistrust the presence or continued scrutiny of Inquisitors and their agents — or to seek out security within an Inquisitor’s employ. Some psykers and astropaths might be confident, without concern that they will be examined and found stained with intolerable Chaos, while others may find themselves nervous even if they have no concrete reason to fear.

Adeptus Mechanicus

Almost an empire unto their own, the Adeptus Mechanicus spares no love for the suspicious gaze of the Inquisition. Their power and insularity as the primary holders of arcane technological knowledge provide them with a degree of untouchability not often seen within the Imperium. The Inquisition is well aware that any attempt to accuse heresy or pry into secrets within the Faction overtly would be met with staunch opposition not even their considerable influence could easily match. Many situations lead the two Factions to cooperate, grudging and tense as such cooperation may be. Members of the Adeptus Mechanicus are irreplaceable sources of knowledge about heretical technology and understand the deep workings of machines that agents of the Inquisition can barely begin to comprehend, including the ability to parse lingua-technis. Inquisitors might find themselves striking relationships with Adeptus Mechanicus members for access to people and places that would otherwise be closed to them as outsiders or consulting frequently with an adept regarding particular technological heresies.

Core to the friction between the Adeptus Mechanicus and the Inquisition is the Faction’s worship of the Machine God, the Omnissiah. Outright conflict is avoided by the generally held belief that the Emperor of Mankind and the Omnissiah are one and the same. Still, wide ideological rifts exist even within the Macharian Sector. A member of the Adeptus Mechanicus may be loyal to belief in the Machine God and the Emperor, serving Inquisition agents without qualms. Others might cleave to more heretical underlying beliefs that the Machine God’s avatar they worship so dearly is not the entity upon the Golden Throne — and should tread carefully within an Inquisitorial retinue to avoid being branded as a heretic or grouped in with their more zealous peers.

Adeptus Ministorum

From the perspective of the Adeptus Ministorum, the Puritan conception of the Inquisition represents a righteous fist and fire, burning out all trace of heretical thought and deed wherever they lay their anointed hand. If the Ministorum seeds and nurtures fervent belief in the Imperial Cult, the Inquisition identifies and prunes out any rot or strangling vines that, left unfettered, would threaten the health of the entire system. As such, relations between the two Factions tend to be good, with their respective roles in the Emperor’s service cleanly definied. However, this is not always the case. The many interpretations of Imperial canon and the worldly political manoeuvring among the higher ranks create intrigues wherein acolytes and clergy might find their motives at odds.

The Ministorum plays a vital role in shepherding the populace in their adherence to the Imperial Cult and reporting any signs of psychic or genetic mutation. This occurrence seems all the more frequent in the Noctis Aeterna’s receding tide. This duty often results in Inquisitorial recognition and recruitment as an acolyte, as uncovering heresy and corruption is another way to serve the Emperor’s will. Clergy based in the holy halls of the Magna Basilica or any of the Macharian Sector’s other shrines and cathedrals can pluck at different threads, quietly observing the political murmurs and creative interpretations of doctrine that could interest the Inquisition. There are even circumstances wherein an Inquisitor might seek out a member of this Faction for their retinue to lend legitimacy and piety to the public image they intend to project or to keep acolytes on the straight and narrow path of purity. Some may also act as confessors and intermediaries with locals.

Astra Militarum

In the years since the upheaval of the Macharian Heresy, unseen wounds and echoes of distrust have festered in the connections between the Astra Militarum and the Inquisition within the Macharian Sector. Perhaps it is a self-fulfilling prophecy — a lack of trust and quickness to paranoia would eventually sour even a strong underlying relationship. Of late, the Astra Militarum withing the sector have been particularly committed to their home planets and systems, having fought and bled on home soil during the Noctis Aeterna. This connection breeds further distrust from the Inquisition, with some murmuring that the lack of movement to more pressing areas of galactic conflict edges upon defiance of the God-Emperor. Layered with questions of xenos exposure and almost imperceptible whispers of Sector Lord Aulus Sejanus eyeing another Crusade, many officers of the Astra Militarum are especially wary about dealings with the Inquisition, lest a wrong word or deed lead to unfortunate consequences.

Despite this, Faction members can find themselves employed by Inquisitors throughout the sector as they seek out the lingering poison of the Ruinous Powers. Those chosen are rarely the ‘average soldier’ but recruited for some particular trait the Inquisitor recognises: exemplary service, acts of valour, examples of combat prowess, or an unwavering faith. Even the means to follow orders to the letter is valuable, particularly the ability to kill without compunction. Lone survivors, witnesses to unique events, and those judged to be especially pious, or merely obstinately loyal, are all taken under the Inquisition’s crimson wing to continue proving their mettle. Many eventually earn the title of acolyte in their own right.

Imperial Fleet

The Noctis Aeterna took a terrible toll on the Navis Imperialis in the Macharian Sector, and those internal conflicts simmer still. Despite this, the voidships and their crews have, for the most part, taken full flight once more. Their role as naval support to the forces of the Astra Militarum draws regular scrutiny from the Inquisition — as their voidships undergo frequent exposure to the effects of the Immaterium, and the source of corruption therein.

Some Captains welcome an Inquisitor with open arms for their ability to root out the earliest suggestions of corruption within their crew. While the risk of being unjustly accused of the taint of the void goes hand-in-hand with Inquisitorial presence, the dangers of undetected corruption spreading throughout a ship are usually frightening enough to warrant cooperation

In the course of their missions, Inquisitors and their agents interact frequently with naval personnel. Inquisitors often recruit capable pilots from within the Fleet and permanently second them to their retinues to ensure that someone is always on hand to get their operatives where they need to be at a moment’s notice and provide support thereafter. Conversely, the Fleet crew might seek out the Inquisition to report suspicions of corruption amongst their crewmates or in the hopes of spiritual protection and succour from the ongoing horrors of the Warp.

Infractionist

The varied Human refuse that makes up the lowest rungs of Imperium society typically fall well below an Inquisitor’s concerns or interests. An Infractionist may not even be aware of the Inquisition beyond glaringly exaggerated tales told by those seeking to puff up their importance and aura of danger. That said, the underbelly of society tends to engage far more freely in the kinds of heretical deeds and notions that could act as a beacon to an Inquisitor on the hunt. Infractionists who have their wits about them are smart to fold quickly on other loyalties and pander to any Inquisitorial forces that cross their path. There are, of course, far more powerful forces which have rejected the strictures of society; the cartels of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#criminal-cartels]{Trackless Chain} or the criminal nobility of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#criminal-cartels]{Jau Clan} are well-organised and more than willing to play dangerous games with the Inquisition’s attention. They have innumerable tricks and routes for throwing any Inquisitorial investigation off the scent and have successfully maintained their illegal webs of trade and influence.

Infractionists are disposable, often easily deniable tools for any Inquisitor, but their usefulness cannot be denied. No one knows the labyrinthine workings of a criminal underworld better than those born into or raised within it. Better still is having someone at hand proven to do terrible things without hesitation or guilt. Infractionists who have run with the bigger fish of the Silent Trade or other criminal cartels of the system may have tangled with agents of the Inquisition in the past and been marked by them as a potential asset for some time.

Rogue Trader Dynasties

As highborn merchants with Warrants of Trade, they were granted immense freedom to explore uncharted territories, create trade routes, and treat with xenos. The Rogue Trader Dynasties command considerable power within the Macharian Sector. These ongoing forays into unknown space and interactions with all manner of dangerous xenos and trade goods mean that the Dynasties, depending on the direction of their loyalties and political interests, are often either allies and confidants of the Inquisition or avoidant suspects frequently under some manner of investigation. Rogue Traders across this spectrum ply their trade in the Macharian Sector.

From the immensely powerful @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#rogue-traders-of-note]{House Iaysus} and their sprawling control over expeditions into the unmapped wilds of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.MzIWAwZ8jPAOydDi]{Yix}, to the hard-up fortunes of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#rogue-traders-of-note]{Captain Ion Hawkscar}.

The motives and desires of the Rogue Trader Dynasties are as deep as they are broad, but an undercurrent of pride and a need to see their lineage names lauded run common between them. A Dynasty will always ask: how do these deeds further the crest of your house and the lore of your name? A Rogue Trader might fall in with the Inquisition out of ambition or fear, a desire to build animosity and ruin towards a rival house, or a hope that their own ventures will benefit from Inquisitorial cooperation.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.CDCRywl9EgXMoTdr]{Ordo Hereticus}

'You think you know heresy? You think the warnings of the Ministorum, the edicts screeched from habway Lex hailers encompass the whole bounds of the law, and that the heretic merely exists beyond these strictures? There are laws so natural, so innate, that no good citizen of the Imperium could comprehend what it is to break them. The Heretic is an unnatural thing, a beast as foul as any mutant or xenos. To slay them is a mercy to be delivered without sentiment, without hesitation, and without doubt.'

— Interrogator Caecilius Elbegdorj

The Ordo Hereticus works tirelessly to ensure the purity of faith within the Imperium, eradicating deviant beliefs, or practices. They ruthlessly hunt and eliminate heretics and cults undermining the Imperial Creed, scouring every corner of the Imperium. Under the guidance of your Inquisitor and their retinue, you will learn the ins and outs of the Imperium, the political machinations between Imperial Factions and Noble Houses, for often heretics hide and fester where they can inflict the most damage. You will infiltrate the highs and lows of Imperium society; to understand if anything beyond the Holy Emperor’s will drives them. You will come to know their weaknesses and what might lure them to corruption — only then can you protect their souls, often from themselves.

Despite the heights of secrecy within the Inquisition, the Ordo Hereticus is the most public-facing Holy Order, the closest to what the average citizen might envision as the Inquisition at large. When you are not undercover or covertly investigating a target, you will often work closely with other factions of the Imperium, particularly the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Ministorum}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum}, and the combined forces of the Adeptus @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}. In these dealings and with the citizenry, you must remember that you represent your Inquisitor first and foremost and the authority they bestow upon you. If you must utter their name, bring forth the weight of their authority with it; sowing fear and paranoia upholds the Inquisition’s notoriety and perpetuates its strength.

Inquisitors of the Ordo Hereticus appreciate an acolyte’s graft and cunning, studiousness to doctrine, diligence, and respect for rank. Due to the Ordo's perceived parallels with the Ministorum and Militarum, and those organisations’ need for rank to reflect authority, any ascension within the Inquisitor’s ranks may appear more official than other Ordos would bother with. Though, with some Inquisitors, you may receive only as little as a nod of recognition to know you have ascended closer to the rank of Interrogator.

Puritans within the Ordo Hereticus are often fastidious fanatics of doctrine and their mission’s exact definitions — to monitor the Imperium and its servants and purge the heretic wherever heresy is found, without mercy or remit. On the other hand, Radical Inquisitors know that working within the exact definitions of the Inquisitorial Mandate can cause more problems than it solves, especially needless loss of life. So they are more calculating and lax with these definitions. There may come a time when your Inquisitor asks you to act against the mission of the Holy Orders — to break Imperial Law or turn your gaze away — and it will be up to you to decide if defying them is worth risking the mission or your life.

Serving a Patron outside of the Inquisition, you must carry the weight of the Ordo Hereticus on your shoulders — do as these people say, but make sure they know that no one can ultimately control you, save your mission, your Inquisitor, or the God-Emperor Himself. In their naivety, they may view you solely as a tool to apply the Inquisition’s leverage on their behalf, to purge their enemies or requisition resources beyond their grasp. Serve them as you see fit, but do not forget to aim your scrutiny at them as well.

Ordo Hereticus Benefits

  • You gain +5 Perception and +5 to either Fellowship, Strength, or Willpower.

  • You have 5 Advances to spend on Awareness, Intuition, Logic, Melee, Rapport, and Presence.

  • You gain the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.iaPxPzO3we3oXSJk]{Ever Vigilant} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.dq7jeHrNvxZrnzI6]{Cult Infiltrator} Talent.

  • You gain +1 Influence with the Inquisition.

  • You gain a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.jNxvsLBybPPenmmn]{Laspistol} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.pmzwts3g5aosWnMr]{Shotpistol}, an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.sYDTAe3hDjoSD0Gb]{Armoured Bodyglove}, and 400 Solars.

  • You gain your choice of either a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.bRoqjRet8tuZzzTM]{Multikey}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.ZsmwbqSWpB1TGkx4]{Power Maul}, or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.uO5IZi3jF2NrIUqS]{Soulguilt Scanner}.

Duty

Rather than picking from the options in the Ordo Hereticus Faction Benefits box, you can choose one of the following Duties to quickly create your character. Additionally, you have +1 Influence with the Inquisition, the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.iaPxPzO3we3oXSJk]{Ever Vigilant} Talent, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.pmzwts3g5aosWnMr]{Shotpistol}, an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.sYDTAe3hDjoSD0Gb]{Armoured Bodyglove}, and 400 Solars. Seeking and hunting daemonic entities and influence requires the support of various duties. As a Hereticus acolyte, your background or particular skills could find you performing the following tasks:

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.upR0izJ77yCchw0b]{Deceptor}

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.XyolzzLXlNj8ubx5]{Militant}

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.ZjtoAVYHcBRBAh7H]{Querent}

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.xb6SwipCKT9Vrvjt]{Ordo Malleus}

‘Look upon this hammer I hold before me, it is far more than a weapon. It is a symbol of the Imperial Justice that smites the diabolic enemies of the Imperium. It is a symbol of my Holy Order and my office, of the authority granted to me by the God-Emperor and the great Inquisitor Raud. Obey me without question, or it will also symbolise your punishment.’

— Interrogator Damien Savantas

The Ordo Malleus is the righteous hammer of the God-Emperor, whose primary goal is to hunt and repel the daemonic forces of Chaos. Wherever the Ruinous Powers curl their dark fingers into the fabric of reality, the Ordo Malleus aim to seek it out and make a righteous stand. Acolytes of the Holy Order draw upon generations of forbidden knowledge to detect the most subtle evidence of Chaotic incursion, be it the constant spread of heretical cults and suspect beliefs or outright daemonic presence. The touch of the Warp is a dangerous necessity within the spacefaring life of the Imperium, making the risk of ruinous corruption amongst astropaths and psykers also ever-present. In the face of so many unseen angles of insidious attack, the Ordo Malleus ensures daemonic forces cannot gain the footholds they need to overwhelm all existence. Moreso than any other Inquisitorial group, the Ordo Malleus has cause to wipe out or imprison entire populations — daemons are too dire a threat, so insidious an enemy, that survivors and witnesses often cannot be trusted to exist.

Over time, Ordo Malleus Inquisitors inevitably educate their acolytes the secrets of daemons and the Warp — and how to tackle them best — as far as their teachings encompass. This enlightenment will be meted out to you gradually, so as not to overwhelm your mind and, at the same time, measure your trust. If the Ordo’s secrets ever fell into wrong and capable hands, they could cause system-wide panic or even be used against you and the Ordo. As such, you must apply the same knowledge and security to your fellow acolytes, and even your Inquisitor. Know that everyone is corruptible, even those who stand beside you.

In the field, it is not unusual for agents of Ordo Malleus Inquisitors to take on the livery of other Holy Orders to conceal the dark secrets of the Emperor’s hammer. Your very existence is a secret; your purpose is known only to yourself and those ranked above you — and you must work hard to maintain this level of secrecy.

You must stop at nothing to keep the existence of Warp entities a secret — and your remit extends to mindwiping and execution to do so. Use this work to prove yourself and your effectiveness. Only then will you be outfitted with the Ordo’s secret arsenal or permitted the knowledge to create them yourself.

To attain status among their retinue and clearance to learn the Ordo’s secrets, Ordo Malleus Inquisitors seek acolytes who are ultimately adaptable and capable of survival in the face of the unknown. Know that your life expectancy is calculably short when your duty is to seek out such constant evils.

Puritan Malleus Inquisitors will stick to the doctrine of the Order and expect the same as yourself — every trace of daemonic activity must be purged from sight and mind, in some cases even your own. Know that the Ordo Malleus consider ‘The Daemon Within’ just as significant a threat as the ‘Daemon Beyond’ — you may not know you are working for a Radical Inquisitor until it is too late, but it is expected you report them as soon as you do, lest you be branded for the same heresies.

Working for Patrons outside the Order, rumours of daemonic activity will have brought you to their service, whether this Patron is aware of it or not. You may have a cover identity or reason to be there that you must uphold at all costs.

Ordo MAlleus Benefits

  • You gain +5 Willpower and +5 to either Strength, Toughness, or Perception.

  • You have 5 Advances to spend on Awareness, Discipline, Fortitude, Intuition, Logic, and Presence.

  • You gain the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.iaPxPzO3we3oXSJk]{Ever Vigilant} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.sP53vAzNCZpgkqL5]{Unwavering Will} Talent.

  • You gain +1 Influence with the Inquisition.

  • You gain a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.GEtUumQVGsSNO7Kt]{Hand Flamer} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.jNxvsLBybPPenmmn]{Laspistol}, an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.sYDTAe3hDjoSD0Gb]{Armoured Bodyglove}, and 400 Solars.

  • You gain your choice of either an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.RJQOgOg4q8krADXi]{Instrument of Divination}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.ZsmwbqSWpB1TGkx4]{Power Maul}, or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.deHQEH976yh9nI9y]{Signal Jammer}.

Duty

Rather than picking from the options in the Ordo Malleus Faction Benefits box, you can choose one of the following Duties to quickly create your character. Additionally, you have +1 Influence with the Inquisition, the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.iaPxPzO3we3oXSJk]{Ever Vigilant} Talent, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.GEtUumQVGsSNO7Kt]{Hand Flamer}, an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.sYDTAe3hDjoSD0Gb]{Armoured Bodyglove}, and 400 Solars.

Seeking and hunting daemonic entities and influence requires the support of various duties. As a Malleus acolyte, your background or particular skills could find you performing the following tasks:

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.z058E7qKD4CHpvoA]{Admonitor}

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.fBy4m9db4vopQEcR]{Crusader}

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.eKp4XtJkKDvt42yA]{Sensor}

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.cY8QqkSqrdfk9Dyp]{Ordo Xenos}

‘Heed my warning, Acolyte. The Imperial Creed teaches us that xenos are foul and corruptive beings, and that is true. But as servants of the Inquisition, we must stand as examples of utmost purity and unwavering devotion. You will be punished for showing any shred of leniency. You will be cleansed for showing any notion of corruption. How do you think Inquisitor Serranus lost his arm? He did that to himself.

— Interrogator Arnaut Cisneros

The Ordo Xenos commits to the unenviable duty of combating the vile alien species that threaten the sovereignty and survival of Humanity. From the savage Orks to the inscrutable Aeldari, the relentless Tyranids to the enigmatic T’au, and the supposedly endless number of undiscovered species hidden across the galaxy, Ordo Xenos Inquisitors must confront each and every one, to neutralise any potential threats that seek to destabilise the Imperium.

Under the tutelage of an Ordo Xenos Inquisitor and their retinue, you will learn the biologies and known behaviours of the xenos cultures the Imperium has encountered so far, the codes and procedures for contact, and what goals drive their inhuman minds so that they can be efficiently destroyed or manipulated. Their contemptible technologies are just as much a threat as the xenos who built them and must be understood all the same — every misinterpreted artefact is a weapon until proven otherwise. Any newly discovered technology must be thoroughly catalogued and methods devised to dispose of it properly. Xenos tech that surpasses the Imperium’s capabilities is constructed by impure means and, even in concept alone, is a threat to Imperium doctrine and culture — it is your duty to shield the people from these terrible methods and ideas.

In the field, you will be sent all across the sector. Often to the farthest reaches of the Imperium, to planets and systems threatened by xenos invasion or pervasive influence. Voidships often serve Ordo Xenos Inquisitors best as mobile bases, allowing them greater freedom of movement among the galaxy’s farthest reaches. There you will encounter the fringes of Humanity — possibly as strange as the xenos you hunt; souls led astray from the Imperial creed. You must cut out the cancerous xenos presence before it spreads further, leading citizens back into the Emperor’s will.

But sometimes, you will be sent to investigate the heart of the sector; the xenos threat can reach any world by underhanded means. Among heretics, the thirst for xenos weapons and artefacts is insatiable, and groups such as the Rogue Trader Houses and Merchant Princes are continually finding ways to bypass regulations and import without oversight — infecting the imperium out of greed alone.

You will undoubtedly encounter ignorance and disbelief in your investigations — being privy to knowledge far beyond the remit of the average citizen or authority, few will understand the existence of a xenos threat, and fewer still have the clearance to know the entire truth — use your influence and authority to get what you need.

There are critical paths towards gaining your Inquisitor’s favour and reaching a position within their retinue. Generating a high kill count of xenos is a formidable position to start — whether applied by your hand or in the form of revolutionary methodology. Know that some of the Ordo Xenos’s most storied Inquisitors are behind the Imperium’s greatest cases of mass xenocide. Otherwise, seek to become the utmost expert in a singular xenos species and culture. Then you can ensure your Inquisitor will see you travelling the galaxy and applying your knowledge where they feel is best, perhaps even joining them in Conclave.

Puritan Patrons demand that you are unflinching in your duty, that you offer no quarter to those who consort with xenos nor traffic in their trappings. Radical Patrons, even those slightly astray, may be more flexible and understanding; they will ask you to exploit every opportunity, even if it means getting disgustingly close to the xenos at the heart of their investigation.

Working for a Patron outside your Ordo means contact with xenos is assured or highly suspected. You are there to be a specialist on behalf of the Inquisition — to bring all your knowledge and methodology to bear — but keep the secrets of the Ordo Xenos close to heart.

Ordo Xenos Benefits

  • You gain +5 Fellowship and +5 to either Toughness, Intelligence, or Perception.

  • You have 5 Advances to spend on Intuition, Linguistics, Logic, Lore, Rapport, and Tech.

  • You gain either the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.iaPxPzO3we3oXSJk]{Ever Vigilant} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.wlIRfeH728nwTPPT]{Logical Liar} Talent.

  • You gain +1 Influence with the Inquisition.

  • You gain a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.42seX9BCENS8ZCwg]{Hand Cannon} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.DEguAzj8uwUgVTs8]{Needle Pistol}, an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.sYDTAe3hDjoSD0Gb]{Armoured Bodyglove}, and 400 Solars.

  • You gain your choice of either an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.dO7XoDXD9QYTy6zZ]{Auspex}, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.Ao3ReFn4WBUSjSY2]{Bio-sample Extractor}, or a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.rgkUmSGkBrOKvo5p]{Pict Recorder}.

Duty

Rather than picking from the options in the Ordo Xenos Faction Benefits box, you can choose one of the following Duties to quickly create your character. Additionally, you have +1 Influence with the Inquisition, the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.iaPxPzO3we3oXSJk]{Ever Vigilant} Talent, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.DEguAzj8uwUgVTs8]{Needle Pistol}, an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.sYDTAe3hDjoSD0Gb]{Armoured Bodyglove}, and 400 Solars.

The duties of the Ordo Xenos are as diverse and complex as the myriad xenos species themselves. As a Xenos acolyte, your background or particular skills could find you performing the following tasks:

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.N8aC89bUnEc78hRE]{Analyticus}

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.UMXPdNRFRDLXnSBj]{Xenologist}

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.CB859tnMPuPPp7wz]{Xenolinguist}

pages.name: Role
pages.text: Your Role defines the purpose for which your Patron has chosen for you. Acolytes of the Inquistion may be assigned any @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.6ve8JEFE4WCFssip]{Role} from those available in Imperium Maledictum. But the Roles on the following pages are additional options for Inquisition acolytes; as per the rules in Imperium Maledictum, you can choose a Role and gain its benefits or allow your Patron to select your role and gain 50 XP.

pages.name: Assassin
pages.text:
‘May foul blood feed my blade this night.’

— Shahin Vane, Hereticus Acolyte

The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.ZJ63PWtcMbeiVhKF]{Assassin} is a dealer of righteous death, cutting down heretical voices and actions before they have a chance to take root. They thrive in the shadowy underbelly of society, infiltrating through the darkness to strike at corruption and cut out its fangs. The Assassin is equally adept at eliciting information as they are at delivering death, and the Inquisition makes frequent use of these dual-sided skills.

Inquisitors value Assassins for their discretion, focus, and duplicitous nature. While meting out mandated death lies at the heart of their role, an Inquisitor’s retinue benefits from their ability to traverse the sticky intricacies of intelligence gathering and provide invaluable data to any investigation. They are often well-versed at guiding others in infiltrating groups of concern. They may find that they spend far more time engaged in subterfuge and information brokering than they do feeding the edge of their blade. Nevertheless, the Inquisitor’s Assassin is always ready to move against the forces of Chaos and corruption.

Inquisitors draw Assassins from various backgrounds into their service. Some come from the Frateris Militia, chosen for their zeal and unwavering faith in the Emperor. Others might be plucked from the ranks of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.7E0Gkel1gSaxTgVu]{Schola Progenium} for their exceptional potential, where the Inquisition competes for prime candidates with the likes of the Officio Assassinorum. Some are proven warriors, enlisted @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ZIodTiyH9W5QBRU9]{Astra Militarum troopers} who have survived gruelling campaigns and have notable skills in surviving behind enemy lines. Any of these would make for mighty @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.fBy4m9db4vopQEcR]{Crusaders} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.upR0izJ77yCchw0b]{Deceptors} within their respective retinues. Those chosen for this role are vital acolytes for any Inquisitor. You must be a stalwart death dealer, standing as a perpetual threat by your Inquisitor’s side. You must enact brutal violence without question, be unwavering in your actions, yet be silent as the sharpest blade, and move through the herd like a wolf among the flock.

Role Benefits

Talents: Choose 2 Talents from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.yaLYVLB3Mani31Bw]{Deadeye}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.WTmX6OvD2dKAfLJ1]{Burglar}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.iaPxPzO3we3oXSJk]{Ever Vigilant}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.aGn9gv2Tk5ijUBsz]{Hit and Run}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.i115C2RujbQE5LUj]{Secret Identity}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.VaaAcbZNA26f8MUy]{Shadow Operative}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.FGtjHfixuOKtRWRA]{Skulker}, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.sP53vAzNCZpgkqL5]{Unwavering Will}.

Skill Advances: You have 3 Advances to spend on Awareness, Dexterity, Intuition, Logic, Reflexes, and Stealth.

Specialisations: You have 2 Advances to spend on any Specialisations in Awareness, Reflexes, and Stealth.

Equipment: You gain a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.items.Item.qQ8Y8nmiaTaKgzvs]{Knife} with a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.rD6BtFSjpfupZss1]{Mono-edge} Modification, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.kZh4o3SszYKFtzHE]{Great Weapon} or a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.tjUKnuDKTCCon28r]{Chainsword}, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.jNxvsLBybPPenmmn]{Laspistol} with an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.0aU07JBpNMjdUABI]{Omnispex} or an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.AfhkWSUYY9y6byiN]{Autopistol} with a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.LqQBByxsreNT3C09]{Silencer}, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.2XMWybp4AQqoEPtI]{Sniper Rifle} or a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.ysX4l2nIrfDY6wnm]{Long Las}, a set of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.items.Item.LmBKbPMN8CsK4B3T]{Heavy Leathers}, a set of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.7lBipnmSZ4lD5WCo]{Magnoculars}, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.O5AtUszQGDbi8qmS]{Survival Gear}.

pages.name: Cruciator
pages.text:
‘A doc’s hands can help or hurt, easy as anything. All comes down to who’s holding the leash.’

— Sliff, Trackless Chain Routerunner

The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.DuUfJmvyY53xYN2V]{Cruciator}, a chirurgeon skilled in the knowledge of the body and repairing injuries of the flesh, provides the invaluable service of managing all minor medicae issues and devastating injuries without needing to show vulnerability to unknown quantities. Many in this role are seen as cold and calculating, but to an Inquisitor, this is a prized quality; the colder the Cruciator’s demeanour, the better they are at fulfilling their duty without complication.

Cruciators are, however, far more than just adept healers. With all of the Inquisition’s staple dedication to wiping the Imperium clean of heretical corruption, Cruciators turn their steady hands to investigation, interrogation, and drawing out earnest repentance as readily as any acolyte. Their specific knowledge of the Human body (or xenos in rare subjects) increases their abilities in close combat and improves their chances at coaxing even the most recalcitrant of heretics into offering valuable information.

Inquisitors source their Cruciators from all corners of the Imperium. Some might have trained within the Priesthood of Mars as a Biologis, requisitioned for their knowledge of both man and machine. Others are drawn from traditional chirurgeon roles, such as the Orders Hospitaller, the Administratum’s Officio Medicae, or even the Astra Militarum, where their skills have been tempered by front-line duty. But beyond a team’s need for medicae support, a Cruciator can serve as a skilled @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.ZjtoAVYHcBRBAh7H]{Querent} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.UMXPdNRFRDLXnSBj]{Xenologist}, if they have the grit and detachment needed to get their hands dirty.

Those chosen for this role should have an insatiable thirst for knowledge. The compact you make with your Inquisitor affords you incredible carte blanche to explore the absolute limits of Human anatomy and design, far beyond the sanctioned learnings offered to most within the Imperium. That’s to say nothing of the mutants, xenos, and daemons you may otherwise encounter. What your Inquisitor expects in return is a trusted acolyte who can act as a versatile chirurgeon, interrogator, or even poisoner or researcher.

Role Benefits

Talents: Choose 2 Talents from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.2ZR3cok7UNA3LF4n]{Applied Anatomy}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.Wgi3zNI6egxLYydq]{Ballistic Forensics}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.k8C1ELU0BtmblnxW]{Bone Breaker}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.au8V1ieKIHkTeA8l]{Chirurgeon}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.rCRBALHdAqxNOtKg]{Field Medicae}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.F3sICRDFcUgn8ZI6]{Gut Instinct}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.CVhToUy8h6VUm5Uf]{Medicae Maverick}, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.SN2BNGF960QVHckL]{Phlebotomist}.

Skill Advances: You have 3 Advances to spend on Medicae, Logic, Dexterity, Discipline, Intuition, and Fortitude.

Specialisations: You have 2 Advances to spend on any Specialisations in Medicae, Dexterity, and Fortitude.

Equipment: You gain a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.qQ8Y8nmiaTaKgzvs]{Knife}, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.jNxvsLBybPPenmmn]{Laspistol} or a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.vCeI41URKYV6iuAD]{Stub Revolver}, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.tDe1U5EtxPowhYKn]{Web Pistol} or a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.GEtUumQVGsSNO7Kt]{Hand Flamer}, a set of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.D9X5jPYYafLyPqKh]{Robes or Light Leathers}, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.V9RLeedbeyoCIgOJ]{Respirator}, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.qjjlckQ3WvF4KLxO]{Chirurgeon's Kit} with 7 uses, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.Aw29y9tfO4Uc9uWb]{Chrono}, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.h1g1g9Rrjt7CnYeW]{Dataslate} or a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.rgkUmSGkBrOKvo5p]{Pict Recorder}, and a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.7ipsWHaVhIsF7b3S]{Writing Kit}.

pages.name: Explicator
pages.text:
‘It’s true that the stain of ruinous knowledge can weigh heavy on a woman, but upholding His word and law will always be its own reward.’

— Carrhe, Second Voice of the Silent

Information is one of the most dangerous weapons the Inquisition wields, and the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.7ueULcEt4hF8R4dr]{Explicator} is a meticulous purveyor of this resource in all its forms. They are versed in various forbidden subjects, seeking out the depths of heretical and daemonic rituals, tomes, and dissertations via dusty research or actively pursuing new lines of inquiry in the field. Venturing blind into any encounter against the Imperium’s enemies means almost certain death.

It is indispensable for Inquisitorial agents to have the ear of an ally with extensive knowledge of the Imperial laws, doctrines, and loopholes that intersect with seeking out heretical practices and influences. Their duty demands they cut through bureaucratic roadblocks to find the quickest path for Inquisitors to assert their limitless authority. The Explicator is no stuffy librarian; they are as well-versed in the arts of swift retribution as any acolyte in an Inquisitor’s retinue.

Explicators are primarily drawn from Imperial factions that curate massive amounts of data. The most exceptional adepts of the Adminstratum are chief among their kin — rescued from the obscurity of datavaults and given greater purpose. Depending on where they specialise, Explicators can make excellent @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.z058E7qKD4CHpvoA]{Admonitors}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.N8aC89bUnEc78hRE]{Analyticus}, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.CB859tnMPuPPp7wz]{Xenolinguists}. However, their function may rely upon how well they can withstand the heresies they face. They are effectively students of the Ruinous Powers and the vile xenos, but only in order to facilitate their elimination, disgusted and fascinated by their research in equal measure.

Those chosen for this role must have a nimble and highly analytical mind. As much as the Inquisition requires of its storied warriors, you must meet the same criteria as a wielder of law and information. Like the @UUID[.j7wtNMhT96bMRSng]{Cruciator}, you will have access to texts far beyond the average scribe’s remit — corruptive materials that have no place in the hands of any righteous citizen. But this you must endure to serve Emperor, Inquisitor, and Ordo, to unravel the sordid mysteries and secretive plots that heretics and cultists so pride themselves on.

Role Benefits

Talents: Choose 2 Talents from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.XNWp0dpd4iB4qhjD]{Artistic} (Literature), @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.kAwBXaop0MNMqqC1]{Apostle of the Lex}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.bPEos4SZ1xIiTF34]{Cypherist}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.sTF7rVvFTa2RE3Vc]{Data Delver}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.UsXorn8M9HGueTWQ]{Eidetic Memory}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.Lbm6mRMiqSGHq9GD]{Forbidden Knowledge}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.7ns8qphjf10f46Ut]{Gothic Gibberish}, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.xkeeVglZIZS85nfi]{Lawbringer}.

Skill Advances: You have 3 Advances to spend on Lore, Logic, Linguistics, Discipline, Intuition, and Fortitude.

Specialisations: You have 2 Advances to spend on any Specialisations in Lore, Linguistics, and Intuition.

Equipment: You gain a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.qQ8Y8nmiaTaKgzvs]{Knife}, an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.AfhkWSUYY9y6byiN]{Autopistol} or a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.vCeI41URKYV6iuAD]{Stub Revolver}, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.YKQFW45Eu7satkSX]{Monotask Servo-Skull} with a function of your choice, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.7ipsWHaVhIsF7b3S]{Writing Kit}, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.Aw29y9tfO4Uc9uWb]{Chrono}, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.h1g1g9Rrjt7CnYeW]{Dataslate}, and a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.rgkUmSGkBrOKvo5p]{Pict Recorder}.

pages.name: Seeker
pages.text:
‘One world. Nineteen days. A hundred damned souls absolved in death by my hand.’

— Confessor Tarn Laggarian

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.dkawZFfwGoaZJjjs]{Seekers} are the unrelenting hounds of the Inquisition: the judge, jury, and executioners of heretics and xenos alike. They are operatives used to hunting their targets behind enemy lines — whether they wield the Inquisition’s authority against them in battle or integrate themselves undercover to root enemies out from within. As much as they are expert hunters of their prey, they are also deft investigators, beating the streets to uncover clues and unravel mysteries — the Inquisition lacks for neither.

Seekers follow trails of corruption to where they are most promising, nose to the ground and teeth bared, courageous against the corruption they will face. They might be lone wolves on the hunt or leading a cell of other acolytes. In most cases, Seekers need to source local contacts and assets themselves to complete their mission successfully, to fill in skill gaps within their cell, or simply gain the advantage of superior knowledge against their foes.

Seekers are often procured from positions of minor authority within the Adeptus Terra. Many come from the ranks of the Adeptus Arbites, Macharian Vigilites, or Naval Security, where they now apply the same exacting authority against the Inquisition’s enemies. No strangers to venturing forth into the void, some Seekers who are experts in hunting psykers were once officers aboard the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Astra Telepathica’s} Black Ships. Those capable of dealing with xenos species may have held significant rank aboard a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.N3xtZGybYbWZlAhS]{Rogue Trader's} voidship. Regardless of origin, Seekers are favourable choices to fulfil the Duties of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.z058E7qKD4CHpvoA]{Admonitor}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.upR0izJ77yCchw0b]{Deceptor}, or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.eKp4XtJkKDvt42yA]{Sensor}.

Those chosen for this role must be exacting and authoritative individuals. Your Inquisitor will expect you to take charge of an investigation and wield their authority as your own, only turning to them in dire circumstances. It takes significant ambition to fill the role; you may even see yourself as an Inquisitor one day. If you prove yourself to them and, more importantly, survive, you may have a chance of taking the first step to becoming your Inquisitor’s Interrogator.

Role Benefits

Talents: Choose two Talents from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.tC0lOr9WiBBPYq1a]{Air of Authority}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.ntymdPZ2ZikZMQoe]{Attentive Assistant}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.yArd1QW5l5mDssVs]{Blunt Force Authority}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.TXMKTpI3FosIpc3O]{Condemn the Witch}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.L2PvRyivXFydM2Lb]{Dirty Fighting}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.iaPxPzO3we3oXSJk]{Ever Vigilant}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.F3sICRDFcUgn8ZI6]{Gut Instinct}, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.xkeeVglZIZS85nfi]{Lawbringer}.

Skill Advances: You have three Advances to spend on Awareness, Discipline, Fortitude, Logic, Navigation, and Presence.

Specialisations: You have two Advances to spend on any Specialisations in Fortitude, Navigation, and Presence.

Equipment: You gain a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.qQ8Y8nmiaTaKgzvs]{Knife}, any Mundane Melee Weapon or a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.tjUKnuDKTCCon28r]{Chainsword}, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.42seX9BCENS8ZCwg]{Hand Cannon} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.GEtUumQVGsSNO7Kt]{Hand Flamer}, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.NLKRLMgcYzandwsL]{Shotgun} (Pump Action), @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.7lBipnmSZ4lD5WCo]{Magnoculars}, a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.AdB3ZzAOrnREfdsv]{Multicompass} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.paXqMCUFqcpVEEBE]{Excruciator Kit}, an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.H4uLhQvXkGBmE79L]{Armoured Greatcoat}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.QEbKaRlz9eZV01ix]{Manacles}, a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.actors.Actor.O49jTi2TzoFQH5GT.Item.Yp1Fmiml09wxHj4h]{Vox Bead}, and a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.7ipsWHaVhIsF7b3S]{Writing Kit}.

pages.name: Final Steps
pages.text:
Your acolyte is almost ready for their first mission. Imperium Maledictum provides options for @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.PwG5oioCaLgyqLWX#name]{naming} your character, developing their @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.PwG5oioCaLgyqLWX#physical-appearance]{appearance}, and fleshing out their @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.uJURMn2glWHhjqJk.JournalEntryPage.dPY9cqcTEXjgtaA7]{motives and ideologies}. Finalising these elements will add the last layer of polish your character needs before it is ready for the table. Below, you will find possible goals and connections more befitting Inquisition characters. These details provide greater depth for your character, informing how they might behave in various scenarios and what decisions they will likely make when faced with difficult choices. They also allow you to build connective tissue between your character and other player characters, offering reasons that the eclectic individuals of your party might interact beyond the demands of a shared Patron. These tables should not be considered prescriptive or exhaustive; create your own connections and goals, or mix and match with the Imperium Maledictum suggestions as best suits your character and campaign.

Inquisition Connections

Connections are the shared histories and experiences that bind your party’s characters. We suggest you choose at least two connections — one to your Patron and another to a player character. You can roll on the following table and negotiate how the connection could make sense with your fellow player/s and add any characterful flourishes. If you wish, you can create your own connections tailored to your character and the campaign your group will be playing.

  • Choose a Faction and gain its benefits.

  • Roll 1d100 to determine your Faction randomly and gain 75 XP.

Ignore any requirements for Talents and Skill Specialisations gained from your Faction.

@TableHTML[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.914z5GE5RvLYOOuh]{Connection}

General Goals Intro

Goals give your character things to strive for and motives to act. Before you select your character’s goals, consider their @UUID[.EvU32m4F3PbGoXdm]{Origin}, @UUID[.oWdbzXo6SveXsQj4]{Faction}, @UUID[.dqu1TgiucNzckzZh]{Role}, beliefs, and any other pertinent details about them to assist in determining the most fitting options. Regardless of how your character would feel about their goals, you should choose concepts you will find fun to play. Your character’s goals are up to you. Still, it’s recommended to discuss them with your GM and perhaps the other players in your group to check that they will align with everyone’s overarching ideas for the campaign.

@TableHTML[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.9P5BUgw6Ft6CfwSr]{Short-Term Goal}

@TableHTML[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.05oiuzgCKwQaGisp]{Long-Term Goal}

pages.name: Sector Threats
pages.text:
The Emperor’s realm is glorious in its expanse and power, united in faith, maintained by the might of its armies and the blood shed by its devoted servants. Wherever the Emperor’s gaze falls, the Imperium is renewed, scoured clean of any tarnish and made afresh in His image. And yet, there are places where the Emperor’s sight cannot reach, warrens of darkness and despair where heresy festers, the loyal suffer, and the vile go unpunished for the crimes. This is as true of the Macharian Sector as it is of any region of the galaxy, and so is the work of the Inquisition set before them — to venture into the darkness and bring with them the Emperor’s cleansing light.

What follows is a selection of Threats to the Macharian Sector worthy of the Inquisition’s wrath. These may serve as useful inclusions for an ongoing adventure or the makings of an entire campaign by themselves. See @UUID[.mgChhx2XpCIhnlea#using-threats-in-your-game]{Using Threats in Your Game} for further advice on using Threats in your game.

Each Threat featured in this chapter presents the following information:

  • Introduction: Covering the Threat’s general backstory, where they might operate in the sector, and most importantly, what they seek to achieve

  • Resources: The powers, influence or forces the Threat has on hand to achieve their goals

  • Methods: The typical means of how they go about achieving their goals

  • Secrets: The secrets that could unravel the Threat’s plans, what could give the players the upper hand in combatting them

Stat-blocks related to each threat are included with their entry, in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.sNyhdSHdHgyUGSgi]{Appendix}, or found in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ]{Bestiary}. Each Threat’s area of operations has been designed to be flexible, so you may move them to wherever you wish to suit your campaign simply by changing the named locations mentioned throughout their text.

Threats by Ordo Target

Heretics

  • @UUID[.bH6ISJRLFkjEbAbY]{Company of the Twisted Sickle}

  • @UUID[.tQvTUutwXMK3Zk5X]{Momas The Murmurer}

  • @UUID[.LLNdJjFAzuDL7L18]{The Storm's Eye}

  • @UUID[.AsvUSCAPODzDNPr6]{Xandro Cosmar & Ankhet}

Daemons

  • @UUID[.kdhuaL9owtI5TFBu]{Gaazrek Weavemaster}

  • @UUID[.XvrTcOyogUXcVtrJ]{Mizrax Tallian, The Herald of Blood}

  • @UUID[.imrbNdJygrtuAgOn]{The Reaper}

  • @UUID[.1hyky8C6K82pcqyp]{Valastra of the Endless Whisper}

Xenos

  • @UUID[.yMEATJaARscPkpVC]{Nar'itor's Kinband}

  • @UUID[.zRZ5A4EkqM6TDzwu]{The Pilgrim's Path}

  • @UUID[.L0bBCDgiHtNXyliH]{Tôk's Firestorm Kindred}

  • @UUID[.fpfmfnvSQlN2YHNh]{Varon Vipersong}

Using Threats in Your Game

You may use these Threats in several ways. Each is flexible enough to serve as the primary antagonist for a campaign arc, or may be used as an effective thorn in the party’s side to be purged once greater threats have been addressed. If you wish, you may simply find the stat-blocks useful game aids and craft Threats of your own, tailored to your party's interests and goals.

It is best to begin seeding rumours of these Threats into your ongoing adventures prior to their actual apperance, building their presence in the background. These rumours could be mentioned by the characters' @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.2TukBjlkS5RG5Qka.JournalEntryPage.cRcDNREGRQvZvuPl]{Contacts} or seeded during their downtime as background chatter. The Inquisition receives requests for aid and investigation from every corner of the Imperium, and rumours of these Threats may appear as part of this near-endless stream of data, attached to intelligence reports or merely mentioned in passing by other acolytes. Regardless, it will always be more satisfying for players to encounter a threat that has been seeded to some degree before they ultimately appear. This will also help to make your campaign feel smoother and more well-connected.

When the time is right, you may reveal the Threat as directly as you wish. They may emerge as part of another adventure, a threat that complicates the primary investigation. Alternatively, the characters’ Patron may simply assign their acolytes to deal with the Threat. Threats can be used as a simple and direct setup for one-shot investigations, the next step in a more extensive planned campaign, or as exciting fuel for a Patron’s @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.aKUb1Ces1eXXDUo3]{Sidereal Quests} Liability.

On a grander scale, you can weave any Threat into the fabric of your campaign. They could act as a Patron’s or characters' nemesis, showing up in person at crucial turning points to throw a spanner in the works — a literal option for a Patron’s @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.Rg69Ap4KU3SM8jHK]{Nemesis} Liability. Consider why they might have crossed paths with the characters' Patron in the past and what enmity lies between them. Wait for the worst possible time for them to interfere in the Patron’s or characters' plans.

Campaign Planning

If you wish to deploy a Threat as the driving force of an entire campaign, this will require some extra work to set up. In this case, consider the following:

  • Do not introduce the Threat right away. Plant clues and create a thread for the characters to pull on, relating to one of the threat’s aspects. Lead them towards an inciting incident to cement the Threat as their enemy.

  • Ensure the Threat has plenty of ways to evade the characters' capture or avoid confrontation until the campaign’s finale — while ensuring the Threat has a consistent presence. This is a delicate balance to achieve. Consider using aspects of the Threat’s organisation (significant minions or lieutenants under their command) to confront the characters instead, or find spaces where they can interact with the Threat on even ground, where no direct conflict can occur.

  • Do not reveal the Threat’s true intentions until the campaign’s midpoint. Instead, allow the characters to pull on threads and discover it for themselves. Pace it out.

  • Consider what other forces (including other Threats) may cross the characters' path or what other situations could complicate matters for them, especially related to whatever setting they find themselves in.

Non-Inquisition Patrons

By no means are these Threats Inquisition-exclusive, though it might take an Inquisitor’s resources to root them out and defeat them. Characters bound to Patrons of other Factions can stumble upon these Threats in their own adventures, becoming a problem they might have to deal with without initial Inquisition support. If you need an Inquisitor (or characters from their retinue) to aid your Patron or characters in combatting the Threat, there is a roster of sample Patrons in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.GgyUuP4mmxygpyOG]{ Roleplaying Inquisitors} to choose from.

pages.name: Company of the Twisted Sickle
pages.text:
Company of the Twisted Sickle

As you consume, you transform into its reflection.

Threat Overview

  • The Company of the Twisted Sickle is a Traitor Guard regiment in league with Nurgle cultists who occupy sectors on the agri world of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok}.

  • They purport to believe they are liberating the planet’s labourers from the Imperium’s oppressive machinations.

  • Their ambition is simple: continue to spread across Goros Pok and exploit the Imperium’s supply chains to infect other worlds

An @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} company, the 203rd Quannus-V regiment, were dispatched to quell an insurrection on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok}. The company had to depend upon local resources to function during the occupation. Their quartermasters requisitioned supplies from local farms and manufactorums to ensure the troopers remained well-fed and ready for action. A hidden Nurgle cult saw an opportunity and intercepted the supplies, contaminating them before they reached the company, allowing them to spread their blight among the newly arrived troopers.

The resulting pox spread quickly among their ranks, culling their numbers substantially, leaving the work of pacifying @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok} to other units. The regiment’s field chirurgeons were helpless, their @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.kous2Ot3MNPfthuo]{diagnostors} unable to offer any useful information on infection, which saw stinking red welts erupt from skin of the face and arms, rendering strong soldiers helpless in a matter of hours. The 203rd were quarantined to prevent the spread of the disease and a supply of broad-spectrum medicae tonics was requested from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.59y8WFXTbwKRwiRI]{Voll}, though there seemed little hope of aid arriving soon enough to be useful. As a final insult, the regiment’s command elements evacuated just hours before the order to quarantine arrived.

Despairing and abandoned, the soldiers of the 203rd expected little more than to suffer and die having never sighted the enemy, until cultists of the Twisted Sickle arrived with offers of another path.

To the suffering soldiery they made a simple proposal — abandon their loyalty to the Emperor, who had so clearly abandoned them, and instead choose to serve a god who could offer them something tangible — relief from their suffering. Had not the illness been so grevious and their suffering so great, doubtless the soldiers would have refused. As it was, many loyalists rose from their deathbed, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.8tlu4X5Qpzl98Uye]{lasguns} in hand, to make a final stand, but they were too few and too ill to resist.

The surviving soldiers swore themselves to the Plague God, and though the pox remained, their suffering ended. Indeed, it seems that the fetid welts became a source of strength, a mark of their god’s favour. Where once stood an entire regiment, only a company’s worth of soldiers remained, but they were remade, and the Company of the Twisted Sickle was born. They discarded their Imperial iconography, drawing new marks onto their uniforms — three black sickles arranged to form a triangle, for it seems a pleasing symbol for their new master.

The Company’s ranks have since swelled, new recruits drawn from other regiments or recruited directly from the planet’s populace. Together, they have undertaken numerous missions to corrupt the planet’s harvests and storage facilities, spreading the same pox that made them what they are. They have spread Nurgle’s contagion to several outposts and destabilised critical agricultural and processing facilities. Now, the Company seeks to expand, securing more of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok} and spreading like a virus across the entire sector.

Resources

After shifting their loyalties, the traitors’ first actions were to seize what arms and armoured assets they could before local authorities recognised their change in allegiance. They now sit on a sizeable stockpile of standard @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} equipment, everything from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.8tlu4X5Qpzl98Uye]{lasguns} to ground vehicles.

In addition, many of the Company’s support elements have become @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.GM0SvY5IcLmeiJ6a]{Poxwalkers}. These contaminated individuals follow the main ranks like a swarm of flies, creating more of their ilk from those who survive the Company’s assaults. Fully trained members of the Company have only undergone this transformation after suffering egregious wounds in combat — a final ‘reward’ for those of proven loyalty.

Methods

As the Company of the Twisted Sickle spreads across @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok}, they have dispatched a handful of squads of traitorous soldiers aboard vessels purportedly carrying agricultural exports. They use the guise of guards assigned to the shipments to infiltrate new worlds and contaminate food and water stockpiles with Nurgle’s plague. The troopers only confront local powers once contamination has taken hold of some of the populace, adding these people to their ranks with the promise of relief. So far, they have met with only isolated greater success, but they have established minor footholds on at least a half dozen worlds. Should they meet with greater success, their next step is often to take over supply depots to arm their new recruits and lead assaults on fortified targets with waves of new @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.GM0SvY5IcLmeiJ6a]{Poxwalkers.}

Among the megafarms on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok} taken over by the host of plagues and poxes unleashed by Nurgle's servants are a small clade of corrupted @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Administratum Adepts} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.CsFqLJu3uHM45otd]{Arbitrators}. The Twisted Sickle rely upon them to set up the export orders and manifests they need to secretly spread their plague across the sector. Under the thumb of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.lpytiuTAh3y4JhNv]{Traitor Enforcers}, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.j3u29w8o6uvvQe0Y]{Traitor Guardsmen} they work round the clock and are always under watch, holed up in a seized @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adminstratum} field office.

Secrets

Though few members suspect it possible, a daemon known as @UUID[.imrbNdJygrtuAgOn]{'The Reaper'} was instrumental in swaying the Company’s loyalty. This daemon has directly blessed the Twisted Sickle’s ranking officers, but few recognise or remember their interactions with it.

Some survivors of the original 203rd Quannus-V regiment still exist on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok}, having evaded capture by the traitors.
