Most still bear the mark of the pox, deep scars where the welts appeared upon their skin. They lie in wait among the populace and desperately seek to contact the Inquisition. Making contact with these troopers would be instrumental in dismantling the Company.

GM Advice

The Company of the Twisted Sickle are a good match for a party that enjoys combat, as the mix of armed soldiers, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.GM0SvY5IcLmeiJ6a]{Poxwalkers}, and a potential daemonic encounter will provide plenty of action. Their presence on Goros Pok will be relatively easy to reveal — they are widespread and, though successful so far, not well-trained infiltrators. The assistance of a Chamber Militant is almost certainly called for, but most Patrons will be at least somewhat reluctant to unleash a war upon one of the sector’s most vital agri worlds. They will expect their acolytes to assess the geographical spread of the threat, identify any enemy strongholds, and eliminate key enemy figureheads in an effort to constrain the scale of the conflict.

pages.name: Gaazrek Weavemaster
pages.text:
Gaazrek Weavemaster

Of course I can provide the training and knowledge you seek, but what can you provide me in return?

Threat Overview

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek Weavemaster} is a Tzeentchian daemon.

  • Through the Immaterium, it seeks out rogue psykers, typically novices, and barters with them to increase their powers and teach them new abilities.

  • It seeks to raise an army of supremely powerful psykers and begin a campaign to unite all Psykers in the sector under their rule — join them or die.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek Weavemaster} has tempted emergent psykers and trained them in the ways of the Dark Gods for thousands of years. The first whispers of its existence appear in Inquisitorial records around M37, but the daemon professes to be genuinely ancient. It proclaims to its students that it watched primordial Humanity emerge from caves on ancient Terra to begin worship of barbaric gods, Gaazrek among them. Its words ring true, but lies are like water to daemons, flowing freely down the surest path.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} is believed to have interacted with Humans in the Macharian Sector for generations, during which time it revealed forbidden truths of the Warp to hundreds of rogue psykers. Many of them were later found by the League of Black Ships, while a few acquired followers and became the centre of substantial Chaos cults. Some remain active today, and the Inquisition has encountered at least three in the past. In all cases, the cults were purged, but the similarity in practices and references to the Weavemaster showed a common connection between all, despite the long centuries and vast distances that separated them. Thus the existence of the daemon was inferred as much as it was discovered, and no agent of the Inquisition has yet encountered the entity directly

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} marks its students with a stylised icon, a symbol of a nine-eyed spider resting on its web. It is a tattoo-like marking that grows in prominence as the cultist earns its master’s favour, often moving painfully across the cultist’s skin to avoid detection.

Gaazrek reaches out to promising psykers at a moment of weakness, just as they fear losing control of their powers. The daemon helps them to regain this control, using its presence in the Immaterium to quash the swelling Warp energies, a practice which earns it few allies among its cursed kin.

The psyker, however, is usually grateful beyond words, and so does @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} first ingratiate itself to its chosen pupils.

To provide further instruction, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} lures the psyker to a natural cave or similar secluded, dark space, and directs them to light a fire fuelled, in part, by various arcane substances. In the shadows cast on the cave wall by this flickering flame, Gaazrek appears and offers further instruction. At first, this is freely given, but soon enough the daemon makes demands, encouraging the promising psyker to give over their tightly held secrets. Gaazrek uses this information to manipulate them and spur their studies towards more dangerous subjects.

Over the millennia, some especially savvy students have tried to use this strategy against @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} — many seek the daemon’s true name in order to control it. Gaazrek knows well what they are trying to achieve and may tell them the true name of a rival daemon in place of its own. This usually results in either a deadly lesson or a daemonic rival being bound to a mortal’s will, much to Gaazrek’s pleasure.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} ultimately expects those under its tutelage to spread the worship of Tzeentch — offered by means of Gaazrek itself — and presses its apprentices to find promising new adepts, either as backups or practical future sacrifices. These new apprentices are sometimes sent on dangerous missions to acquire forbidden knowledge locked away by the Adeptus Terra. This act is a common rite of initiation and a means to test the limits of their soul and sanity. The daemon presses its will into them, manifesting this task as a hunger or maddening obsession, ensuring they will do anything to complete their task. Few of these unfortunate souls return, but those that do bring with them useful and dangerous lore.

Resources

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} can draw upon other daemons of Tzeentch to undertake tasks and support its students when needed. On rare occasions, Tzeentchian daemons (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.Boq9jjqKp2eDcVe8]{Blue Horrors} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.jPEYTvQIqOBwHU6q]{Brimstone Horrors}, have been ushered into realspace to support rogue psykers against Imperial authorities. However, their mischief and viciousness often test the psyker they have been sent to aid, even if they do aid in achieving victory.

Gaazrek is a daemon of Tzeentch, obsessed with knowledge and sorcery. Its followers benefit from this sorcerous acumen and are often possessed of forbidden knowledge and powerful psychic abilities. These are powerful tools that can be used against characters who do not have access to countermeasures, such as a blank.

Methods

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} haunts the places where the barrier with the Immaterium is thinnest and has ensured dark rituals have created such spaces in the secluded caves it prefers. In these places, it can help emergent psykers recognise their potential, taking credit for every new success, preferring to let its apprentices grow in power rather than merely ravage the minds of a vulnerable psyker as many other daemons do. The daemon avoids sanctioned psykers, thinking them more inflexible, indoctrinated, and rigid. As an exception to this rule, they keep an eye on pyskers who work with the Inquisition, particularly Radical Inquisitors, who inevitably become corrupted to the point of malleability. Though it has yet to find success, Gaazrek would like nothing more than to corrupt an Inquisitorial agent.

Among those it instructs, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} searches for mortals bearing true potential, hoping to elevate nine — a favoured number of Tzeentch — to be his personal apprentices. To these, it teaches the method of summoning a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.fHzYwLoDQ2KoLVWQ]{Disc of Tzeentch}. This is both a great honour and a final test, for these are daemonic beasts in their own right and brook no meagre masters. Those apprentices who fail to fully bind the Disc to their will are ultimately devoured by it. It may be some time before Gaazrek has assembled a cabal of nine psykers, but it cares little for how many die in the effort.

Secrets

The daemon has connections with rogue psykers hidden in numerous positions of power. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek }has trained these people to keep their abilities hidden until called upon or implemented so subtly to avoid detection. Its agents could be anywhere, though more likely within institutions outside the Adeptus Terra.

‘@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek Weavemaster}’ is a false name fabricated to appease the mortals they deal with, as knowing a daemon’s true name gives one great power over it. However, Gaazrek is not quite so clever as it believes, and long ago one of its pupils won the name. Gaazrek ultimately fed the unfortunate psyker to a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.fHzYwLoDQ2KoLVWQ]{Disc of Tzeentch}, but not before a record was made. The name now lies written upon a cave wall hidden in a remote region of a death world. Were it ever found, Gaazrek would be truly undone.

pages.name: Mizrax Tallian, The Herald of Blood
pages.text:
Mizrax Tallian, The Herald of Blood

The skies are full of Ork roks, and the trenches already full of the dead and dying. Blood flows freely in the habways. You never lived before this day, Sergeant, so why now fear death? There is a better way…

Threat Overview

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7RBUr5GqvTTAfxfc]{Mizrax Tallian} is a mortal servant of Khorne.

  • He is drawn to places on the eve of terrible battles, somehow able to sense the bloodshed to come.

  • He fosters Khornate blood cults among the soldiery, bolstering their martial prowess for the battle to come in exchange for allegiance to the Skull Throne.

Among many regiments of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum}, there are rumours of a figure known to appear on the eve of battle, a warrior whose threadbare robes hide crimson armour, and who bears an axe of gleaming brass. Some claim he is one of the Emperor’s own sons, who comes to bolster His righteous warriors before a great battle. Others say he is an omen of doom, a portent of the endless slaughter to come, and death to any who lay eyes upon him.

In truth, he is @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7RBUr5GqvTTAfxfc]{Mizrax Tallian}, a warrior and an orator, a swearer of dread oaths and a tool of Khorne, Lord of Slaughter. Mizrax is an anomaly, for he is often subtle in his ways and unpredictable in his appearances. This is a far cry from most servants of Khorne, who typically favour direct assault over every other approach, and who revile trickery in all its forms. Mizrax is no stranger to slaughter, and his axe has claimed a respectable number of skulls for his master, but his strength lies elsewhere.

Mizrax has a sense for impending conflict that borders on the peternatural. He knows when bloodshed is coming, and precisely where he should be to expand and inflame it. In the weeks before a mighty battle, Mizrax will appear, arriving by means known only to himself. He will then find a means to ensconce himself among the soldiers to take part in the coming battle, taking on whatever guise is best to do so. He may appear as a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Ministorum} preacher, a minor officer just recently transferred, or a simple mercenary offering his services to those in need of them.

Once he is firmly entrenched, he will begin to spread the worship of Khorne, at first organising training bouts between soldiers, then assuaging the fear that naturally arises in the days before combat by instilling a lust for battle and bloodshed that most naive commanders see as quite commendable.

Once battle is joined, the truth often reveals itself — those who have given themselves over to @UUID[.XvrTcOyogUXcVtrJ]{Mizrax}’s teachings are mighty warriors, but they know neither restraint nor temperance in their pursuit of blood. Orders are ignored, allies are ruthlessly overrun, and every chance at a tactical advantage or strategic gain is ignored in favour of endless slaughter. His duty done, Mizrax inevitably disappears, on his way to the next battleground. Among those few of his proteges who survive, a nascent blood cult forms, often subsuming whole regiments in worship of the Blood God. Thus has he earned the title, Herald of Blood.

Mizrax’s very existence is a question that has riven Inquisitorial Conclaves, and indeed any discussion of him seems to lead to disagreement and often violent conflict. Though sightings would suggest he is a mortal man, his presence has been recorded at battles as far back as the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-macharian-heresy]{Macharian Heresy} itself, suggesting he is centuries old. Many Inquisitors have claimed to have slain @UUID[.XvrTcOyogUXcVtrJ]{Mizrax}, only for him to appear once more on the eve of a great battle, years later and a dozen worlds away. Some suggest that his identity may be a title rather than that of a single individual, while others think him a daemon rather than a mortal servant of the Ruinous Powers.

Resources

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7RBUr5GqvTTAfxfc]{Mizrax} arrives on worlds bearing little more than an axe and a thirst for bloodshed, but he quickly builds a band of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.dPJKFex2tEKcZevv]{devoted followers}. He is unusually charismatic and considered for a follower of the Blood God, able to talk his way out of difficult questions as to his identity, drawing the fearful and the violent to him with ease. Any who would confront Mizrax should do so quickly, for otherwise they may quickly find themselves facing a well-armed, capable group of warriors. He is also unusually skilled at finding his way to the site of a coming battle, slipping into voidships unseen or stowing away amidst ordinary soldiers on their way to the fight.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7RBUr5GqvTTAfxfc]{Mizrax} undoubtedly has the favour of Khorne and is a fine warrior by any mortal standard. More unusual is his gift for sowing strife and discord among his enemies — any discussion of Mizrax quickly descends into disagreement. Some within the Inquisition have guessed at this dark gift, but it is naturally difficult to discuss it in any reasonable way. Only blanks or powerfully gifted psykers are immune to this effect, and characters discussing Mizrax should make a Challenging (+0) Discipline (Composure) Test to avoid finding everything being said about him by others to be intensely disagreeable.

Methods

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7RBUr5GqvTTAfxfc]{Mizrax} moves often, travelling from battlefield to battlefield, sowing the word of Khorne among common soldiers wherever he can. He usually begins by offering useful training and advice — he is a skilful warrior and well-versed in combat — and reassurance to the fearful. He preaches of the glory of combat, the joy of overcoming one's foes, and the simple purity of slaughter in the name of… Well, Mizrax rarely lies, but he does allow people to draw their own conclusions from his words. Many take him for a particularly devout and militant follower of the Imperial Creed, and this is a guise he has worn often.

Once he has established a loyal band of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.dPJKFex2tEKcZevv]{followers} among the rank-and-file, Mizrax will begin to turn his attention to the officer corp, targetting those with the authority to change battlefield plans. He encourages close engagement and brutal melee over all else, and artillery crews will often find themselves reassigned to front-line combat, aircraft will be grounded, and all other considerations ignored within the corrupted officer's zone area of responsibility. Though Mizrax’s influence has surely won some battles, it has doubtless lost a great many wars.

Secrets

@UUID[.XvrTcOyogUXcVtrJ]{Mizrax }is indeed a mortal man, one whose life has been inexplicably prolonged during his service to Khorne. In fact, he was once an advisor to General @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#machariuss-generals]{Borgan Crassus}, and commander of the 26th regiment of the Harakoni Warhawks. On Adrantis V, during brutal attritional warfare, Mizrax proved his valour over and over again, leaving a wake of victories — and bodies — behind him. When morale appeared to falter, it was Mizrax who bolstered it, speaking of the glory of war and the mighty victory that they would inevitably win once the planet was liberated. When, appalled at the losses suffered during the Adrantis Campaign, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW]{Lord Solar Macharius} ordered the world all but shattered by a diverted comet, Mizrax was left a broken man. Every sacrifice, every victory, every death was rendered meaningless by unthinking megatons of ice and rock. Into his broken soul poured the fury and bloodlust of Khorne. Of all of Crassus’ closest advisors, only Mizrax turned traitor during the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-macharian-heresy]{Macharian Heresy} that followed Macharius’ death. Facing death, Mizrax chose to serve his new-found master in other ways and has been doing so ever since.

Though all this occurred centuries ago, there remains something of that honourable soldier in Mizrax’s heart. If the Herald of Blood could be reminded of this, though it would not change his dedication to Khorne, it may well cause him to falter just long enough to land a killing blow.

pages.name: Nar'itor's Kinband
pages.text:
Nar'itor's Kinband

We fought for their Greater Good, saw the benefit, and saw the cost. Now we are stuck here, surrounded by malignance and darkness. The only good left is for us to survive and return home, whatever the cost.

Threat Overview

  • Nar’itor’s Kinband are a group of Kroot stranded in the Macharian Sector.

  • They are luring voidships into traps, ambushing them, killing everyone on board, and salvaging what tech and supplies they can.

  • Their goal is to survive and repair their warsphere. Then, leave the Macharian Sector behind for good and return to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tau-empire]{T’au Empire} space.

Note: The kinband’s crash site can be tucked away on a frontier or feral world, but could just as easily be hiding within debris fields and wreckage belts in a place like @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.rwTMhBwRA6wCOgIA]{Arrian’s Wrath} or the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.MzIWAwZ8jPAOydDi]{Sargassum Reaches}.

In the Macharian Sector’s salvage fields, strewn with destroyed voidships and orbiting junk, prospectors and salvage crews are disappearing. The culprits are a substantial kinband of Kroot from a crashed warsphere known as the Rawk Klikaw. Led by the flesh shaper @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor}, the kinband is stealing salvage, spare parts, and supplies from those they lure and ambush before disappearing quickly into the wilds, leaving none alive to tell the tale.

After being struck down by @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari} pirates while scouting the Macharian Sector, they aim to survive and get the Rawk Klikaw void-worthy again. But the pace of their repairs has been slow, their supplies are dwindling every day, and the kinband continues to take heavy losses. Each raid costs them more warriors, who were already thinned dramatically by the crash of the warsphere.

The longer they linger, the more likely they are to be discovered. Recently, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-hereticus]{Ordo Hereticus} acolytes were investigating the area, looking for an escaped rogue psyker. Both fell afoul of the kinband and were consumed, their voidships stripped for parts and scuttled, left as hulks waiting to lure the next group of investigators.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor} is cunning, like most shapers. He will not press his luck and attack a much larger force than he has prepared to face. Nor will he give away the location of the crashed warsphere and the rest of the kinband if he can help it.

His losses are weighing on him, though, and with each new raid, he carefully weighs their options. He prefers to outnumber his enemies two to one at a minimum; he will not throw away precious Kroot lives for an obvious lost cause.

But he would push the kinband further if the opportunity arose to harvest parts from a Warp travel-capable voidship. He knows that if he can salvage from such a vessel instead of the shuttles and other smaller craft they regularly trap, the chances of finding what they need to complete the repairs to the Rawk Klikaw go up dramatically.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor} is also not beyond talking to achieve what he needs. He prefers to be the first to strike in any conflict, but if someone attempts to engage him in dialogue, he will take a moment to listen. He is not above doing mercenary work for Imperial assets if it means avoiding punishment for the damage the kinband has already done and the parts they need fix to their warsphere.

Resources

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor's} kinband are down to a few dozen @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0Sws6uyhkY2nx4Go]{Kroot Carnivores} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.8EOYNULRU7nA8acm]{Kroot Mercenaries}. He is the last remaining flesh shaper among them. They have plenty of salvaged weapons, their own Kroot weaponry, and nearly three scores of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.15cqsEnrFd3vBoSA]{Kroot Hounds}. Their ship can be powered up, though it generally remains dormant so that it is not detected. Within the crashed ship, the decks are a mishmash of Kroot construction, with Imperial machinery used to repair the superstructure and most vital systems. Though there is no guarantee the two technological systems can be made compatible, Kroot philosophy encourages taking the strength of others and making it one's own. They have a pair of salvaged shuttles they use to travel to nearby areas and hunting grounds.

Besides the weapons they carry, the kinband has gathered a lot of useless salvage. They aim to barter it, especially for more materials to fix the warsphere. Initiating a bargain with them will be difficult for any characters since the kinband’s first reaction will be to try and eat them. A Silent Trader has made this work, but they have no exclusive deal. While the trader is only interested in xenos tech, the kinband has quite a stockpile of Imperial tech in which they have very little interest.

Methods

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor's} plan has worked well so far, so the kinband sees little need to deviate from it. The kinband attacks vessels that arrive to salvage the existing debris. They consume the crew, salvage what they can, and then use the new wreckage to draw in others to try and attack them. Sometimes they set off a distress signal to ensure another ship arrives but are sure to leave only the most recent signal running.

SHAPED WARBAND

Members of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor}’s Kinband have consumed the flesh of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.RsIGQ61VYTusa8TR]{Imperial citizens} and some @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari}. They have gained the following modification:

Hypersensitive Quills: The Kroot have consumed hyper-aware creatures, allowing them to detect movements within Medium Range with Advantage and potentially reveal hidden creatures.

Secrets

A Silent Trader is feeding @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor} information on happenings in the system in return for scraps of xenotech the kinband has salvaged. The trader refuses to provide them direct aid to fix the warsphere. If the warsphere is repaired, the kinband will leave the system for good, which does the trader no good. However, the trader is weak-willed, and if Inquisitorial agents press them, giving up the kinband’s location may be their best leverage.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor} is concerned about some of the modifications a few of his band have started to exhibit. It is subtle, but he fears that some of the flesh they have consumed is beginning to lead their strand toward an evolutionary dead end. The last thing he wants is for them is to finally be freed, only to discover he has guided the kinband into extinction.

pages.name: Momas The Murmurer
pages.text:
Momas the Murmurer

You can hand me that parcel, or I can reach into your mind and make the hands holding the parcel my own. Either way, I leave here with what I want.

Threat Overview

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.iuJElT9PKfrFYQTp]{Momas the Murmurer} is a mysterious psychic entity that coerces and influences individuals throughout the sector for its own mysterious ends.

  • In truth, this psychic monster is a rogue psyker named Balen Kho, his powers amplified by a powerful machine built during the Macharian Heresy.

  • Kho’s will is no longer entirely his own, and for reasons he no longer fully understands, he seeks to build a network of influence across the sector, shuttling odd components and construction materials to the world on which the machine is based.

Note: The Emanation Engine’s underground facility can be located on any relatively populated world in the Macharian Sector. The Inquisitor, Kho’s nemesis, could be any operating in the Macharian Sector or the characters' Patron.

For decades now, a whispered fear has passed among citizens on worlds across the Macharian Sector — that of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.iuJElT9PKfrFYQTp]{Momas the Murmurer}. Though details vary, the rumours concern an entity that can possess anyone anywhere at any time, commandeering their bodies like puppets before vacating without a trace. None are sure of its exact nature — or if it is anything more than a myth. Some believe the Murmurer to be a xenos bent on disrupting the sector. Others suspect it may be the work of a heretic cult with access to an astropathic choir. Those aware of the Empyrean fear it could be a daemon reaching across the veil to meddle in realspace.

The Murmurer is — at least in part — a rogue pysker, a Human telepath named Balen Kho. Though powerful in his own right, Kho’s powers are amplified and extended through his link to a device called the Emanation Engine, located deep below the surface of a forge world. Xenarite Tech-Priests, now all long dead, built this machine in league with a Radical @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-hereticus]{Ordo Hereticus} Inquisitor during the Macharian Crusade, using blasphemous technology and forbidden lore. Its original intent was to amplify a psyker’s powers, allowing them to spy upon the Imperium’s populace from a great distance without traditional surveillance devices.

Ultimately, the Emanation Engine exceeded expectations, allowing psykers to not only extend their psyniscience throughout the sector, but also project their powers and potentially @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.FlK5TFyjJNmgnExw]{dominate} the minds they sought to observe. In a rare moment of insight, the Xenarites recognised their creation was too dangerous, especially in the hands of a Radical Inquisitor. They clashed with the Inquisitor’s forces and ultimately succeeded, leaving the Emanation Engine abandoned and buried deep below the planet’s crust.

Kho discovered the machine, he believes, quite by accident. Little more than a manufactorum overseer troubled by occasional flashes of psychic insight, one particularly vivid vision led him through the deep tunnels beneath the forge world. He seemed to already know the path, the long-forgotten binharic access codes for bulkhead doors coming unbidden to his lips. Deep below the planet’s crust, Kho found an empty seat amidst conduits thrumming with energy. Drawn by his visions, Kho stepped within and opened his mind to the arcane machine. It amplified his powers immensely, allowing him from that moment to reach across interstellar distances to tamper with minds throughout the sector.

The power the device granted Kho was intoxicating. He began by taking petty revenge on those who had troubled him — a strict supervisor, a rival overseer, a wayward friend — but was quickly intoxicated by the power he now held. It was not absolute — strong minds could still resist him, other psykers could sense his presence, and he could hold only the weakest minds in thrall for any substantial length of time — but nevertheless, he has become extremely formidable. His ambitions have grown, and indeed are no longer entirely his own.

The strange phenomena of unusual behaviour and periods of amnesia — all signs of Kho’s possession of an individual — have given rise to the myth of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.iuJElT9PKfrFYQTp]{Momas the Murmurer}, due to the mutterings his victims are prone to. These soft utterances are Kho’s own thoughts, bleeding through to his victim's mind. Oddly, if listened to carefully, the words spoken are almost entirely pleas for help — or death.

Resources

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.iuJElT9PKfrFYQTp]{The Murmurer} has manipulated the Macharian Sector for decades, building a vast network of informants, minions, and accomplices. Though this power base has no formal structure, virtually every faction and organisation within the sector has at least a few members at various levels working for the Murmurer. Even without his psychic panoply, the Murmurer’s vast reach and access allow him and his representatives to use conventional motivators like bribes, blackmail, and threats to compel people into serving the cause. Through this network, the Murmurer can access virtually any resource or information. Should the need arise, the Murmurer can possess any of these agents at any time, their minds made especially pliant by careful psychic preparations.

Methods

Though @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.iuJElT9PKfrFYQTp]{the Murmurer} wields incredible power, his will remains singular and can only direct his attention to one subject at a time. He is in no way omnipotent. He focuses on overseeing crucial activities, leaving the day-to-day operations of his shadow empire to his subordinates.

When dealing with situations directly, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.iuJElT9PKfrFYQTp]{the Murmurer} operates almost exclusively through dominated proxies, hijacking their bodies to physically interact, abandoning them once they no longer serve his purposes. Enamoured with the Murmurer persona’s ephemeral nature, Kho loves to boast. He taunts witnesses through his proxies, informing them they have been graced by his presence, reminding them that anyone they meet could be him, sometimes dominating a series of bystanders to speak a single sentence just to prove the point.

Secrets

If one were to ask Kho his motivations, he would struggle to explain them. Sometimes, he believes he is seeking revenge, at other times, he is protecting himself or improving the Imperium in some way. All that is certain is that he is gathering power and influence for some purpose, his proxies occupying roles across the sector.

In fact, Kho’s own will was long ago subsumed by the machine itself. Not unlike his dominated victims, Kho’s personality is now little more than a mask worn by the machine. The Xenarite Tech-Priests who built it made extensive use of xenos technology salvaged from a dead and airless world graced by crumbling ruins and little else, in orbit around a star whose heat was spent long ago. In doing so, they awoke an alien will within the machine. This entity has but one purpose — to return to the blessed silence it once knew, and it is using Kho to achieve this goal.

Slowly but surely, it has used Kho's resources to expand its form. Even now, on the forge world above, labourers build devices based on schematics no Human mind could conceive of, connecting them to the Emanation Engine below, thinking all their work is approved by the Forge Lord, for indeed he has at times graced their presence and said as much — even if he does not recall doing so. If the device is finished, it will allow Kho to reach into every mind in the sector at once and, though he will not understand why he wishes to do so, snuff them out.

Within the Engine, much of Kho has long rotted away, as the machine had little need for anything other than his mind. From time to time, Kho will consider leaving the machine, only to find the thought unaccountably uncomfortable. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.iuJElT9PKfrFYQTp]{The Murmurer} requires Kho’s psychic ability to function, and until it is done with him, he will not be allowed to die.

pages.name: The Pilgrim's Path
pages.text:
The Pilgrim's PAth

The stars are distant and lost, but we must walk the paths to them and spread our blessings. For the day will come when the stars awake, and then they will come to us.

Threat Overview

  • The Pilgrim’s Path is a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cult} operating on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Macharia}.

  • Their Patriarch senses that the greater Hive Mind is yet distant, and so their focus has been on spreading to other worlds.

  • The cult uses its influence to infect pilgrims on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Macharia} who have arrived from other worlds. Some ships leave bearing @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.fZRrr5DJMuUoveZe]{Acolyte Hybrids} among the faithful, while others carry whole clutches of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.KvLrPAQ0gmIWSvfX]{Purestrain Genestealers} hidden within their hulls.

The shrine world of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Macharia} is a beautiful jewel of the faithful in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Donia Magna} system. Far from prying eyes, a blasphemous secret profanes this sacred world. The most zealous and stalwart members of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum} fail to recognise the unholy cult that hides within the shrine’s depths.

The Pilgrim's Path is a small @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cult} brought to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Macharia} by infected pilgrims from a world now long since claimed by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Tyranid} Hive Fleet. The pilgrims established themselves among the faithful of Macharia, never straying far from the most important places of worship. They target pilgrims who, often caught up in the rapture of walking the holy ground of Macharia, are unobservant to the danger. Dragged off and infected by the Genestealer’s Kiss, these unfortunates are left with the powerful urge to return to their place of birth to spread the curse, often cutting their pilgrimage short to do so.

There, they settle back into their lives and begin the horrific cycle of infection anew. Often these nascent cults are undirected, but by the fourth generation, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.KvLrPAQ0gmIWSvfX]{Purestrain Genestealers} are born to hybrid parents and, if no other has arrived, one will undergo the biological processes required for it to arise to the status of Patriarch. Once the cult has grown in strength, the true work of preparing the world for the arrival of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Tyranid} Hive Fleet can begin in earnest.

This too would have been the fate of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Macharia}, but either by a quirk of the Patriarch of the Pilgrim’s Path, or through the cunning intelligence of the greater hive mind, this has not been so. The cult here has kept a low profile, and benefited greatly from the world’s status as a nexus of faith for the sector’s many pilgrims. Many who seek to follow in the footsteps of the Macharian Crusade begin their long pilgrimage here, while others merely to see where @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW]{Saint Macharius} began his long and storied career in the Emperor’s service. Regardless of the reasons, all provide a suitable vector for the cult to spread its xenos taint.

Resources

Though modest by the standard of some infestations, the cult’s members are as dedicated as any other, and perhaps more practised in the art of subtle sabotage and infiltration than most. The cult’s Biophagus, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.ZVtbub70IiLYQm8u]{Gantus Black}, is especially well-practised in evading the Imperium’s methods of detecting his brothers and sisters. He provides outgoing ‘pilgrims’ with various tinctures and elixirs that confound the biological auguries that are sometimes employed to screen populations for xenos taint by those who know to look for such things, chiefly the Inquisition and certain Magi Biologis of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus}.

Though the cult has fewer resources than most, they are not without the means to destroy any threats to their nest. Hidden beneath the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Shrine of Macharius Ascendant} is a warren of tunnels which grew out of a Ministorum Arch-Deacon’s tomb centuries prior. These bunkers are home to hundreds of the Pilgrim's Path’s sons and daughters, with those no longer able to pass among the common masses confined to the lowest levels, and those not so blessed occupying the upper levels. All are willing to die for the cult, armed mainly with flamers procured from the faithful seeking a blessing before departing on crusade.

Methods

The cult’s plots move slowly, spreading their taint to other worlds by means of pilgrims. This might come to the Inquisition’s attention in a number of ways — a pattern of emergent cults might arise from a single infested pilgrimage departing @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Macharia} for other worlds, or evidence of the cult might be found in Macharia itself. Should the Path's increased ability to escape detection by means of the cult’s biochemicals be discovered, perhaps during a routine inspection of a pilgrim’s belongings, this will quickly be identified as a novel threat worthy of the Inquisition’s attention. It is already difficult enough to detect a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cult} — the ability to defy even those few techniques known to exist would be a worrying development.

If the cult were discovered, it may well attempt to escape @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Macharia} rather than make a pointless stand. They maintain a number of reliable members within Macharia’s voidport for just this reason, on standby to smuggle even the cult’s Patriarch aboard a voidship should the need arise.

Secrets

The very presence of a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tyranids]{Genestealer Cult} on Macharia is the Path’s most carefully guarded secret, with the location and techniques of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.ZVtbub70IiLYQm8u]{Biophagus}’ laboratory a close second. This facility would be a worthy prize for any Inquisition acolyte to acquire intact, for in finding ways to masque the presence of the Genestealer’s curse within the blood of a victim, Gantus was forced to profile several of the prominent biomarkers of infection. In the hands of a sufficiently skilled Tech-Priest, those markers not already known to the Inquisition could be revealed, allowing new ways to detect the curse in a population.

pages.name: The Reaper
pages.text:
The Reaper

We reap the harvest eternal, because we sow Grandfather’s blessings wherever we go

Threat Overview

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.OgCSwwJiQkk3X60B]{The Reaper} is a daemon of Nurgle.

  • It has cultivated a sizeable cult on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok}, who have direct access to some of the world’s food production and supply lines.

  • Once it has spread Nurgle’s plague across @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok}, it wishes to turn the planet into a daemon world, one that can serve as a base for infecting all others.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok} had a serious storage problem. As the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#silence-and-darkness]{Noctis Aeterna} disrupted the sector, vessels failed to pick up the agricultural tithes from the world, causing many stockpiles to spoil. Critical planetary resources were refocused on increasing the planet’s storage capacity. Labourers from many backgrounds were tasked with converting existing facilities or constructing new structures for agricultural storage. Much of this work was completed with little direction or oversight, as the local @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} institutions were stretched thin.

These workers struggled with their tasks, and some lost their lives. Few knew the basics of construction, but all of them saw first-hand the overflowing warehouses and silos. Nevertheless, new harvests from around the planet continued to arrive. Escorting one was a worker named Willem Argaunt, a newly awakened psyker who went undetected in the absence of the Black Ships. His mind reached into the Immaterium, praying for aid and searching for the God-Emperor’s light. But Willem drew the attention of a darker power than he could have intended.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.OgCSwwJiQkk3X60B]{The Reaper} heard his cries for help and was all too eager to assist. Using the latent psyker as a conduit, it crossed the thinning barrier, manifesting for just long enough to bear some of its master’s blessings onto @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok}. For seven days and seven nights, Nurgle’s blessings were spread far and wide by an unnatural, pustulent rain, tainting the grain stores of half a continent. Any who ate even a morsel had their hunger sated but, in doing so, opened themselves to Nurgle's fetid touch, and was corrupted. Many died, sowing the ground with their rotting corpses, or rose again as Poxwalkers. Those who persisted were granted the Mark of Nurgle, sanctifying them as cultists of a more significant cause.

What @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} forces could be marshalled during the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#silence-and-darkness]{Noctis Aeterna} responded quickly to what was happening around the new storage facilities; word of rampant death and decay spread fast to their commanders. But even as they arrived, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.OgCSwwJiQkk3X60B]{the Reaper} marshalled Nurgle’s forces. Using its new mortal agents, it corrupted the first regiments, forming the @UUID[.bH6ISJRLFkjEbAbY]{Company of the Twisted Sickle}.

Where the Company of the Twisted Sickle are focused on securing @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok} and reaching out to other systems, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.OgCSwwJiQkk3X60B]{the Reaper}’s remaining cultists work to keep its plague-ridden manufactorums and mega-farms going. Especially Silo Facility 77, where the Reaper first manifested; its cultists see this as a holy site, ground-zero for their work to turn Goros Pok into a daemon world. Any who die among its followers (and any corpses they can get their hands on) are planted there to join the rot.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.OgCSwwJiQkk3X60B]{The Reaper}’s weapon of choice is a large sickle, and it always manifests with it in hand. In accordance with an ancient myth on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok} depicting the Emperor as the ultimate harvester of any crop, the daemon was given the moniker of the Reaper.

For the Reapers followers, use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.GM0SvY5IcLmeiJ6a]{Poxwalker} stat-block and entries from the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.KN6hJOFxExaZ7fYL]{Heretics} section of Imperium Maledictum.

Resources

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.OgCSwwJiQkk3X60B]{The Reaper} has a growing network of followers on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok}. Many of these are active agricultural workers who spread Nurgle’s contamination in all the food they prepare. However, the cult’s membership includes some positions of planetary authority, including a burgeoning company of traitors to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.lpytiuTAh3y4JhNv]{Traitor Enforcers} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.j3u29w8o6uvvQe0Y]{Traitor Guardsman}).

Other nurglite entities have begun to interact with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.OgCSwwJiQkk3X60B]{the Reaper}’s followers. Most of these are @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.GM0SvY5IcLmeiJ6a]{Poxwalkers}, who constantly make more of their kind in conflict. In addition, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.pGOi4dyYeKojE9vm]{Nurglings}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vvgA1lyNkcTDw1xP]{rogue psykers}, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.4bhFOh1nTrYloc8s]{Plaguebearers} have been identified as hostiles during the ongoing insurrection

Methods

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.OgCSwwJiQkk3X60B]{The Reaper} is primarily focused on spreading corruption through greed and gluttony, driven by sickening hunger. Its prime targets are storage facilities on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok} — furthering the spread of his pox and dealing crippling blows to the Imperium supply chains. Getting a shipment of contaminated materials off-world allows its cultists to establish a foothold at the destination.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.pGOi4dyYeKojE9vm]{Nurglings} are commonly @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.OgCSwwJiQkk3X60B]{the Reaper}’s preliminary agents in these activities. Cultists can blend in effectively among Human populations, but Nurglings can sneak through gaps far too small for mortals. They readily infest food storage or water purification facilities and spawn more of their feculent kin before the facility’s security agents become aware of the intrusion.

Secrets

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.OgCSwwJiQkk3X60B]{The Reaper} has cultists at critical positions within @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok’s} port authorities. Evidence suggests that outgoing supplies are not being inspected in a way consistent with standard @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} doctrines. If correct, the entire port system may already be compromised.

The Sect of the @UUID[.bH6ISJRLFkjEbAbY]{Twisted Sickle} has other competition on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok}, who have begun to notice its prominence. The Harrower-In-Green and the Season’s Turn are cults representing the other Chaos Gods, and they all want a piece of the planet for themselves. Some have seeded cultists into the Sect of the Twisted Sickle to see how far their plans have progressed.

pages.name: The Storm's Eye
pages.text:
The Storm's Eye

Come to your rightful place in the eye of the storm. Watch as your old masters and oppressors are caught in the roil!

Threat Overview

  • The Storm’s Eye is a cult that secretly worships Tzeentch.

  • They have wandering cells working across the system, led by a central dark commune of powerful but cautious fanatics.

  • They seek to open a Warp rift to engulf the entire system in the name of the Changes of the Ways.

Note: The Storm’s Eye can be placed in any planetary system you require.

People drawn to the Storm’s Eye are led to believe they are joining a splinter cult of the Imperial Creed. Their leadership proclaims they will raise hard-working Imperial citizens and offer the downtrodden a place to fit in, work hard, and recognise their accomplishments. Simultaneously, they claim to shelter citizens from an impending doom — a resurgence of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#silence-and-darkness]{Noctis Aeterna} they claim will happen in the coming years. Their fearmongering easily attracts the lowborn, downtrodden of society. Before their recruits know what is happening, they unwittingly participate in darker and darker rituals. This same act also works on bored nobles and curious intellectuals, anyone who thinks they could do a better job than those in power of running society. They quickly fall sway to the whispers of the Storm’s Eye and their promises of more.

Each cell is compartmentalised, aware that others exist, but not where or how many. Above the cells sit the dark commune, the cult’s leadership, who weave their machinations through cyphered vox traffic and intermediaries. Once a cell has been thoroughly indoctrinated and has accepted Tzeentch as its true master, the cell is splintered as its members go about starting up a new cell, spreading the winds of change and proclaiming safety within the Storm’s Eye. As such, a cell rarely stays in one place for long.

Taliana Gaulista currently leads the dark commune. She recently took over and is still working on figuring out how best to step into the shoes of her predecessor. She is pragmatic and cautious, though not above instigating larger-scale operations than what the cult is used to. The very storm they preach of is one of their own design; they plan to unleash a Warp rift to engulf the system, giving it over to the Lord of Change.

They aim to do so by spreading throughout the system, embedding a cell into as many centres of population as possible. They believe that a synchronised psychic ritual — one they have been experimenting with for centuries — to call forth as many daemons as possible will break realspace and create a system-spanning Warp rift, affecting the actual change upon the system they desperately seek.

STORM’S EYE STAT-BLOCKS

All the following stat-blocks can be found in Imperium Maledictum. Some among them, particularly high-ranking members and leaders, carry the Mark of Tzeentch.

  • Use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ppicZvgr0bEuhWeh]{Cultist} stat-block to represent average Storm’s Eye members.

  • Each cell has around a dozen @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.utelXH1DahFI5iHt]{Accursed Cultists}, with a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vvgA1lyNkcTDw1xP]{Rogue Psyker} or two among them.

  • Use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.pGE97yqMKNMkyzgL]{Cult Leader} stat-block to represent Taliana Gaulista.

  • Use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.7GvkaaVAd69ORno0]{Chaos Spawn} stat-block to represent Getharius Malicain.

Resources

The cult’s primary resource is its reach and capability to hide. It has cells hidden in every aspect of Imperial society, from groups of dilettantes in hive spires to organised dregs working in the system’s manufactorums. They have loyal members among voidship crews and local merchants who see that the cult remains agile. Among the local Adeptus Terra is a cell within the local @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Ministorum} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} that doctor papers and strikes the cult's existence from public record.

However, their disconnected cell structure means getting these assets to bear against a particular problem would take time and effort. A full-scale mobilisation of the entire Storm’s Eye is possible, but it would mean exposing the cult's leadership and every cell in it to reprisal. The dark commune would only order this if they are directly threatened or think they can enact the final stages of their centuries-long plan to open the Warp rift.

Methods

The Storm’s Eye is interested in subtle changes and spreading its influence slowly over time. They favour exploiting any societal weakness they can find. They foment sedition, insurrection, anarchy, criminal activity, and rebellion wherever they find it. Generally, they like to get others to do their work for them. Why fight @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.CsFqLJu3uHM45otd]{Arbites} when you can get a gang war started that will pull the Arbites into conflict? Why get involved in noble politics if you can instead set them against each other with a careful reveal of the truth at an inopportune time?

Through information gathering from cells, the dark commune learns many secrets, secrets they use to ensure their members’ safety or gain leverage on those around them. Officers with secret dalliances, officials on the take, and corrupt @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Ministorum} officials are all assets within the Storm's Eyes network.

Secrets

The former leader of the cult was Getharius Malicain. He was a fanatic who, over time, became afflicted with various mutations. As Taliana Gaulista rose through the cult’s ranks, she took the chance to tamper with Gatharius’s last ritual, which caused him to turn entirely into a Chaos Spawn.

Since then, she has kept Getharius locked away in an abandoned void station. None of the dark commune wish to harm him; some have begun referring to him more reverently, whispering about his strong connection with the Lord of Change. Taliana is unsure what to do with Getharius but often parades unfaithful members in front of him to test their mettle and show the cult’s power.

Long ago, Inquisitorial agents infiltrated one of the cells closest to the dark commune. However, they failed to reach the cult’s leadership before the cell they were investigating sacrificed itself to keep the commune from being discovered. The Inquisitor’s notes from the investigation are archived on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W.JournalEntryPage.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis}. While the discovered cyphers they once used to communicate are long out of date, they might serve as a starting point for any investigators picking up the trail.

pages.name: Tôk's Firestorm Kindred
pages.text:
Tôk's Firestorm Kindred

See this, ceramite from our forges. I guarantee that it is purer than any ‘factorum in the sector. Take this sample and make any tests you need; we will return to place your order, eh?

Threat Overview

  • Tôk’s Firestorm Kindred are a group of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#the-leagues-of-votann]{Votann Kin} operating in the Macharian Sector.

  • In their prospecting and trade efforts with other cultures, they operate from small voidships and work to keep the existence of their mothership, The Cleansing Flame, from being discovered.

  • They aim to prospect the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.MzIWAwZ8jPAOydDi]{Yix Subsector} of the Macharian Sector and present their superiors with a case for expanding into the region.

The Kin only entered the Macharian Sector within the last few decades. Their initial focus in the region has been to explore the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.MzIWAwZ8jPAOydDi]{Sargassum Reaches} and interact with the factions established in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.riXKYZYMko558MLs]{Iron Archipelago} of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.MzIWAwZ8jPAOydDi]{Yix Systems}. They have engaged in preliminary trade, mainly as a means of gathering information and assessing the technological aptitudes of the cultures active in the region. As they carefully test the diplomatic waters, the Kin have gone to great lengths to maintain their secrecy. They recognise the importance of revealing only some of their assets, using shorter-range voidships to conduct these interactions.

This is because Tôk’s Firestorm Kindred have a Bastion-class mining vessel prospecting and mining the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.MzIWAwZ8jPAOydDi]{Sargassum Reaches}. The Cleansing Flame has conducted preliminary operations on several asteroids, moons, and habitable worlds. Their early conclusions are that the opportunities could justify a significantly increased Kin presence in the region. However, the Kindred’s elders continue to review @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.76CFMEzdNOznVcNf]{Hernkyn} reports about the various factions and threats in the sector. Until those analyses are completed, they remain uncommitted to significant, long-term extraction and refining operations.

The vessel’s commander, Tôk Stonehewer, acting on guidance provided by a venerable Ancestor Core, believes that trading with the Imperium may ease relationships and bring about some sort of accord. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.76CFMEzdNOznVcNf]{Hernkyn} groups have made discreet visits to dozens of worlds in the sector. They have yet to identify any ideal trading partners, though they have identified a few potential ones, particularly among Imperial organisations secretly involved in the Silent Trade.

The Kin’s components and goods are often superior to what is produced locally on many Imperial worlds, and would prove valuable. However, dealing with xenos is heresy, and though the Kin are often careful to conduct trade through intermediaries posing as abhumans (the so-called Squats found on many worlds), it is only a matter of time before the sheer volume of goods and their superior quality raises suspicion. Many of Stonehewer’s underlings understand this, but are unwilling to contradict their leader, especially as he is acting in accordance with an Ancestor’s guidance.

The Kin are willing to trade for information, particularly if they have reason to believe that a source is trustworthy and well-informed. They prefer to trade replaceable raw materials or salvage acquired in the region rather than relinquish their own artefacts. In some instances, the Kin supplied refurbished Imperium supplies to Imperial outposts without the final recipients recognising that xenos had performed maintenance on the devices.

Tôk’s Firestorm Kindred wear the sigil of a stylised, redorange flame within the outline of a grey cloud. It is generally worn as a shoulder patch and inscribed on all significant pieces of Kin equipment. Notably, they do not typically conceal the sigil when interacting with outside cultures. When asked about it, they refer to it as a family crest.

Resources

The Kindred are well supplied and equipped within the Macharian Sector. The Cleansing Flame is fully crewed and provisioned with equipment, including trade goods. It includes a wing of void shuttles capable of carrying @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.76CFMEzdNOznVcNf]{Hernkyn Yaegirs} to explore the region while the mining vessel continues its extraction and prospecting duties. During their exploration, the mining vessel’s storage capacity has begun to fill with rare and valuable metals and other resources.

When visiting other cultures, the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.76CFMEzdNOznVcNf]{Hernkyn} bring recording devices, scanners, and samples of their manufactured trade materials. Notably, they also carry duplicate personal equipment for their Yaegirs. That way, if a particular tool appears to have an immediate trade value, it can be bartered and later replaced from ship’s stores. Several of these tools have made their way into the hands of various Tech-Priests, who now hunt for their source.

Methods

Tôk’s Hernkyn are risk-averse as they investigate the Macharian Sector, and have prioritised stealth in their explorations. Whenever possible, they attempt to sneak into facilities — especially Imperial ones — and investigate them from within, posing as travellers from other parts of the world. At the first sign of resistance, the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.76CFMEzdNOznVcNf]{Hernkyn} attempt to withdraw before the situation escalates. In keeping with this approach, the Kin usually target isolated settlements. The dangers of entering and safely escaping from major cities and hives exceed their calculated safety parameters.

To the best of their abilities, the Kin try to bluff past their physical appearance and clothing differences — most Imperial citizens will always think of them as Squat abhumans upon first impressions. However, any apparent xenos technology they wield will act to out them. Only if they are unable to withdraw peacefully do the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.76CFMEzdNOznVcNf]{Hernkyn} resort to violence, and they do not hold back. Instead, they quickly escalate to the best of their lethality and attempt to leave no witnesses behind. The Kin understand they might need to depart from the sector entirely if identified as a threat. Their biggest concerns are preserving or at least recovering any of their members and critical equipment. If either is captured, Kindred will escalate the situation. If necessary, they may bring The Cleansing Flame to bear.

Secrets

The Kindred’s presence within the Macharian Sector and their connections outside the region remain a vital point of secrecy. They do not admit to any associations with any @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#the-leagues-of-votann]{Leagues} outside the sector or that such a notional civilisation exists.

The Kindred have found a stable route from the Galactic Core to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.MzIWAwZ8jPAOydDi]{Yix Subsector}. This means that if they can find worthwhile mining opportunities, they may choose to expand aggressively into the region. Other factions may be very interested in discovering that route, to use themselves or heavily blockade to prevent incursion.

pages.name: Valastra of the Endless Whisper
pages.text:
Valastra of the endless whisper

Hear me in your dreams, little scribe. I’ve been watching you… You’ve had your eye on shelf 45-A82 f or some time now… All those volumes with such a thick layer of dust… Not touched for a century I’d say… What if it were all lost to ruin? All forgotten?… You can’t let that happen… Wake up!

Threat Overview

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.SkjfCdcXvxERWyeo]{Valastra} of the Endless Whisper is a Slaaneshi daemon.

  • It has formed a cult within the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy]{Persepolis}, tempting lowly scribes and adepts to consume massive amounts of data, some of it forbidden.

  • While it continues twisting its followers' minds, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.SkjfCdcXvxERWyeo]{Valastra}’s end goal is to escape the Immaterium and sow the seeds of the Dark Prince’s madness as far as possible.

The @UUID[JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#silence-and-darkness]{Noctis Aeterna} was a harrowing time for the people of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy#hive-skarthius]{Hive Skarthius} on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy]{Persepolis}. During savage attacks from Heretic Astartes, most reliable lines of communication were cut off, and the Emperor’s light was cast into the deepest of shadows.

A handful of Hive Skarthius’ @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.cvpsLwcsXf4myIpK]{Adeptus Administratum}, all low-ranking scribes and archivists, searched for meaning in the darkness of those days. They came together to form the Last Light, and were determined to stand against the enemy that threatened to overwhelm their world. Where others took up the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.8tlu4X5Qpzl98Uye]{lasgun}, however, they reached for the quill. They viewed their pursuit as a higher calling, To them, at least in their minds, fell the noble goal of preserving all the knowledge they could, fearing the @UUID[JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#silence-and-darkness]{Noctis Aeterna} would never lift, condemning them to the horrors of Old Night once again.

They visited long-forgotten libraries tucked away in their labyrinthine halls. They journeyed into the depths of the hive — hooded, cloaked, and defended by carefully requisitioned servitors incapable of repeating what they saw in those cramped tunnels and chambers — for relics and records unseen by Human eyes for centuries. They did not seek something to help their beleaguered world, some scrap of lore or ancient machine that might promise salvation. They merely attempted to record.

With a focus and a zeal unseen in most outside of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum}, this handful of librarian-errants amassed the truths they so desperately wanted to protect. They filled scrolls, data spools and, when all else failed, carved reams of data into each other’s flesh. It was this final act of obsession that drew the attention of the servants of the Dark Prince.

Their obsession called out through the Immaterium as a beacon that @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.SkjfCdcXvxERWyeo]{Valastra} of the Endless Whisper followed to its source. There, it found minds ripe for exploitation and a cause perfect for corruption. Acting quickly to stave off the interests of the Changer of the Ways, whose daemons were drawn to secrets and knowledge, it appeared in the dreams of the Last Light’s disparate members and began to twist them to its own nefarious ends.

Resources

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.SkjfCdcXvxERWyeo]{Valastra} is a relatively new threat to the Macharian Sector. It prefers to appear in dreams and whispers, and many of its thralls still consider themselves loyal members of the Imperium who are committing minor heresies, at worst, by seeking out forgotten truths or by administering their own justice. As a result, Valastra’s servants are as likely to appear as allies to the characters as they are to act against them.

It encouraged some followers to delve deeper into the hive, claiming ever more esoteric tomes and artefacts containing forbidden knowledge, playing on their unacknowledged need to experience life outside of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum}. Others it bade catalogue and record every fact and find in maddening detail, encouraging a drive for perfectionism within them. To its handful of founding members @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.SkjfCdcXvxERWyeo]{Valastra} entrusted the most significant task: recruitment.

Use the various Administratum stat-blocks (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Administratum Adept}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.CsFqLJu3uHM45otd]{Arbitrator}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.gQxTENJSdTQTVfDM]{Enforcer}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.wzB86nJHHIRHMQTO]{Overseer}) to represent Valastra’s followers on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy]{Persepolis}.

Methods

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.SkjfCdcXvxERWyeo]{Valastra} prefers to encourage its followers to obsess over knowledge above all else, leaving pleasures of the flesh to other servants of the Dark Prince.

It is making a concerted effort to find a piece of archaeotech that the Last Light believes to be buried somewhere in the wastes of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X0XXyOc86SRCgd4h]{Asterion}. The device is rumoured to be capable of instantly replicating any tome placed within it. This is hardly a remarkable feat in most cases, but @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.SkjfCdcXvxERWyeo]{Valastra} knows the device can make so fine a copy that even psychic compulsions placed upon the book by its own daemonic sorceries can be replicated and spread.

To recover the device, the Last Light is arranging a private expedition — with carefully forged paperwork — to locate and retrieve it. They are also bribing and blackmailing engineers, mercenaries, and labourers to design, build, and defend a bastion within the depths of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy#hive-skarthius]{Hive Skarthius}. This bastion will act as a vault and the Last Light’s formal headquarters; @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.SkjfCdcXvxERWyeo]{Valastra} is orchestrating things to ensure that the correct sigils and materials are used in its construction to allow the daemon to manifest fully within its walls.

Secrets

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.SkjfCdcXvxERWyeo]{Valastra} is not strong enough to manifest within @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy#hive-skarthius]{Hive Skarthius}, but its time approaches as its influence grows. If either of the daemon’s schemes come to fruition on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.zzHVmjdxrrYtjScl]{Crultus} or the expedition to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X0XXyOc86SRCgd4h]{Asterion}, the daemon will have the means to manifest fully into realspace.

It has recently begun obfuscating the Last Light’s activities by relying on pleasure cults elsewhere in the sector, using the more overt behaviour of those cultists to draw the eye of the Inquisition and any other forces that would act against it. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.SkjfCdcXvxERWyeo]{Valastra} does its best to ensure nothing ties back to its recruiters from the Last Light.

pages.name: Varon Vipersong
pages.text:
Varon Vipersong

Tread carefully Mon-keigh, I have killed countless of your kind and captured countless more. But I will give you a chance, unlike your fallen kin. Tell me what you know of your supposedly merciless Inquisition…

Threat Overview

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.KZk1yGduhULvMbmP]{Varon Vipersong} is a rogue Kabal Sybarite, leading a band of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.b8x4YQfSyzlvU4LX]{Drukhari Kabalite Warriors} from the Dripping Fang Kabal, operating in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.4LYxCIJ2ansZ5wFk]{Andosk Subsector}.

  • He and his Kabalites move through hidden Webway portals in the Macharian Sector as they scout for ripe targets and claim captives where possible.

  • He aims to gain enough strength and favour to raise his group of Kabalites to become the ‘Hand of the Archon’, the Archon’s most elite kill team and trusted agents.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.KZk1yGduhULvMbmP]{Varon Vipersong} was destined for greatness. He is a Trueborn @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari} descended from a highly influential family within the Dripping Fang, one of the devious Kabals that rule Commorragh, and is related by blood to the Kabal’s Archon, Vypar S’Threil. Regrettably for Varon, his family tore itself apart during one of the many bouts of betrayal and infighting that marks Drukhari life. Only Varon survived, in a single night losing his influence, his status and, though it mattered somewhat less to him, his closest kin. Varon threw himself upon the feet of the Kabal’s Archon, Vypar S’Threil, and plied his remaining favour to avoid being cast into the Kabal’s fighting pits. As a mercy, Varon was granted a place among the lowly Kabalites and told to ‘prove his worth’ by leading raids to secure more captives for the Kabal. It did not take long for him to rise to the rank of Sybarite; his tragic fall only stoked his ambition.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.KZk1yGduhULvMbmP]{Varon} is a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari} caught between two worlds, once hailing from the Kabalite courts of Commorragh but forced to survive among the ‘half-born’ warrior class. He is at least as deadly and cunning as the average Sybarite, and far more driven that most. He inherited his family’s last remaining favours and knows he must call them in effectively to maintain his position within Commorragh while putting pressure on his targets. His Trueborn status and growing reputation among the lower Kabalites as a cunning warrior has gathered him a following. He chooses the strongest warriors from among them to join his squad, promising that one day they will rise with him to become the Hand of the Archon.
