pages.name: Briefing & Debriefing
pages.text:
To stand in the presence of an Inquisitor inspires awe and terror in all Imperial citizens, but perhaps none more so than their acolytes, those they expect the most from. Acolytes who serve them will become accustomed to this tension with cold familiarity, for to one who holds such absolute power, their lives are only as valuable as their duties.

Meetings between Inquisitors and their agents become regular punctuation to the lives of both parties. Evidence is traded for inscrutable orders: coordinates, targets, and names, with duties of investigation, destruction, and execution — while the Inquisitor has absolute authority, it is their acolytes who must venture to enact their instruction, however righteous, however cruel.

Inquisitors rarely communicate with their acolytes as straightforwardly as an officer of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} marshals their warriors. Limited contact, coded messages, and Interrogators following the chain of command are all ways an Inquisitor may obscure their communications from an ever-vigilant enemy. Direct contact often suggests significant importance to the task set before them and an indication that the Inquisitor is beginning to consider them more than expendable. These communications take on ever more vital importance when an Inquisitor orders that, as needs of their investigation impose, their retinue operate under compartmentalised status — communicating only between one another, to the exclusion of all other Imperial forces, even the Inquisition.

Briefings and debriefings are the primary ways characters interact with their Inquisitor Patron. Consider the advice below in conjunction with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.f5PuitUGgp6jQz5K.JournalEntryPage.qsaLi310r4uyLu4R#running-investigations]{Running Investigations} section included in Imperium Maledictum. Beyond receiving orders and presenting evidence, briefings and debriefings allow characters to get to know their Patron, building the mystery around them and gradually presenting aspects of their motivation, philosophy, and goals with each subsequent meeting.

To begin with, characters will know very little of the depths of philosophical conflicts that make the Inquisition such an interesting organisation to centre campaigns around, so these meetings should allow them glimpses into the organisation’s byzantine nature of competing philosophies and the clashes from bickering to total enmity that arise among Inquisitors as those uniquely allowed to act as individuals in their service to the Imperium.

@TableHTML[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.FlLe70joG4yXI3EG]{Method of Communication, description, no-center}

Briefing

When an Inquisitor summons their acolytes for briefing, their deployment into the field is certain, and the trials to come inexorable, borne in shadow by the heretic, mutant, and alien. The true breadth of an Inquisitor’s plan is rarely revealed, only the objective to which their acolytes must risk their lives, chancing a death in which they never know the consequence of their service. To these orders, they arm themselves with prayer and wargear, board their transport and hope that their preparations were enough to tide them through the mission ahead.

Running a Briefing

Unless characters are mid-mission, sessions of Imperium Maledictum, wherein the characters' Patron is an Inquisitor, typically begin with the characters receiving a briefing from their Patron. This may be their only active communication with their Patron until their mission succeeds or fails. Inquisitors frequently avoid association with the actions of their acolytes in the field, especially when those actions might skirt the boundaries of Lex Imperialis.

In a briefing, despite any convoluted means of communication, avoid giving characters any unclear orders. Simply ordering characters to, for example, ‘Investigate the Highborn Thrax family of Jocasta Hive on Persepolis’ gives them little to go on, and may be frustrating for players, particularly during the start of their investigation when they are effectively without leads. Instead, aim to offer more direct commands. Briefings benefit from including:

  • Objective: Describe duties given to the characters. Avoid vague verbs like ‘Investigate’ and instead aim to provide clear, specific mission objectives. For example, ‘steal records from a datavault,’ ‘find evidence of heresy among a specific group,’ or ‘learn the connections between the operations of two factions.’

  • Location: Investigations can span sectors, but a mission should have a precise location or contained area of operation. For example, ‘the lower levels of a hive city’, ‘an asteroid research void station’, ‘a voidship’ or ‘an Astra Militarum fortress’. Sometimes, the Patron could grant characters a secure safehouse to work from within or nearby the required location — or make it part of the characters' mission to set one up. See the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.9PUkIflsW5d1R7T9]{Inquisition Safehouses} for ideas.

  • Contacts: Introduce NPCs likely to be central to the characters’ investigation. They could be known @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.2TukBjlkS5RG5Qka]{Contacts} to the Inquisitor, their Ordo, a whistleblower, or witnesses embroiled in events. For example, ‘a voidship officer who witnessed strange Warp phenomena’, ‘a Commissar who saw strange behaviour spreading through the ranks of their regiment’, ‘a Ministorum informant who has worked for multiple Inquisitors’, or ‘a scribe who suspects they are receiving altered records’.

  • Clues: These provide the initial leads for characters to follow at the outset of their investigation. They may be material evidence, reports, testimonies, or records of events; some might need to be sought out and retrieved in the field to be analysed further. For example, ‘a testimony from a heretical Rogue Trader’, ‘a seized shipment of xenos-produced goods’, or ‘details on a recent uprising in a hab-block’.

  • Additional Stipulations: Discretion is often essential for the Inquisition to complete its holy work. Many missions may require characters to disguise themselves as members of other Factions or operate from the shadows. Their Patron should make it clear at the outset of the mission if there are any lines they should not or are expected to cross (some of these stipulations could affect their @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.tuASnDHy4WyxFVOZ#subtlety]{Subtlety}, if broken).

Briefing Example

The characters’ Patron gives them the following instruction during their briefing: ‘Gather evidence of heresy among the Highborn Thrax family of Jocasta Hive on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy]{Persepolis}. Upon arrival, make contact with Sister Famula Phaedymia and inform only her that you are in service to His Holy Inquisition. She will introduce you as servants of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Ministorum}.’ This introduction gives them a clear objective to their investigation (looking for evidence of heresy), a location ( Jocasta Hive on Persepolis), a contact with whom they will likely see a lot of interaction, and can provide clues and guidance if needed (Sister Famula Phaedymia), and a stipulation (only Phaedymia can know the party serve the Inquisition, their cover story is that they are servants of the Ministorum, and must therefore disguise themselves and act in a manner appropriate to resemble this allegiance).

@TableHTML[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.9PUkIflsW5d1R7T9]{Strange Meeting Places, description, no-center}

Debriefing

When characters return from a mission, how long does any sense of relief last? The lull offers safety in private offices, fortified barracks, or voidship cabins, but they know the Inquisitor awaits their report. Their Patron requires them to divulge the events of their mission and provide any evidence in relation to their stated goal (as well as any other evidence suggesting further heresy). Information imparted in debriefs will shape the course of future operations undertaken by the characters, regarding both direction and force permitted for the characters to utilise.

Debriefings may readily include admonition if a mission was not performed to their Patron’s standards, such as through unsanctioned extrajudicial killings or the gathering of limited evidence. Inquisitors rarely provide comfort or positive reinforcement to acolytes beyond the cold acknowledgement of an adequately performed job and the responsibility to wield ever more brutal force in their Patron’s name. As GM, it is an opportunity for players to see behind the curtains, revealing some of what they might have missed or the consequences of unforeseen actions.

Running a Debriefing

During a debriefing, characters must present the evidence they gathered on their mission and discuss their actions and methods (ensuring that the evidence gathered justified any more dubious means employed). You can use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.5VEhavnLClS1FAIR]{Strange Meeting Places} Table to pick or inspire a clandestine location to run your debriefings.

When characters present the evidence gathered during the debriefing, each piece of evidence grants +1 SL on Fellowship Tests made in conversation with their Patron. Characters may have to present convincing arguments to their Patron in the following ways, with Tests ranging from Challenging (+0) to Very Hard (−30), depending on how far they may have strayed from orders or authorised actions:

  • Justification: Characters may have to justify more extreme actions undertaken on a mission, from breaking the strictures of the Lex Imperialis or arresting suspects, to extrajudicial executions or engaging in combat. Successful justification may convince their Patron to dispatch additional aid in future missions, such as extra security operatives or access to forbidden knowledge.

  • Shaping Future Investigations: Guided by their evidence, an Inquisitor may send their acolytes to follow up any identified lead further or to apprehend those condemned by damning evidence. Inquisitors with intense preoccupations may be convinced that evidence gathered by their acolytes is worth diverting their attention, mainly if characters identify a threat the Inquisitor was unaware of. Enough evidence of a severe threat may even force the hand of an Inquisitor and see them joining their acolytes in the field.

  • Knowing Thy Foe: Strong evidence can guide an Inquisitor to commit their assets to better preparation. Characters may gain +1 Superiority in a coming conflict if their evidence can offer guidance. It may convince the Inquisitor to prepare additional aid for the cell, including special weapons or equipment to fight their particular foe or provide @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.2TukBjlkS5RG5Qka]{Contacts} with relevant information.

  • Strange Complications: The characters should inform their Patron of any strange complications — the interference of unlikely groups or clues that lead towards unrelated heresies. Informing their Patron allows them to use other cells and Contacts within their network to determine if something else is amiss. In some circumstances, characters may believe hiding or obscuring information from their superiors may benefit them, but this is their chance to come clean without repercussions. Their Patron will undoubtedly discover the truth eventually and be less forgiving, although hiding such information could lead to some powerful dramatic moments in the future.

@TableHTML[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.5VEhavnLClS1FAIR]{Strange Meeting Places, description, no-center}

Rewards and Downtime

Part of the Inquisitor’s debriefing is an opportune time to reward characters for their efforts; this will also help build their relationship with their Patron. Additionally, it is unlikely their Patron will have their next mission ready for them, as they are still processing the outcome of the last, so characters should be granted a period of downtime after the debriefing is complete. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX]{Between Missions} and the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.r6clx5uYnIpkdaRq]{Inquisition Player’s Guide} cover downtime activities, Endeavours, and Events.

Standard character rewards are outlined in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.f5PuitUGgp6jQz5K.JournalEntryPage.qsaLi310r4uyLu4R#rewarding-players]{Running the Game}, but as acolytes are special operatives of the Inquisition, consider offering them an extra gift from their Patron. This could be a new weapon or tool from the Inquisition’s armoury, something that might serve them well in a future mission. As a group, they could be granted a more secure safehouse, vehicle, or the funds to secure such a thing for themselves.

It is also the perfect time to consider whether their Patron receives a new Boon, Liability, or subsequent increase or decrease in their Influence with certain Factions. Consider what the characters' mission results mean for their Inquisitor Patron. Did they clash with or favourably cooperate with another Faction? You could also consider if events caused the Patron to overcome one of their Liabilities and have it stricken from their Patron sheet.

pages.name: Ksenia Baek
pages.text:
‘It is my destiny to find the God-Emperor’s next vessel, a task passed down from Thorian to Thorian, from my mentor to me. My duty is to herd the psykers of the sector and cull the impure from them, find the best among them and train them to be better. Holy Terra awaits.’

Ordo: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-hereticus]{Hereticus}
Philosophy: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.0vHms9BJQGOVa0dO]{Thorian}
Known Interrogators: Severina Melnyk
Operational Territory: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.y6qA7KARTXADwzeV]{Cytheris Subsector}
Primary Concerns:

  • Seek out pure psykers across the sector.

  • Hunt rogue psykers and heretical cults.

  • Train psykers to bolster the Inquisition’s strength.

As a member of the Ordo Hereticus, Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.B0kjmCWM6na30YqG]{Ksenia Baek} has carved herself a reputation within the Macharian Inquisition as the sector’s foremost expert on psykers and witchcraft. Her work has kept her close to the goals of her Thorian philosophy — to seek out a pure psychic avatar for the God-Emperor to inhabit upon his eventual return. Ksenia chases psykers across the sector to seek out this prophesied avatar, spurred by reported miracles and psychic divinations.

The now deceased Inquisitor Onderghast identified Baek’s psychic abilities in her early childhood, during an investigation of a xenos cult on her home agri world of Rauss V. Onderghast noted the child emitting an unnerving psychic presence, disrupting his connection to the Empyrean. Through training and mentorship, he instilled within her the tenets of the Thorian philosophy — believing for some time that she might become the God-Emperor’s new avatar. But through extensive testing and trials, Onderghast eventually deemed her not pure enough. Instead, it was Baek’s destiny to succeed him and take up his task.

Baek brokered a deal with the League of Black Ships, aiding them in investigating and capturing problematic psykers in return for a base of operations aboard one of their voidships. On The Penitent Burden, Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.B0kjmCWM6na30YqG]{Ksenia Baek} has overseen the training of hundreds of Inquisitorial acolytes and fledgeling psykers. Baek has long worked alongside the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.upGG1JZPDbC7dpJJ]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}, her investigations generating a wellspring of psykers. Many are loaded aboard the Black Ships as part of their damned cargo, but a select few go on to serve the Inquisitor, sometimes bypassing their sanctioning when Baek sees fit, and installed within her acolyte cells across the sector.

Baek's Secrets

Baek is sure that an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.cKepLkmLocC4tuPy]{Ocularian} Inquisitor from the Calixis Sector is secretly operating in the Macharian Sector, collecting information to fuel their grand divinations. She believes the collective information and prophecies the Ocularians have made can guide her to the destined avatar she has spent most of her life looking for — she is also curious to see what divinations they hold about herself.

Baek’s closeness to the League of Black Ships works towards the culmination of her plans. Once she has secured the God-Emperor’s avatar, she plans to commandeer The Penitent Burden or whatever Black Ship is nearest (by force if necessary) and make haste for Terra — dropping whatever Inquisitorial investigations she is in the middle of. Though the chance of this happening is improbable, her hopes rest on a personal divination she received in her early years of training from Onderghast — a vision he saw of her aboard a Black Ship back to Holy Terra. Perhaps naively, Baek interprets this divination positively rather than as a sign of future damnation.

Psykers in the presence of Baek and her acolytes have been known to experience a similar, disquieting phenomenon to that reported by Inquisitor Onderghast. Baek is afraid to pick at this psychic scab within her soul, fearful it will confirm her impurity. Regardless of her intentions, every expression of Baek’s considerable psychic might is deeply unsettling to non-blanks in her vicinity. Most are left with recurring nightmares for days or experience waking visions of death — usually their own.

This is because the Inquisitor has a shadow, a Daemon calling itself Baek. It has haunted her since childhood, confined to the Warp but always nearby. Time in the Warp is fluid, ebbing and flowing as it wills, frequently turning back upon itself. Baek keeps the Inquisitor close because it knows that she will one day be responsible for its own creation. If he became aware of the unusual aura she projects, @UUID[.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} would be interested in studying her.

pages.name: Aegidius Halikarn
pages.text:
‘Heretics are like vermin. Unless discovered and purged, they breed incessantly in the shadows, until the walls of your hab are composed more of traitorous inclination than of rockcrete.’

Ordo: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-hereticus]{Hereticus}
Philosophy: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.7Aqg1D2wSmKjmzWj]{Recongregationism}
Known Interrogators: Caecilius Elbegdorj
Operational Territory: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.y6qA7KARTXADwzeV]{Cytheris Subsector}
Primary Concerns:

  • Root out heresy and cult activity amongst the sector’s most populated worlds.

  • Uncover systematic corruption among the major factions of the Imperium in the Macharian Sector.

As a Recongregator and in contact with other likeminded Inquisitors across the Imperium, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.UFulYcpdvsqsr4dk]{Halikarn} focuses on upending the Macharian Sector’s noble houses. He believes that the sector’s twisted histories obscure a terrible truth. That it was established (and subsequently re-established) incorrectly. This revisionist history is ignorant of the finer points of the Emperor’s will and enmeshes heretical practices into the very fabric of this western arm of the Imperium.

Based on these lines of inquiry, the Ordo Hereticus Inquisitor has already exposed innumerable heresies within noble families and Imperial factions. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.UFulYcpdvsqsr4dk]{Halikarn} operates with as much secrecy as he can manage, ousting and replacing those in positions of power while maintaining a veneer of as little personal involvement as possible. But he has garnered some infamy; some use his name as a byword for protracted Inquisitorial presence, as his preferred methods involve investigating leads at lower levels of Imperial organisations and then proceeding rank by rank until a source of corruption is identified at the top.

The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus} have developed a particular frustration with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.UFulYcpdvsqsr4dk]{Halikarn’s} methods, as his escalating levels of investigation have the potential to cause delays at multiple stages of production, leading to manufactorum backlogs and quota errors, through which the same frustration is passed directly to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum}.

Halikarn has a history of working alongside @UUID[.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Inquisitor Raud} following their collaborative investigation of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.JbRBjmzRfWtxIo40]{Leonova} Orbital Rebellion in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.y6qA7KARTXADwzeV]{Cytheris Subsector}, which toppled two @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.h6Z6Ia2q5RkRUlDG]{Rogue Trader Dynasties} responsible for trade in heretical, Warp-tainted artefacts. They maintain a lasting level of what could almost be called trust — despite Halikarn viewing Raud's means as overly destructive and Raud thinking Halikarn’s philosophy a fruitless pursuit.

Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.UFulYcpdvsqsr4dk]{Aegidius Halikarn} was the featured sample Patron of the Imperium Maledictum Starter Set adventure @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.arjSGA9gcUykxq0z]{The Blazing Seraph}. Characters can continue to serve him as a Patron, going into @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W]{The Heresies Macharia}, following on from their adventures on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.59y8WFXTbwKRwiRI]{Voll}.

Halikarn's Secrets

Among @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.UFulYcpdvsqsr4dk]{Halikarn’s} favoured operatives is a squad of acolytes referred to by Halikarn as ‘The Faceless’, formerly in the service of @UUID[.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Inquisitor Horst}, who thinks they are dead. These agents willingly accepted serving Halikarn and his Recongregator philosophy, knowing that it spites their former patron.

While working in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.JbRBjmzRfWtxIo40]{Leonova}, @UUID[.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Inquisitor Raud} claimed to have destroyed all the Warp-tainted artefacts they uncovered. In truth, she collected most of them at her base near the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.1AsBzkbw2InKayw2]{Ayzinith Abyss} for further study. If @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.UFulYcpdvsqsr4dk]{Halikarn} learns of Raud’s @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.s88kgPSDiogPL4aB]{Xanthite} beliefs, he will lose trust in her. Raud planted several agents within Halikarn’s retinue, and he has yet to discover them.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.UFulYcpdvsqsr4dk]{Halikarn} has been aided by Drukhari raiders in the past. In his fleeting contact with these Cabalites, he directed them to targets from which the aliens could mock the weakest Imperial power structures, aiding him in dethroning the corrupt within. But he knows these heretical agreements must be obscured from his peers. Eventually, he seeks to feed information on their whereabouts to @UUID[.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Inquisitor Serranus} to keep the Ordo Xenos Inquisitor from interfering with his @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.7Aqg1D2wSmKjmzWj]{Recongregator} goals.

pages.name: Sylvestrine Horst
pages.text:
‘The Emperor has determined a path for each of us. You have strayed from your path. The consequence is as written for each traitor before you.’

Ordo: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-hereticus]{Hereticus}
Philosophy: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.R7LueEsDUhrSYHNn]{Amalathian}
Known Interrogators: None
Operational Territory: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.UbH7oOtTYfjFlKRt]{Gallosque Nebula}
Primary Concerns:

  • Maintain the status quo among the Imperium’s noble houses.

  • Discover the truth of what happened to former Inquisitor Lord Hieronymo Drake, and understand the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W.JournalEntryPage.jt0zc7az5xNehcIZ#the-kryptman-protocol]{Kryptman Protocol}.

  • Become the new Inquisitor Lord of the Macharian Sector, or find a suitable candidate to elevate (see @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W]{The Heresies Macharia}).

As an Amalathian, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.aVVwuxbGv4b1Lcnm]{Horst} believes that the Emperor’s grand plan for the Macharian Sector, the Imperium, and the entire galaxy is progressing precisely as His perfect mind has foreseen, and any deviation from the status quo is a form of heresy.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.aVVwuxbGv4b1Lcnm]{Horst} grew up in and around the shrines of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Macharia}, among the Sororitas Order Dialogus of the Solar Quill, before joining the Inquisition at Inquisitor Lord Hieronymo Drake’s request. She was tasked with investigating the upper echelons of Imperial society for heresy, seeking out those who would threaten the status quo. Her success and proliferation of assets under her control elevated her to the rank of Interrogator. Her public piety has helped to cement the Sisters Famulous as a contact network among Highborn houses throughout the Gallosque Nebula, granting her access to generations worth of records kept by these families under the Sororitas’ watch.

Among other Inquisitors, she is known for sending her supplicants on hazardous missions, often bordering on suicidal — @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.aVVwuxbGv4b1Lcnm]{Horst} believes that such crushing hardships are some necessary part of His divine plan.

Acolytes who please her and show some semblance of sacred purpose are rewarded with a new face, an impassive plasteel death mask cast in the visage of a revered saint. These masked figures have taken on a mythic quality amongst the noble houses of the Gallosque Nebula, lurking taciturn in the shadows to punish any misdeed ruthlessly. Oppositely, acolytes who fail her and survive are forced to serve penance as her ‘Faceless’, receiving similar surgeries with completely blank masks.

Horst's Secrets

The brutal standard to which @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.aVVwuxbGv4b1Lcnm]{Horst} holds her operatives is not without drawbacks. Horst lost contact with a group of her acolytes several years ago while they were engaged in heavy fighting in the bowels of the city-vessel Cassian on the oceans of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.wHl3ZP7wM7OQvSLC]{Jotungarth}. Horst has since received troubling reports from her other operatives that a covert group bearing arms and equipment that mirrors their own is attempting to sabotage her ongoing investigations.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.aVVwuxbGv4b1Lcnm]{Horst} remains unaware that these operatives have served as mercenaries to @UUID[.W50MW8gfyrDts9g3]{Inquisitor Halikarn} on several occasions. It is less the case that their attacks have been to counteract Horst’s goals but somewhat further Halikarn’s broader @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.7Aqg1D2wSmKjmzWj]{Recongregator} goals, naturally opposed to Horst’s @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.R7LueEsDUhrSYHNn]{Amalathian} beliefs.

Despite outward appearances and theatrics, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.aVVwuxbGv4b1Lcnm]{Horst} was woefully involved in the death of her mentor, Inquisitor Lord Hieronymo Drake. She is shaken that her mentor was a secret heretic, and puzzled by his mysterious ‘@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W.JournalEntryPage.jt0zc7az5xNehcIZ#the-kryptman-protocol]{Kryptman Protocol}’ (the evidence of which is uncovered in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W]{The Heresies Macharia}) and is worried that his taint will reflect poorly on her and her legitimacy as an Inquisitor.

pages.name: Alis Raud
pages.text:
‘The Emperor has determined a path for each of us. You have strayed from your path. The consequence is as written for each traitor before you.’

Ordo: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-malleus]{Malleus}
Philosophy: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.s88kgPSDiogPL4aB]{Xanthite}
Known Interrogators: Damien Savantas
Operational Territory: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.d0lv2v4FkeIb43jj]{Drimor Subsector}
Primary Concerns:

  • Maintain the secrets of the Ordo Malleus

  • Hunt daemonic entities and cults she believes are connected to the ostensibly centuries-dead heretical @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#machariuss-generals]{Generus Cyrus} of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-macharian-conquests]{Macharian Crusade}.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.NbBJGOYw7Is2Hsj0]{Raud} is a veteran Inquisitor who has uncovered heresy in a thousand forms and sees its shadow everywhere. Her long service has seen her philosophy tempered by @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.s88kgPSDiogPL4aB]{Xanthite} beliefs; Chaos is ultimately beyond the possibility of defeat, and Humanity’s only hope is to bend daemonkind to its will. She closely guards the secrets of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-malleus]{Ordo Malleus} against other Inquisitors in the sector, to the benefit of her Ordo, but also to keep her Xanthite research hidden from her peers.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.NbBJGOYw7Is2Hsj0]{Raud} has spent much of her time as an Inquisitor cultivating a sprawling web of spies across the sector, including agents planted within the retinues of all the sector’s Inquisitors. From this, she wrests much of her influence and vigilance, hidden archiviums filled with secrets and blackmail, and hair-trigger signals ready to warn her of daemonic activity. Her eagerness to pounce upon heresy at first trace has led to the deaths of numerous unsanctioned psykers, to the frustration of her fellow Inquisitor, @UUID[.sNDdDGlvY5m1HQ4R]{Ksenia Baek}.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.NbBJGOYw7Is2Hsj0]{Raud} is currently engaged in a personal hunt for the heretic @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#machariuss-generals]{Generus Cyrus} of Saint Macharius’ Seventh Army Group that has spanned decades of her life. Despite previous Inquisitorial investigations concluding that Cyrus fell in battle, Raud holds that as the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.d0lv2v4FkeIb43jj]{Drimor Subsector} was undeniably shaped in Cyrus’ passing. She believes his twisted intentions linger, hidden deep within the sector's power structures, waiting to strike.

Of particular interest to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.NbBJGOYw7Is2Hsj0]{Raud} is the spatial anomaly rumoured to have been the origin of Cyrus’ corruption, for if the heretic general still draws breath, the path to finding and destroying him may begin in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.1AsBzkbw2InKayw2]{Ayzinith Abyss}. Raud regularly commandeers the data of listening posts on its perimeter to trace potential signs of daemonic or heretical presences in its inky depths. However, this has led to a fraught relationship with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}'s presence in the subsector.

Raud's Secrets

For some time now, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.NbBJGOYw7Is2Hsj0]{Raud} has held suspicions of heresy against @UUID[.y8Wjo2ThhVq782nY]{Eskender Thracius}, that the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} Inquisitor has cavorted with xenos entities, but more to the point, that he has built strange networks that often lead to dead ends and several of her lost agents. She continues to build evidence on him, waiting for the right time to strike against him.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.NbBJGOYw7Is2Hsj0]{Raud} remains uncorrupted despite the pitfalls of her Ordo’s duties and Radical research. Daemons who sought to corrupt her have begun to target her Interrogator, Damien Savantas, instead. Daemons whisper in his dreams, planting unconscious seeds of betrayal. But his corruption is a double-bluff on Raud’s behalf; she is fully aware of it — secretly using methods upon him similar to preparing a daemonhost, Raud has been luring daemons towards Savantas to keep them from interfering or manipulating her work. Dangerously, he is the only man worthy of succeeding in her role as Inquisitor.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.NbBJGOYw7Is2Hsj0]{Raud} commands a void fortress hidden at the edge of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.1AsBzkbw2InKayw2]{Ayzinith Abyss}. In addition to being the central hub of her spy network — routing communications throughout the sector — she keeps her damnable collection of twelve daemonhosts and the bulk of her @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.s88kgPSDiogPL4aB]{Xanthite} research into demonology. She believes that the daemonhosts, in particular, are the perfect bait to draw out General Cyrus.

pages.name: Konstan Serranus
pages.text:
‘The hand that touches that which has been tainted by xenos must be severed to maintain the purity of the whole.’

Ordo: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Xenos}
Philosophy: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.yds9IfgKQlwxLqq6]{Monodominant}
Known Interrogators: Arnaut Cisneros
Operational Territory: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.4LYxCIJ2ansZ5wFk]{Andosk Subsector}
Primary Concerns:

  • Curtail any xenos interference or invasion in the Macharian Sector.

  • Use this knowledge to strike out at alien foes beyond the borders of the Imperium.

  • Investigate the uptick of Genestealer Cult activity across the sector.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.1tBL8qTxUkWlvoDX]{Serranus} is a hard line firebrand of the Monodominant philosophy, a staunch absolutist who believes wholeheartedly in eradicating xenos, seeing their corruption as if it were a literal disease. Serranus is infamous for cutting off his own hand when it came into bare-fleshed contact with a piece of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari }technology, and he has executed many acolytes for similar ‘crimes’ that taint the purity of their Humanity.

Of the Inquisitors operating in the Macharian Sector, Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.1tBL8qTxUkWlvoDX]{Serranus} is one of the most active in the field, for how else can one ensure the destruction of the loathsome xenos than by personally overseeing its obliteration? Serranus possesses a short temper kept in check by his fervent faith, a strength he presses upon his acolytes to ensure their motivation and loyalty.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.1tBL8qTxUkWlvoDX]{Serranus}’ upbringing in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.4LYxCIJ2ansZ5wFk]{Andosk Subsector} ensured that he would carry the flame of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.rwTMhBwRA6wCOgIA]{Arrian’s piety}, kept burning by generations of devout who formed their faith in the wake of the zealous master of Saint Macharius’ Sixth Army. Serranus’s beliefs were solidified long before his ascension to Inquisitor. In his youth, Konstan was a rare survivor of an Ork assault that the mighty @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#the-deathwatch]{Deathwatch} quelled before his eyes.

Most acolytes under Serranus’s command are heavily augmented, as their flesh and former prosthetics are frequently replaced to prevent xenos contamination. He is unwavering in his beliefs that even to witness heresy is to foster corruption, ensuring that the eyes of long-serving acolytes are replaced with augmetics. His personal guard of former @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} troopers who accompany him in the field could be mistaken for warriors of the Machine God for the breadth of augmetics they bear. Serranus also heavily uses expendable servitors and has established a staunch alliance with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus} of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.bdYvHMokSJTHhbCx]{Forkas-63} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.EfRX41lj9XqAOfxa]{Ibal Primus}. Dealings between the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} Inquisitor and the Magos of the Machine Cult are often tense, but in return, Serranus is dogged in his pursuit of hereteks meddling with xenos tech on their behalf.

Serranus' Secrets

A former Inquisitor named Agrippa Gandash, was declared Excommunicate Traitoris for consorting with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari}, a xenos species for which Serranus still holds a highly personal disgust. Allegedly, Gandash went so far as to incorporate their blasphemous technologies into his own flesh. Serranus sees this as the ultimate perversion of pure human flesh, and has sworn to find Agrippa himself. Reluctantly, Serranus recently accepted the aid of specialist Valerius Nabopalassar. Nabopalassar's knowledge of the Aeldari has already aided in this hunt, but in fact the 'specialist' is more than he seems, and has already marked the intractable Serranus as a threat to his own agenda.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.1tBL8qTxUkWlvoDX]{Serranus} is so consumed by his Monodominant beliefs that he is not even above his own suspicions — his long service to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} has irredeemably exposed him to the loathsome alien. He knows that his mind is the last bastion of their corruption within him. Secretly, he has subjected himself to mind-wiping procedures to erase specifically haunting memories and expunged the Inquisition’s matching records. To his own detriment, Konstan is unaware that he is perhaps the sector’s foremost expert on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#necrons]{Necron} activities.

pages.name: Eskender Thracius
pages.text:
‘The Macharian Sector gives credence to the saying, ‘survival of the fittest’. Long ago, Lord Solar Macharius crushed or bent the will of weak houses and rebels, uniting the sector as one, but that was a long time ago. The Imperium cannot prosper while on the back foot, and I have the perfect enemies in mind.’

Ordo: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Xenos}
Philosophy: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.UAWh0hEvWDwob6CT]{Isstvanist}
Known Interrogators: Julios Macrio
Operational Territory: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.y6qA7KARTXADwzeV]{Cytheris Subsector}
Primary Concerns:

  • Study of xenos designation @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari}.

  • Use this knowledge to prepare for the return of the God-Emperor.

  • Maintain his web of aliases and avoiding death or capture.

Long before his excommunication from the Inquisition, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.M3LcQ68Fm8nP7KJT]{Thracius} used his position as a member of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} to further his Isstvanian goals — drawing the Imperium into conflicts with xenos forces in and around the Macharian Sector. He believes that xenos are Humanity’s most potent enemy — bizarre enough to test and broaden the skills of Humanity’s war machine and a uniting enemy, one that all of Humanity can easily agree to rally against.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.M3LcQ68Fm8nP7KJT]{Thracius} has spent long years consorting with the Aeldari, investigating their culture and technologies, but for the end goal of luring several Craftworlds into open warfare with the Imperium. He knows that other Inquisitors in the sector, particularly @UUID[.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Raud} and @UUID[.gRAiiRJkLKviH0K5]{Serranus}, have shreds of evidence towards his meddling, though more towards declaring him an outright heretic than a Radical Isstvanist.

Since the recent death of Inquisitor Lord Drake, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.M3LcQ68Fm8nP7KJT]{Thracius} has turned his trade towards the Macharian Inquisition itself — partly to occlude his heretical operations but otherwise to apply his Isstvanist beliefs from a different angle. He feels that if the Inquisition were put at war with itself, in its currently weakened state, it could lead to the ascension of more Inquisitors and perhaps the entitling of a new Inquisitor Lord.

Thracius' Secrets

Fearing the Inquisition’s wrath, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.M3LcQ68Fm8nP7KJT]{Thracius} has spent decades building a roster of aliases, allowing him to remain active within the Macharian Inquisition. Each one he can perform in person, using the scarce substance known as polymorphine, or from afar using various technologies to reroute his communications and shroud locations.

Thracius' Active Aliases

In his guise as Valerius Nabopalassar, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.M3LcQ68Fm8nP7KJT]{Thracius} has earned his closest allies in the Xenarites of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus}, a radical sect of the cult of the Machine God, who deem the collection of alien knowledge their holy work. Far from their homeworld of Stygies VIII, a small Xenarite sect formed unnoticed on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.jB9sg2SDLZJGZrac]{Eskutchax} during a siege of the world from Chaos forces. The Black Templars' arrival on the planet as reinforcement has driven the Xenarites to tighter secrecy; thus, interaction with Thracius has become a vital lifeline to their research, with Thracius’ acolytes readily equipped with xenos tech and wargear in return.

pages.name: The Holy Orders
pages.text:
Three Ordos Majoris serve as the backbone of the Inquisition: Hereticus, Malleus, and Xenos. The Ordo Hereticus prevents psykers, mutants, and heretics from tearing the Imperium apart from within, battling against the burgeoning malevolence in any Human soul. The Ordo Malleus battles the foul Warp entities and executes those vile or foolish enough to help them. The Ordo Xenos are sworn to eradicate the taint of xenos from the galaxy and assure Humanity’s domination beyond the Imperium’s borders. Sometimes, Ordos Minoris are formed to deal with a localised, specific, or short-lived concern, at least by the standards of the Imperium; the work of the three Ordos Majoris is already an unrelenting toil against impossible odds. The fight for Humanity’s survival is a ferocious battle that will only end if the Imperium is lost, something Inquisitors will do anything to prevent — sacrificing armies, worlds, or even damning their own souls.

An Inquisitor’s Ordo reflects their focus and the threats they actively seek out. Many Inquisitors are single-minded in their pursuit of their enemy and, once committed to rooting out a particular foe, are unlikely to waver for decades or even centuries. Each Ordo functions as a loose organisation of individuals, by necessity united under a common cause, but each guarding their secrets closely. Ostensibly this restricts the spread of dangerous information, though the motivation for doing so can be competitive, or even political. Knowledge is power, and projection of power is an Inquisitor’s stock in trade.

An Inquisitor’s place in the hierarchy of their Ordo is a shifting estimation of their current power, prestige, and the resources they can reliably call upon. Even the title of Inquisitor Lord is claimed or bestowed rather than by measured rank and ascension. These Inquisitors are universally acclaimed by their peers or otherwise begrudgingly acknowledged for wielding the most power and respect amongst a sector’s Inquisition. In the Macharian Sector, this title belonged to Inquisitor Lord Hieronymo Drake — a dauntless man who brought Inquisitors within the sector together to cooperate and share resources to combat the sector’s heresies.

That said, Inquisitors famously answer to none but the God-Emperor Himself; in truth, they are always answerable to each other. Constant scrutiny for signs of heresy or corruption further erodes trust between secretive and strong-willed individuals, honing their paranoia to a fine edge.

Ordo Hereticus

Across the Imperium, the stoic agents of the Ordo Hereticus fight heresy in all its forms: rogue psykers, Chaos cultists, dangerous mutants, and heretical preachers. These insidious enemies root themselves within Human society, so Inquisitors of this Ordo are expert investigators first and foremost. They must be able to detect and identify a myriad of taints and corruptions and know how to subdue or destroy their foes while protecting themselves from hideous mutants and the nightmarish powers of psykers, at least long enough to complete their mission. While the mass of Humanity is weak and corruptible, these Inquisitors are resolute, resisting temptation while mercilessly purging heresy in all its grotesque manifestations.

There are more Ordo Hereticus Inquisitors throughout the Imperium than any other Ordo. Where the reputation of these Inquisitors precedes them, they inspire fear and awe more than any other. Citizens call them ‘witch hunters’, and the stories whispered about them have created a fearsome reputation. Some Inquisitors play into this reputation to ensure honesty and compliance with those they encounter.

Other Inquisitors might question the reliability of testimony from terrified locals and attempt to allay their fears. Of course, stories of ruthless Inquisitors are indeed true. The nature of an Inquisitor’s dangerous hunt demands that they are unforgiving, and often, an Inquisitor decides to destroy a suspected heretic or psyker without confirming their ultimate guilt since wasting time to consider the truth could be otherwise disastrous.

Goals

Where the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum} shepherds their innumerate flock, the Ordo Hereticus hunts among the herd for those that turn from the Emperor’s light, seeking to eradicate heretical cults before they can begin to challenge the Imperium’s rule. The uncompromising brutality of daily life in the Imperium leads to many desperate citizens turning to the Ruinous Powers for answers, relief, and succour. Inquisitors of the Ordo Hereticus know these weak-willed and apostate individuals are the kindling that can strike a wildfire. They must uncover and destroy these cults before they threaten to burn down the Imperium.

Hunting psykers, mutants, and all forms of heresy across the Imperium of Man is a gargantuan but necessary task. A powerful psyker might walk unnoticed among innocent citizens, ignorant of their own perilous powers, and even the smallest mutation might be evidence of greater corruption within that could spread like a fungal rot. If left unpunished, minor heresies, such as carrying traditional talismans, can lead to more serious ones. Heretical preachers might quickly turn an otherwise compliant workforce into a dangerous mob in a surprisingly short space of time.

For the Imperium to survive on such a titanic scale, it must employ the dangerous powers of the psyker, captured and controlled by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.upGG1JZPDbC7dpJJ]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}. Rogue psykers capable of twisting reality leave themselves vulnerable to the predation of vile daemons that bolster their maleficent might. Yet the Black Ships cannot be everywhere at once. When a psyker eludes capture, the witch hunters of the Ordo Hereticus must hunt them down.

Philosophies

Puritan Inquisitors of the Ordo Hereticus consider any psychic tendency, slight mutation, or ill-advised comment on the Emperor’s rule a form of heresy and punish accordingly. They believe any taint must be cleansed, as even the slightest corruption begins small but, left unchecked, grows and spreads like a contagion across a world and may even spread to others. Some, like @UUID[.yds9IfgKQlwxLqq6]{Monodominant} Inquisitors, are even uncomfortable with the use of sanctioned psykers despite knowing they are essential to the Imperium. They are constantly alert for evidence that any psyker needs to be destroyed rather than used as a tool.

Radical Inquisitors of the Ordo, such as those who follow the @UUID[.vJmDVccuyJJLooV4]{Polypsykana} philosophy, instead use sanctioned psykers to aid their work or might even be one themselves. They are not more forgiving than their Puritan counterparts but are more willing to see heretics and their methods as tools to be adequately exploited towards their mission’s goals. In that sense, they might prefer to capture a rogue psyker rather than outright purge them — but that psyker’s life now hangs in the balance; stepping out of line for even a moment will cost them dearly.

Techniques

Inquisitors of the Ordo Hereticus are specialists who have each developed their own ways to expose and neutralise unsanctioned psykers and other heretics. They must be shrewd to protect themselves from the dangers they might encounter, using espionage, military tactics, or even psychic powers to survive. They organise planetwide witch hunts, coordinating operations so swift and brutal that all rogue psykers are contained before they can unleash unholy powers. Cults are infiltrated or stalked from the shadows and raided once their corrupt leaders are exposed. Mutants are sought and identified at all levels of society, then tracked to their dwellings, leading Inquisitors to whatever spire, ramshackle town, or derelict voidship is the source of mutation.

Many Inquisitors carry tools to identify psykers, such as arcane @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.7zxAcZPjoFW6mDR5]{psyocculums}, specialist weapons like blessed stake launchers to fight them, and protective tools such as blessed incense to protect themselves. Capturing a psyker is arduous, and if the means for nullifying a psyker’s power is not available, the Inquisitor must keep them otherwise incapacitated. Captured psykers might be put on a Black Ship if one is available nearby, or an Inquisitor may transport them to a null-prison for containment until one arrives. Psykers deemed too dangerous to capture must be otherwise purged — a public display will remind any locals of the dangers in harbouring such individuals and the threat of their unsanctioned powers.

Ordo Malleus

Few truly know of the daemon hunters’ existence, the most mysterious of the Ordos Majoris. The Ordo Malleus have hidden their work and redacted their charge from public view since their inception. Their grim duty is to battle horrors that defy mortal comprehension, and their primary goal is to detect and prevent daemonic incursions from even occurring in the first place. Inquisitors of the Ordo Malleus are forever on the watch for a rogue psyker with inexplicable powers, a daemonic cult on the rise, or a void anomaly that defies understanding — any might create a rift to the Warp, allowing daemons to swarm into reality via the Warp.

These Inquisitors are understandably wary of psykers and often find themselves working alongside, or occasionally at odds with, Inquisitors from the Ordo Hereticus. Their agents are regularly exposed to potent sources of corruption and frequently become overwhelmed and fall victim to daemonic influence or even outright possession. Even within their tightknit Ordo, Malleus agents spend significant time policing and purging their own — they must drive back daemons ideally before they breach realspace, or otherwise destroy them, even if it means taking their comrades’ life.

Goals

The main goal of the Ordo Malleus is to protect Humanity from the influence and presence of Warp entities. They prevent daemons from entering realspace wherever possible by hunting down and destroying any daemonic artefacts, cults, or rogue psykers whose powers risk the integrity of realspace. Their armies of savants scrutinise proscribed texts under the watchful gaze of hexagrammically warded enforcers while sanctioned psykers and prognosticars scry arcane portents, attempting to predict where these potential breaches in the Immaterium will take place long before they occur.

As if this task was not challenging enough, the Ordo’s secondary goal is to protect all citizens from learning about daemons. Knowledge of their very existence is enough to drive some citizens mad with fear. Yet that dread, spread by malefic whispers and temptation, is the root of damnable curiosity, driving some to heretical practices to grasp daemonic power for themselves. Daemons are by nature terrifying and manipulating, and anyone who makes contact with them, even for an instant, risks corruption. Methods for suppressing such knowledge can range from mind cleansing to outright eradicating the persons or groups involved. In extreme cases, whole worlds have been quarantined or destroyed to keep these terrible secrets safe.

Philosophies

The most Puritan members of the Ordo Malleus destroy anything related to daemonic activity they encounter on sight, burning tomes of forbidden knowledge, killing anyone who has seen or even heard of a daemon, and eradicating every last physical trace of any daemons they defeat.

By contrast, their more Radical colleagues wish to learn from daemonic tomes, interrogate anyone who has encountered these vile monsters, and dissect anything left after a fight. Most Inquisitors of the Ordo fall somewhere between the two extremes, and each must rely on their own judgement to know what is right.

Even some Puritans, such as @UUID[.0vHms9BJQGOVa0dO]{Thorians}, believe the study of Chaos necessary, but Radical Inquisitors tempt themselves to go too far, at least in the eyes of their brethren. Those who summon daemons to interrogate or to bind and use as a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.M6XWkYc0lfuKl2hU]{daemonhost} may find other Inquisitors investigating them for heretical practices, if not confronting them directly. @UUID[.zilJJMaYtaWZrNtO]{Horusians} might allow a daemon to possess their flesh, supposedly to build an immunity. Use of such methods are only discovered if the process goes demonstrably wrong, since Inquisitors and acolytes are forced to work in the shadows to avoid condemnation from their brethren.

Techniques

Some Inquisitors of the Ordo Malleus wear suits of sanctified armour or carry weapons blessed by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum}. They seek to use anything that might give them an advantage against the daemons they face, including everything from flamers and bolters to fleets of voidships. While preventing a daemon incursion can mean leaving the armour behind to infiltrate a daemonic cult or catch an unwary psyker, their missions often require firepower sooner or later. Even an undercover Inquisitor of the Ordo Malleus is likely to always keep weapons on them. Daemons come in a variety of foul forms. Many can be harmed by flame, lasfire, or humble frag grenades — an Inquisitor should always be prepared and ensure they have access to a varied arsenal that can destroy every foe they find.

Battling daemons is a demanding duty, and some are so large and powerful that even the best weapons of the Imperium seem inadequate. Some Ordo Malleus Inquisitors turn to less orthodox means to take them down. They may attempt to turn the daemon’s weapons against them or use xenos-made armaments to make victory more likely. Some study daemonic tomes to learn effective ways of countering or controlling daemons, while others go so far as to bind a daemon to a host, and force a daemon to join the fight against their own kind.

Ordo Xenos

The alien hunters of the Ordo Xenos work to protect the Imperium of Man from any and all xenos threats. Whether this means annihilating a xenos species so far as to scour their presence from the galaxy or merely preventing or delaying their ingress into Imperial sectors depends on the Inquisitor and their chosen target. Some Inquisitors consider anything of xenos origin to be inherently impure, so eradicate xenos artefacts and ruins as well as the xenos themselves on sight. Other Inquisitors willingly overlook such things, focusing solely on the threat of invasion and ways to use a species’ strength against itself. There are still fringe locales in the Macharian Sector where xenos trade with or even live among Humans, and such is repellant to Puritan Inquisitors. At the same time, the more Radical differentiate between hostile and relatively benign xenos and reserve their hostility for species they believe pose a significant threat.

While daemons and psykers appear in varied nightmarish forms and capabilities, respectively, xenos are the most diverse foes the Inquisition faces. Xenos species range from the brutal Orks to the technologically advanced T’au, from the flesh-eating Tyranids to the mysterious Aeldari, and many more species barely understood or undiscovered across the galaxy. On the one hand, this means that the Inquisitors of the Ordo Xenos aim to be ready for anything. On the other hand, it means that most Inquisitors specialise in one xenos species for most of their accursed career.

Goals

The primary goal of the Ordo Xenos is to protect the Imperium of Man from the threat of xenos, following the God-Emperor’s ancient will that Humanity rules the stars and all other species expunged.

Inquisitors might hunt xenos who infiltrate Imperial worlds, find and prevent the smuggling of xenos artefacts and technologies, or visit xenos ruins to learn about their foes or remove any trace of them. Even the most Puritan Inquisitors acknowledge that learning about the innumerate xenos species is essential since understanding the alien enables Inquisitors to better hunt and kill them and might even make it possible to anticipate their attacks.

Inquisitors must be alert for signs of incoming invasion and more subtle infiltration of Imperial worlds. Not all xenos rely on brute force tactics; some take advantage of the desperation of the Imperium’s poor and oppressed citizenry. Xenos cults, particularly Genestealer Cults, are incredibly dangerous and a prime example of the insidious, corrupting nature of xenos — if a Genestealer Cult is not discovered and destroyed in time, it can overrun the world and make it a foothold for spreading influence to other worlds, damning them all to the fate of Tyranid invasion.

Philosophies

Most Ordo Xenos Inquisitors learn what they can about the enemy’s biology, technology, and society to better understand and combat them. However, where Puritan Inquisitors might examine xenos tech before quickly destroying it, Radical Inquisitors study these artefacts far more closely, often adding them to their arsenal. Both study xenos societies and lore, but the Radical might do so with first-hand experience, or even seek out potential alien collaborators. Puritan Inquisitors are aware that some xenos species are less dangerous than others, but see it as no excuse to risk corruption.

Radical Inquisitors of the Ordo Xenos believe in using the enemy’s weapons against them, or even against other xenos. The infamous Fidus Kryptman once orchestrated a protracted war between the Orks and a Tyranid Hive Fleet to stave off their invasion of the Imperium, a move considered a master stroke by some, despite the vast collateral damage. Conversely, the most dogmatic Inquisitors typically keep their distance, using the likes of servitors to examine alien technology and disposing of them afterwards. A @UUID[.yds9IfgKQlwxLqq6]{Monodominant} might consider even this too dangerous and simply destroy any xenos artefact on sight. An @UUID[.UAWh0hEvWDwob6CT]{Isstvanist} might use xenos tech to conduct false flag operations, provoking a wider war. Within an Ordo that has so many varied fields of study, disagreements are frequent, and often lead to Inquisitors clashing with one another.

Techniques

The techniques of an Ordo Xenos Inquisitor vary depending on the nature of their foe, as most specialise in countering one particular alien threat. However, any Inquisitor might encounter an unexpected xenos on their travels; their duty is to destroy them and record such encounters for future study.

When opportunities arise, xenos are captured and dissected to learn about their biology and any weaknesses. This is especially true of newly discovered species. The Ordo Xenos maintain vast archiviums of information on xenos threats. Many Inquisitors also rely on networks of contacts and informants among @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.h6Z6Ia2q5RkRUlDG]{Rogue Traders} to stay abreast of xenos activity across the sector. Some have contacts within the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus}, who are often key in identifying and understanding alien technologies.

Part of the Ordo’s remit is to control the spread of information about xenos species within the Imperium. This involves everything from propaganda techniques to mind erasure and servitorisation. Citizens are better protected if they are n’ot aware of the threats faced by the Imperium, and better submit to the God-Emperor’s will if they believe the dominance of Mankind is inevitable. The Ordo’s Inquisitors spend considerable time cleaning up the aftermath of xenos incursions, as it is crucial to ensure the Imperium’s borders appear essentially impenetrable.

Forces of the Imperium

One Inquisitor, their retinue, and, by extension, their acolyte cells are rarely enough to investigate a potential threat thoroughly. They are undoubtedly insufficient to march against their enemies on a broader scale, let alone wage an emergent war. Inquisitors need to rely upon the local forces of the Imperium to do so, wielding their limitless authority to order them into battle.

Beyond forces drawn from the leading institutions of the Adeptus Terra, the Inquisition has ties with unique specialist forces across the Imperium and within the Macharian Sector that can bring nigh-apocalyptic might to bear if they are justified in being called upon.

The Deathwatch

Known as the Shield that Slays, these Space Marines are stationed across the galaxy, watching for and fighting back xenos invasions wherever they find them — deployed in precision-action kill teams, they cut to the heart of a xenos threat and purge it from within. The positions and quantity of their Watch Fortress bases in the Macharian Sector is a secret shared between the Deathwatch and the sector’s Inquisitors.

The Deathwatch works closely with Ordo Xenos Inquisitors, particularly when evaluating or developing strategies to purge their shared enemies and build upon each other’s battlefield intelligence. However, one organisation is not subservient to the other; like an Inquisitor’s limitless authority, the Deathwatch has autonomy and sacred oaths that are not to be trifled with.

The Adepta Sororitas

Members of the Adepta Sororitas share the fundamental aims of the Ordo Hereticus, so they are natural allies. Any Sister encountered is duty-bound to aid in the fight against heresy, and though they might lack subtlety, they can be a great boon to any acolyte cell. As a whole, they are a formidable fighting force, a spearhead that draws with it the militant might of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Ministorum}.

Their power armour-clad Orders Militant lead the charge on the battlefield, followed by scores of Ecclesiarchical crusaders, death cult assassins, and legions of faithful Frateris Militia. Together, they are a force that epitomises the might of faith in the God-Emperor and his Imperium. As such, Radical acolytes should watch their behaviour around these excessively devout and puritanical warriors, lest they become placed on the wrong side of the Sisters’ crusade, in among the heretics.

The Order Famulous of the Hallowed Glass, based on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Macharia}, works closely with the sector’s Inquisitors. Since the aftermath of the Macharian Crusade, their task has been to effectively police noble houses across the sector, which might require discreet investigation and the threat of force, to prevent another @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-macharian-heresy]{Macharian Heresy from taking root.

Based on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.Cx5xblXFKBJu9lrf]{Saint Isidore’s Rest}, the Order Militant of the Charred Veil operates primarily within the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.UbH7oOtTYfjFlKRt]{Gallosque Nebula} and has a fortress cathedral on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Macharia}. They support missionary expeditions sent to worlds wrought with heresy or not yet fully converted to the God-Emperor’s service. These sisters have vast experience fighting Orks, having defended their shrine world countless times from xenos invasions.

The Grey Knights

The Grey Knights are the most secretive, deadly, and most specialised of all Space Marine Chapters. They are based on Saturn’s moon of Titan, a closely guarded secret even among Inquisitors of the Ordo Malleus.

Furthermore, they maintain clandestine patrols and other secret bases across all sectors of the Imperium from where they can rapidly deploy. Their Prognosticars — specialist psykers within their order — burn their minds to ruin in desperate efforts to detect fluctuations in the Warp from great distances. This allows the Knights to set off towards incursions long before their daemonic scheming begins. It is not unheard of for Inquisitors who request their aid to find one of their Strike Cruisers already inbound to their location.

These mysterious Space Marines are the God-Emperor’s finest daemon hunters, each an accomplished and dominating psyker. Their knowledge of hunting daemons is second to none and closely guarded; even the most long-lived Ordo Malleus Inquisitors would only scratch the surface of their knowledge and capabilities. Yet each organisation has its role in safeguarding the Imperium from the horrors of the Warp. The Grey Knights are the God-Emperor’s holy hammer — a blunt-edged vengeful manifestation made to enact total obliteration — while the Ordo Malleus is His deft eyes, ears, and exacting judgement, able to work within the Imperium without raising suspicion.

ESCALATION

The information outlined in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.tFbQS9Pwk46yjwFq]{Inquisition Player’s Guide} covers the breadth of options available and their potential ramifications, from local Vigilite squads to ceramite-clad Space Marines. Players and GMs should understand what bringing these forces to bear means for their current investigation, the local populace, and the locales in which they operate. As GM, your players and their characters must understand why they cannot solve a problem simply by crash-landing a drop pod of Space Marines on it. The forces of the Imperium are vast and powerful, but most lack subtlety in their approach and cause collateral damage. Espionage and intelligence are the true tools of the Inquisition; employing the God-Emperor’s mightiest warriors should only be viewed as a last resort when circumstances are far beyond reproach.

The Macharian Sector

Centuries ago, after Lord Solar Macharius’ death, the seventy bloody years of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-macharian-heresy]{Macharian Heresy} began. It brought uprisings and mass heresy across hundreds of worlds in the sector, and many took the opportunity to throw off Imperial rule. In this turbulent period, Adeptus Astartes and Adepta Sororitas were dispatched in vast numbers to restore order. Several Inquisitors arrived to help crush dissent, including the infamous Fidus Kryptman of the @UUID[.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos}.

His bold and brutal tactics crushed insurgence on multiple worlds and brought whole systems back into the God-Emperor’s domain using merciless methods. Kryptman set the bar for Inquisitors operating in the sector, demanding discretion, ruthlessness, and utmost ingenuity. By the end of the era, he was named Hero of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-macharian-heresy]{Macharian Heresy}.

Even after the worst of the fighting and the epoch brought to a close, some worlds continued to resist when @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#machariuss-generals]{General Sejanus’s} armies tried to wrest back control. In contrast, others submitted reluctantly, only to cause trouble later. Despite greater heresies left in the past, shadow wars constantly threaten to ravage the sector, wrought by ongoing rebellions and underhanded power grabs. Since the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#silence-and-darkness]{Noctis Aeterna}, only a handful of Inquisitors remain in operation, yet they are needed now more than ever.

Rogue psykers are a growing concern across the sector. Due to the Noctis Aeterna, many Black Ships were lost to the Warp, and others were considerably delayed in fulfilling their duties. Some planets are sitting upon a surplus of captive psykers with little space left to put any more. Others have taken to executing the excess but fear failing to fulfil their tithe. Either way, more rogue psykers have slipped through the cracks of Lex and bureaucracy and are free to plot and garner their terrible powers.

The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum} struggles to stamp out or re-educate wayward Imperial cults on many worlds. Divergence from the Imperial Creed in any way is outright heresy. The masses stand divided between wild interpretations and false prophecies. This gap has left room for apocryphal preachers and pretenders to step in and sway countless souls towards heresy under the influence of vile xenos or the Ruinous Powers.

Many heresies stem from the sector’s noble houses, some still originating from the power grab that punctuated the beginning of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-macharian-heresy]{Macharian Heresy}.

The sector’s nobility engages in underhanded plots and quiet betrayals, allowing them to slither into positions of power or keep what they believe is their rightful place. The worst of them are backed by xenos or daemonic influence. Here, the Inquisition must tread carefully not to upset the balance of power.

Several xenos species are known to have an interest in the sector, some having occupied worlds prior to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW]{Lord Solar Macharius's} conquest. Rumours say there are planets where they surreptitiously maintain control and expanses of the void where they quietly hide and watch the Imperium like a predator preparing to strike. Too many inexplicably slip past the sector’s borders; the Inquisition must prevent these incursions.

Worse still, there is growing evidence of daemonic interference across the sector, particularly in the Yix and Andosk Subsectors and the fringes of the mysterious Ayzinith Abyss. The Ruinous Powers are manipulating heretical cults across the sector, urging them to conduct profane rituals with the ultimate goal of opening Warp rifts, allowing daemons to slip into reality and lay waste or claim to the Imperium.

Inquisitor Lord Hieronymo Drake’s death during the Noctis Aeterna left a power vacuum in the Macharian Inquisition — respected by all Inquisitors of the sector; he was crucial in ensuring Inquisitors had the support they needed to fight the Imperium’s enemies. In the wake of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#silence-and-darkness]{Days of Blinding}, his former apprentice, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.CbYL1IrXodXyGuyV]{Sylvestrine Horst}, calls the Macharian Inquisition to Conclave. She hopes to strengthen unity among the Inquisitors of the sector in the halls of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W.JournalEntryPage.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} — the Inquisition’s holding on Suluk, a moon of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy]{Persepolis}. It will soon host some of the most influential and powerful Humans in the Imperium. Together, united or divided, they will determine the fate of the Macharian Sector.

This is the current state of the Macharian Sector and setup to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W]{The Heresies Macharia}. There you can begin the decades-long campaign to save the Sector. The Macharian Inquisition’s most prominent Inquisitors are described in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40]{Roleplaying Inquisitors}; each plays a part in the Heresies to come and can act as Patron to your players, tentative ally, or secret enemy.
