pages.name: Philosophies
pages.text:
Inquisitors are a diverse group of individuals, each with their own beliefs and goals that drive their methods. Their philosophical views land somewhere between the scale of Puritan and Radical, and it is common for an Inquisitor’s philosophy to shift towards one of these extremes given time and the ever more terrible decisions they face.

An Inquisitor’s philosophy may be a private matter, a set of beliefs that privately influence their actions, or it might prompt them to join a group or faction of like-minded individuals. Depending on how Radical a philosophy is, its followers may have to keep it a secret, especially from their peers within the Holy Orders. So while on the surface an Inquisitor shares the goals of their Ordo, they likely have their own furtive agenda they are working on beneath the surface.

Always remember that an Inquisitor believes they are doing the right thing for the Imperium through the lens of their Puritan or Radical philosophy; this is a core ideal and driving force for any Inquisitor. Their philosophy should not drive them to act selfishly or for characteristically malevolent reasons.

During @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.ZzHsqdssD6GJyhDE]{Inquisitor Patron creation}, discuss with your players what Philosophy their Patron should follow and whether they lean more Puritan or Radical. Options presented in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.ZzHsqdssD6GJyhDE.JournalEntryPage.lFT1A8eGYjmaOne2]{Inquisition Player’s Guide} and their accompanying summaries are good starting points, but this section fleshes out the existing and more esoteric options.

If players are unsure or undecided, feel free to introduce their Patron’s Philosophy further down the line once they have had a chance to explore the setting and run a few missions, or feel free to roll on the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.1gzUacqcHeN4JwkK]{Inquisition Philosophies} Table to determine it randomly. A Patron’s Philosophy can be a significant part of their general mystique. Discuss with your players if they want to know their Philosophy upfront. They may grant you carte blanche to choose one on their behalf to better suit the stories you want to tell. Remember, it is not uncommon for Radical Inquisitors to present themselves in a more Puritan light to survive, then dramatically reveal their true Philosophy later. On the other hand, Puritan Inquisitors can appear just as unhinged as some Radical counterparts, the purity they strive for taking a toll upon them, or imbued with sheer fervor for the tenets they follow.

All to say, an Inquisitor of one stance can easily be mistaken for the other, which is another tool you can use to build their Patron’s character.

A Patron’s Philosophy guides what variety of stories your players wish to explore. In terms of Inquisitor Patron creation, Philosophy replaces Motivation but fulfils the same drive. While characters investigate the Inquisition’s threats, aspects of their Patron’s Philosophy quietly bubble away in the background. Their Philosophy can act as the setup for entire missions or buildup to your campaign’s grand finale, where their Patron might achieve their Philosophy’s goals or see their hopes dashed — by their enemies or even by the players’ hands.

From a character’s perspective, often more concerned with their survival, a Patron’s Philosophy primarily represents ways they could get into trouble. Consider how you react to a player character’s decisions from their Patron’s point of view. Whether a character’s beliefs align with their Patron’s is up to the player at hand — but do they even have the power to oppose or work around what their Inquisitor demands of them? How would their Patron punish them for disobeying the tenets of their Philosophy? You will need to figure out these aspects, but staying consistent in these manners will undoubtedly enrich their Patron’s character.

@TableHTML[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.1gzUacqcHeN4JwkK]{Philosophy}

pages.name: The Inquisition & the Imperium
pages.text:
The following sections discuss the Inquisition’s place in the Imperium: the truth of an Inquisitor’s limitless authority, what laws they must adhere to, and how they deal with the multitudinous factions of the Adeptus Terra and beyond. Some of these aspects have been outlined in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.tFbQS9Pwk46yjwFq]{The Holy Orders of the Inquisition Player’s Guide} to instil knowledge required by players and their acolyte characters. Rather, the following information is for the benefit of GMs to understand better the Inquisitors they roleplay and the limits of these powerful and enigmatic characters.

Power Scale

While their means and methods vary wildly, all Inquisitors have a limitless authority. In theory, this is absolute; they can commandeer any resources they might need and command everyone from the heads of noble houses to decorated generals of the Astra Militarum to work on their behalf.

In practice, however, Inquisitors must constantly fight for their authority to count as such. The galaxy is vast and far from Terra, and an Inquisitor may find themself at the edge of the God-Emperor’s influence. Even on worlds that pay their tithes to the God-Emperor, the governors may claim the Inquisition is no better than a myth or recognise their authority without significant backup. Often, Inquisitors can rely only on themselves.

The work of an Inquisitor sometimes requires making enemies as well as friends, and the nature of their foes often means that the longer an Inquisitor pursues their prey, the more they are tempted, tested, and possibly even tainted. So the more power and resources an Inquisitor accumulates, the more Liabilities they have. Working out an Inquisitorial Patron’s history leads to adding certain Boons and Liabilities, or, if preferred, selecting Boons and Liabilities might naturally inspire a particular backstory.

Acolyte to Inquisitor

For characters who play Inquisitorial agents, the route from lowly acolyte to Inquisitor or beyond is a long and dangerous road that might take several lifetimes to achieve. To preserve knowledge and skills in an organisation as secretive and dispersed as the Inquisition, rejuvenat extends the life of the most esteemed members. Anyone who has lasted long enough to reach a position of supreme power and influence in the Inquisition is unlikely to be superseded soon. Some Inquisitors train acolytes to join their fight as fully-fledged Interrogators, but few take more than one or two at a time, and success is never guaranteed. For these characters, having an Inquisitor as a Patron might be the next best thing to a personal mentor, and impressing their Patron might even improve their standing with the Inquisition.

Resources

Members of Ordos Majoris might have access to the data and resources of their Ordo when preparing for a mission, but less so once a mission is underway. Inquisitors are powerful, but they are still individual mortals standing against a hostile galaxy of nightmarish foes. Theoretically, any Inquisitor can ask for help from another in those rare cases when they meet, but even Inquisitors of the same Ordo cannot afford to trust unquestioningly.

It is often safer for an Inquisitor to commandeer staff as necessary in their work, individuals whose ignorance makes them easier to control. Some of these are used and discarded, while those proven loyal and useful become acolytes. Acolytes face the same horrors as their superiors but operate without the benefit of experience and only second-hand authority from their Inquisitor while in the field.

In the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96]{Macharian Sector}, the most successful Inquisitors tend to learn all they can about the sector and its significant players and then set themselves on gaining personal power and influence within. Inquisitors who have been in the sector longest have had time to develop networks, make contacts, and earn favours. Some work alone with nothing but their personal weapon to rely on or recruit a small, select team, while others may have Inquisitorial training facilities or a null-prison available, a large staff and military force, sanctioned psykers, vast databanks, voidships, and a seemingly endless fortune of solars.

If the characters’ Patron is an Inquisitor, then their Boons make clear the resources they can make available. Since an Inquisitor who works alone and undercover is less likely to become a Patron than one with means and influence, they likely have something to offer the characters, and the more solars they have at their disposal, the more likely they are to pay the characters well.

Eyes and Ears

Many acts of Inquisitors and their agents are never revealed to the masses, but the Inquisition is said to have eyes everywhere. Whenever a character prevents a catastrophe, destroys a shipment of xenos weapons, or exposes a cult, there is a surprisingly good chance that the Inquisition will eventually become aware of it.

Many Patrons monitor their agents closely, but even if a particular Patron does not communicate with an Ordo, there are other ways the Inquisition might find out. Either another Inquisitor will have been conducting a similar investigation and share the report with their Ordo, or an Inquisitor’s contacts in the Arbites or local police force might inform them after the fact.

Messages and reports take significant time to cross the Imperium, but most Inquisitors keep meticulous records and are always interested in promising agents or contacts. Many Inquisitorial agents can make reputations for themselves without even realising it.

Interfactional Interactions

In theory, Inquisitors, with their limitless authority, can command armies and order planetary governors to do their bidding. In practice, plenty of planetary governors and military commanders might make things difficult if an Inquisitor makes unreasonable demands, especially if they work alone and might be considered a problem easily removed. Most Inquisitors would soon correct such attitudes, but none let such petty obstacles compromise a mission.

Imperial agents across the sector fear the Inquisition, but there are systems in the Macharian Sector where Imperial presence is minimal or completely absent. An Inquisitor might have to bring Imperial forces with them rather than rely on the compliance of the locals or simply work alone. While working alone presents challenges, it appeals to those Inquisitors who are reluctant to trust anyone during the ongoing shadow war. A solitary operation can also be an advantage for undercover work. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists} often actively resist Imperial rule and Imperial agents of all kinds, including Inquisitors. Inquisitorial agents might have to conceal their true identities and even stoop to making dangerous deals with criminals to gain information — especially those tracking aspects of the Silent Trade.

There are several wealthy, powerful, and well-travelled @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.h6Z6Ia2q5RkRUlDG]{Rogue Trader Dynasties} in the Macharian Sector. They travel across the sector and beyond Imperial space, especially from the borders of the Cytheris Subsector. Many captains claim noble lineage, and their ancient warrants grant them freedoms most citizens can only imagine. They are still obliged to bow to the authority of the Inquisition of course, but some might overlook this when encountering a single Inquisitorial agent, alone in the void. Far from civilisation, authority means little in the face of a gun.

Given the turbulent nature of the Macharian Sector, the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.cvpsLwcsXf4myIpK]{Adeptus Administratum} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} work closely together. Inquisitorial authority is greater than either, but an Inquisitor might require the cooperation of both in their work. Between them, the Administratum are responsible for the smooth running of the sector. While the Administratum’s influence in the Macharian Sector is not as universal as it once was, the Astra Militarum’s power seems to have grown since the Noctis Aeterna, with its close ties to the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.WE1MLa1KVRHMD8wJ.JournalEntryPage.P8rukYyQeyPJ1ubs]{Imperial Navy} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum}. The Astra Militarum may be the most powerful organisation in this sector, and they are generally on good terms with the Inquisition. Inquisitors would do well to nurture contacts within this organisation. But some may believe that the Militarum has grown too influential here and would refuse to bow to Inquisitorial authority if there was a disagreement. However, this has not yet been a problem, as their goals typically align.

Inquisitors, especially of the Ordo Hereticus, work closely with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.upGG1JZPDbC7dpJJ]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica} since both work to identify psykers and contain them. In the Macharian Sector, the work of the Adeptus Astra Telepathica has been made more difficult by problems with communications, transport routes, and the growing number of psykers. Inquisitors are actively trying to ease the growing burden on the Black Ships, and ties are particularly close between the Inquisition and Adeptus Astra Telepathica.

Inquisitors may well encounter the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.CBLdHnFWFqdhfRKx]{Sisters of Silence} in the Macharian Sector since their work on the Black Ships carries them all across the Imperium. Elite psyker hunters, their mission is to collect and transport unsanctioned psykers for the Astra Telepathica. This task often causes them to work alongside Inquisitorial agents of the Ordo Hereticus. They are useful allies, immune to psychic and daemonic power, as long as an Inquisitor's purpose remains aligned with theirs.

The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus} is afforded greater freedom under the ancient Treaty of Mars than most factions within the Imperium are premitted. This has often been a point of contention between the Inquisition and the Cult Mechanicus, in the Macharian Sector as elsewhere. Several of the sector's forge worlds are under surveillance, and many Tech-Priests are aware of these intrusions, further souring relations.

The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum} is generally grateful for the work of the Inquisition since both organisations are united in their devotion to the God-Emperor above all else. The Ministorum is quite powerful in the Macharian Sector, at least among those worlds that the Astra Militarum has successfully repacified since the Noctis Aeterna. Nevertheless, some Inquisitors see the obsession with the Saint Solar Macharius as dangerous. On some worlds, the saint seems to receive more devotion than the God-Emperor. More than one member of the Adeptus Ministorum is currently under suspicion of encouraging such behaviour, and the local Adeptus Ministorum bristles at the implication that it requires such scrutiny.

Lex Imperialis

Every sector, subsector, and world of the Imperium has its own set of laws, but the Lex Imperialis sits above these laws, consisting of the God-Emperor’s own word and must take precedence. It is a vast, complicated, and ever-growing collection of decrees and mandates, so numerous that most citizens of the Imperium could never hope to learn them all.

Theoretically, Inquisitors function above local laws, remaining bound only by the Lex Imperialis. However, by respecting local laws, Inquisitors are more likely to find planetary governors and local rulers more cooperative and avoid trouble with local enforcement. After all, most enforcers, such as the ubiquitous @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.actors.Actor.O49jTi2TzoFQH5GT]{Macharian Vigilites}, answer directly to their planetary governor. Adhering to the letter of the Lex also makes challenges from other Inquisitors less likely

It is the Inquisitor’s duty to enforce Imperial Law wherever they can. If a world resists the Imperium for no reason other than its leaders’ greed, then an Inquisitor is likely to inform the Arbites and leave them to their work. Sometimes, a world resists for more nefarious reasons: the workings of a daemonic cult, the foul promises of a Chaos God, or the influence of a powerful, unsanctioned psyker. In these cases, an Inquisitor’s presence and authority are necessary, drawing together the Imperium’s forces and applying their knowledge in combatting such a threat.

The enforcement of the Lex Imperialis is necessary for the continued existence of the Imperium through its bearing on the Imperial Tithe. Imperial worlds must all pay a tithe to the Emperor, whether in crops, troops, materiel, or captured psykers for the League of Black Ships. Obedience in this matter is non-negotiable, as from the perspective of the Inquisition, all should understand that the God-Emperor’s tithe benefits all. Yet, in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96]{Macharian Sector}, there are still worlds that resist the Emperor’s rule and are lax with what they provide.

Given that the Imperium is stretched so far across the galaxy, it is easy for a planet’s indiscretions to be overlooked for a considerable time as long as they pay their tithe. Many worlds, particularly after a period of turbulence, might forget the Lex Imperialis’ importance. The arrival of Imperial agents, such as an Inquisitor, should be enough to remind them. In these cases, local governance may attempt to conceal evidence of their infringements, and it is up to the Inquisitor to determine whether these are petty crimes that can be ignored, dangerous violations that must be forcefully dealt with, or instead used as leverage to further their goals.

Most worlds are likely to deal with some element of criminality in their society. Some citizens live outside the law, using secrecy to avoid detection or bribes to avoid punishment. Others might even use knowledge of the Lex Imperialis to their advantage, especially if it can override local laws they might otherwise fall foul of. An Inquisitor who needs to circumvent the law may use similar tactics as necessary, especially if they are attempting to conceal their identity as an Inquisitor or those of their acolytes.

In Imperium Maledictum, it is up to the GM to decide how much of an obstacle local enforcers will be to the characters’ mission. On one world, a citizen’s activities might be severely limited by arbitrary local laws, while on another, chaotic lawlessness might make the characters' activities dangerous. Inquisitorial agents are likely to find their authority respected on some worlds, whereas on others, they would be wise to keep their associations to themselves. The prevalence of Imperial Law on all these worlds means that Chaos or xenos cults, unsanctioned psykers, and criminal enterprises are all likely to work in secret and outside of the law. However, there may be worlds where the local law enforcers, the government, or noble houses are corrupt, and the characters must actively break local laws to obey Imperial ones.

Shadow Wars

As they serve only the Emperor, answering to no other authority, Inquisitors must watch each other for signs of corruption. A traitorous Inquisitor is a hazardous thing, and it is the duty of all Inquisitors to police each other. Unfortunately, since Inquisitors vary so much in their philosophies and methods, what is considered heresy by one is considered necessary by another. After enemies of the Imperium, the greatest threat to an Inquisitor is another Inquisitor.

An Inquisitor who suspects another of corruption or treason may deal with the matter personally if they can. If they are not certain or not confident in their ability to capture or kill the Inquisitor in question, they may call upon other Inquisitors to form a Conclave and discuss the matter. Depending on the power and influence of the Inquisitors involved, this may be a small group whose existence will remain a secret or a grander assemblage, including Inquisitor Lords.

The Conclave investigates the suspect and then debates the best way to proceed. The Inquisitor may be called upon to defend themself personally or be kept unaware of the Conclave’s existence. There is no set procedure to follow since every case, and the threats involved, will differ. If in doubt, the Conclave often decides that in the best interests of the Imperium, the Inquisitor must be eliminated since a corrupt Inquisitor is an incredibly dangerous threat.

These wars must be fought in the shadows of the Imperium. The factions of the Adeptus Terra learning of an Inquisitor’s betrayals or shifts towards heresy undermines the limitless authority they need to protect the Imperium. An Inquisition that appears in any way divided is therefore ineffective. The same goes for the citizenry; though fear aids in asserting their authority, Inquisitors should never be seen as outright enemies of Lex-abiding people.

pages.name: The Inquisition
pages.text:
‘I, Inquisitor Lord Hieronymo Drake, authorise, order and declare Exterminatus upon the fourth planet of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.lpu6iuTHw50UavbI]{Belnshudha}. The planet is lost to an immeasurable foe and is irredeemably corrupted. We must ensure no one can tread upon its surface again. I cannot make it to my extraction vessel, so these are my final words: despite the necessity of atrocity that is about to occur, know you have served the God-Emperor’s will this day. Canis Vator Avit Abominus.’

— Final order of Inquisitor Lord Hieronymo Drake @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#battle-group-fortis]{Battle Group Fortis}

The Inquisition is the Imperium’s most terrifying and secretive organisation. They exist beneath the surface of ordinary Imperial society, subtly influencing the everyday lives of citizens in the public consciousness, and yet they wield the ultimate authority across all walks of life.

Inquisitors across the galaxy protect the Imperium from terrible and insidious foes. They consider themselves justified in taking any necessary measure to fulfil this sacred charge, including sacrificing the lives of those they seek to protect.

By an Inquisitior’s word alone, thousands have perished in a moment, High Lords have been brought low, noble lines extinguished, and entire worlds have burned. Were it not for the magnitude of the threats they guard against and the dire necessity of their actions, the Inquisition would indeed be counted among the most terrible scourges to befall the Imperium.

The threats they face are myriad and complex, insidious and brutal, enigmatic and overwhelming. The heretic, the daemon, the xenos — each gnaws at the underbelly of the Imperium, robbing it of strength never to be recovered. Inquisitors know that their task is one pitted against inevitability. Though the Imperium continues to claim new worlds, it cannot stem the tide of losses — with every Astra Cartographica survey, former strongholds are erased, snuffed out by the growing darkness.

Most believe Inquisitors stand united against these enemies of the Imperium; few know that the Inquisition wars within itself. Inquisitors are divided by their philosophies and methodologies — their limitless authority means most grow accustomed to their orders going unquestioned. Only another Inquisitor has the right to judge one of their kind, and so they often find themselves at odds. Branding one another as puritans, radicals, or heretics, they fight an endless shadow war beneath the auspices of the Adeptus Terra, each warring for what they think is the best way to protect the Imperium.

The Inquisition is ultimately necessary for Humanity’s survival, its every excess, its ever hidden crime a tithe of blood and suffering that will one day come due. Without the Inquisition, the Imperium would have long ago been devoured by its enemies within, without, and beyond. This knowledge is a harrowing burden to bear, and few have the force of will, the strength of soul, or perhaps even the arrogance needed to become one of the Emperor’s Inquisitors.

Players lacking sufficient clearance should beware of this sanctioned tome; it is intended for the GM's eyes only! However, players and GMs alike will be interested in the Inquisition Player’s Guide, a companion book containing rules for @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.QU6vEOUu69z190da]{Inquisition character creation}, new options for existing @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.ZzHsqdssD6GJyhDE]{Patrons and characters}, and many new @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.J8NVn5iNgM57cKmw.JournalEntryPage.2MqLlcSMDCxkumCk]{Skills}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.J8NVn5iNgM57cKmw.JournalEntryPage.ZoyVpQ2Wtbz5JA3x]{Talents}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.3mzwixuzgerGUpu1]{Psychic Powers} and iconic @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.BbyZqcWs3HbrAO3Y]{Inquisitorial Equipment} to outfit and reward players. It contains a host of new rules — most importantly the new @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.KbejcPMug5gfoWWz]{Subtlety} mechanic which is also used throughout this book.

pages.name: Amalathian
pages.text:
Amalathian

"This is HIS IMPERIUM, and shall continue AS HE MANDATED! For a mere mortal to deign to change even the most minute cog of its workings is blasphemous arrogance. This sector is a testament to His divine will, and I am an arbiter of His merciless judgement"

Amalathian Tenets:

  • The God-Emperor’s divine plan is unfolding as it should.

  • The status quo within the Imperium must be maintained at all costs.

  • Strength is achieved through unity.

Modus Operandi:

Strike down emergent heresy within the Adeptus Terra, especially Radical Inquisitors. Cooperate and promote unity with all factions of the Adeptus Terra, sharing information with them wherever necessary. Quell any interfactional infighting that threatens to destabilise the Imperium.

For millennia, the Emperor has led His Imperium through the darkness of a hostile galaxy, miraculously conducting a plan beyond mortal comprehension to ensure the domination of Mankind. This is the core belief of the Amalathian philosophy, swearing absolute fealty to the Emperor and believing with unquestioning absolutism that every machination of His bellicose realm is operating strictly as intended.

The monolithic Amalath, the largest mountain of the world Gathalamor in Segmentum Solar, can be considered the spiritual genesis of this Puritan philosophy and the Macharian Crusade. The Conclave held there at the dawn of the 41st millennium saw mighty exemplars of the Imperium redouble their oathbound dedication to the Master of Mankind, fervent in believing that all past obstacles were merely preparations for what was to come.

For Amalathians, change heralds disaster, and any misguided attempt to ‘improve’ the labyrinthine workings of the Imperium must be prevented. Any action outside of His will could have dire, unforeseen consequences. Radical philosophies of any kind are akin to heresy to the Puritan Amalathians, but their hard line nature can appear Radical to their peers.

Amalathians in the Macharian Sector often operate secretly and in isolation, allowing other Imperial factions to perform their crucial work and prioritising any threats that might destabilise existing power structures. Forbidden knowledge must remain proscribed, and the Inquisition must remain an unseen force, protecting the Imperium from infestations by xenos beyond His realm and daemons beyond reality, preserving all institutions from the heresy of change.

Roleplaying an Amalathian:

  • They wield a holier-than-thou attitude, holding their moral superiority over the heads of heretics like a guillotine. Yet for those who put the needs of the Imperium before their lives, Amalathians hold a quiet admiration and respect.

  • To protect the status quo, they must be experts in it; they should know the internal machinations and bureaucracies of the Imperium inside out.

  • They should be critical of any purported change or deviation from the Lex Imperialis or Imperial Creed and readily punish those who strive to alter the Imperium’s laws or institutions.

House Alencar

The party’s Patron is investigating House Alencar on planet Paleo. The noble house has introduced changes to improve living conditions for their workforce at the cost of their economic output; some of these unsanctioned reforms are already gaining headway within other local houses. The party must uncover what heresy has caused this shift in the noble house’s ideals.

Stalemate of Tithe

Osmodia Beta’s planetary tithe has come to a standstill. The local @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus} believe their forge world should be re-tooled to produce Imperial Titans, but the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} has outright blocked their proposal, knowing that the billions of las packs the planet typically produces are crucial to defending the sector. The stalemate is causing the planet’s workers to suffer; riots are sure to occur if left unresolved.

pages.name: Horusian
pages.text:
Horusian

"We all serve the God-Emperor and work with what tools we can… Why, then, must we all be at odds?"

Horusian Tenets:

  • One day, the God-Emperor will return, requiring an appropriate vessel to embody.

  • The power of the Warp can be harnessed to create a Divine Avatar or facilitate the process of transferring the God-Emperor’s soul from its current form into the body of a living god.

Modus Operandi:

Maintain strength and status as an upstanding Inquisitor of the Holy Orders. Find ways to pursue necessary research in secret and gather trusted acolytes to your actual cause. Pursue daemonic activity as a means to gather knowledge and test theories.

Horusians follow an offshoot of @UUID[.s88kgPSDiogPL4aB]{Xanthism} and are experts in the nature of daemons and the power of the Warp. For this reason, many are members of the Ordo Malleus, though their views are certainly considered Radical by the rest of their Ordo. Horusians hope for the resurrection of the Emperor but believe that a simple Human form is not enough to house Him. Therefore, they seek ways to create vessels suitable for the God-Emperor’s soul and search for ways to harness the power of the Warp. Most controversially, they hope to one day create a being like the Primarch Horus, a Warp-infused warrior raised as a new — and less destructive — leader of Mankind.

Roleplaying a Horusian:

  • Horusians are extremists for their cause but refrain from openly displaying their fanaticism unless pushed to the edge. Long-lived Horusians are masters of self-control.

  • They know their beliefs are heretical in the eyes of the Imperium. To survive, they must maintain levels of subterfuge that can rebuff the Inquisition itself. They would not suffer a breach in their security from anyone, especially their acolytes.

  • Horusians constantly test the loyalties of their acolytes, putting them into situations to show their trustworthiness. They are only brought into the Inquisitor’s retinue when they prove utterly loyal or enthusiastically believe in the Horusian philosophy.

  • The powers of the Warp should never be viewed as a fast route to success, but this is precisely what Horusians are doing. They are constantly battling with temptation.

A new host

The party’s Patron has discovered a heretical cult on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.JbRBjmzRfWtxIo40]{Leonova}, who appear close to creating a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.M6XWkYc0lfuKl2hU]{daemonhost}. The party has been tasked with infiltrating the cult and ensuring their plans come to fruition but do not spill out of control. Afterwards, purge the cult, retrieve the daemonhost, and work with a local smuggling cartel to deliver it to a secure location.

Watchful eyes

The party’s Patron believes another Inquisitor’s agents are watching them for signs of heresy. The party must uncover these spies and find a suitable way to dispose of them — either prove to the spies that the Inquisitor is above board or find a way to dispose of them that will not raise further suspicions from their Inquisitor.

pages.name: Isstvanism
pages.text:
ISSTVANISM

"The greatest heroes are forged by war and tempered by suffering."

Isstvanian Tenets:

  • Conflict is vital to the survival of the Imperium.

  • Strengthen Mankind through ongoing adversity.

  • Humanity’s greatest achievements are results of war and conflict.

Modus Operandi:

Promote warmongering across the Imperium by instilling superstition, suspicion, and the need for violence within the citizenry. Seek out anyone with a base of power and work their phobias and prejudices until they march to war, believing it was their idea to begin with.

Isstvanians believe in the evolutionary power of war and incite conflict to strengthen Humanity across the Imperium. Others think them Radical, but they see evidence to confirm their beliefs throughout the Imperium’s history, where great generals proved the strength and ingenuity of men on the battlefield and in the void. And they see it in the current Imperium, where the wealthy have grown soft and the masses weak. They believe war drives invention and pushes Humanity to improve. At the same time, the destruction it wreaks clears the way for new and better societies across the Imperium, something sure to please the Emperor.

Isstvanians see the Macharian Crusade as the sector’s golden age but will not stand aside and let it slip into a decadent peace now. With the high military presence and turbulent politics here, Isstvanians can work subtly, nudging local governors into resisting Imperial rule. Such work, if exposed, would damage the relations between the Inquisition and local Imperial forces. Of course, such machinations are not easy to identify or prove.

While Isstvanians rarely declare their philosophy, many are sympathetic to their cause in the Inquisition and the Astra Militarum.

Many rely upon the Imperium’s war machine to give purpose to their lives or as a means to wield certain powers, just as the Imperium relies upon warfare to survive. However, due to the chaos it can wreak, the Isstvanian tendency to provoke violence wherever they go does not sit well with @UUID[.R7LueEsDUhrSYHNn]{Amalathians} or the Imperium’s bureaucrats.

Roleplaying an Isstvanian:

  • Isstvanians are agitators wherever they go. They will attempt to stir characters up, leading them towards violent solutions or get them to march their forces to war. They will not shy away from stirring up both sides of a conflict to see who comes out on top.

  • To them, every agent, asset, or enemy is little more than a regicide piece in a greater game. They need their ‘pieces’ to always be in top form. They will not suffer from their agent’s pointless minutiae, especially personal issues.

  • Isstvanians are highly calculated individuals. Though they seek to promote warfare, they only act when they know their chosen side can win. Often, their choices and orders appear bizarre or off-target, but everything is in favour of building up to their next coup de grace.

Stand up and Fight

An Ork Waaagh! fleet has been detected moving towards the remote shrine world of Iota Primaris. The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet} will be unable to deploy there on time, and the weary planetary leaders seek ways to evacuate the world. But the Isstvanian Patron sees an opportunity. Characters must travel to Iota Primaris, find what heresy weakens the leadership, oust them, and rally the populace to fight the xenos threat.

Two Hives, Two Heresies

Heresy has taken hold over two hive cities on Opulus Major — Koria and Vinov each have deeply embedded Chaos cults manipulating the leadership. The Isstvanian Patron knows they can save one hive, but only by sacrificing the other. Characters must infiltrate each hive’s leadership and push them to war against the other. One of the two hives will come out on top, rooting out these cults and ultimately becoming stronger to withstand future heresies.

pages.name: Libricar
pages.text:
Libricar

"The foulest rot is corruption that seeps down from on high."

Libricar Tenets:

  • Maintain the status quo within the Imperium at any cost.

  • No one is beyond reproach, be it planetary governors or the lowliest hab rat.

  • Death to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionist}, the revolutionary, and the heretic.

Modus Operandi:

Seek out heresies within the Imperium’s factions and ruling classes. Corruption from within is the greatest threat to the status quo, so purge extensively when it is found. Maintaining the Imperium’s long-term stability is worth any cost, so sacrifices should be made across all levels of society and rule.

Libricaranism is a relatively new philosophy borne in the Calixis Sector. Its adherents believe maintaining the Imperium and the smooth running of its various factions is of supreme importance, and the key to this is ensuring good leadership. If the rulers of planets and organisations across the Imperium were freed from corruption, then the Imperium would be both pure and efficient.

A Radical offshoot of the @UUID[.R7LueEsDUhrSYHNn]{Amalathians}, Libricars also believe in the perfection of the GodEmperor’s plan but fear it has already been corrupted by the greed and corruption of those in power. Since @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW]{Lord Solar Macharius}’s death, the rule of the sector has degraded to the point that some Libricars claim a complete overhaul of the local powers is required. Such claims infuriate Amalathians, and Inquisitors of these two philosophies continually clash.

Libricars seek out the slightest taint or indiscretion in the ruling classes and purge the Imperium of any corrupt individuals. They blame rulers for evidence of corruption within the planet or organisation they rule, so not only do they destroy a cult when they find it, but they execute the rulers who let the cult take root.

Their extreme methods of purification make them unpopular. Like @UUID[.yds9IfgKQlwxLqq6]{Monodominants}, Libricars are known for being overzealous and are quick to resort to drastic measures, such as Exterminatus.

Roleplaying a Libricar:

  • The Libricar philosophy demands that adherents be unyielding and ruthless. Inquisitors expect the same from their acolytes — when wielding extreme measures, they do not expect their authority to be questioned.

  • Knowing, and likely experiencing in the past, that heresy can take root even within the ruling classes of Imperial society, Libricars have little patience or respect for people in positions of power.

  • Libricars know that the greatest threat to their plans is the oversight of other Inquisitors. They are always wary of being spied on, and so typically distance themselves from the rest of the Inquisition or their Ordo. They will not tolerate dissent or any hint of betrayal from those within their retinue.

Suitable replacement

The Inquisitor’s Interrogator, Naevea Green, was sent to usurp the Planetary Governor of Calicot and install less corrupt, more malleable leadership. But the Interrogator deemed herself the only suitable candidate, installing herself and enacting martial law. Clean up Green’s mess and extract her before the populace rises against her and the Inquisition loses its hold on the planet.

HIVE FORLAN

The Governor of Hive Forlan on Desperion has been assassinated. The nobility is pointing to rampant infractionism supposedly led by heretical cults. But intel reports that the Forlan Goods & Services criminal cartel is based there and may be involved. Stability on Desperion must be reasserted — assess the local powers, ensure the most beneficial ruler is put in place, and purge the rest.

pages.name: Monodominant
pages.text:
MONODOMINANT

"Supremacy is both the right and duty of Mankind. In the God-Emperor’s name, all else must fall."

Monodominant Tenets:

  • The Imperium should be the most dominant force in the galaxy.

  • The Imperium can only survive if all opposing forces are eradicated.

  • All impurities within the Imperium must be exterminated.

Modus Operandi:

Seek to purge any xenos or non-human entities that Humanity encounters without compromise. Promote the message of a dominant Humanity within the citizenry. Strive for purity within the Imperium by purging those guilty of witchcraft, heresy, and mutation.

Monodominants are ruthless Puritans who seek to perfect the Imperium and ensure the survival and dominance of Mankind by obliterating non-humans of all kinds, including daemons, mutants, and xenos in all their horrifying forms. Theirs is a militant stance, and they are notorious for ordering Exterminatus in situations where other Inquisitors might seek another solution. They also keenly watch their Inquisitor brethren, searching for even the slightest signs of heresy. They do not hesitate to condemn their peers as heretics and take on the role of their executioner if necessary

They proudly trace the origins of their philosophy back to Inquisitor Goldo’s Monodomination, inscribed in the third century of the 33rd millennium. However, Inquisitor Jeriminus established the philosophy hundreds of years later when he swore to turn Goldo’s idealist vision into a reality. For the Monodominants, the Macharian Crusades stopped too soon. They would have preferred the fleets press on into the dark, annihilating all that is inhuman in their path, but Lord Macharius decided otherwise. Now, they work across the sector to purge any trace of heresy or taint.

Monodominants are seldom as secretive as other Inquisitors, using their reputation and the fear it inspires to encourage citizens to reveal mutants, xenos, and psykers wherever they go. While their cause is in line with the Inquisition’s, their methods are often more destructive than their brethren’s, and their tendency to turn on their own at the slightest suspicion of heresy makes them dangerous to work with.

Roleplaying a Monodominant:

  • Monodominants must be uncompromising in their views and actions. They will never consider allying with xenos, daemonic, or heretical forces. They will prescribe death to anyone in their presence who falters from their stance.

  • Many revere Humanity and its accomplishments, citing Humanity’s victories and most outstanding achievements as reasoning for their beliefs, as much as removing opposition as a necessity for survival.

  • They are less interested in subterfuge than their brethren in the Holy Orders. Monodominants often work out in the open, lean on their authority, act as militant leaders, and wield their terrifying presence openly as a weapon.

UNSANCTIONED TRADE

Informants report that the leaders of several voidports around Kharmin have been trading with xenos entities for additional supplies. Investigate these claims, purge those responsible and install new leadership at the voidports. But act with care; you must use the opportunity to set a trap for the xenos and destroy them.

Mark of the Emperor

Local cults on Pathway have mistaken a new mutation spreading throughout the populace as the God-Emperor’s blessing — improving people’s strength and overall size; some claim to be ‘angels’. Travel to Pathway, seek the source of this mutation, and purge all those affected. Reaffirm the people’s beliefs and get them to turn on these foul mutants.

pages.name: Oblationist
pages.text:
OBLATIONIST

"That you would give your life for the God-Emperor, I have no doubt. But would you damn your soul to protect His Imperium?"

Oblationist Tenets:

  • Taking up the arms of the enemy is a necessary measure of victory.

  • But in doing so, personal damnation and determined sacrifice are inevitable.

  • All Radicals are impure, lacking devotion to sacrifice, and thus must be purged.

Modus Operandi:

Take the Oath of Oblation and a new name with it. Seek out the weapons of the enemy and use them to achieve victory — bind daemons, hoard forbidden knowledge, and employ damnable psykers if required. Wade into the worst heresies and sacrifice yourself to protect the Imperium.

Oblationists are damned, body and soul. They dare to use heretical weapons and powers but do not suffer others to do the same. They believe it is necessary to use the enemy’s weapons, but most mortals cannot be trusted with such power. Oblationists know they are not immune to the taint of the foul weapons and methods they employ and know they are damned for doing so, yet they make the ultimate sacrifice; it is a price worth paying to defend the Imperium with such improved strength.

The Oblationist philosophy hails from the Calixis Sector, where Inquisitor Lord Godella Morn took up daemonic weapons of the enemy to fight against the infernal forces of Chaos during the War of Brass. After her execution, some Inquisitors saw her actions as selfless rather than traitorous. Morn had damned herself to serve the Imperium, and since then, other Oblationists have done the same, not least in the Macharian Sector, wherever daemons and xenos are a constant threat.

As Radical as they come, Oblationists keep their beliefs to themselves. Many Inquisitors, especially of Puritan leanings, would execute them as tainted traitors if they knew the truth.

Yet, with their methods hidden, Oblationists can appear model Inquisitors, whether hunting xenos, battling daemons, or burning out all traces of heresy they find. While they use damned tools in their work, they are ruthless and suffer no such taint in others. They are a danger to all but the most Puritan and careful Inquisitorial agents, anyone who dares to use heretical weapons or xenostech, as well as unfortunate souls who exhibit psychic abilities or bear visible mutation.

Roleplaying an Oblationist:

  • These Inquisitors are utterly bitter characters. It is the root of Oblationism, a white-hot anger fuelled by having lost what others merely throw away, their own sacred purity.

  • They wield their self-corruption as if it were purity in and of itself, which they believe to be an effective justification for action against their Radical peers.

  • While they accept their own self-radicalism, they would never suffer the presence of another ‘lesser’ Radical; they know the Inquisition is loathfully corrupt because of them.

Rescue the radical

A Radical Inquisitor and their retinue have gone missing hunting daemon-worshipping cults near the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.1AsBzkbw2InKayw2]{Azynith Abyss}. Investigate their disappearance as dutiful acolytes should — but if they appear weakened, seize the opportunity to execute them for their heresies and purge their allies; make any necessary sacrifices to ensure the job is done. Taking over their networks and resources would be a great boon to the Oblationist Patron.

Time is of the essence

The characters' Oblationist Patron has discovered heretek activity on Hexas Panan. The forge world is already lost; the Patron is organising an assault on the planet to cleanse it — but they need a team of acolytes to secretly raid the hereteks and retrieve any useful xenotech experiments and equipment before the orbital bombardments begin.

pages.name: Ocularian
pages.text:
OCULARIAN

"To read the future, one must have the capacity to understand it, the will to shape it, and the strength to keep it safe."

Ocularian Tenets:

  • Perfect knowledge of future events is the greatest power in the universe.

  • Protect the future by combatting those who seek to alter fate’s outcome.

  • Knowledge of the future must be treated like forbidden knowledge, kept secret and protected at all costs.

Modus Operandi:

Seek out proven methods of divination. Collate and cross-reference their results to determine the most likely outcome of destiny. Guard these secrets closely; they must not fall into the wrong hands but use them to stay one step ahead of the enemy. Determine the best way to use this knowledge; careful nudges to affect critical moments.

Ocularians do not concern themselves with the present petty concerns of the Inquisition but are obsessed with the desire to foresee the future. Whatever divinatory methods an Ocularian chooses to use, they not only read the future but aim to manipulate it, ensuring that what comes to pass benefits the Imperium.

Ocularian Inquisitors are rare and long considered to operate only in the Calixis Sector of Segmentum Obscrurus. In part because when Ocularians travel across the galaxy for a rumoured divinatory tool or source of information, they do so secretly. The Macharian Sector contains numerous anomalies and sites of interest for Ocularian researchers, who study divinatory forms wherever possible, even if their sources are xenos.

While Ocularians are considered Radical, and their prophetic rituals borderline heretical, they are mostly tolerated. Ocularians keep the details of their practices a closely guarded secret, making their actions seem unpredictable to other Inquisitors. Only with their own do they discuss divinatory tools and methods, informing others only when they have warnings to impart.

Being accepted into the Ocularians involves much more than merely professing to share their beliefs, and many of those who are admitted into their ranks subsequently consider themselves superior to others within the Inquisition.

Roleplaying an Ocularian:

  • Ocularians are obsessive characters — they may appear easily detached from things happening around them, instead focused on their work and its outcomes.

  • Most Ocularians see themselves as protectors of the Imperium’s future, more important than the here and now. A calculated loss today that ensures a better future later is a loss graciously accepted.

  • Despite those points, Ocularians remain loyal to the Inquisition; the knowledge they glean is, after all, for their favour and the defence of the Imperium — even if they may appear aloof at times or the strangest of Radicals in the eyes of their peers.

The saint to-be

The Ocularian Inquisitor’s compiled divinations speak of an Imperial saint coming to light on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok}, one the people desperately need. But evidence of Tzeentchian cults on the planet suggests a likely opposition to this fate. Defeat the cult without causing any commotion, and heed the Inquisitor’s prophecies: ‘protect the severed hand’, ‘hide from the wings of the watcher’, and ‘three boats shall herald their arrival.

Forewarned

The Ocularian Inquisitor has uncovered a ring of heretics producing and selling blasphemous daemon-influenced Tarot. The characters must halt this corruption before it spreads further through the sector’s black markets. The trouble is, the blasphemous Tarot appears reliably divinatory, so the cult always appears to be a step ahead.

pages.name: Phaenonite
pages.text:
Phaenonite

"Without faith to blind us or laws to constrain us, without the limits of morality or sluggishness of bureaucracy, we are free to become the best of Mankind. No one can ever hope to stop us, not the Inquisition or the Militarum, not the daemons who stalk the Warp or xenos who cower in the void."

Phaenonite Tenets:

  • Both the Imperium and the Ruinous Powers must be destroyed.

  • The Imperium should be reborn under Phaenonite leadership.

  • Humanity’s future is a fusion of man and machine, made immortal by the powers of the Warp.

Modus Operandi:

Seek out technologies to understand and control the Warp and its daemons. Gather allies in hereteks and other Radicals, and stockpile powerful weaponry. Subvert the power structures of the Imperium to bring its collapse and free Humanity from its slow death.

The Phaenonites are among the most Radical Inquisitors and have long been declared Excommunicate Traitoris. They no longer serve the God-Emperor and claim they could do a better job of ruling the Imperium than the current regime, an unforgivable heresy in the eye of their former peers. They believe that the survival of Mankind requires mastery of the Warp and all its powers, and they are willing to sacrifice anything to achieve their goal.

The Phaenonites began as a cabal of @UUID[.s88kgPSDiogPL4aB]{Xanthites} who surreptitiously conducted blasphemous experiments on daemon-tainted technology during the Angevin Crusade. They were soon exposed and declared Excommunicate Traitoris. Universally loathed, the Inquisition and Adeptus Mechanicus have attempted to eradicate the Phaenonites, but when quashed in one sector, their adherents only spread to another.

There are signs that the Phaenonites’ pursuit of forgotten and forbidden technologies has drawn them to the Macharian Sector, including rumours of strange automatons and whole settlements forced to undergo horrific experiments. The Adeptus Mechanicus is concerned about tech-heresy, and the sector’s Inquisitors are keen to deal with this potential problem quickly, lest it damage the reputation of the Inquisition as a whole.

Since they are Excommunicate Traitoris, it is the duty of any Inquisitorial agent who encounters a Phaenonite to execute them. This may be extremely difficult since they use forbidden weaponry and employ Chaos cultists as minions. Phaenonites have no moral constraints, are bound only to their own twisted rules, and are experts at subterfuge. They may have brethren working openly within the sector, professing to be of some other philosophy, their true agenda carefully concealed.

Roleplaying a Phaenonite:

  • Phaenonites, having been declared Excommunicate Traitoris, must operate in the dark. Around other Inquisitors, Interrogators, or their agents, they are more likely to present themselves as believers in less Radical philosophies.

  • Phaenonites believe they should be leading the Imperium — their characters are power-hungry and believe themselves to be superior, especially against leadership within the Imperium.

  • Despite how their goals appear, like other Inquisitors, they still believe they are doing the right thing for Humanity. They will still act to defend Humanity from xenos, daemon, and heretics, though they might have a difference of opinion on the latter.

Deploy the stalker

The forge world of Dannock III is ripe for a subtle takeover, but its leadership must first be purged before it is replaced. The Phaenonite Inquisitor asks the characters to aid the heretek Malavont-9- Zeta in deploying their Malatek Stalker to the world — a death cultist augmented with machinery and daemonic power, a veritable assassination engine that can get the job done.

A Heretek's bounty

A Puritan Inquisitor has slain a heretek and gathered the contents of their workshop for analysis and logging before purging it all. The Phaenonite Inquisitor tasks the characters to find the hidden cell of acolytes and recover the heretek’s artefacts before they are all destroyed. Leave no trace behind.

pages.name: Plutonian
pages.text:
PLUTONIAN

"In the fight against Chaos, we use whatever we must to win — because failure is not an option."

Plutonian Tenets:

  • Controlled use of daemonic possession creates warriors resilient to daemonic powers.

  • Through possession, knowledge can be plied from daemons that can ultimately be used against daemonkind or to aid the Imperium.

  • Protect the secrets of the Exorcists Space Marine Chapter.

Modus Operandi:

Investigate daemonic activity across the Imperium and facilitate ongoing experimentations with the Exorcists Chapter. Capture daemons worth studying and return them to the fortress monastery Basilica Malefex on the Exorcist Chapter’s Homeworld of Banish.

The secretive Plutonians are Radicals who seek to harness daemonic possession in order to create formidable daemon hunters. They do not undergo possession themselves but work closely with the Exorcists, an Adeptus Astartes Chapter who specialise in fighting daemons, implanting and removing these daemons to strengthen themselves, and harnessing any forbidden knowledge they may leave behind in the formerly possessed's mind.

The first Plutonians were Ordo Malleus Inquisitors tasked with investigating the Exorcists, given they display an unusual spiritual resistance. These Inquisitors formed the radical theory that the source of this resilience was their close contact with daemons. Working with the Exorcists, Plutonians usually keep close to their homeworld of Banish in the Narasima Straits, but a task force is currently in the Macharian Sector. Rather than joining the fight for the sector’s boundaries, however, they travel from system to system as though searching, or hunting, for something. Rumour has it that a Plutonian Inquisitor travels with them, a Radical member of the Ordo Malleus who occludes the Exorcists’ activities in the sector and whose acolytes aid in the Chapter’s scouting efforts and investigations.

The Plutonians’ experimentation with daemonic possession and exorcism, which they claim leaves subjects more resistant to daemonic influence, would be enough for other Inquisitors to execute them for heresy. They harbour a particular interest in the Chapter’s Broken Ones, daemonhosts with the rare capability to hold indefinite numbers of daemons within them.

Roleplaying a Plutonian:

  • Plutonian Inquisitors must operate with the utmost secrecy — in the presence of other Inquisitors or acolytes, they would never reveal their true identity, philosophy or intentions.

  • Their philosophy leans on the idea that great knowledge can be obtained from unconventional means — though characteristically radical behaviour, Plutonian Inquisitors are rare open-minded characters.

  • Plutonian Inquisitors are used to dealing with daemons and possessed individuals, so it would take much to shatter their composure when facing such foes.

Whispers of the abyss

A Broken One on the Exorcists' prison-craft known as the Purgatomb has whispered omens concerning the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96]{Azynith Abyss}, speaking of a planet-devouring daemonic threat. A Librarian has been dispatched with the Broken One and Plutonian Inquisitor in tow to investigate these dire omens — characters are required to complete more discreet aspects of the investigation, chasing down local cults, Warp phenomena, and aspects of these omens.

The swords of epiphany

A warband of failed Exorcist Aspirants turned to the influence of Chaos are loose in the Macharian Sector — known as the Swords of Epiphany. The Plutonian Inquisitor has been tasked with quietly recapturing them and ensuring any daemons contained within them are thoroughly exorcised. The characters must act quickly before their corruption can spread and Exorcist secrets are revealed. Their movements were last spotted on the war world of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.VeiDfnkV55kTAkRw]{Kallastin}.

pages.name: Polypsykana
pages.text:
Polypsykana

"Mankind will evolve, and all those who resist this great transformation will fall behind."

Polypsykana Tenets:

  • Humankind is destined to evolve into a psychic species.

  • This transformation must be shepherded and defended from those who oppose it.

  • Psykers, especially fledgling psykers, must be protected and trained.

Modus Operandi:

Seek out psykers across the sector to contain or protect them. Train psykers and experiment with psychic powers and phenomena. Be wary of anti-psyker elements across the Imperium, especially those within the Inquisition.

Polypsykana Inquisitors, many of whom are psykers, believe that Humanity will, and should, eventually ascend to becoming a psychic species. They say the growing number of psykers verifies their beliefs, and the number of Inquisitors following their creed has increased in recent years. They make it their mission to prevent the unnecessary burning of psykers and spend their time monitoring the actions of Inquisitors who might kill rather than capture psykers so they can prevent them from doing so.

The origins of the Polypsykana are lost to history, as this philosophy may be one of the oldest. Its adherents appear wherever there is a surplus of psykers or tales of psykers of unusual power — and since the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#silence-and-darkness]{Noctis Aeterna}, there has been an excess of psykers in the Macharian Sector.

There are rumours that a Polypsykana Inquisitor in the Macharian Sector is hunting those who carry the Pariah Gene and executing them on charges of heresy. Other rumours speak of Inquisitors interfering directly with the Black Ships and their damnable cargo. If it proves true, such interference would not be tolerated — and could permanently damage relations between the Inquisition and the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.upGG1JZPDbC7dpJJ]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}.

Some Polypsykana experiment with ways of awakening and enhancing psychic abilities to facilitate Mankind’s inevitable evolution. They may study the Warp itself, daemonic lore, xenos, or the anatomy of Humans with and without the Pariah Gene. Their activities are generally conducted secretly, at the far edges of civilisation — with test subjects no one will miss. No Puritan Inquisitor would condone their beliefs, but while the God-Emperor requires psykers, few can dismiss their claims that psykers are, at the least, sometimes useful.

Roleplaying a Polypsykanan:

  • Polypsykana Inquisitors are utterly fascinated by psykers and hold reverence for their powers and phenomena, so much it might distract them in the moment from whatever task is at hand.

  • A psyker Polypsykana Inquisitor may be sympathetic to the plights weighted upon the shoulders of emergent psykers in the Imperium.

  • Polypsykana Inquisitors are resolute in their beliefs; when opposed, they cite the Imperium’s reliance on psykers to function, the advances the Imperium has made utilising them, and that, ultimately, the God-Emperor Himself is a psyker.

Inquisitorial interference

One of the Polypsykana Inquisitor’s research stations has been attacked and ransacked by another Inquisitor. The characters must investigate the base to discover who opposes their Patron. Some of the psykers there were taken into custody — track them down before they reveal any more of the Patron’s plans and ideally before they are handed over to the League of Black Ships; rescue or silence them.

Crash Landing

A Black Ship has crashed on the small feudal world of Octavian Secundus. Sabotage is suspected, but the immediate concern is to round up all the psykers who escaped the wreckage. The Polypsykana Inquisitor requests the characters aid in the cleanup but has given them a list of names to investigate — psykers who were aboard — to check if they survived and secretly bring them into custody.

pages.name: Recongregationism
pages.text:
Recongregationism

"When corruption takes hold of a limb, we amputate. Why should we treat the head differently?"

Recongregationism Tenets:

  • The Imperium has reached a level of stagnation that threatens its survival.

  • The Imperium must be audited throughout and rebuilt from the ground up.

  • Existing traditions and authority only serve to hold the Imperium back.

Modus Operandi:

Investigate the ruling noble houses and factions of the Imperium for corruption, gross inequality, and ineffectuality — any given failure is heresy. Bring balance to bear by whatever means necessary; surgically remove corrupt members of noble houses or arm the downtrodden to incite revolution.

Recongregators ardently believe that the Imperium has become decadent and corrupt, and it is their duty to right this great wrong. They see evidence of this truth in every noble house and ruling council across the sector. Every growing slum, plague outbreak, and xenos incursion is proof of the ruling class’s inadequacy.

Macharian Recongregators believe the sector’s corruption stems from the time of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-macharian-heresy]{Macharian Heresy} when power was distributed to Lord Macharius’s generals following his death. Then, the power-grabbing and greed of those strong enough to seize power closed their eyes to the Emperor’s will. Now, their descendants exercise power and wealth they have no right to wield.

Some Recongregators work subtly, undermining the authority of those in power and replacing them with worthier candidates. Many rulers and noble houses have secrets that might be exposed to destroy their popularity, while some might fall victim to their own decadence or have unfortunate accidents. Other Macharian Recongregators use more destructive methods, such as arming a dissenting group, planting explosives on a day of mass worship, or sabotaging a planet’s economy and inciting chaos.

When Macharian Recongregators encounter other Inquisitors or work with other Imperial agents, they often conceal their true purpose. This is especially true when they encounter @UUID[.R7LueEsDUhrSYHNn]{Amalathians}, whose goals oppose the fundamentals of Recongregationism.

Roleplaying a Recongregator:

  • A Recongregator will keep their actual goals close to their chest, presenting solid excuses for their investigations — suspected heresy or xenos collusion within a noble house is a way in to shake the house down from top to bottom.

  • They are wary of leadership within the ruling factions and houses of the sector; though they recognise their authority, they do not necessarily respect it. They know these people are often the root of the Imperium’s internal problems.

  • They know the price of altering the structure of the Imperium will be terrible but ultimately necessary. Therefore, they are prepared to make extreme sacrifices to achieve their goals.

The long play

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-defiant]{House Hysperion}, rulers of hive world Dominus Gamma, have reported Drukhari activity encroaching upon their planet from the nearby Osterum Shoals. Known as a defiant house by the Imperium, this is an opportunity to sway them and their assets to the Recongregators' cause. Aid them in their plight, embed Inquisition agents in their house, and garner favours for the future.

False tallies

In gathering information about noble lineages in the sector, the Recongregator Patron has discovered inaccuracies in the archiviums of the cemetery world Eternan — bolstering the dead of one noble house and reducing the count from others. Travel to Eternan, cut deep into the local leadership, and punish those behind these inaccuracies. Replace the culprits with the Inquisition’s own agents.

pages.name: Seculos Attendous
pages.text:
Seculos Attendous

"There is nothing so dangerous as misplaced faith. Save your prayers for the God-Emperor!"

Seculos Attendous Tenets:

  • The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum} is slowly corrupting and hampering the growth of the Imperium.

  • The God-Emperor does not need the Ministorum to reach those who embrace His Power.

  • For Mankind to be free, the Imperial Cult must be removed from power.

Modus Operandi:

The Ministorum is such a hulking organisation that it must be infiltrated and dismantled from within. Monitor and subvert its activities throughout the sector, particularly on shrine worlds. Manage the Imperial Cult’s contact with frontier and reclaimed worlds, where its influence can be easily undermined.

These Radical Inquisitors believe that the Adeptus Ministorum is failing in its role to lead the masses in their worship of the God-Emperor. Only their devotion to the God-Emperor prevents them from being branded heretics, even as they deny the Ministorum’s power and campaign to abolish the Ministorum.

As the Macharian Sector is a major pilgrimage destination for Imperial citizens, the Seculos Attendous have made their presence here known. These Inquisitors do not approve of the worship of Lord Solar Macharius over the God-Emperor, and their agents have made loud announcements on days of mass worship, reminding attendees of His supremacy. Others send their agents to shrine worlds to quietly undermine the influence of the Adeptus Ministorum. There are even rumours of a secret cult growing among the Imperial worlds of the Macharian Sector that worship under the guidance of Inquisitors, and this is likely the work of the Seculos Attendous.

The Seculus Attendous disapprove of @UUID[.0vHms9BJQGOVa0dO]{Thorians}, @UUID[.zilJJMaYtaWZrNtO]{Horusians}, and those of similar philosophies, but seek to convert rather than destroy them. In turn, they are unpopular with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum}, and @UUID[.R7LueEsDUhrSYHNn]{Amalathians} object strongly to their operations.

Roleplaying a Seculos Attendous:

  • A Seculos Attendous Inquisitor is often wholly focused on their secret war with the Adeptus Ministorum — they might care little for more ‘regular’ heresies that arise that do not involve the Ministorum in any way.

  • The Ministorum is an organisation that ultimately dwarfs the Inquisitors' powers. They must maintain a meticulous cover, perhaps presenting themself as a follower of another philosophy. They know that retribution from their peers within the Inquisition and the Ministorum would be swift if they were to be discovered. 0

  • A Seculos Attendous Inquisitor will keep their friends close, and their enemies closer — whatever they can do to ingrain themselves with the Ministorum will help further their goals.

Breaking Cover

An undercover agent on Lux Eternus has contacted the Seculos Attendous Patron, requesting immediate extraction. Their attempt to foster a rebellious cult on the hive world has come to light. The Patron may have left them to die if they were not the Planetary Governor’s liaison with the Ministorum, Cardinal Mirrad Vorn — people might believe them if they invoked the Inquisitor’s name.

Golden opportunity

The Ministorum is attempting to re-indoctrinate wayward cults on the reclaimed world of Olympia. A mix of false and conflicting doctrine is causing conflict between the cults, and the Ministorum is failing to wrest control. Now is the perfect opportunity to infiltrate both the cults and the Ministorum, solve the crisis and install some deep cover agents for future use.

pages.name: Thorian
pages.text:
Thorian

"One glorious day, the God-Emperor Himself will lead us into a new age."

Thorian Tenets:

  • The God-Emperor’s spirit wanders the Warp, occasionally manifesting when His people truly need Him, in chosen vessels that can only contain a sliver of his power.

  • One day, He will return and require a Divine Avatar or vessel to inhabit.

  • Seeking out these vessels or means to implement them will hasten His return.

Modus Operandi:

Seek out pure vessels for the God-Emperor’s eventual return or the means to create one. Investigate signs of the Emperor’s divinity throughout the sector, and seek for ways to guide or transfer His soul from the Warp to realspace.

For Thorians, the Emperor travels in spirit through the void and the Warp. He has already moved among the populace, granting an element of his divinity to various saints over the years. Still, Thorians believe that one day, He will inhabit a vessel that can contain Him in His entirety. Thorians, therefore, seek a suitable Divine Avatar to contain His spirit. This avatar must be exceptionally pure since a corrupt vessel might merely use the Emperor’s power for diabolical ends.

The Thorians’ philosophy is named for Sebastian Thor, who overthrew a High Lord of Terra’s tyrannous rule and ended theAge of Apostasy. Thorians believe that the Emperor worked through Thor Himself and has lent his power to other great mortals since, including Lord Solar Macharius. Some believe this means the next avatar will be found in the Macharian Sector.

Thorians investigate potential avatars and destroy those deemed unworthy. There are plenty of psykers, fortunetellers, and supposed ‘saints’ in the Macharian Sector, and an Inquisitor could spend a lifetime searching in just one hive. However, some might instead devote their time to their secondary task, learning to transfer consciousness to and from the Warp so that they might guide the God-Emperor to a new vessel.

Some Inquisitors think the Thorians misguided, but the @UUID[.R7LueEsDUhrSYHNn]{Amalathians} consider them dangerous, as putting faith in some powerful mortal would threaten the rule of the real God-Emperor on His Golden Throne. @UUID[.vJmDVccuyJJLooV4]{Polypsykana} Inquisitors object to Thorians’ tendency to destroy the many psykers they find unworthy, while @UUID[.2uYpfwwAdPf6e21L]{Oblationists} call their experiments heretical.

Roleplaying a Thorian:

  • Despite its wild claims about the God-Emperor’s divinity, the Thorian philosophy is still considered Puritan. Its Inquisitors strive for purity and truth in the vessels they chase and are more willing to admit they have found yet another failure than trick themselves into ill-gotten beliefs — their standards are impossibly high and exacting.

  • Yet Thorians are often headstrong and singular in vision; many ignore the idea that if the God-Emperor returned as they envision, it would cause a civil war across the Imperium that could rival the Horus Heresy.

  • Regardless of their keen interest in the Warp and psychic abilities, Thorian Inquisitors will not suffer the influence of any daemon nor any psyker who exhibits corruptive behaviour.

The battle of capisaj

A recent skirmish near the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.1AsBzkbw2InKayw2]{Ayzinith Abyss} has left a voidship graveyard in its wake, wreckage from both Aeldari and Imperial vessels floating in the void. Investigate the Aeldari wreckage under the guise of an Inquisitorial cleanup — their technology is said to have the power to manipulate psychic energies and capture souls; it could prove fruitful in the Patron’s research.

Fentessa of paleon

The Thorian Inquisitor is concerned about a missing noble, Fentessa, daughter of Barius Perrore, governor of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.A9cvKlA41X8qPyEw]{Paleon}. Rumours say Fentessa has an uncanny way of knowing people’s secrets, and local officials are relieved she has disappeared. Her absence has caused unrest among Paleon’s lowborn, with whom she was inexplicably popular — even revered.

pages.name: Xanthism
pages.text:
Xanthism

"The power of the Warp is a weapon. We can put this infernal power to righteous use in the right hands."

Xanthism Tenets:

  • The monsters of the Warp and the powers of Chaos should be bent to Humanity’s will.

  • Chaos cannot be defeated, but it can be understood and tamed.

  • Wield that which is forbidden in order to better combat it.

Modus Operandi:

Investigate Warp breaches, phenomena, and Chaos activity throughout the sector. Safely capture Warp-twisted artefacts and daemons where possible in order to study and understand them. Apply what is learned to fight back against the Ruinous Powers and save the Imperium.

Few Inquisitors would openly advocate using Chaotic power in their work, but Xanthism promotes such an approach. This extremely Radical group of Inquisitors believe that just as the Imperium harnesses the power of the Warp for interstellar travel, so too can Warp power be utilised in the fight against the Imperium’s enemies. Such Inquisitors learn forbidden lore from tomes that most would consider dangerous and heretical, attempt to capture and control daemonic entities, and hunt out Chaos artefacts. Even the most ardent follower of Xanthism would admit there are risks to such ventures. Still, given the foes the Imperium of Man faces, they often consider extreme methods a necessity to ensure its survival.

The ancient philosophy of Xanthism began with Zaranchek Xanthus, executed for heresy in the early 32nd millennium. He believed that Chaos could — and should — be utilised for the benefit of Mankind. Despite his execution, many Inquisitors have adopted his views over the millennia, and Xanthites are surprisingly common, especially among the Ordo Malleus. Xanthist Inquisitors might come to the Macharian Sector hoping to uncover new sources of Warp-based power, some searching among the strange discoveries already logged in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.MzIWAwZ8jPAOydDi]{Yix} Subsector.

Most Puritans outright oppose the methods used by Xanthist Inquisitors. When most Inquisitors find Warp-charged items, they destroy or lock them away under stasis fields. But Xanthists believe they should be wielded against the enemy instead. With a threat as great as the daemons of the Warp a constant concern, any such advantage is invaluable.

Roleplaying a Xanthite:

  • A Xanthite would exude understanding and superiority, perhaps even arrogance when pitted against the powers of Chaos or the Warp.

  • As followers of a highly radical Inquisitorial philosophy, they fear interference from other Inquisitors. They are uncomfortable with or act reserved toward their peers or their peers’ agents and would likely shy away or outright ignore the chance to collaborate.
