  • Many Xanthites are unaware they are being used as pawns by the Ruinous Powers until it is too late — they might not know themselves as well as they think.

Expunged Knowledge

The Xanthite Inquisitor has learned that one of his peers in the Ordo Malleus has discovered a Chaos cult harbouring a collection of nine rare forbidden tomes: the ‘Enneadex of Naxos’. Retrieve these books for study to ensure the rival Inquisitor cannot destroy them. Make sure you leave no trace.

A double-edged blade

One of the Xanthite Inquisitor’s cells was recently destroyed. They were on the hunt for a daemon, and provided a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.ucp7Z81P4kMxGcMN]{Daemonblade} to aid them in the task — but it was not recovered from the scene. Before returning to the hunt, fearful the blade has fallen into dangerous hands, this weapon must be found and retrieved — or destroyed — at all costs.

pages.name: Open Case Files
pages.text:
The Inquisition is vast in its remit and powers but pitifully limited in terms of its absolute size. Very few individuals have the strength of will to take on the mantle of Inquisitor, and every day, many more threats to the Imperium arise than the Inquisition could hope to address.

What follows are just a few of these Open Case Files, short adventures that should take a few sessions to complete. These can be used as introductory missions for newly minted acolytes within the Macharian Sector, as detours from a more extensive investigation, or as opportunities to allow your characters to explore more of their current locale. Resolving these Cases could inspire future stories, missions and characters within your campaign. Many can help fill in the years between Conclaves presented in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W]{Heresies Macharia} and relate to similar threats and concerns, allowing your group to dig deeper into the sector’s threats and intrigues.

Each Case File consists of three parts. First, the Hook pulls your party in — an inciting incident they could easily stumble upon or discover as part of their characters' downtime. Second, a Response — where you begin their investigation.

Finally, the Resolution — outlines the Case’s potential outcomes. Each stage of the Case contains helpful advice, challenges that must be overcome, and mechanical suggestions to keep things interesting for your players.

As with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.2TukBjlkS5RG5Qka]{Contacts } and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.SJPyRkdBEOCtmD8R]{Sector Threats}, Open Case Files are flexible — change a few details, such as featured planets, systems, and the characters involved, if they will better fit your campaign. Inject as many local characters and flavours as possible, especially NPCs your characters have already interacted with. For example, any local Contacts they have can make the characters aware of the case file’s Hook, introducing them to the mission at hand.

When a mission is complete, see the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.f5PuitUGgp6jQz5K.JournalEntryPage.qsaLi310r4uyLu4R#rewarding-players]{Rewarding Players} section of Imperium Maledictum to award characters with the appropriate amount of XP. Most Open Case Files have the characters interacting with one or multiple Factions within the Imperium, and they award additional Influence depending on how the Case is ultimately resolved.

pages.name: A Grave Mistake
pages.text:
All manner of rumours make their way to agents of the Inquisition, and most are ignored. Not so for a missive from Virida, as it arrived with the characters' Patron bearing the cypher key of an Inquisitor thought dead a century past. The message itself was short, the fact of its existence far more unusual than its content, and warranting an investigation on that account alone. This was, as it happens, precisely the sender’s intent.

Message from Inquisitor Bartolos

++ Priority alert. Planet Virida, Drimor Subsector. Suspected xenos infiltration. Possible compromise of high-ranking individuals within Imperial authorities. Assistance required. End message. ++

This Case File works best as an isolated part or detour of a more extensive campaign. It can introduce the characters to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari} xenos threat (such as @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.KZk1yGduhULvMbmP]{Varon Vipersong}). Though it takes place on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.WFgd7THvx3MHyhNd]{Virida}, any world that might invite the presence of Drukhari raiders may suit.

Hook

Inquisitor Bartolos vanished in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.d0lv2v4FkeIb43jj]{Drimor Subsector} in 850.M41. An @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} Inquisitor of modest achievement, Bartolos was on the trail of a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari} sympathiser when he disappeared. Several attempts to locate the Inquisitor failed, and his name was added to the long list of worthy dead carved into the monolith of service on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W.JournalEntryPage.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF#mare-cinis]{Mare Cinis} and recalled after that only in the records held there.

While it is not impossible that Bartolos still lives, it seems unlikely that, if this were the case, he would have waited so long to contact his fellow Inquisitors or be without any explanation for his absence.

Further, the message, though bearing his seal, does not conform to his previous writings, which tended to be verbose and elaborate rather than short and direct.

In fact, the message has been sent by Proctor Llewellyn Verane, Inquisitor Bartolos’s daughter. Wearied by his long service to the Imperium, Inquisitor Bartolos cast off his pledge to the Emperor. He retired — an almost unheard-of luxury for an Inquisitor and a betrayal of every oath he had sworn in the Emperor’s name. Worst of all, he has escaped punishment by the simplest means of all — he died in his bed several decades ago.

He told his daughter something of his life as an Inquisitor — more than he should have, and enough for her to know the peril of reaching out using her father’s name as an alias. However, Verane has cause for alarm and — rightly, as it happens — believes it warrants the Inquisition’s attention. As an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} clerk on the jungle-covered world of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.WFgd7THvx3MHyhNd]{Virida}, she has been tracking deaths among the citizens. She noticed an unusual pattern of deaths confined to a particular zone of the jungle and brought it to her superiors. The region was investigated, but nothing unusual was found; her concerns were quickly written off as a statistical anomaly or paranoia. Now Laal’s Citadel, one of the great servo-cities that strides across the surface of Virida, is approaching the zone, and the proctor fears the worst — that whatever threat stalks the forests will claim the population of an entire city. Desperate, she did as she promised her father she would never do and used her Adminstratrum connections and his Inquisitorial seal to plead for aid.

In truth, the jungle itself is not to blame, but a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari} presence hidden within it. The xenos raiders found the planet inimical to them and decided to lure their prey to them instead. Bribing the governor of Laal’s Citadel to alter its route towards a hidden entrance to the Webway, they intend to launch a surprise raid. Should they be successful, the entire servo-city and its millions of citizens might find themselves dragged off to captivity in the dark city of Commorragh.

Response

Of course, the characters may find themselves more interested in locating Inquisitor Bartolos than listening to his daughter’s wild tales of disappearances in a jungle with a history of hostility towards intruders. If pressed, she can show them to his final resting place, an unmarked grave at the mouth of a cave atop the Juncta Plateau, a truly inhospitable region of the planet-spanning jungle. He was not consigned to the corpse recyclers lest Inquisitorial marker-pathogens in his blood alert the wider Inquisition to his death. The interred skeleton is indeed the Inquisitor’s, the lone augmetic eye still staring from one eye socket, the digital weapon gifted for his routing of the heretek Loftus Kar from Hexas Panan gleaming upon one skeletal finger.

The coordinates attached to the message sent using Bartolos’s cyphers lead to Laal’s Citadel, a mighty serv-ocity. When the characters reach it, Verane will contact them, guiding them with messages hidden amidst a ceaseless barrage of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} paperwork, much of it delivered by randomly appointed couriers, minor scribes, servo-skulls, and other obscure means. She attempts to direct the characters towards her discoveries — the excessive deaths and a sudden change in the city’s trajectory towards the anomalous region of the jungle.

If the characters pursue her leads, they will find the sharp scribe quickly sets them on the right path to the office of Cityspeaker Naurane Wicht, one of the servo-city’s highest-ranking officials. Offered a simple deal by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari} — bring us your city in exchange for your own life — Wicht chose her own pitiable life over that of the millions whose safety was entrusted to her. When confronted by Inquisitorial authority, she quickly breaks down and will offer no resistance.

Resolution

However, it is up to the characters how they wish to proceed. They may use Wicht to lure a party of Drukhari raiders to their doom, preparing the servo-city's void shields and interception batteries, which Wicht had promised to disable for their attack under the pretence of essential maintenance. Alternatively, they may wish to avoid the area near the Webway portal or seek to destroy it.

They may also wish to pursue Bartolos and, in the process, discover Verane. She has no love for the Inquisition but would make an exemplary operative if convinced to join them by a persuasive character. Either way, the characters' Patron will point out that she knows far too much to be allowed to remain beyond the Inquisition’s reach and must be recruited or killed. Recovering Bartolos’ corpse for post-mortem punishment is also a priority — any Inquisitor who betrays their oaths must be made to answer for it, in spirit if not in fact.

If the characters are successful, Laal’s Citadel remains standing. If Verane is recruited, in addition to standard XP and solar rewards, their Influence with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} increases by 1.

pages.name: Dog Days
pages.text:
Kastan Marsd, an Interrogator from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud}'s retinue has been independently investigating daemonic activity across @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy]{Persepolis}. In his zeal, he has allowed himself to be baited into a trap and disappeared three cycles ago, deep within the Abyssal Levels of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy#hive-skarthius]{Hive Skarthius}.

This Case File works best when used as part of a hive-based investigation, although the specifics of the hive can be altered to fit your planet of choice. The characters may have met Interrogator Marsd at a previous @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W.JournalEntryPage.Y1wjtyi7JdgHxQiF]{Conclave }, discovered his disappearance through a known @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.2TukBjlkS5RG5Qka.JournalEntryPage.cRcDNREGRQvZvuPl]{Contact}, or mentioned via Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud} herself.

Hook

Through a network of favours almost as labyrinthine as the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.cvpsLwcsXf4myIpK]{Adeptus Administratum}, the characters' Patron has been called upon to investigate the disappearance — this could be as a favour to Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40.JournalEntryPage.9vSAxxrma5zbEIKL]{Alis Raud}, or the characters' Patron may seek to ply information from Marsd upon his rescue about Raud before she can retrieve him herself.

Shortly after they arrive in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy#hive-skarthius]{Hive Skarthius}, the characters are approached by a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.Y6oJff3F4qo2Xhlx]{Servo-skull} bearing Inquisitorial insignias. It has been combing the hive’s voidport for someone with Inquisitorial clearance for some time. The servo-skull is Interrogator Marsd’s failsafe, set to activate if he disappears. It refers the characters to an address in the mid-hive that Interrogator Marsd has been using as a safe house. The servo-skull wipes its memory and deactivates as the characters move on.

Response

The address the characters have been directed to is a warehouse in the hive’s middle layers. It is a squat and unwelcoming ferrocrete building near a small cargo port for access. Immediately, the characters can see that a group of enforcers have cordoned off the building. Four @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.gQxTENJSdTQTVfDM]{Enforcers} guard the cargo port, refusing to let anyone inside. They are led by Proctor Sai Darak, who does whatever he can to stymie the investigation without drawing suspicion.

Darak and a handful of her enforcers are secretly tied to the cult the characters encounter later, and are responsible for Marsd’s disappearance. Within, characters can find the remains of Interrogator Marsd’s current investigation.

Papers detailing maps of the Abyssal Levels, enforcer arrest transcripts, and detailed medicae reports on many patients are found scattered across a large holo-table in the office overlooking the warehouse. Going through all of them takes time, and gleaning any helpful information is a Challenging (+0) Extended Logic (Investigation) Test requiring a total of 8 SL, with one Test allowed per hour. Piecing together the clues reveals that an inordinate number of people who voyage into the Iron Sprawl district of the lower hive return with no memory of their time there and strange bruises and scars covering their bodies.

Characters can make a Hard (−20) Tech (Security) Test to access Marsd’s holo-table and retrieve a map of the Iron Sprawl with a couple of locations of interest marked on it. If no one succeeds, the characters can obtain a map or guidance to the area elsewhere, but this slows down their investigation. The warehouse also contains a battered ground vehicle whose engine rests on a nearby table, a sparse living space, and all the equipment needed to maintain a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.mVvzTcb8LJKDroT7]{cyber-mastiff}.

The Iron Sprawl itself is a twisting maze of tunnels, dead ends, and flooded maintenance passages. Corrosion speckles every surface, and the air feels oily. Characters can make Hard (−20) Rapport (Inquiry) Tests to interrogate the locals; they are cautious of talking to outsiders, but the people who live and work here remember a man matching the Interrogator’s description. Failing these Tests can draw the unsavoury attention of local @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.bB0rMr6Gez3M9bME]{Gangers}. By the end of their inquiries, they are directed to a place called the Cistern.

The Cistern is larger than some cathedrals and a mass of Humanity toils to repair the mechanisms in this part of the Abyssal Levels. Workshops line the walls, some stacked five or six high before reaching the ceiling, and the smell of unwashed menials sticks in the back of the throat. A successful Difficult (−10) Presence Test (Specialisation determined by the character’s method) is required to obtain the information for free, otherwise, a bribe is called for. Someone remembers seeing a man matching the Interrogators’ description leading a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.mVvzTcb8LJKDroT7]{cyber-mastiff} into a sealed area of the Iron Sprawl less than a few hours walk from the Cistern. They also warn the characters about an exaction squad hunting an escaped criminal in the area (a cover for the heretic enforcers’ activities).

Resolution

Following the directions, the characters find a bulkhead recently forced open. Years-old purity seals that used to hang from it, purporting to ward against daemons, lie cracked on the floor. Despite endemic overcrowding, no one lives nearby, and the corridors beyond the bulkhead bear the telltale marks of promethium burns.

The twisting, scorched passages beyond are seemingly empty, but the characters hear a distorted sound akin to a dog barking. Eventually, they come across a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.mVvzTcb8LJKDroT7]{Cyber-mastiff} with an Inquisitorial seal hanging from its collar. It has been clawing at the door to a sealed hab-block. The characters can bypass the door or break it down. Still, whatever they choose, the cyber-mastiff ensures their entrance is not quiet, and the cultists within, who are attempting to turn the Interrogator into a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.M6XWkYc0lfuKl2hU]{daemonhost}, are alerted to their presence.

Zones across the interior of the hab block are Poorly Lit. Some close to the central communal spaces are Warp-touched. Broken furniture scattered throughout the hab can be used as Light Cover. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.Eirl3ldJXIrs2frc]{Interrogator} Marsd is unconscious and tied to a table in the central space, daubed with heretical runes. If the characters do not hold the cyber-mastiff back, it does everything possible to break the table and drag him free. It will attack any cultist who gets in its way.

The cult are members of the enforcer team who were involved in the cleanup of this area during a past incident. Proctor Darak and one additional fallen enforcer are present for each combat-orientated member of the party (use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.gQxTENJSdTQTVfDM]{Enforcers} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ppicZvgr0bEuhWeh]{Cultists} profiles).

Wrapping up the investigation, the characters learn that Darak is one of the enforcers who cleared the hab of heresy a year prior and are now within the thrall of a daemon’s machinations. They felt spurned in their duties, which the cult plied into influence over them. They promised them whatever they desired in return for aiding the cult’s ‘master’, a daemon of Slaanesh who once almost managed to manifest in the depths of the hive before its cult was purged. Acting for the daemon, the cult pressed them to create a host for it, though each attempt ended up in bloody failure. The characters also learn that the original call for the Inquisition’s aid was intercepted by someone higher up in the enforcers' chain of command or by someone on the seat of the planetary council — which is where Interrogator Marsd’s inquiry points next.

If the characters are successful, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.Eirl3ldJXIrs2frc]{Interrogator} Marsd is recovered. His wounds are extensive and will take significant time to recover fully. In addition to standard XP and solar rewards, the characters' Influence with the Ordo Malleus increases by 1. If Marsd’s @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.mVvzTcb8LJKDroT7]{cyber-mastiff} survives, Marsd may be added as an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-malleus]{Ordo Malleus} Contact for any character who cares for the familiar during his recuperation.

pages.name: The Fallen Captain
pages.text:
Captain Louis Gontir has returned from the frontlines a storied war hero, but also a broken and mangled man. As an exemplary servant of the Emperor, he was awarded a relatively safe position as an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} drill master and planned to spend his remaining days in relative quietude. Unfortunately, he brought home a trophy from the frontlines, an artefact corrupted by the foul blood of Chaos Daemons it slew. Since his return, Gontir’s war stories and charisma have inspired a following, becoming a cult whose leader is slowly spiralling into madness and corruption due to the trophy he holds dear.

When the characters investigate, they find a man wielding far more influence than he should and a fanatical group of followers under his sway. They must determine if this is proper Imperial zeal or something more sinister. When events turn sour, the characters face a brutal tactician and his dedicated followers.

This Case File works best as an isolated part or detour of a larger campaign — related to daemons and daemonic influence. It can take place on any world with a significant Imperial presence.

Hook

The characters are alerted to the presence of a burgeoning sect of the Imperial Cult on a nearby world — either by their Patron or through one of their Contacts. What is troubling is the swiftness at which the sect has gained influence within the lower echelons of society — local authorities within the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Ministorum} are concerned.

The sect’s leader spent significant time in a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Ministorum} re-education program after his tour of duty. Requesting aid from the Ministorum and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Miliatrum} to review Gontir’s service record will take some time and influence (remotely or on location). The characters will find aspects of his record classified under Inquisitorial order beyond their level of access. In truth, Gontir’s unit ran afoul of daemonic activity in their last battle and barely survived. The classified information was redacted by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-malleus]{Ordo Malleus} Inquisitor Lark, who oversaw the cleanup. Impressed by Gontir’s service — his actions almost certainly saved her life — Lark broke with protocol to allow the man to continue his service to the Emperor in a quiet role, rather than recruiting him or outright silencing him for having witnessed a daemonic incursion.

The characters are advised to observe the sect and get close to Captain Gontir to interview him. They need to determine whether the sect is corrupted or legitimate. If so, they must do whatever they can to neutralise the sect’s leadership, especially Gontir, and snuff them out by whatever means.

Response

The characters can find the cult operating within the bowels of Imperial society, often called ‘Gontir’s Men’. The cult consists of primarily downtrodden folk — manufactorum workers, labourers, and scavengers — who see Captain Gontir’s return as a historic moment, rare for any trooper to return from the frontlines to their home. Though not without scars, Gontir’s body leans heavily on a crutch due to a mangled leg, the right half of his face marred with burnt scar tissue. Despite this, when he speaks of war, battle, and glory, the horrors he had been through, he focuses on the heroic and inspirational moments rather than the abject horror and pointlessness of his experiences. What began as informal lectures for his more promising students and unguarded conversations in local watering holes grew over time into talks in front of small crowds, and ultimately into cathedrum sermons in front of a fervent audience that grows each week.

Discovering the nature of the subtext of his sermons is not easy for a layperson or anyone not paying close attention to the details. Passing a Challenging (+0) Linguistics Test or a Difficult (−10) Intuition (Humans) or Lore (Theology) Test allows a listener to detect subtle variations in how he talks about the God-Emperor. While he pays lip service, the deity described sounds more vengeful and active. He talks about the God-Emperor’s return and other aspects that do not align with known texts. What he says might sound positive to many, but goes directly against the Imperial Creed and the teachings of the Ministorum. It does not reach outright heresy, but it should raise suspicions for the characters and warrant further investigation.

Getting close to Captain Gontir takes work. Bodyguards surround him: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ppicZvgr0bEuhWeh]{Cultists} and a group of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.bB0rMr6Gez3M9bME]{Gangers} who all act like @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} troopers. Gontir is a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.pGE97yqMKNMkyzgL]{Cult Leader}, though his Speed is Slow and he lacks a Mark of Chaos. To access Gontir will mean talking their way through, or sneaking past, his outer guards and other fanatical cult members trying to talk to him. Characters can make a Challenging (+0) Presence, Rapport, or Stealth Test according to their chosen method to gain entry successfully.

Once the characters meet with Gontir, it should be clear that the captain has lost what was left of his mind. In private, he lacks the charisma seen in his rousing speeches. Without the crowd’s attention, his mind wanders back to his battles and mutters dark thoughts about the horrors he witnessed. They notice he clutches the handle of a broken @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.tjUKnuDKTCCon28r]{chainsword} covetously, keeping it bundled under his robe.

Any psyker within a few feet of the chainsword can feel the malevolent Warp energy flowing from the broken blade. If examined, something Gontir will not readily allow, what is left of the blade’s teeth is caked in gore that has stained and pitted the metal. Touching it is a source of @Corruption[minor]{Minor Exposure} to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.PuzopCeKzYgcYAwh]{Corruption}. Gontir and his closest followers revere the corrupted blade — representing what Gontir and many of their brethren in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum} have gone through. They are lost to its influence.

Resolution

The Warp-tainted blade needs to be disposed of or at least quarantined, but Gontir and his men will not simply hand it over. Gontir’s tactical mind will kick in; he will try to protect himself and the blade. He claims the characters are agents of Chaos and instructs his cultists to capture them. The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.bB0rMr6Gez3M9bME]{Gangers} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ppicZvgr0bEuhWeh]{Cultists} should outnumber the party two to one, and Gontir’s @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.pGE97yqMKNMkyzgL.Item.iPGUzffs0rQvAA6k]{Fanatical Zealotry} Traits works on both the Gangers and Cultists in this case (do not forget to account for Superiority if the characters have done reasonable reconnaissance and preparation before confronting the cult leader).

Gontir’s first order of business will be to ensure he has enough followers between him and the characters to protect himself. His followers are zealots and will all lay down their lives for him. They can all use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.dZFX8HOdsFDpI7l0]{Look Out, Sir!} rule.

Once it is clear to Gontir that all is lost and the characters have the upper hand, Gontir will draw the broken blade and call upon his interpretation of the God-Emperor to aid him, triggering his The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.pGE97yqMKNMkyzgL.Item.t4VMzwCK0mcIDPlk]{Price of Failure} Trait. Once his transformation into a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.7GvkaaVAd69ORno0]{Chaos Spawn} is complete, the minds of his followers will break — they will still fight for their lives, but escape will be their only priority.

Once the characters defeat Gontir, they must dispose of the broken blade. Reaching out to their Patron, they will be put in contact with some @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-malleus]{Ordo Malleus} agents who can help. In addition to standard XP and solar rewards, their Influence with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.HURMpEU0Nnc93Ocv]{Adeptus Ministorum} increases by 1. The Ministorum spends the next several years working diligently in the area to re-educate citizens affected by Gontir’s false dogma.

pages.name: Lost in Transit
pages.text:
Captain Barik Thale, a recently promoted @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet} officer, was found dead within a cargo container in a storage area of the hive’s voidport during a routine inspection of the world’s tithe. A lone corpse — even that of a fleet officer — rarely elicits much response in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf]{Hive Rokarth}. However, as his weight had been included in that day’s accounting of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.59y8WFXTbwKRwiRI]{Voll’s} tithe, a potential violation was flagged, and the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.actors.Actor.O49jTi2TzoFQH5GT]{Macharian Vigilites} were obliged to investigate. This was expected to be perfunctory, as all involved wished to see the matter swiftly resolved and shipments resume, but a weapon of xenos origin was found on Captain Thale’s corpse. With all eyes on the hive’s governor, and the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} beginning to rack up punitive additions to Voll’s tithe, the Inquisition were at last called upon.

This Case File works best set in a populated hive city; it features much travel between hive levels and a cast of characters from across a hive’s societal classes.

Hook

The characters arrive to find the offending cargo container guarded by Vigilite Emilia Tark, a handful of irate @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Administratum} clerks, and Maul Berisk, a representative of the ruling @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#castyx]{House Castyx}. Vigilite Tark is dour-faced and overworked and simply wants to hand over this politically fraught investigation as soon as possible. Berisk is present to greet the agents and direct them to conclude their investigation as quickly as possible. The Administratum clerks simply wish to finish processing their now staggering amount of paperwork.

Response

Inside the container is Thale’s body, nestled among a collection of medicae supplies destined for delivery to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6Yav4onpokz5e5jg]{Astra Militarum’s} frontline. Of significance is the rather large hole in one plasteel wall of the container, which Tark is reluctant to admit is the result of one of her officers accidentally discharging the gun. The weapon itself, a squat-looking pistol of robust design, lies where it was dropped next to Thale’s body.

Any character with even a single Advance in Ranged can tell that this is no mere las weapon. Anyone making a Difficult (−10) Tech (Engineering) Test can identify the weapon as some kind of ion blaster, used by certain xenos species, most notably the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tau-empire]{T'au} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#the-leagues-of-votann]{Leagues of Votann}.

Inspection of the corpse reveals it is several days old, though much of this was spent awaiting the characters' arrival, which Tark or Berisk can both confirm. Further inspection reveals that he is missing medals on his uniform from his recent promotion, but a hefty pouch packed with solars has been left behind — if this was a robbery, it was poorly executed, which anyone with an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionist} background or who makes a successful Routine (+20) Logic (Investigation) Test can easily tell.

Ion Pistol

A pistol designed by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#the-leagues-of-votann]{Leagues of Votann}, the Ion Pistol and its larger variant, the Ion Blaster, are advanced weapons, utilising technology proscribed by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.9frbPZ9v3lFR9Kva]{Adeptus Mechanicus}. It bears markings that a successful Difficult (−10) Lore (Xenos) Test can identify as belonging to the Leagues of Votann. They mark the weapon as having come from the forge of someone named Theyn Hyvor.

Ion Pistol: Ranged (Pistol), 7 + SL Damage, Medium Range. Rend (2), Supercharge (4).

In fact, this was a deliberate execution perpetrated by the person who sold the weapon to Thale, who was concerned he was being a little too indiscreet with it. The killer would have retrieved the weapon if they had the time but were interrupted while attempting to stage a common mugging and dumped Thale’s body in the cargo crate. Anyone examining the body can tell Thale was shot cleanly with a las weapon. The shot was administered from above. A Challenging (+0) Logic (Investigation) Test reveals this is a likely sign that Thale was kneeling at the time.

The port’s security logs indicate there were no unauthorised entries to the port around the time of the murder, but a high-level override code with @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#castyx]{House Castyx} designation was used around this time. This is not unusual, and Berisk will be outraged at any suggestion of his house’s involvement.

He can (truthfully) explain that the code cannot be traced to any individual but could have been accessed by any ranking member of his house or its client dynasties — far too many people to investigate practically.

Beneath the Hive

Their Vigilite contact suggests that a weapons dealer named Hector Crug may prove useful. She grudgingly admits that the Vigilites are unlikely to get any information from the man, given his distrust of them.

Crug’s store is a small rockcrete shack with a broken, gaudy sign backlit by flickering lumens at annoying, unpredictable intervals. Crug is reluctant to help but can be convinced to talk with a payment of one-thousand solars, or a favour that probably involves having someone killed or a credible threat of violence.

When Crug agrees to tell the characters what he knows, he retreats to a small back room to recover his records. After a sudden shout, he returns surrounded by three squat, well-armed, armoured figures holding Crug at gunpoint, demanding to know the characters’ interest is in the weapon. Their own weapons are strikingly similar to the one found near Thale’s body, and they speak Low Gothic in a thick but unplaceable accent. Characters can make a Difficult (−10) Lore (Xenos) Test to realise these people are no mere abhuman Squats, but xenos Kin of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#the-leagues-of-votann]{Leagues of Votann}.

Their leader, Theyn Hyvor, demands the characters surrender the ion weapon if they have it. Characters can make a Difficult (−10) Presence (Leadership) or Rapport (Charm) Test to diffuse the situation, becoming Routine (+20) if they return the weapon. Hyvor can explain that he has been tracing several weapons and pieces of technology stolen from his people by raiders (including an Ironkin’s cerebral unit, though he will not be forthcoming with this information). Hyvor insists his people did not kill Thale but merely want the weapons back or a fair trade for them.

Seeing the opportunity to save his skin, Crug finally spills what he knows. The weapons were recently sold by one @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.2TukBjlkS5RG5Qka.JournalEntryPage.oCoWi7HnppfXcryy]{Celestina Visconti}, a socialite with extensive contacts among the nobility. Visconti is a minor client of House Castyx, which is how Celestina accessed the port and eliminated Thale. She is a key lynchpin in the Silent Trade, the illegal black market for xenos technology in the Macharian Sector. If Crug dies, this information can be recovered from a dataslate on his person.

The Kin will agree to let the characters handle things if they promise, truthfully or not, to return any weapons and tech that remain with Celestina. She can be found in a lavish (for Rokarth) suite of apartments. Celestina is a graceful socialite with an ease of speech that catches many off guard, but she keeps one of the ion pistols nearby should she need it.

If the characters reveal they are Inquisitorial agents or threaten violence, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.2TukBjlkS5RG5Qka.JournalEntryPage.oCoWi7HnppfXcryy]{Celestina} will offer a deal, trading her safety for what she knows about the Silent Trade and especially the Rogue Trader @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.SJPyRkdBEOCtmD8R.JournalEntryPage.AsvUSCAPODzDNPr6]{Xandro Cosmar}, from whom she acquired the weapons and related tech. Otherwise, this information is available in a dataslate of blackmail information she has retained as insurance. Celestina explains that she had Thale killed after he waved his newly purchased weapon around several Macharian Vigilites, whom she had to pay off. She was afraid the weapon would lead back to her, which, evidently, it has.

While occupying the characters with this story, Celestina has had her bodyguards — a trio of former Vigilites lured into her employ by her wealth — into a position to ambush the characters. If they do not cut a deal with Celestina for her continued freedom, she silently orders them to attack and lunges for her own hidden weapon. Use the Astra Miliatrum @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.060QdCc5DdlQwdhI]{Trooper} statblock to represent Celestina’s bodyguards. The remaining weapons and tech can be recovered from a locked storage area hidden beneath Celestina’s quarters.

Resolution

Removing @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.9kYI2Oshwn0wqWUo]{Celestina} will be a blow to the Silent Trade on @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf]{Rokarth}, though she might also make a useful Contact. Resolving issues with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#the-leagues-of-votann]{Votann} peacefully grants the characters' Patron the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.S56anxusJpE26v03]{Arms of the Alien} Boon . Consider carefully how their Patron might feel about this — Radical Patrons will be more open to cutting a deal with the xenos. In addition to standard XP and solar rewards, the characters' Influence with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.cvpsLwcsXf4myIpK]{Adeptus Administratum} increases by 1, as does their Patron’s.

pages.name: The Lost Kabalite
pages.text:
@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.SJPyRkdBEOCtmD8R.JournalEntryPage.fpfmfnvSQlN2YHNh]{Varon Vipersong} and his Kabalites have been using a hidden Webway portal on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.59y8WFXTbwKRwiRI]{Voll} to steal away Imperial citizens and influence corrupt leaders. So far, they have remained undetected, but one of his scouting Kabalites ran afoul of the Macharian Vigilites and was captured. The Vigilites have called upon the aid of the Inquisition to take the Kabalite off their hands before the Drukhari’s threat for retribution comes to fruition.

This Case File works best as an isolated part or detour of a more extensive campaign or the means to introduce the Sector Threat of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.SJPyRkdBEOCtmD8R.JournalEntryPage.fpfmfnvSQlN2YHNh]{Varon Vipersong}. Though it occurs on Voll, any significantly populated world or other hive would suffice.

Hook

While the characters are on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.59y8WFXTbwKRwiRI]{Voll}, they are contacted by their Patron or an authority within the Macharian Vigilites (if their standing is positive and their presence known). Vigilites in Hive Sanksorak have captured what they believe to be a xenos operative, asking to talk directly to Inquisitorial representatives. Characters can make a Challenging (+0) Lore (Voll) Test to recall that Hive Sanksorak is the holding of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#vylathi]{House Vylathi}. They are publically known for breeding the planet’s farmed tardigrades and processing them for meat, but privately, they are known to trade in secrets and dark favours while maintaining deep ties to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#castyx]{House Castyx}.

The characters are directed to the Vigilites' precinct fortress in Hive Sanksorak to meet with Vigilite Bekker, who is overseeing the captive. She brings the characters to the deepest and most secluded cells in the precinct fortress’s confinement block. Most of the other Vigilites are keeping themselves out of the way. Characters can make a Challenging (+0) Intuition (Human) Test to understand that these Vigilites are acting cagey, fearful of the alien they have captured and of Inquisition agents stalking their halls — word has gotten out that the characters are visiting.

Bekker introduces the characters to the captive and quickly backs away. The xenos is bound to a chair within their cell, stripped of their armour and weapons. Those have been collected onto a nearby table for examination (see the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.b8x4YQfSyzlvU4LX]{Drukhari Kabalite Warrior} statblock). Though they may initially appear @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#aeldari]{Aeldari} in origin, characters can make a Difficult (−10) Lore (Xenos) Test to determine they are the far more aggressive @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari}. The captive is struggling in their restraints, frothing at the mouth with anger.

The operative knows a handful of Low Gothic phrases to communicate with the characters. However the characters decide to get information out of the captive, they can learn the following:

  • Their name is Grevyth, and they are a warrior of the Dripping Fang Kabal.

  • Grevyth is offering themself over to the Inquisition. This is an act of the utmost desperation — they know the Inquisition may kill them, but are certain that their Sybarite (commander) @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.SJPyRkdBEOCtmD8R.JournalEntryPage.fpfmfnvSQlN2YHNh]{Varon Vipersong} will do far worse as punishment for failure. Varon will not tolerate one of his warriors being captured.

  • Grevyth knows that Varon is dealing with a prominent noble in Hive Sanksorak and can give the characters her name as a show of faith (Severin Vy’Gharst). They also know that the pair have been working together for some time.

  • Grevyth knows the location of a hidden Webway portal on Voll, one they have been using to conduct operations in and around Hive Sanksorak (no amount of coercion will extract this location out of Grevyth).

  • Grevyth can also generally inform the characters about aspects of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari} society (their Kabal’s capabilities and former missions) but will always steer the conversation back to securing ‘asylum’ with the Inquisition, even if what that means is long-term captivity

Response

The characters may wish to investigate Severin Vy’Gharst to confirm that Grevyth’s information is legitimate. The noble has a compound in the mid-hive and oversees several meat-processing manufactorums, with thousands of workers under her thumb (some of whom she has already traded to Varon as captives). Confronting her directly, Vy’Gharst attempts to bargain with the characters. She claims @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.SJPyRkdBEOCtmD8R.JournalEntryPage.fpfmfnvSQlN2YHNh]{Varon} is under her control, not the other way around, and is eager to hand this ‘asset’ over to the Inquisition. She is terrified and thinks she was too clever to be caught.

Vy’Gharst used @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.SJPyRkdBEOCtmD8R.JournalEntryPage.fpfmfnvSQlN2YHNh]{Varon} to assassinate a few minor members of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#vylathi]{House Vylathi} and assure her ascension within the house, which she characterises as ‘petty games the Inquisition surely has no interest in’. She offers a deal — allow her to remain free, and she can lure Varon in with news of his captured warrior. Then, the characters can deal with the far greater threat, just as Vy’Gharst claims to have always intended. Should she remain free after this encounter, Vy’Gharst secretly informs Varon that the Inquisition await him — the noble is keen to see the characters destroyed to save her own neck. If the characters decide to investigate stealthily or simply kill Vy’Gharst where she stands — not an unreasonable action to take with one who trades in Human lives with xenos — they can retrieve similar information from her personal cogitator.

Regardless of how the players handle Vy’Gharst, word reaches @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.SJPyRkdBEOCtmD8R.JournalEntryPage.fpfmfnvSQlN2YHNh]{Varon Vipersong} about his captive warrior, and he will soon attempt to recover or destroy Grevyth and his captors. He will infiltrate and attack the precinct fortress with his Kabalite Warriors. Alternatively, Varon will attack en route if the characters decide to extract or move Grevyth to their own secure location or hand him over to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} operatives.

Beyond silencing Grevyth, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.SJPyRkdBEOCtmD8R.JournalEntryPage.fpfmfnvSQlN2YHNh]{Varon} would only love a captive Inquisition agent to drag to Commorragh for interrogation, partly for his own pleasure, partly to seek information about his Archon’s lost Nightmare Doll. Varon seeks to capture some of the characters in his attack. If he is successful, it would be a monumental effort to recover them — Commorragh is a place of horror and dread, where even the most unflappable of Inquisitors might fear to thread. It may be possible to bargain for their return, perhaps for information that would aid Varon in his ascension. Of course, this would make the party little better than Vy’Gharst.

Truly ingenious characters may wish to set up a double-bluff, using Grevyth as bait to track Varon back to his hidden webway portal, so long as they can trick Grevyth. The Webway portal would be infinitely more valuable to the Inquisition than the life of a single Drukhari lowborn.

Resolution

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.SJPyRkdBEOCtmD8R.JournalEntryPage.fpfmfnvSQlN2YHNh]{Varon Vipersong} makes for an interesting recurring nemesis, and if you intend to use the scheming Drukhari in this way, you should allow for his escape. He will sacrifice any of his own warriors to ensure he gets away. If Varon succeeded in capturing any Inquisitorial assets or agents, the characters may wish to pursue him in the future.

Without tracking @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.SJPyRkdBEOCtmD8R.JournalEntryPage.fpfmfnvSQlN2YHNh]{Varon} directly or saving Grevyth from execution, securing and shutting down the Webway portal will take more time to locate. Tracking Varon’s former movements in and around the hive without directly following him is challenging but ultimately leads back to the Webway portal. If interrogated, Vy’Gharst suspects a few locations where the Webway portal could be and provides the characters with maps and notes. Whether the Inquisition destroys or quarantines the Webway portal is between the players, their Patron, and how their Philosophy would direct them. Regardless, once Varon knows the portal is compromised, he will never use it again.

How the characters wish to deal with Severin Vy’Gharst is up to them. The noble will not go willingly without a fight. The characters may wish to call upon the local Vigilites for aid in capturing her or go over her head and seek help from more prominent figures in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#vylathi]{House Vylathi} to get her to back down. However, the noble house would be more interested in covering up Vy’Gharst’s heretical activities to maintain its public image. Vy’Gharst can provide additional information on the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari} and Silent Trade through interrogation. Publicly executing her as an example would show the Inquisition’s prowess and suppress xenos collaborators and Silent Trade activity on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.59y8WFXTbwKRwiRI]{Voll}.

In addition to standard XP and solar rewards, the characters' Influence with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} increases by 1, and the same goes for either the Macharian Vigilites or @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#vylathi]{House Vylathi}, depending on how their investigation resolves.

pages.name: Between Missions
pages.text:
The shadow wars fought by acolytes of the Holy Orders are often long and arduous, their conditions unforgiving and their stakes high. Yet it does not end there. Even between their missions, they must hone their skills and expand their contact networks, lest the next assignment fails and a world — or even the Macharian Sector — is lost. It is a grim saying repeated in the Imperium that duty only ends in death, and those who serve the Inquisition are all too aware of every aspect of that truth.

This chapter expands on the material found in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX.JournalEntryPage.rl3sK1nTwQm9MChN]{Between Missions} of Imperium Maledictum, covering how this unceasing vigil impacts what passes for downtime among the agents of the Inquisition. There are new random Events that can impact downtime periods and subsequent missions, new Endeavours for both the whole group and for individual acolytes, and a new system for Long-Term Endeavours that can influence events over an extended campaign, lasting for in-game years between narrative time jumps; going hand in hand with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W]{Heresies Macharia}.

The GM can find advice for adjudicating all these new resources and perhaps find some inspiration for future missions from their players’ results.

Inquisition Events

Acolytes of the Inquisition often deal with strange and troublesome occurrences, even in their downtime. As described in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX.JournalEntryPage.nS7OsUr7I8LzMRJK]{Imperium Maledictum}, players should roll a random event for their character to go through before selecting an Endeavour during downtime. The following Inquisition Events Table can be used instead of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-tables.RollTable.TRQuuaBtW30wpGTq]{Events} Table of Imperium Maledictum at the player’s or GM’s discretion.

Several events in this new table are thematically linked to the Ordos Malleus, Xenos, and Hereticus. But there is no restriction on whether acolytes serving a particular Ordo can experience a given event. Still, at the GM’s discretion, an event more closely tied to another Ordo’s mission may be rerolled or replaced with one of the GM’s choosing to maintain a tighter narrative theme on the campaign if desired.

@TableHTML[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.O6yJARMmeEqVmXYX]{Event, no-center}

pages.name: Inquisition Group Endeavours
pages.text:
The servants of the Inquisition do not always agree on the value of unity. Some factions, particularly the Radical Isstvanians, believe in strife over cooperation as a means of shepherding strength. However, even Isstvanian cells cannot operate wholly alone and must turn to nominally trusted allies for difficult tasks. The Group Endeavours in this section include tasks that cannot be completed by any single character alone. As with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX.JournalEntryPage.AuM2Lzd784VPe32b#group-endeavours]{Group Endeavours} rules outlined in Imperium Maledictum, every member of the group must commit to the Endeavour at the same time for it to succeed. GMs using the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.KbejcPMug5gfoWWz]{Subtlety} rules should consider how these Endeavours affect the group’s status. Certain methods of completing the Endeavours or Failed Tests could impact Subtlety at the GM’s discretion.

Several of the group Endeavours listed in this section are associated with a specific Holy Order of the Inquisition and are most commonly carried out by acolytes associated with that Ordo. As such, they have an associated requirement of that Ordo’s presence in some way, as little as having a player character or NPC related to that Ordo present. See the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.BbyZqcWs3HbrAO3Y.JournalEntryPage.aq3meonzDWNY8A0W]{Requisitions} section, which outlines how acolytes can gain interfactional support to pursue these restricted Endeavours.

Prepare Hexagrammatic Wards

Requirement: Ordo Malleus presence.

The group utilises techno-arcana and other secrets of the Inquisition to strengthen the boundaries between realspace and the Warp in a small area, reducing the effects of warp incursions.

The group can secure a region equivalent to a hive city hab-segment, feudal world town, or the command centres of an embattled front. Until the group’s next downtime period, the presence and intrusion of the Warp is lessened, weakening psykers and daemonic entities. However, these wards must be regularly maintained against both mundane and metaphysical wear to sustain their effect, requiring a new instance of this Endeavour to function past that point.

While in the affected area, attempting to manifest a Psychic Power normally requires a Hard (–20) Discipline (Psychic) Test in addition to all normal Tests. Failure inflicts the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#fatigued]{Fatigued} condition on the manifester. In addition, all rolls on the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-tables.RollTable.9aSbu2mswOOI43J1]{Psychic Phenomena} and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-tables.RollTable.2YYlAUyaVIt4bZVa]{Perils of the Warp} Tables are resolved with a −30 to the final roll. Psychic Phenomena manifested during this time never become permanent. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.O9kga3ngGfFyIsze]{Daemons} in the warded area are even more severely impacted, suffering Disadvantage on all Tests and reducing the Armour gained from Lesser Daemon or similar Traits by 2 (to a minimum of 1).

Search for Xenos Infiltration

Requirement: Ordo Xenos presence.

By various methods, from studying import records and augur data to scrutinising gene-samples from flora, fauna, and even the local population, the group secures possible avenues by which xenos contaminants and infiltrators could have entered.

This work both examines the possibility of past weaknesses and closes vulnerabilities for the future. In cases where xenos infiltration has not occurred, the visible state of alert also serves to remind the populace about the hostile threats of the galaxy and to keep them focused on their tasks for the Imperium, grateful for the dubious protections of its grinding war machine.

After the group chooses to undertake this Endeavour, each character should make a Challenging (+0) Presence (Intimidation), Rapport (Inquiry), or Tech (Security) Group Test. If half of the characters involved are successful (rounding down), then their apparent vigilance serves to galvanise Imperial support among the locals and cow dissenters, providing +1 SL on Tests to acquire popular or immediate support for their actions before their next downtime period. If all characters involved are successful, the GM should provide them with one or more clues about the presence or absence of xenos infiltration in the area, granting Advantage on Tests where the provided clues are relevant.

Punish Dissent

Requirement: Ordo Hereticus presence.

Innocence Proves Nothing. The Inquisition has never tolerated ideas such as the need to prove guilt of a crime or to spare punishment of those whose status is merely free of a particular sin as anything more than spurious weakness. Even if a citizen of the Imperium is not the heretic they seek, any Inquisitor hardened enough to bear the rosette would still prefer them as a casualty to excessive zeal than a future weakness in the Imperium’s armour. So it is that whole cities have been rounded up for torment and questioning to no avail, then brutally executed to prevent the possibility that the survivors would seek revenge or rebellion.

Groups that choose this Endeavour pursue the path of authority through fear to its bitterest conclusions. They wield their power as Inquisitorial agents openly. However, they may conceal their identities behind masks or lackeys to avoid future recognition or reprisal. When performing this Endeavour, the group makes a Challenging (+0) Presence (Interrogation) or Presence (Intimidation) Group Test. For every character who was successful during this Endeavour, successful Presence Tests made before the next downtime period have their SLs increased by 1 as the population sets themselves to unquestioning obedience. However, should a character be known to have participated in this Endeavour, all Rapport (Charm) Tests with those they have oppressed are at Disadvantage. Unlike the compliance of the populace, this penalty lasts indefinitely unless the GM rules that the character manages to impress their victims with a righteous display of punishment or a persuasive piece of indoctrination.

Pool Knowledge

Requirement: Inquisition Patron.

The group’s Inquisitor calls upon other Inquisition forces and prominent acolytes in the area, aiming to pool knowledge in hopes of mutual advantage or to aid in thwarting a particular threat. Inquisitors and their agents are insular by nature. They operate in small cells that communicate little with each other, partly to prevent their network from being compromised by a single cell’s failure but also out of distrust for one another. On occasion, Inquisitors may put aside their paranoia and condescend to meet in person or send representatives to attend in their place.

Once a meeting place has been found and secured, and characters have travelled to the meeting, the characters conspire to gain as much useful information as they can from their fellow agents, revealing as little as they can of their operations. Of course, the other attendees are playing the same game! Each character must make a Difficult (−10) Rapport (Inquiry) Test. For every character who is successful, the party may reroll two Tests during the next mission based on the intelligence or secret knowledge they received. The player and GM are encouraged to discuss the events of the conclave and who the characters interacted with, which may provide narrative benefits regardless of the Test outcome.

pages.name: Inquisition Individual Endeavours
pages.text:
The pursuits of acolytes are frequently varied and eclectic, as strange a lot as the specialities of the acolytes themselves. Common threads exist, however, and frequently relate to the control of knowledge, allies, and power. Another common focus for activities is the study of others, both allies and enemies. An array of activities built around these common themes is provided in this section for characters to pursue between their missions on behalf of the Inquisition.

Condemn Nemesis

You dedicate yourself to destroying a particular foe, scouring any available lore to learn their weaknesses, or customising wargear into your nemesis’ anathema.

Cultivating extremely dangerous enemies is an occupational hazard for Inquisitors and acolytes alike. Fortunately, they have access to bespoke equipment and knowledge they can tailor towards individual adversaries. An acolyte may seek out fragments of a daemon’s true name, concoct biological toxins coded to a creature’s genetic makeup, or dig up family shames to make their taunts extra personal.

The character specifies a specific enemy when they choose this Endeavour. This must be an individual, not a general enemy type (e.g. a specific Genestealer Patriarch, not Genestealers or their cults in general). Until the next downtime period, if the character meets this enemy, they immediately gain 2 Superiority. If they do not encounter their nemesis until a time beyond that, they immediately gain 1 Superiority instead. These benefits cease to apply if the enemy adapts to the character’s existing tactics or any special wargear they use is no longer available.

Cultivate Network

You expand your sphere of intelligence by recruiting new spies and commissioning reports from existing assets. It is said the Inquisition’s eyes are everywhere, but in reality, Inquisitors are not as omniscient as they wish, compared to what the oppressed Imperial masses believe. Recruiting new agents, processing reports, monitoring surveillance, and intercepting communications sector-wide requires tireless effort.

Handling this colossal intelligence network is daunting, but there is no surer way for an acolyte to become informed besides visiting a flashpoint themselves.

The character makes a Challenging (+0) Rapport (Inquiry) Test. If they succeed, they choose one of the following benefits to apply for the next mission only:

  • The character’s Influence Level with a chosen Faction increases by 1.

  • The character gains an Influence value of 1 with a new Faction.

If the Test fails at −3 SL or more, the character’s informants are captured by a faction’s counter-intelligence operatives and interrogated until their paymaster is revealed. At the GM’s discretion, the character reduces their Influence by 1 with the relevant faction instead of increasing it, or the slip-up negatively affects their party’s @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.KbejcPMug5gfoWWz.JournalEntryPage.XyTxLhjDZDkpE0Lz]{Subtlety}.

Erase Truth

You eliminate remaining trace evidence of heresy, corruption, and the Inquisition to preserve the blessed ignorance of the Emperor’s subjects.

Knowledge is power, and the Inquisition does not tolerate rivals to its authority. As such, none in the Imperium are permitted to know as much as the Inquisition, with knowledge of the organisation itself being the most dangerous and forbidden of all. In the aftermath of Inquisitorial operations, acolytes may protect their identities by cleansing surveillance, redacting records, and silencing witnesses, acting by their ultimate authority to protect themselves and their work. The moral cost of such drastic action is high. Yet, the Inquisition’s doctrines state that morality only impedes righteousness, and few acolytes dare question it.

The character makes a Test to cover up evidence of their previous mission. Which Skill is appropriate depends on the mission and the approach the characters adopted in the aftermath, but Challenging (+0) Presence (Intimidation), Stealth (Conceal), or Tech (Security) Tests are commonly appropriate.

If the character succeeds, they gain Advantage on all future Tests to deny or conceal their involvement in the previous mission. In addition, when the character Tests to persuade another person to accept their (likely fraudulent) account of what happened in the previous mission, they gain +1 SL.

Familiar Training

Life is no easier in the Imperium for animals than it is for the multitudes of man; anyone seeking to care for a Familiar, to ensure they are healthy, and the bond between Master and Familiar remains strong, will need to put in significant time to ensure they are a fit and able tool to aid them in their missions.

A character with one or more Familiars must undertake this Endeavour at least once between every two missions. If a character has multiple Familiars, taking this Endeavour covers the training for all of them at once. If neglected, each Familiar suffers a −10 penalty to all Tests they make until the next time they take this Endeavour — as it takes too long for the creature to register a command, hesitates, malfunctions, or simply refuses to listen.

During this Endeavor, the character can change one of the Familiar’s Combat or Preservation @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.UHAAGHOTknUiUTUj.JournalEntryPage.YTjT0gYfJiYRSTIZ]{Instincts}. They may also choose one of their Familiars. If that Familiar is a Construct, they make a Challenging (+0) Tech (Augmetics) Test. If that Familiar is a Beast, they make a Challenging (+0) Rapport (Animals) Test. For each SL Achieved, the Familiar gains 10 XP it can spend on Advances and Talents. For complete information on Familiars and how to use them, see @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.UHAAGHOTknUiUTUj.JournalEntryPage.BWMw4bzQxBwJjUIm]{Chapter VI: Familiars}.

Fortify Sanctity

Anticipating the trials that lie ahead, you brace your mind and body to be subject to the wiles of the Enemies Within, Without, and Beyond and make what preparations you can to emerge unscathed.

The preparation process to confront the horrors that threaten the Imperium is arduous, although nothing so severe as the consequences of failing to resist them. A gruelling regimen of medicae, prayer and fasting, or some combination of these and even more esoteric methods, causes the practitioner to achieve a heightened sense of spiritual resilience. This battery of preventative measures creates a bulwark that may prove enough to see them return from their missions unscathed by the sinister power of their foes.

Upon taking this Endeavour, the character selects the severity of their preparations. They may reduce their Maximum Wounds by an amount up to their Toughness Bonus for the next mission, suffering the reduction until their next downtime period. For each point reduced in their Maximum Wounds, the character may attempt to nullify a single Exposure to Corruption on their next mission with a Discipline (Composure) or Fortitude (Pain) Test. The Difficulty of the Test is based on the severity of the exposure: Challenging (+0) for a @Corruption[minor]{Minor Exposure}, Difficult (−10) for a @Corruption[moderate]{Moderate Exposure}, or Very Hard (−30) for a @Corruption[major]{Major Exposure}. Success on the test means the character’s preparations prevent the Corruption from taking root.

Litanies of Recollection

In high-stakes and stressful investigations, in a place so cluttered with information as the Imperium, it’s easy for acolytes to miss or overlook clues. Acolytes should take the time to meditate, reflect on what they’ve learned so far, or revisit scenes or witnesses to glean new context. This may allow them to realise that they have missed important clues, see connections between clues that may not have been obvious, or otherwise recall information that will assist in moving their investigations, and the campaign, forward.

The character makes a Hard (−20) Logic (Investigation) Test, or any other the GM deems appropriate relating to aspects of the investigation. For each positive SL achieved, the GM confirms a link between two clues, highlights a clue the characters may have overlooked, or reveals a new clue they missed altogether. If multiple characters choose to undertake this Endeavour simultaneously, they can @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.xf46pBDy93sT0ZDl#help]{help} each other make the Test.

Mental Sanitisation

You cleanse your mind and soul by subjecting yourself to the scourging process of Imperial re-education. Acolytes confront appalling, existentially horrifying dangers in their missions, the pressure of which can shatter their conditioned loyalty to the Inquisition and leave them easy prey to the Ruinous Powers. Characters wary of the looming dangers can temporarily forestall their doom by correcting their deviant thoughts with psycho-spiritual treatments. The processes are as varied as they are unpleasant: telepathic mind wipes; pharmaceutically-induced amnesia; hypno-suggested conditioning; or Ecclesiarchy-observed flagellation. Only the tremendously fortunate will be prescribed anything as prosaic as rest.

The character removes 1 point of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.PuzopCeKzYgcYAwh]{Corruption}, then makes a Challenging (+0) Fortitude (Pain) or Discipline (Composure) Test. If they succeed, they may remove an additional point of Corruption. For the duration of the next mission, the character reduces their Maximum Wounds by 2 due to the physical trauma they sustained in the sanitisation process.

Petition for Guidance

Requirement: Influence of 2 or Greater with the Inquisition.

You reach out to your superiors in the Inquisition for more information, hoping your need is great enough not to overly test their patience. They can spare only limited time for all but the most urgent tasks and are ruthless to those who waste their time.

Reaching out to an Inquisitor without prior instruction requires a Challenging (+0) Rapport (Inquiry) Test to secure an audience, while approaching another ranking member of the Inquisition, such as an Interrogator or rival Inquisitor, requires a Hard (−20) Rapport (Inquiry) Test. In failure, they are rebuked for wasting the time of their betters.

However, success grants them a brief but valuable window to access the information network of the Inquisition. The player whose character is taking the Endeavour should present the GM with a number of questions up to their Influence with the Inquisition. If the GM deems the knowledge reasonable for the superior to possess and the character has sufficient clearance, the information is granted in whatever way feels appropriate.

Rejuvenat Treatment

Requirement: Taking this Endeavour costs 5,000 Solars unless the character has Influence with the Inquisition or another relevant Faction at a level of 3 or higher.

You submit to a pharmaceutical programme that extends your natural life in the long term and boosts your vitality in the short term. For those wealthy or influential enough to afford the treatment, the care of rejuvenat adepts can extend a mortal lifespan by decades or centuries. A cocktail of alchemical curios combat the natural degradation of Human bodily processes and generate artificial energy boosts that restore youth’s vivacity within the subject. Though the costs are exorbitant and the side effects brutal, most Inquisitors and highly-valued acolytes consider the trade-off worth it. In a sector as dangerous as this, Inquisitors are simply too busy to die.

For the duration of the next mission, the character increases their Maximum Wounds by 2. The character also extends their natural lifespan by 1d100 years.

Secure Information Network

You take steps to ensure that the knowledge you trade in travels in only one direction, searching for weak links amongst your contacts. Information only known to yourself is significantly more valuable than open knowledge or secrets revealed to the public or your enemies. To avoid such situations and prevent the rise of double agents within your ranks, you must monitor your contacts secretly and apply pressure where needed.

When taking this Endeavour, the character selects up to three of their Contacts in the same Faction and makes a Challenging (+0) Rapport (Inquiry), Presence (Intimidation), Stealth (Conceal), or Tech (Security) Test. For every −2 SL, the character must choose one of those Contacts and reduce their influence with that individual by 1, as their investigation is discovered. On a success, they learn the highest Influence each Contact has, plus an additional Influence possessed by each Contact for each SL past the first — learning who might sway the loyalties of these Contacts.

pages.name: Inquisition Long-Term Endeavours
pages.text:
The typical framework for Endeavours can cover the brief windows of respite between an Inquisitorial party’s efforts during active duty, but sometimes a campaign requires more. Inquisitors can extend the service of their acolytes for years, decades, or even centuries if peril does not claim their lives. In the context of Imperium Maledictum, that can be reflected with periods of extended downtime in which acolytes are retasked, sent to new positions, or otherwise withdrawn from the front lines of service, only to reassemble later to face a new threat. From a GM’s perspective, these periods can be perfect for spacing out the narrative beats of different story arcs or allowing past events to grow to fruition in the background. For players, they are the ideal time to take Long-Term Endeavours.

As the name suggests, Long-Term Endeavours operate on a different time scale than the more normal Endeavours presented earlier in this chapter and Imperium Maledictum. Given the time scale of events, they should be granted in addition to other downtime opportunities. Other than this extended length, Long-Term Endeavours function similarly to the existing rules and can be undertaken by as many party members as they wish. Characters can drop in and out of contributing towards these Endeavours depending upon the character’s priorities. The more characters who participate, the more likely they are to receive a reward. In most cases, all characters involved make a single Test during each downtime period — the highest rolled result among characters is applied to determine success.

Given the incredible investment involved in undertaking a Long-Term Endeavour for a character or group, GMs should consider adapting them to the specifics of their campaigns. The following Long-Term Endeavours represent examples of goals that a character or group might work towards in the shadows of their ongoing work. They can be altered to fit the circumstances of a particular narrative at the table — ‘Xenos Diplomacy’, for example, applies to many sentient xenos species, depending on who the characters wish to seek out. Like Group Endeavours, they may require the presence of characters from a @UUID[.zt3agZuaQd99PTyc]{specific Ordo}.

Craft Anointed Weapon

Requirement: Ordo Hereticus or Malleus presence.

Anointed Weapons are holy relics and formidable tools against Chaos and its tainted servants. Countless stories and fables of ancient and apocryphal relics exist; their legends are well-documented within the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.PdQjDIH5C6kx3vAy]{Adeptus Ministorum}’s annals.

Crafting an Anointed Weapon takes considerable time. To even consider crafting an Anointed Weapon, the acolytes involved must have a Corruption Score equal to, or lower than, their Willpower Bonus (WilB). Then, follow the rules for the
