or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX.JournalEntryPage.AuM2Lzd784VPe32b#crafting]{Crafting} Endeavours. The character can decide to anoint one of their existing weapons. In this case, the modifications required are so extensive that the effort required is the same as following the Crafting Endeavour. Multiple characters can work together in crafting a single weapon; if they do, they each roll and the highest result is used at each stage.

Once completed, the characters make an additional Challenging (+0) Test to anoint the weapon completely. Choose a Skill the GM deems appropriate, such as Tech (Engineering) or Lore (Theology). The GM may grant a +1 SL bonus to this Test when made on a Holy World or within a suitable blessed or sanctified structure. On a failure, the weapon is completed but does not receive an Anointed Effect. On success, each player rolls on the Anointed Weapon Effects Table and can choose from among the results. On an Impressive Success (+3 SL or more), they can choose what effect their weapon gains from the Table instead.

@TableHTML[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.gk5lzqNOFByEQLwo]{Effect}

Attracting Puritan Attention

Some Endeavours cross the line towards what many Inquisitors consider to be Radical Behaviour — seeking to harness the power of a daemon, bind one, or even allying with xenos factions are all damning activities that could see a member of the Inquisition be declared Excommunicate Traitoris.

The following Long-Term Endeavours may attract attention from Puritan Inquisitors and their acolytes: @UUID[.56xpJ7ADckt2kxHB#craft-daemonblade]{Crafting Daemonblades}, @UUID[.56xpJ7ADckt2kxHB#xenos-diplomacy]{Earn Trust with the Aeldari}, @UUID[.56xpJ7ADckt2kxHB#learn-a-true-name]{Learn a True Name}, and @UUID[.56xpJ7ADckt2kxHB#prepare-a-ritual-of-binding]{Prepare a Ritual of Binding}.

Depending on which Inquisitors, acolytes, and informants are operating in your area and how aware they are of your plans, they may seek to investigate you directly or work towards stopping your activities. Having a high level of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.KbejcPMug5gfoWWz.JournalEntryPage.XyTxLhjDZDkpE0Lz]{Subtlety} may offer some protection from their purview — but in the same vein, any failed Tests within these Endeavours may affect your Subtlety negatively.

Craft Daemonblade

Requirement: Ordo Malleus presence.

To even consider crafting such a tainted weapon is a level of heresy that might condemn even some Inquisitors. Still, brazen Radicals and their acolytes often believe it is all in service of their greater goals and that the enemy’s tools are sometimes needed to defeat such terrible foes — fighting fire with fire.

For acolytes to consider crafting such a weapon, they must have some knowledge that these weapons exist or are possible to create. Encountering such a weapon alongside a post-battle analysis might be enough, but GMs can also consider participation in the @UUID[.56xpJ7ADckt2kxHB#prepare-a-ritual-of-binding]{Prepare a Ritual of Binding} Long-Term Endeavour or the characters having Lore (Forbidden) as an avenue of personal knowledge.

A specially wrought weapon is required to contain the daemon. The weapon requires runes and sigils of daemonic command and summoning, wards for the wielder, and an array of occult paraphernalia that is sure to get an unwary acolyte immediately executed. Follow the rules for the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX.JournalEntryPage.AuM2Lzd784VPe32b#crafting]{Crafting} Endeavour, set at Very Hard (−30) Difficulty, requiring at least 10 SL or more depending on the type of blade they wish to create. Characters can use Lore (Forbidden) instead of, or in combination with, Tech (Engineering) Tests in this Crafting Endeavour. The GM should also track the number of failures generated within the Crafting Endeavour. Multiple characters can work together in crafting a single weapon; if they do, they each roll and the highest result is used at each stage (only count the failures of the highest result).

After making the final Crafting Test, the characters involved gain 2 Corruption points each, and the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.ucp7Z81P4kMxGcMN]{Daemonblade} is created. They can choose a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.t5Da1EFHdmn5gFVv]{Feature} and a Quirk. If more than three failures occur during crafting, the GM chooses or randomly rolls on the Daemonblade Flaws Table and grants the weapon that drawback.

The characters can choose to work further on the Daemonblade by completing the @UUID[.56xpJ7ADckt2kxHB#learn-a-true-name]{Learn a True Name} Long-Term Endeavour to learn the True Name of the daemon bound to the blade or the @UUID[.56xpJ7ADckt2kxHB#prepare-a-ritual-of-binding]{Prepare a Ritual of Binding} Long-Term Endeavour to bind the daemon within the blade fully. Completing either of these Long-Term Endeavours removes any Flaws the Deamonblade has, and grants it an additional Feature from the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.t5Da1EFHdmn5gFVv]{Daemonblade Features} Table.

@TableHTML[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-tables.RollTable.QOcHAy8SBplgs81N]{Drawback}

Infiltrate a Cult

Sometimes, the easiest way to extract information from a cult is to do so from within. But this is a dangerous task; undercover acolytes must be utterly convincing in their manufactured identity. They must appear as heretical as the corrupt individuals they seek to gain the trust of and perform tasks the cult asks them to appear genuine and garner their trust. However, the potential rewards are worth such self-corruption; it may take years to access a cult’s inner circles, but the information given freely is often more potent than what torture can achieve, and a cult unshaken by direct interference can be as susceptible as a slumbering beast.

Multiple characters can work together in this Endeavour. If so, they must choose who among them is infiltrating the cult (minimum of 1). Each downtime, all characters involved make a Test with a relevant Skill; such as Intuition (Humans), Presence (Leadership), or Rapport (Deception).

Each Test is Hard (−20), and all characters involved make the Test, but only the highest result rolled is counted. No more than one Test per character can be made in a given period of relevant downtime. Any characters who fail their roll, gain advantage the next time they pursue this Endeavour, showing they have learned from their previous mistakes. Additionally, those infiltrating the cult gain +1 Corruption if they fail this Test.

Every time the characters succeed at this Endeavour, they gain one stage of reward, described below. No reward can be gained more than once. Those chosen to infiltrate the cult gain deeper access. If all characters involved fail this Test, a Stage is removed from the Infiltration, and the party loses the last reward gained. Additionally, any characters infiltrating the cult must make a further Challenging (+0) Rapport (Deception) Test; if they fail here, they are discovered as enemy agents and ejected from the cult. Without the Cult Infiltrator or Secret Identity Talents, the infiltrator cannot go undercover with this cult again.

  • Stage 1: The infiltrators are accepted by low-level cult members (Troop-tier NPCs). They can garner information from them as if they were regular contacts. The party gains +1 Superiority whenever they confront this cult.

  • Stage 2: The infiltrators have gained the trust of a few mid-level cult members (Elite-tier NPCs) and can extract useful information from them about the cult’s movements and priorities. The party gains +1 additional Superiority whenever they confront this cult.

  • Stage 3: The infiltrators have gained access to the cult’s inner circle, accepted by at least one high-level member (Leader-tier NPC). They can extract information such as the cult’s ultimate goals and where other cells may be hiding. The party gains +1 additional Superiority whenever they confront this cult.

Learn a True Name

Requirement: Ordo Malleus presence.

The daemons of the Warp are perfidious and deadly enemies for even the mightiest and most righteous of the Emperor’s servants. As immortal beings from another reality, finding ways to truly harm them is all but impossible. However, the most learned Inquisitors of the Ordo Malleus know that all daemons have a weakness in their True Name, a set of syllables expressing the daemon’s essence in their own foul tongue.

By research, investigation, and even the practice of fickle warpcraft, acolytes can divine fragments of a True Name and eventually assemble them to turn against the daemon that bears it.

When characters first select this Long-Term Endeavour, they must choose a particular daemon they have encountered or learned of as the object of their investigations. During each Long-Term Downtime period committed to this Endeavour, the characters can then select an avenue of research to pursue (such as consulting prescribed texts, interrogating the daemon’s worshippers, or even wrestling with the daemon itself in psychic contest). They make a Test using a Skill agreed upon with the GM appropriate to the method of research. Examples include Discipline (Psychic) for divination or consultation of the Emperor’s Tarot or Linguistics (Forbidden) to decipher the intricacies of the Daemonic tongue.

Multiple characters can work together in this Endeavour; if they do, they roll, and the highest result is used at each stage. But for all involved, each failed Test during this Endeavour causes the character to gain 1 Corruption, with no possible Test to resist — such are the consequences of willfully seeking out daemonic lore! Additionally, GMs are encouraged to increase the Difficulty of the Endeavour’s Test, depending on the perceived power of the daemon they seek. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.dZFX8HOdsFDpI7l0#troops]{Troop}-tier daemons are Challenging (+0), @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.dZFX8HOdsFDpI7l0#elites]{Elite}-tier daemons are Difficult (−10), and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.dZFX8HOdsFDpI7l0#leaders]{Leader}-tier daemons are Hard (−20). Inform the characters of the Difficulty after they roll, as this may reveal additional information about their enemy.

Every time the party succeeds at this Endeavour, they gain one stage of reward, described as follows. No reward can be gained more than once — they grow closer to completing their understanding of the daemon’s True Name:

  • Stage 1: The characters cannot become @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#frightened]{Frightened} by the daemon in question.

  • Stage 2: The characters gain +1 SL on successful Opposed Tests against the daemon in question.

  • Stage 3: The characters gain Advantage on opposed Tests against the daemon in question.

  • Stage 4: The characters learn the daemon’s True Name in full. They receive +3 SLs on any Tests to bind, banish, or combat the daemon in question (included within the @UUID[.56xpJ7ADckt2kxHB#prepare-a-ritual-of-binding]{Prepare a Ritual of Binding} Endeavour). This benefit stacks with those previously listed.

Prepare a Ritual of Binding

Requirement: Ordo Malleus presence.

Knowledge of the daemonic is a potent weapon, but one of the many in the arsenal of Ordo Malleus Inquisitors. When Inquisitors determine that a particular daemon has made itself a threat warranting the most extreme measures possible, they often turn to their acolytes to prepare a ritual to seal away the daemon forever, binding it into a forsaken relic never to be unearthed. This is of particular appeal to Radical Inquisitors, who may later have plans for the bound daemon-relic in their ongoing war.

Multiple characters can work together in this Endeavour. All characters involved choose a Skill that represents how they are contributing to the ritual, such as Linguistics (High Gothic) to inscribe blessed canticles or Tech (Security) to ward the ritual site against tampering, both physical and metaphysical. During each downtime, including the first, each character must make a Challenging (+0) Test using their chosen Skill and note the total SLs accrued. The Endeavour is complete when the total SLs earned by the characters reach 20 SL. The ritual benefits those working on it at certain thresholds of accrued SL:

  • 5 SL: The characters are sufficiently invested in the dubious sanctity of their work that they receive Advantage on Discipline (Composure) Tests to continue their efforts despite meddling, temptation, or outside investigation.

  • 10 SL: The relic or host within which the daemon is intended to be trapped is sufficiently completed. Serving as an anathema to the profane, a character bearing this relic gains Advantage on Opposed Tests against Daemons while wielding it.

  • 15 SL: The selected ritual site is secured against nearly all interference and becomes a veritable fortress against daemonic incursion. Daemons entering the vicinity of the ritual space (as determined by the GM) suffer Disadvantage on all Tests unless the space is subsequently unconsecrated or defiled. Such actions can reduce the accumulated SLs of the Endeavour if the damage is sufficient.

  • 20 SL: The ritual of binding can be attempted. This should be handled as a mission in full rather than by the Endeavour system, wherein the characters gain all benefits previously attained during the mission and their subsequent efforts to seal away the daemon.

Reinforce Anti-Xenos Propaganda

Requirement: Ordo Xenos presence.

As the Imperium’s contact with the Macharian Sector became limited via the Noctis Aeterna, some worlds began to follow paths divergent from Imperial doctrine. With little or no help from the greater Imperial bureaucracy, they have turned to any means necessary for survival, including hiring xenos mercenaries such as the Kroot or even paying an abominable tithe in citizenry to Drukhari raiders to be spared their depredations. Where the Imperium finds such arrangements, they are broken up by force. Still, many worlds persist in secrecy or consider renewing their activities after the authorities move on without providing long-term aid.

Inquisitors of the Ordo Xenos are particularly interested in suppressing these arrangements, well aware of the dangers of xenos infiltration. As such, the Inquisitor’s acolytes are often tasked with reinforcing the Imperial status quo on frontier worlds, whether by making examples of suspected alien sympathisers, distributing limited resources in a show of beneficence, or simply repeating the official dogmas until they sink in.

Multiple characters can work together in this Endeavour. Each character involved should choose a Skill that represents how they are contributing to the spread of propaganda on a specific world, such as Presence (Intimidation) to cow advocates of xenos ties into silence or Linguistics (Low Gothic) for writing missives and pamphlets for mass distribution. During each downtime, each character must make a Challenging (+0) Test using their chosen Skill; the highest result is used to determine success. Any characters who fail their roll gain advantage the next time they pursue this Endeavour, showing they have learned from their previous mistakes. Every time the party succeeds at this Endeavour, they gain one stage of reward, described as follows. No reward can be gained more than once:

  • Stage 1: Wariness regarding even seemingly benign xenos begins to reassert itself among the locals, who gain +5 Willpower when making Tests that resist the wiles of the xenos due to increased vigilance. This bonus does not apply to the characters, as they are presumably already as aware as they can be!

  • Stage 2: The group’s efforts have created a network of willing informants who report on xenos activity to the authorities. The characters gain +1 SL on Tests to gain intelligence on local xenos and their actions as long as they are either present on the world where the propaganda has been distributed or are inquiring about activity on that world from elsewhere in the Macharian Sector.

  • Stage 3: The world’s xenophobic zeal exceeds even the Imperial norm as the recently impious seek to prove their devotion to the returned status quo. The benefits of the previous level increase to +2 SLs instead of +1, and inhabitants of the affected planet all gain the Hatred (Xenos) Talent.

Research Cultist Network Ciphers

Requirement: Ordo Hereticus presence.

Cults of the Ruinous Powers or those under xenos influence are among the many threats Inquisitors of the Ordo Hereticus deal with regularly. While they are ever-vigilant, the cults often adapt in turn. The most powerful and entrenched cults spread their influence not through direct recruitment but through a network of loosely connected cells. These tenuous links between cult groups grant them enough internal cohesion to spread their influence but make rooting out the cult’s membership en masse nearly impossible.

Fortunately for the Inquisition, the very tools the cultist cells use to communicate can be turned against them. Acolytes skilled in ciphers, codes, and other esoteric forms of communication often find themselves tasked with decrypting cultist messages not just to learn what the cult is saying and doing but to break down the entire cult network if enough knowledge of signs and counter-signs can be gleaned.

Multiple characters can work together in this Endeavour. All involved must choose a cult network whose ciphers they have encountered in the past and will commit to decoding them. During each downtime, each character must make a Challenging (+0) Linguistics (Ciphers) Test or a similar Test using another Skill approved by the GM, such as Tech (Security), Stealth (Conceal), or Lore (Forbidden). The highest result is used to determine success. Any characters who fail their roll gain advantage the next time they pursue this Endeavour, showing they have learned from their previous mistakes.

Every time the party succeeds at this Endeavour, they gain one stage of reward, described as follows. No reward can be gained more than once:

  • Stage 1: The characters have grasped the essential identity markers the cult uses to authenticate their identities internally. Although not enough to incriminate specific individuals as cultists, the group can now identify suspected cultist correspondence with a mere Easy (+40) Linguistics (Ciphers) Test.

  • Stage 2: The characters have learned to tell specific cultist signifiers apart and can determine the particular cell from which a piece of correspondence originates, as well as the planet or region from which that cell hails, with a Routine (+20) Linguistics (Ciphers) Test. If the message was routed through multiple cells, determining the cell of origin is Challenging (+0) instead.

  • Stage 3: The characters recognise the cell from which messages originate and which cult figure sent a given message or signal. This is not the same as knowing their public identity but may assist with other clues in identifying such individuals. The group automatically learns the sender of a message upon determining its cell of origin, as described above.

  • Stage 4: The characters have laid bare every sign, code, counter-sign, and identifier in the cultist lexicon. If the cult does not realise its system is compromised, the groups can forge convincing false messages, tamper with messages en route, and commit other deceptions. They gain +2 SL when making appropriate Tests to meddle within the cult’s network.

Xenos Diplomacy

Requirement: Ordo Xenos presence.

Imperial doctrine holds that all contact with xenos is abhorrent, and no cooperation is possible at any scale. However, the Ordo Xenos is aware of multiple occasions on which the commonly-held dogma has been proven wrong, at least for a time. Although such instances are rare in the extreme, the Imperium has reaped benefits from temporary alliances of necessity with certain xenos species — foremost among them the Aeldari, specifically the Asuryani culture that inhabits the vast voidfaring vessels known as Craftworlds, aspects of the T’au Empire and their mercenaries, and recent contact with the Leagues of Votann.

Partnerships are possible even on the level at which the acolytes of the Inquisition operate, but xenos trust is never given without effort. There must be more than repeated contact to draw their interest in collaboration, even against mutual enemies. An acolyte hoping to appease members of any xenos culture must prove themselves worthy by the inscrutable standards of the alien. Such contact often requires significant research beforehand; it is impossible to understand the alien but this ensures that Imperial representatives do not show weakness or trip over themselves.

When a group performs this Long-Term Endeavour, they must make a Test with relevant Skills relating to the xenos species they aim to interact with, such as Lore (Forbidden) or Intuition (Group).

Each Test is Hard (−20) and no more than one Test per character can be made in a given period of relevant downtime. Multiple characters can work together in this endeavour; if they do, they each roll and the highest result is used. Any characters who fail their roll, gain advantage the next time they pursue this Endeavour, showing they have learned from their previous mistakes. Every time the party succeeds at this Endeavour, they gain one stage of reward, described as follows. No reward can be gained more than once.

  • Stage 1: The xenos group have noticed the character’s interest and may occasionally send Troop-tier contacts or other operatives to make contact. Characters involved gain +1 Influence with this xenos Faction.

  • Stage 2: Additional measures of leniency are extended to the characters by the xenos in their dealings. It is not enough to forgive a genuine wrong, but they accept minor missteps and poor communication more readily. Characters involved gain another +1 Influence with this xenos Faction.

  • Stage 3: The characters have tentative acceptance by the xenos as an ally — or at least, a useful pawn worth cultivating. Characters involved gain an additional +1 Influence with this xenos Faction. At the GM’s discretion, xenos NPCs may be willing to aid the characters in their future missions, providing unique pre-mission intel and in-mission support that Imperial Factions cannot.

pages.name: The Holy Orders
pages.text:
The Imperium is beset within and without by threats beyond counting and horrors beyond imagination. That it endures at all is a miracle of steadfast determination and the callous sacrifice of uncountable lives. Some of the Imperium’s foes can be met head-on, on unending battlefields and in the deep void of space. These threats can be cleansed by blessed promethium, cut down by the volleys of a thousand, thousand lasguns, or turned briefly into glittering clouds of expanding gas by a voidship’s macrocannon.

Other foes are stranger and more insidious, far more difficult to root out, but no less of an existential threat to the entire Imperium. The eternal vigil against such threats falls to @UUID[.AyQTdRJpdVm3zqdF]{The Holy Orders} of the Emperor’s Inquisition, as merciless and menacing an organisation as Humanity has ever known.

To citizens of the Imperium, Inquisitors appear omniscient, incomprehensibly powerful, and terrifyingly merciless in their duty to protect the Imperium. Countless tales have been told of the exploits of Inquisitors and their loyal acolytes, whispered amongst habworkers during a brief reprieve from their labours or shared between shivering @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} soldiers huddled in the muddy sanctuary of a frigid foxhole. Even the most outlandish of such stories can only begin to touch upon the truth of what it is to serve the Inquisition.

How could any who had not been there to witness his sacrifices understand why Inquisitor Tranth ordered the death of an entire world based on the testimony of just a single trusted acolyte? How could any who had not sworn secret oaths before an Inquisitor of the @UUID[.AyQTdRJpdVm3zqdF#ordo-malleus]{Ordo Malleus} know what it was to save a million lives, only to forfeit their own soul to the warp in the process?

Most Imperial citizens cannot begin to comprehend how much they owe to the Inquisition, nor can they guess at the horrors its Inquisitors have committed in their name.

While some might imagine a unified, all-knowing organisation, with nothing and no one beyond its reach, this is far from the truth. The Inquisition is an organisation of independent, often mutually hostile Inquisitors operating alone in the dark. Their alliances are temporary and rife with suspicion, their enmities enduring and often lethal. An Inquisitor has theoretically boundless authority, but its application lies entangled amid the Imperium’s bureaucratic and political hegemonies. Some of Humanity’s finest mortal warriors are among the Holy Orders — but none are infallible.

Every day, Inquisitors and their loyal acolytes face corruption that must be purged, though the very effort risks their own damnation. These hand-picked outcasts, oddities, and adepts act as an Inquisitor’s clandestine vanguard in their galaxy-spanning war. Despite their servant’s loyalty, many an Inquisitor has met their end at the hands of their most trusted acolyte — the prime witness of them crossing a line from which could be no return.

Nevertheless, without the Inquisition and its servants, the Imperium would surely burn.

GMs may also be interested in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7]{The Inquisition GM’s Guide}, a companion book that can aid them in crafting unforgettable stories — full of heretical plots, adventures, and NPCs to help them run investigative and espionage-focused missions. Players lacking sufficient clearance should beware of that sanctioned tome; it is intended for the GM’s eyes only!

pages.name: The Inquisitior
pages.text:
‘We are neither spies, soldiers, nor enforcers, yet we are all these at once. We are whatever the Imperium needs us to be. We alone know the horrors that await Mankind should the Imperium fall, so we alone are willing to do whatever it takes to prevent it. Whatever that makes us.’

— Lord Inquisitor Fidus Kryptman

In legend, an Inquisitor’s authority is second only to the Emperor Himself. Their holy duty is to identify and resolve threats within the Imperium: psykers, mutants, rebellion, corruption, xenos entities, and even traitorous incompetence fall under their jurisdiction. None are beyond their reach or above their scrutiny; even the most resolute, including the High Lords of Terra, are all vulnerable to corruption and failure. Ambition and greed cause immeasurable damage alone, but worse, they provide fertile soil for the Ruinous Powers to fester.

Inquisitors are terrifying individuals; in many cases, they are just as unnerving as the inhuman enemies they hunt. The burden of power they must wield is staggering. If their task suits them, Inquisitors can call on the resources of an entire world. Space Marine Chapters, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum}, Adepta Sororitas, and even Imperial Assassins are at their beck and call.

But Inquisitors know they must tread carefully with their authority; as much as they know their enemies, they understand the duplicitous nature of the Imperium’s factions and political landscape. Resources are finite, influence is never a guarantee, and bureaucracy always delays. Most Inquisitors prefer to operate from the shadows, employing acolytes and deniable assets to operate with utmost discretion.

Ascending to the position of Inquisitor is no simple task. It takes decades to build up networks of operatives, gather influence within the Adeptus Terra, and know their enemies so well as to risk corruption.

Parties can create their own Inquisitor Patron in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.ZzHsqdssD6GJyhDE]{Patrons of the Inquisition}. There are some sample @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.b06xyMjo4E4cYc40]{Inquisitor Patrons} available in The Inquisition GM's Guide. Each of these Patrons have their own guarded secrets and backstories tied to greater plots within the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W]{Heresies Macharia}.

Most have already proven themselves against the foes of the Emperor in one way or another — as battlehardened warriors, battlefleet generals, or indomitable psykers. Others may rise through an Inquisitor’s retinue via a direct apprenticeship as their Interrogator, an Inquisitor’s most trusted and capable acolyte, inheriting the position and power upon their mentor’s demise or when their master considers them ready for elevation.

It is a terrible truth that most Inquisitors die in service to the Emperor, survive long enough to succumb to radicalised ideas, or become corrupted by the Ruinous Powers they fight — an unfortunate byproduct of their necessary individualised methods and selfgarnered philosophies. Indeed, a staggering number of Inquisitors rose to their position by eliminating their former mentors as prime judges or witnesses of their fall from purity.

The threats they face are so beyond reason that the fear and antipathy they spread is a necessary evil of their work, all in service to the Imperium. Inquisitors know their duty must be unwavering, and mercy is a luxury no one can afford. No threat, within, without, or beyond, would hold back from eradicating Humankind if it gained a single foothold. They know that if one planet falls, certainly the next will, and so on, until hundreds of worlds and billions of lives are lost.

The Inquisitorial Rosette

Each Inquisitor, upon their ascension, forges a badge of office that admits them the highest level of clearance across the Imperium. This artefact is called an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.UmYkx98dKv97QSJy]{Inquisitorial Rosette}, and many of them have ingrained the Inquisitor’s genetic encoding within them. The Inquisitor designs their Rosette to represent their aesthetics, history, and mission, becoming a unique identifier of their authority. Theoretically, a Rosette can bypass any lock or barrier, physical or bureaucratic, that gets in the way of their investigation — the only barrier it cannot bypass is fickle Human behaviour.

pages.name: Philosophies
pages.text:
‘And yet you accuse me of being a madman, you who have never had your sanity tested so sorely. What right have you to call me heretic and blasphemer, who have not heard the whisper of the dark gods in your ear? You are weak. Vulnerable. Human in your frailty. I am strong, and yet you still judge me for my sins, thou who art most sinful to the heart? Every scholam child knows, “Only the insane have strength enough to prosper: only those who prosper truly judge what is sane”.’

— Eskender Thracius, Ordo Xenos Inquisitor, declared Excommunicate Traitoris

Each Inquisitor interprets Imperial doctrine differently. Given time and exposure to the Imperium’s greatest threats and the terrifying consequences of failure, their beliefs and ideals are tested constantly. Inquisitors find new ways to tread the line between faith and heresy to survive and succeed at their mission. However, new ways of thinking can harden into steadfast ideals that separate them further from the Imperial creed and their peers.

Foremost in this division, Inquisitors describe each other as Puritan or Radical: those who hold tight to their Ordo’s tenets and operate within fiercely conservative parameters, versus those who view the technologies and insights of their enemies as effective tools. Yet each Inquisitor believes they are right and just in their methods; those at opposite ends of this spectrum rarely cross paths without conflict.

Whether their investigations simply tread the same ground, strive for a different methodology in slaying the same foe, or see unacceptable losses in the outcome of the other’s plans, shadow wars can spark between Inquisitors and their acolytes, where the whole Imperium becomes their battlefield.

Most began their great mission as Puritans, their ascension to ultimate authority founded on their Holy Order’s or predecessor’s traditionalist beliefs. It is not until their beliefs are thoroughly tested that most Inquisitors begin to deviate towards Radicalism — when presented with a problem that requires drastic measures to solve. Some Inquisitors are well aware of the schisms their newfound actions and beliefs cause and the price it puts upon their head, so they often hide their true Philosophy behind one more traditionally accepted by their peers.

All these Philosophies, Puritan or Radical, have rich names and mystic ideals. But to an acolyte, initially, these points mean little. Rarely will an acolyte know of the particulars of their Inquisitor’s Philosophy; they are expected to believe in their Inquisitor no matter what they observe or are ordered to do.

Acolytes are expected to stay vigilant against heresy, but it is complicated when their masters cross unexpected lines. Their only choice is to rebel against the Inquisitor who uplifted them from obscurity or to believe wholly in their actions.

The most prominent Inquisition Philosophies represented in the Macharian Sector are outlined in greater detail in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.ZzHsqdssD6GJyhDE]{Patrons of the Inquisition} whilst many more are presented in depth in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.DvP1i46KYTgkMN0W]{Philosophies}, with accompanying plot hooks for GMs to draw their players into action and begin unravelling the Macharian Sector’s conspiracies.

pages.name: The Macharian Inquisition
pages.text:
When the Noctis Aeterna receded from most of the sector, Inquisitor Lord Hieronymo Drake, the Inquisition’s highest representative in the Macharian Sector, was discovered dead. Details surrounding his death remain a mystery, but as Inquisitor Lord of the sector, Drake was the only Inquisitor the others trusted or at least respected. Currently, no one has taken his place.

Inquisitor Sylverstrine Horst of the @UUID[.AyQTdRJpdVm3zqdF#ordo-hereticus]{Ordo Hereticus} was Lord Hironymo Drake’s former Interrogator. She learned long after the fact of her master’s demise, far from his side during the Noctis Aeterna. She’s since re-secured many of Drake’s assets and rebuilt what she could of his network. Horst now calls upon the Inquisitors of the Macharian Sector to gather in Conclave to regroup and co-ordinate the Inquisition’s missions — but Horst also suspects foul play on the death of Lord Drake, believing the other Inquisitors of the sector are withholding information.

Inquisitor Konstan Serranus of the @UUID[.AyQTdRJpdVm3zqdF#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} holds an exacting hatred of his alien enemies. His agents have evidence of increased Genestealer Cult activity at an alarming synchronicity across the sector. Serranus theorises that the Noctis Aeterna was the perfect cover the cults needed to accelerate their activities and infiltrate facets of the Macharian Adeptus Terra. He can see that the infestation is more advanced than anyone realises.

Inquisitor Alis Raud is a member of the @UUID[.AyQTdRJpdVm3zqdF#ordo-hereticus]{Ordo Hereticus}. Yet some suspect she serves a more obscure Holy Order, the @UUID[.AyQTdRJpdVm3zqdF#ordo-malleus]{Ordo Malleus}, whose mission combats daemons and monsters of the Warp. But speaking aloud of this Ordo and their enemy is a crime in and of itself. Daemonic activity can spawn wherever heresy plagues, so Raud has the most widespread and well-informed network of spies and operatives of her peers — who she also undoubtedly surveils.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.actors.Actor.Oh1HWiuX3Lmk0q0l]{Inquisitor Aegidius Halikarn} of the @UUID[.AyQTdRJpdVm3zqdF#ordo-hereticus]{Ordo Hereticus} believes a significant threat lies within the noble families who defied the Lord Solar Macharius during the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-macharian-conquests]{Macharian Crusade} and fled compliance. Halikarn suspects that the remnants of these nobles, now declared Excommunicate Traitoris, are working in the shadows. They seek to regain control of their former territories, plant themselves into other positions of power, or worse, they have already succeeded, and none are the wiser. Inquisitor Halikarn was introduced in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.arjSGA9gcUykxq0z]{The Blazing Seraph}, the featured adventure included in the Imperium Maledictum Starter Set.

Inquisitor Kai Varol of the @UUID[.AyQTdRJpdVm3zqdF#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos} investigates all manner of alien activity in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96]{Macharian Sector} and is a known expert in the Aeldari. Drukhari raiders and Aeldari Corsairs, in particular, are a bane to the sector’s voidborn and the Imperial fleet, leading waves of piracy across the outer reaches of the sector, assaulting Rogue Traders, and still settling worlds. If left unchecked, they may seek to claim Imperial worlds as their own.

Inquisitor Ksenia Baek of the @UUID[.AyQTdRJpdVm3zqdF#ordo-hereticus]{Ordo Hereticus} works tirelessly to investigate the threats posed by psykers and psychic phenomena. The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica} was stricken dearly by fallout from the Noctis Aeterna, causing many populated worlds to generate a considerable backlog of captured psykers. Until the Black Ships arrive, most worlds are ill-equipped to hunt down and contain this surplus. As a result, rogue psyker activity is on the rise. Inquisitor Baek is tackling the problem head-on, coordinating between the Astra Telepathica, their Black Ships, and Ministorum-led witch-hunts across the sector.

For GMs, the investigations and machinations of these Inquisitors continue in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.FNEW8e33IisZh27W]{Heresies Macharia}, a campaign framework filled with unique NPCs, missions, and plot hooks to drive Inquisition-focused campaigns throughout the Macharian Sector.

pages.name: Perception and Propaganda
pages.text:
‘The soul of the Imperium teeters on the edge of damnation. Our role is not only to prevent its fall, but to ensure that the blessedly ignorant masses never learn just how close we have come to failure.’

- Inquisitor @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.actors.Actor.Oh1HWiuX3Lmk0q0l]{Aegidius Halikarn}

In life, citizens of the Imperium are taught to fear and hate the xenos, the mutant, and the heretic. This education is proffered primarily by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.PdQjDIH5C6kx3vAy]{Ministorum} and seconded by every other facet of the Adeptus Terra; blessed is the mind too small for doubt.

But citizens are not taught to understand these horrors, for in understanding lies the first step on the path toward damnation. This task falls to the Inquisition and its acolytes. Few citizens understand the work that needs to be done, the sacrifices required, and the galactic scale of threats facing the Imperium.

Their fears and attitudes towards the Inquisition come from rumours and propaganda. Legends twisted through generational tale-telling and spread from hab level to spire, versus what measures the Inquisition has taken to spin worse truths in digestible lies, aiming to bolster their authority. But more often than not, an acolyte will stride into a world that is foreign to their presence, where no citizen has been before.

Acolytes should know what to expect when investigating or working alongside @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.RsIGQ61VYTusa8TR]{Imperial Citizens} or those under the banner of the Adeptus Terra — their initial reactions to Inquisitorial authority and why it might be in an acolyte’s better interest to obscure their identity. Following are some examples.

‘Of course, esteemed Acolytes, the planetary council will do everything in their power to aid you. My personal guard will be your guide, at your side night and day, even as you sleep. I’ll arrange for you to stay in private quarters at my estate. Your every need will be met, and you’ll never be left alone.’

— Jaspar Castyx, Planetary Governor of Voll

‘The eye that sees all, searching among my flock! Heresy is present here; I should’ve known. Extra services each day, benedictions and flagellations! We’ll sweat the heresy out of them, Acolyte! All must be told of your presence here! Bring the Emperor’s judgement to the people.’

— Sister Celestia of the Orders Hospitaller

‘Understood, Acolyte, I will aid you in your request, but understand, yours is not my highest priority. You and your master must respect the rights and privileges of the Priesthood of Mars, afforded to us by the Emperor of Mankind, just as He has afforded your authority here.’

— Artisan Hailon Epsilon Vorn, Tech-Priest

‘Curse me! Joven spoke of your kind the other day on the line. I told him to keep his mouth shut, or you’d appear out of thin air to damn us. I shouldn’t be talking to you; the Magos will put me in servitude imperpituis if they find out.

— Talin Stride, Manufactorum Worker

‘Take your authority back up the spire with you! You lot’re no better brutes than the Vigilites, and I’ve been fighting them for years. I won’t turn on my boys; you’ll have to kill me first.’

—Blister, Cutters Ganger

‘Emperor’s mercy! Please don’t scour my mind sir acolyte. Don’t take me away, I’ve a family to care for. We don’t know anything, please! I’ll say whatever you need me to say...’

—Fidget, Hab Rat

You should be talking to the Commissar. I’ve got my orders, too, and that’s to watch the line. Might not have to watch it so hard if you lot had done your job purging these foul xenos before they took over the planet. Me and the squad might still be back home rather than spend the best of our life guarding piles of mud…

— Kalli Tannerin, Militarum Trooper

pages.name: The Acolyte
pages.text:
Where Inquisitors are the iron will that refuses to bow to the enemies of mankind and the cunning mind whose plans thwart foul heretical schemes, their acolytes make up the rest of the Inquisition’s might. They are the sinew and muscle that execute the plan, the nervous system that ensures all limbs act in concert, and the mouth that gathers support or suppresses dissent. They are often specialised, unassuming, somewhat deniable, and largely expendable.

An acolyte’s duties do not offer excellent prospects for their futures; many who serve are damned to begin with. They face the Imperium’s worst enemies at every turn, horrors that can unravel the mind or confront them with fates worse than death; as such, very few survive for long, and most die horribly in the dark. The Imperium will never celebrate their names, but acolytes should know that their sacrifice is necessary for the Imperium to survive

Creating your Acolyte begins in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.QU6vEOUu69z190da]{Acolytes of the Inquisition}. In @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.beAtErDMWYboLh9i]{Skills, Talents and Psychic Powers}, you can grant new and existing characters with Talents and Psychic Powers and outfit them via the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.BbyZqcWs3HbrAO3Y]{The Inquisition's Armoury}.

++ URGENT COMMUNIQUE++
++GENE-CODED ENCRYPTION: ACOLTYE 57-DY894++
++IDENTIFICATION: INTERROGATOR MELNYK++

Acolyte, I pray your transportation to Goros Pok is going smoothly and that you remain undiscovered among your fellow travellers, the newly recruited labour workers from the Quannus system. You may have heard whispers from them that the Administratum has recorded a massive downturn in tithed materials exported from Goros Pok, and they are partly a solution to this problem. But this is all part of the Inquisition’s guise.

This is your mission: You are to accompany the labourers, embed yourself among them, and join them in their righteous toil to serve His graces each day. Become one of them, make them family, get to know their secrets and habits, who they talk to, and if they serve a master other than our great Emperor.

Inquisitor Baek suspects numerous heretical cults rooted among the planet’s labour forces, and they are skimming off the planet’s tithe. Furthermore, the Inquisitor is most interested in uncovering Rogue Psyker activity, especially in and around these cult leaders. We suspect Goros Pok is so riddled with heresy that eyes will be on you everywhere you go. Keep your wits about you.

It should go without saying, but it is imperative that the cults do not discover you. They may suspect an Inquisitorial presence, but the truth cannot evolve beyond their suspicion if we are to conduct our investigation efficiently.

I instruct you to memorise this information and destroy this communique before you make planetfall. We will be in contact. May the Emperor protect you.

Origins

‘I was a farmer for most of my life. We didn’t know the xenos were already living among us. I was forced to take up arms against the invasion when the war began. I needed to learn all I could about them to lead the fight; I had no choice. When the Inquisitor came and purged the xenos from our land, they spared my mind from being purged too, said I knew the enemy too well, and that my fight continues elsewhere…’

— Josef Karta, Acolyte

Inquisitors recruit their acolytes from among any of the Imperium’s organisations or agencies or from those they encounter during their investigations. The assets, informants, and casualties of the heresies they hunt who greatly impress them with unique or unspoken qualities.

Many individuals relish the opportunity to hand over a specialist from their faction, believing it can curry favour with the Inquisitor or thinking they can plant a loyal spy into the Holy Orders, while others resent their assets being commandeered altogether. Regardless, it is rare for an acolyte’s call to be refused by their faction or patron due to the Inquisitor’s limitless authority. Some are recruited directly from the Schola Progenium, particularly those who exhibit the rare qualities of an Inquisitor-in-training.

Other acolytes originate from the opposite end of this spectrum. Inquisitors often collect menageries of oddities and irregulars, those caught up in the collateral damage of their investigations, or those who reach the very edge of heresy but can still be redeemed — damaged survivors of xenos operations, rogue psykers who seek penance, cultists led astray by twisted doctrine — those with experiences as unique as any Inquisitor’s past.

Duty

‘That reverence you hold for the Emperor, the stuff you’ve been taught since you were a kid? Treat the Inquisitor just the same. They are an extension of His Will. Inquisitor says jump, you say, ‘off what spire?’. Inquisitor says purge, you use tooth and nail if that’s all you’ve got. Inquisitor says die; you run headfirst into whatever monstrous thing is staring back at you.’

— Interrogator Melnyk

The acolyte’s charge is to investigate heresies within the Imperium and purge them from existence. As straightforward as this sounds, how an acolyte conducts their investigations is as complicated as the heresies they must unravel. Most Inquisitors require acolytes to operate with utmost discretion and subtlety at all times and never to invoke their Inquisitor’s name. By the end of an investigation, it should appear as if they and the enemy they purged were never there, in neither the minds of the citizenry nor written Imperial record.

The grand stories and urban legends that people speak of the Inquisition; of holy wars, grand-scale purging and Exterminatus, are a product of propaganda or missions that got vastly out of hand. Acolytes should pray their investigations do not end in the latter state

Authority

Acolyte, I gave you no more of a stern warning than your fellows. My Rosette is not a child’s toy nor a ticket to be brazenly waved for passage. Though your actions saved Hive Sepkos for now, you have abused the authority I presented you. You will submit for re-indoctrination immediately or be hunted and executed by your peers. Conduct yourself properly, for once.

— Note attached to Reindoctrincation Order KL8934-M2d, Inquisitor Alis Raud

The Inquisitor cannot be in multiple places across the galaxy at once. Their acolytes act as an extension of their will, just as the Inquisitors act as an extension of the Emperor’s Will. So often, an acolyte’s authority begins and ends with their Inquisitor, how well they can draw on the threat of their influence and cult of personality without them being present.

This second-hand authority must be plied surgically. An acolyte could walk into a planetary court and present them with an @UUID[.8VTOoxqcL2uC3eZm#the-inquisitorial-rosette]{Inquisitorial Rosette}, but this is a foolhardy play for power. Any acolyte who did this would make as many enemies as allies, and would be outright dismissed as a hoax by just as many. As few as they are, long-lived acolytes spend decades building their own limited base of resources and influence to avoid invoking their Inquisitor’s authority until the moment is right.

Advancement

Make no mistake, doing what an Inquisitor asks is not the same as impressing them. Doing so is nigh impossible. Anyone mad enough to seek advancement in the Inquisitor’s retinue — anyone who truly sees the necessity of what the Inquisition does — should start by doing what their Inquisitor has already done: seek knowledge, garner assets and contacts, act decisively in the field, and steel themself against corruption. Smart acolytes will work with others in the retinue and become assets to each other, reaching towards the inner circle.

Ultimately, an acolyte will only rise as far as the Inquisitor deems necessary. Indeed, it takes an immaculate record, utmost competency, and blazing determination to become one of the Inquisitor’s most trusted acolytes, their Interrogator. Most Inquisitors have at least one to secure their legacy and lead in their stead; their rarity indicates how high a bar Inquisitors hold to truly earn their trust.

pages.name: Inquisitorial Espionnage
pages.text:
In many situations, it is helpful for acolytes to operate as covertly as possible, knowing that the eyes of the enemy lurk in every shadow and that even a granular leak of information could mean the failure of their operation or their death. The deeper the cover and obfuscation from their foes, the greater the moves they can make in their shadow war, without hindrance or risking death, and to the unacknowledged appreciation of their Inquisitor. However, there are complicated rules to follow when maintaining this level of subterfuge. Acolytes should gather an excess of information. Build a second life of integrity that no one can question. Always be ready for their enemy, and always have a backup plan.

++ SURVEILANCE TRANSCRIPT++
++ SUBMITTED: ACOLTYE 83-MU548++
++ SUBJECT: HOUSE REPRESENTATIVE++
++KORV SUMALAK++

…

[DAY VI] Subject never left villa. One visitor, an unidentified representative of House Vylathi, description forwarded to contacts for identification. Both were inside for close to three hours, visitor appears clearly angered.

[DAY VII] Subject left villa only once, visit to Sumalak House Commissary IGH-93 in the lower hive. The location flagged for further investigation.

[DAY VIII] Subject never left villa, once again. Received delivery of goods from House Sumalak servants. Will reposition surveillance during next change of guard to get better vantage on subject’s quarters.

[DAY IX] Subject spotted on villa balcony. Right hand ungloved, appears to have an extra finger on their right hand. Requesting higher fidelity optics to be sure.

Acolytes acting together in a cell can share the burden of espionage, dividing tasks among those who can best complete them — a stiff @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Mechanicus} @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.rilaQaBPslIRzGco]{Tech-Priest} may not be the best choice to parlay with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{infractionist} contacts, nor an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} warrior the best at sourcing and tuning the team’s equipment. One acolyte’s extravagant failure can negatively affect the cell, but failure can often be avoided by choosing the best acolyte for the job.

In play, many of these aspects can be represented by deft roleplaying, but larger drawn-out tasks can be tackled by characters between missions, from the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.r6clx5uYnIpkdaRq.JournalEntryPage.zt3agZuaQd99PTyc]{Endeavours} included in this book or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX.JournalEntryPage.AuM2Lzd784VPe32b]{Imperium Maledictum}, some particular examples we will list in the following sections. Most investigations take months or years, so GMs are encouraged to give players ample time to enact these Endeavours and build the necessary resources.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.KbejcPMug5gfoWWz]{Subtlety} is another threat and tool to consider. While everything a character does will likely impact the party’s Subtlety levels, it can also be invaluable to know how close they are to crossing the line of discovery. If they are close to discovery, they must decide whether to enact their masterstroke or retreat expeditiously and bear the wrath of their Inquisitor instead of their enemy.

Contacts

A well-wrought network of Contacts can provide an acolyte or cell with information or opportunities they could not otherwise obtain. Just as the Inquisitor often picks acolytes to fill a gap in their knowledge or capabilities, acolytes should do the same with their Contacts.

Each Contact is often worth investigating to some degree to gauge how trustworthy they are, what secret ties they might have, and even to garner some blackmail to hang over their heads. Finding good contacts can be time-consuming, as can keeping them loyal to the cause.

Those at the fringes of their organisations, those less loyal, scorned, or close to being branded as infractionists, are often the best Contacts to make. If played right, these individuals will fear an acolyte’s authority outright, be caught between the Inquisition and their own faction, or see the cell as their salvation and be more willing to turn on their former masters.

Characters can explore the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.r6clx5uYnIpkdaRq.JournalEntryPage.z9PTik4AMrYlbVhR#cultivate-network]{Cultivate Network} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.r6clx5uYnIpkdaRq.JournalEntryPage.z9PTik4AMrYlbVhR#secure-information-network]{Secure Information Network} Endeavours or the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX.JournalEntryPage.AuM2Lzd784VPe32b#consult-savant]{Consult Savant} Endeavour. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.2TukBjlkS5RG5Qka]{Inquisition Contacts} provides more advice for using Contacts, including a roster of sample Contacts that the GM can weave into their adventures for players to encounter.

Escape Plans

Acolytes should always be prepared to drop their investigations and run at a moment’s notice. Most Inquisitorial investigations take a long time to prepare, but being confronted by their enemy before they’re ready can mean certain death. Obtaining transportation off-world or finding a quiet place to go to ground until the heat is off them is often up to them to secure.

A truth that new acolytes often find hard to swallow is that the information they’ve gathered in an investigation is usually more important than their lives. Extracting that information safely or placing it into the hands of another acolyte cell — via dead drops or highly trusted contacts — should take priority over their lives.

In both instances, the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX.JournalEntryPage.AuM2Lzd784VPe32b#scout-surroundings]{Scout Surroundings} Endeavour could be used to find an escape route from the cell’s hideout or secure dead-drop locations for other acolytes to find.

Leaving No Trace

The Inquisition relies on its secrets to stay just so — far away from the average citizen’s awareness. This includes aspects of its own operations but also extends to its enemy’s presence. If citizens learned of the unimaginable horrors that secretly surround them and those that claw at the edge of the Imperium, there would be widespread unrest, mass hysteria, and even civil war.

Acolytes need to clean up after themselves and take care of the bodies at hand so no skeletons remain to haunt them or their Inquisitor later. In addition to scouring the presence of their enemies, this could mean silencing witnesses, sending them for hypno-indoctrination to wipe the very memories from their minds, or implementing a propaganda campaign to rewrite the history of what happened. The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.r6clx5uYnIpkdaRq.JournalEntryPage.z9PTik4AMrYlbVhR#erase-truth]{Erase Truth} Endeavour can aid acolytes here, but they may need to make some hard decisions and put in extra effort to truly wipe the slate clean.

Low Profiles & Alter Ego

Acolytes need to tread lightly and keep their heads down at all times. Even minor mishaps could draw the attention of local guards or Vigilites, who may misunderstand the character’s intentions or put a greater spotlight on the Inquisition’s presence within their jurisdiction. Acolytes should guard their true identity with their lives, even better if they have an entirely new identity that can burn instead of their own.

Once their true identity is revealed, or they are caught out in the open, that damning information often spreads like wildfire, and their usefulness as nameless agents is lost. This brazenness plants a clear target on their head, making the remaining days of the investigation numbered or over.

Though the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX.JournalEntryPage.AuM2Lzd784VPe32b#garner-reputation]{Garner Reputation} Endeavour may not help in keeping a low profile, consider using it to solidify the integrity of a character’s Alter Ego.

Tools Of The Trade

A well-armed acolyte can certainly threaten or kill a target, but they need an altogether different arsenal to aid them in other aspects of their investigation. Their base of operations could be better protected with a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.deHQEH976yh9nI9y]{Signal Jammer} or outfitted with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.rgkUmSGkBrOKvo5p]{Pict Recorders} to surveil nearby comings and goings. An @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.paXqMCUFqcpVEEBE]{Excruciator Kit} or a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.uO5IZi3jF2NrIUqS]{Soulguilt Scanner} might work better than the threat of death in an interrogation. Even a solid pair of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.7lBipnmSZ4lD5WCo]{Magnoculars} shouldn’t be forgotten by those surveilling their targets. Plentiful tools are available in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.BbyZqcWs3HbrAO3Y]{The Inquisition's Armoury} or the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y]{Armoury} chapter. Bespoke or modified equipment can be obtained by petitioning the character’s Patron or using the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX.JournalEntryPage.AuM2Lzd784VPe32b#commission]{Commission} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX.JournalEntryPage.AuM2Lzd784VPe32b#crafting]{Crafting} Endeavours.

pages.name: Know Thy Enemy
pages.text:
‘I have clashed with creatures the sight of which would sear your soul to the core. I have bested horrors that chill with a gaze and tempt unreasoning terror. I have faced death eye to eye and blade to blade. I have stared into the eyes of insanity and met their all-consuming stare. I have done all this for you, for your protection, and to guarantee a future for Humanity. You dare, you who cowers, quivering in the safety of your glittering hive, to question me!?’

— Inquisitor Alis Raud

The average citizen of the Imperium, toiling loyally in service to the Emperor’s will, knows well enough that heretics hide amongst them. Does the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum} not preach against them, and warn all of the heretic’s wiles and vices? Most have also heard of the mighty battles waged against the Imperium’s foes, foul xenos and traitorous souls who blindly oppose His will. Each of these is a terrible threat and yet, bereft of both faith and the Emperor’s grace, little more than fodder for the Imperium’s vigilant protectors. Few understand the true scale of either threat, that heretics have claimed whole worlds for their foul masters, or that entire sectors are overrun by inhuman xenos, their worlds despoiled, and their populations slaughtered.

Even fewer know the truth of the Warp and its daemons, which for most are little more than myths, hinted at only in esoteric passages drawn from the Imperial creed. Nor is it widely known that the Inquisition, purportedly the Imperium’s most vigilant guardian, is often at war with itself. Inquisitors frequently brand each other as radicals or heretics, and the shadow wars that have played out have often been ruinous.

All this is kept hidden in the name of peace, the gift of ignorance bestowed by means of propaganda and blatant lies. As a result, most are blind to the horrors of the galaxy until just before they are devoured by one of them — the Imperium’s final gift to its loyal servants.

This comforting mantle of ignorance is ripped away from the newly inducted acolyte. Some have difficulty adjusting to the harrowing truth, but mercifully no acolyte is burdened with all of it at once; most come to steady realisations through their investigations alone.

Within the borders of the Imperium, the Inquisition’s insidious enemies operate in secrecy, and the earliest stages of an investigation typically seek to determine what threat the cell faces. The sooner this is discovered the better, both to prepare for the battle ahead and to call for further resources if required.

Acolytes must be fearful of making assumptions. To presume that every enemy they face will matche the chosen foes of their Inquisitor’s Ordo is a mistake. What appears as a heretical cult on the surface may be ruled by a rogue psyker, Genestealer Cultist, or a force utterly esoteric. Each presents novel dangers and requires a different exacting method to purge.

An acolyte should be ready for anything, including the opposing forces of other Inquisitors. Disagreements between Inquisitors can escalate quickly, as most are used to their nigh-infinite authority and become incensed at having their methods questioned. Few foes are as deadly as the forces of another Inquisitor who, tempered by the trials of their service, are often as inhuman and lethal as any alien, mutant, or heretic.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.3j1kargHBeCTssE7]{Superiority} is a massive boon to any acolyte cell and a measure of their preparedness. A primary method of securing Superiority is a natural reward for meticulous investigation.

The Enemy Within

Action I: Verbal interview without duress.
Action II: Verbal threat of and description of Actions that may follow.
Action III: Light physical torture.
Action IV: Light physical torture and psychological manipulation.
Action V: Sensory and physical deprivation.
Action VI: Psychic interrogation.
Action VII: Intensive psychic interrogation.
Action VIII: Use of psycho-chemical drugs.
Action IX: Classified. (Exact details not described, but two days of Ninth Action would probably kill a subject.)

— Standard actions of interrogation, as described within Inquisitor Crowe’s Rubric of Protocol

Mutant filth, rogue psykers, traitors and apostates of false creeds; heretics, one and all, and the foremost threat to the soul of the Imperium, a rot from within its very heart.

As their first lesson in hunting heretics, acolytes are taught an unfortunate truth: their charge hides among the people they have sworn to protect. Yet they can afford no mercy or hesitation in cutting heresy down wherever they find it. Some traitors may not even believe in their heresy, fed toxic doctrine, or false promises of salvation. Most are damned from such corruption. Those close to crossing the line can be re-educated or granted penance, handed over to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Ministorum}. In the worst cases, the Inquisition has hypno-indoctrination programs to erase, bury, or realign memories in a person’s mind. Still, such methods always carry risks and should be applied to essential assets.

Many acolytes of the @UUID[.AyQTdRJpdVm3zqdF#ordo-hereticus]{Ordo Hereticus} monitor particular institutions of the Adeptus Terra, surveilling where corruption has appeared in the past in case it rises again. Acolytes may be assigned to liaise closely with these factions or be planted as an undercover operative, often supported by a web of informants. The target of their investigations is carefully monitored. Left to fester for too long, even minor heresies can give rise to tremendous fractures — such as the rise of dissident cults within the Ministorum or Hereteks within the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}.

Most cults use subtle symbols and cryptography to communicate with and identify their hidden members. These icons could range from simple, intentional alterations to existing Low Gothic glyphs to deeper subversion of Imperial iconography. An acolyte is likely to encounter the most prominent icon, an eight-pointed octogram or star, a symbol of Chaos that dates back to the traitor legions of the Horus Heresy. The Inquisition recruits cryptographers from across the Imperium to study heretical icons, find links between different cults, and understand their communication methods

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.KN6hJOFxExaZ7fYL#witch-marks-and-other-heresies]{Witch marks} in particular, brands of the Ruinous Powers, are said to empower those afflicted with unnatural powers. Nurgle cultists are often branded with boils and rot, diseases they carry with a twisted pride. Tzeentchian cults are deeply obsessed with the number nine and brand themselves in nonagonal patterns. Khornate worshippers are rarely without a branded skull or markings daubed with blood, whereas some Slaaneshi cultists appear with contortions or knots in their flesh that border on mutilation. Many more of these associations can be uncovered by studious research and in-field investigation — all said, acolytes must have their wits about them to recognise patterns or marks of heresy that could point their inquest in the right direction.

Acolytes should be vigilant for signs of mutation among groups of heretics. By their very nature, mutants are already far down the path of corruption, malleable clay for the Ruinous Powers to mould into new agents of Chaos. Living on the edges of Humanity, mutants are easily driven into the arms of charismatic leaders, desperate to find communities where they fit in. Those who carry a similar affliction often want to band together — and as with Marks of Chaos, similarities in mutations are frequently a pattern worth investigating.

The most dangerous heretics are Rogue Psykers. Acolytes who suspect they have encountered a Rogue Psyker should immediately report their existence to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica} and work with local authorities to capture or monitor them until backup arrives. Proceed with caution, as these aberrations often exhibit dark and unnatural powers, from casting mutating hexes or conjuring witchfire to mind control, telekinesis, or bewildering illusion. Unnatural distortions in the Warp usually antecede the presence of their vile powers: lingering hoarfrost, distorted reflections, knots in memory, or gravitational shifts.

The Enemy Beyond

‘Disregard the gaps you feel in your memory – know that you have seen too much, and removal was necessary. The [REDACTED] completed their mission on [REDACTED]; the [REDACTED] threat led by [REDACTED] were effectively purged by their supreme will. But take heed; perhaps we overshot our ambitions this time.’

— Message from Acolyte Peytr Strolke, Sent to Acolyte Peytr Strolke.

Beyond mundane reality, the Immaterium holds innumerable daemonic horrors and unthinkable entities. Humanity can only begin to understand the nature of these warp abominations; even those within the Inquisition only understand a small measure more. What is understood is their tenacity to corrupt, their unstoppable scheming, and their covetous nature towards the material. To stand against the enemy beyond is to place your life on the path of their corruption — acolytes who do so find themselves altered forever but stand against the greatest threat to life itself. Even less is understood of the ancient entities atop this chaotic pantheon — personified deities and concepts of mortal obsessions and fears given form — that wield unimaginable power and foster infinite malice.

In the cultist’s tongue are Khorne, Tzeentch, Nurgle, and Slaanesh. These deific nightmares garner power as Humanity’s fears and corruption grow and can spread their psychic whispers anywhere Humanity is at its worst.

Paramount to any acolyte’s mission when hunting daemons is containment and cleanup, especially in the eyes of the populace. Imperial citizens have some notion about the nature of daemons but in a largely symbolic context. The truth of the Warp would break the mind of an average Human, and if enough minds break, the integrity of the Imperium would suffer irrecoverably. Daemonic activity must be suppressed and scoured from the record as if it were never there. As a last resort, people should believe that strange occurrences are attributed to ‘xenos’ or ‘mutant’ meddling rather than a breach of reality as they know it.

In worse cases, swathes of the populace can meet execution for their exposure to daemonic corruption. As always, the dire ends justify the means, but such a sacrifice tarnishes the Inquisition’s reputation — for any incursion to reach that level often means someone was not doing their job correctly. Physical daemonic corruption cannot stand in any case. Exorcism is possible, but it is a dangerous and costly procedure, prone to disaster. Despite what whispers an acolyte may have heard about Daemonhosts, the existence of such vessels cannot be tolerated; such is the Puritan stance on the matter.

No daemon, even the lowliest @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.pGOi4dyYeKojE9vm]{Nurgling} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.jPEYTvQIqOBwHU6q]{Brimstone Horror}, should be treated lightly. In the face of such horrors, most acolytes would rather flee to safety. But as agents of the Inquisition, they are obliged to stand against the enemy and make necessary sacrifices. In most cases, they will be the only ones standing between the Immaterium and those they are sworn to defend. The best they can do is signal for help through secure channels and hold out for as long as possible.

Where most @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.O9kga3ngGfFyIsze]{daemons} appear as unthinkable horrors, others are more insidious and lurk among Humanity, wearing Human flesh or plying their influence through hidden heretical cults. Some must do so to emerge from the Immaterium fully, urging their worshippers to conduct profane rituals to cut a rift in the Warp. Among these heretics, the ultimate betrayers are keen to barter their Humanity to the Ruinous Powers. They seek to ascend to daemonhood, standing as Daemon Princes beside their unholy brethren, grasping for immortality and powers beyond their comprehension.

The Enemy Without

Invading forces beset all borders of the Macharian Sector — foul xenos entities seek to reach in and claim Imperial worlds as their own. The militarised arms of the Adeptus Terra face these foes in the void or upon contested soil. Meanwhile, the Inquisition looks inward, where invaders have slipped through defences or appear seemingly out of nowhere. The enemy without works its machinations to prey upon Mankind, as if the God Emperor’s children were no better than vermin or cattle.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.6FUPGNRUs8T8uoa5]{Xenos} are countless in vileness and variation. It is impossible for an acolyte to study them all, so like their Inquisitors, they may find it beneficial to hone their research on a singular xenology. Aiming to understand an alien’s true purpose is folly, some would say more challenging than the entities of Chaos, for at least they bear some relationship to Humanity’s desires, even in grim reflection. Inquisitorial doctrine states: that which is inhuman is unclean and must, therefore, be eradicated. Afford xenos no more mercy than a heretic or a daemon.

Two species, in particular, appear to pose a significant threat within the Macharian Sector, yet the Inquisition understands only fragments of their technology, culture, and capabilities.

The Aeldari employ unknown void travel technology to slip through the Imperial Fleet’s defensive lines and conduct cryptic missions unimpeded. Their Drukhari sub-species are better known as void pirates who assault Imperial fleet vessels. They are swift and vicious aliens. Some have been spotted planetside raiding Imperial outposts and capturing citizens for reasons unknown. Some have been caught subjugating Imperial bases of power for equally inconclusive ends.

During the Noctis Aeterna, lax security allowed several Genestealer Cults to take root among Imperial settlements, particularly Hive Cities. It’s suspected that these insidious cults are playing a generations-spanning long game. Many of their agents look barely different from the average Human; most are trained in deception and subversion. Their tactics and methods corrupt Humanity without a doubt; one Inquisitor believes they are working towards a more destructive endgame for the sector.

Traces of other xenos threats claw the sector’s worlds, all highly classified within the @UUID[.AyQTdRJpdVm3zqdF#ordo-xenos]{Ordo Xenos’} archives; many represent existential threats to the Imperium. Ork invasions can appear without much warning and raze nearly any Imperial world to ruin. Genestealer Cults in the sector, by extension, prove the existence of a Tyranid Hive Fleet. One is on its way, though arriving at a time the Inquisition is yet to ascertain. Tomb Worlds are believed to be hidden throughout the sector, those belonging to the Necrons, who may one day rise to reclaim their ancient empire. The Inquisition knows that the Imperium’s time is numbered — but every Inquisitor and their acolytes must fight to stay the tide for as long as possible and pray for the Emperor’s salvation.

Some xenos position themselves as traders or mercenaries and claim to stand on equal footing with Humanity — such as the enigmatic Leagues of Votann or Kroot Carnivores hailing from the T’au Empire. An acolyte should not believe these lies. Xenos artefacts work wonders to undermine the Imperium’s sanctified technologies, yet are another form of subversion and corruption, proven by the sector’s prolific silent trade. As for mercenaries, their loyalties will always lie with their xenos kin. Anyone who works with xenos entities proclaims themselves a traitor to Humanity and should be treated no better than the xenos with which they ally

pages.name: The Holy Orders
pages.text:
‘HERETICUS – FAITH IS MY SHIELD
MALLEUS – ZEAL IS MY SWORD
XENOS – HATE IS MY SPEAR’

— Inscription upon Conclave chamber doors, Mare Cinis, Suluk

Though Inquisitors primarily operate as individuals, most belongs to a Holy Order that defines their primary targets, general mission, and access to highly restricted resources. The Ordo Hereticus, Ordo Malleus, and Ordo Xenos represent the Imperium’s most significant threats and categorise the Inquisitors within by their mission and specialities.

For Inquisitors to be part of a Holy Order does not place extra burdens upon their shoulders, wrap a chain of command around their necks, nor lessen their authority in any way — the Holy Orders are better defined as an association of equal individuals who freely collaborate to share information or pursue a common target.

Inquisitors know that too much organisation or over-collaboration can restrict their authority and further complicate their missions. Inquisitors rarely agree on the exact method of achieving their goals; even under the banner of the same Order, Inquisitors can quickly come to a clash in philosophy or risk leaking secrets that could facilitate their demise.

Acolytes should also be aware of Conclaves: secretive in-person meetings between various Inquisitors, brought together under the banner of a particular sector or gathered by shared expertise. In practice, any Inquisitor can call for a Conclave, and their brethren should do their best to answer the call — yet attendance may rely upon the trustworthiness or respect others have for the instigator.
